docs.x: Reads: servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/**, servers/fastapi/api/v2/**, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/nextjs/app/api/**/route.ts, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts, nginx.conf · Builds on: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP, Auth and multi-user · Time: ~30 min (reference) This appendix is a complete, mechanically built index of every HTTP surface in the Presenton snapshot: all 102 FastAPI application routes, the 11 Next.js API route files, the MCP tools, and every nginx location block. For each FastAPI route you get the method, the full path after all router prefixes, the handler function, the exact decorator line, the access class enforced by SessionAuthMiddleware and the handler, and a one-line purpose. The first steps explain how the index was produced and how to read the access column, so you can rebuild it after upstream changes.

docs.t: Step 1: How the full paths are assembled
docs.x: FastAPI composes a route's public path from the prefix of every APIRouter it is nested in. Presenton nests routers at most three levels deep. servers/fastapi/api/main.py:68 to servers/fastapi/api/main.py:74 include seven top-level routers on the app: servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) API_V1_PPT_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22, prefix /api/v1/ppt) includes seventeen endpoint routers, API_V1_AUTH_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:27) includes the Presenton Cloud provider router at servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:28, and API_V2_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v2/router.py:6, prefix /api/v2) includes API_V2_PPT_ROUTER (prefix /ppt), which includes PRESENTATION_V2_ROUTER (prefix /presentation). The complete prefix table, with the line that declares each router: Router variable Declared at Own prefix Effective prefix API_V1_AUTH_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:27 /api/v1/auth /api/v1/auth PRESENTON_OAUTH_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:29 /presenton /api/v1/auth/presenton API_V1_ADMIN_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:41 /api/v1/admin /api/v1/admin API_V1_ASYNC_TASKS_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py:14 /api/v1/async-tasks /api/v1/async-tasks API_V1_WEBHOOK_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/webhook/router.py:10 /api/v1/webhook /api/v1/webhook API_V1_MOCK_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/mock/router.py:9 /api/v1/mock /api/v1/mock FILES_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:16 /files /api/v1/ppt/files FONTS_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py:18 /fonts /api/v1/ppt/fonts OUTLINES_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:40 /outlines /api/v1/ppt/outlines SLIDE_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:30 /slide /api/v1/ppt/slide IMAGES_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/images.py:31 /images /api/v1/ppt/images ICONS_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/icons.py:7 /icons /api/v1/ppt/icons OLLAMA_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/ollama.py:13 /ollama /api/v1/ppt/ollama OPENAI_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/openai.py:9 /openai /api/v1/ppt/openai OPENROUTER_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/openrouter.py:11 /openrouter /api/v1/ppt/openrouter ANTHROPIC_ROUTER servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/anthropic.py:9 /anthropic /api/v1/ppt/anthropic GOOGLE_ROUTER

docs.t: Step 2: How the index was built and checked
docs.x: The route rows below were extracted with a short Python script that parses every file under servers/fastapi/api/ with the standard ast module, finds every decorator of the form @<NAME>.get|post|put|patch|delete|api_route(...), reads the literal path argument, and joins it with the effective prefix of <NAME> from the table in Step 1. That produced 101 decorated routes. A second pass with grep -E "_ROUTER\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|api_route)" found 102 matches; the extra one is the only route in the codebase registered without decorator syntax: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py (excerpt) There is no add_api_route, no @app.get, no api_route and no websocket route anywhere outside the tests. The only other decorator on app is the HTTP middleware at servers/fastapi/api/main.py:106. As an independent cross-check, the committed OpenAPI document servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json (the file the MCP server loads) contains 93 paths and 100 operations. Every operation in it appears in this index. Two routes in the code are absent from that file: POST /api/v1/ppt/images/test and POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/regenerate. Gotcha openai_spec.json is a static snapshot written by servers/fastapi/scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py (json.dumps(app.openapi(), ...)). It is not regenerated at startup. The MCP server reads it at import time (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:281), so if you add or change a route that an MCP tool maps to, you must regenerate the file or the MCP tool keeps the old schema. In this snapshot the file already lags the code by two routes. Total: 102 FastAPI application routes. On top of those, FastAPI itself serves /openapi.json, /docs, /docs/oauth2-redirect and /redoc, and the app mounts /static (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:86) plus seven owner-scoped static mounts /app_data/{exports,fonts,images,pptx-to-html,pptx-to-json,templates,uploads} created by mount_app_data_assets (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:39) when APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is set. Route count by area: Area Routes Area Routes Auth (local + Presenton Cloud link) 9 Images 7 Admin 10 Icons 1 Async tasks 2 Fonts 5 Webhook 2 Templates 14 Mock 2 Providers (models, Ollama, Codex, generation defaults) 15 Presentation (v1) 17 Chat 5 Outlines 3 Community 2 Slide 2 Presentation (v2, Smart) 2 Files 4 Total 102

docs.t: Step 3: How the access class is decided
docs.x: Access control is applied in two layers. The first is SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:55), which runs for every request. The second is a per-handler dependency on a few routers. The relevant lists, verbatim: servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt) A principal is resolved by resolve_request_principal (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22): first the presenton_session cookie (a JWT, method="jwt"), then an Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... API key (method="api_key"). The admin-only check requires principal.method == "jwt" and is_admin, which is why an administrator's API key is still rejected on admin paths. The legend used in the Access column: Access value Meaning Public Listed in _PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS; the middleware lets it through without a principal. The handler may still check the cookie itself. User Any principal: a browser session cookie or a valid user API key. Rows the user does not own are filtered by the ORM owner scope described in Auth and multi-user. Admin (JWT) Matched by the middleware admin_only rule: the caller must be an administrator using a browser session cookie. API keys get 403. User, handler admin The middleware accepts any principal, but the handler dependency (get_current_admin, require_settings_admin or require_presenton_manager) reads only the session cookie and requires is_superuser. Gotcha DISABLE_AUTH=true (the Electron runtime) short-circuits the middleware completely: every route is reachable without a principal. However, the admin handlers that depend on get_current_admin (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:219) still read the cookie, find no user, and return 401. So in auth-disabled mode /api/v1/admin/api-keys and /api/v1/admin/users are unusable, while /api/v1/admin/provider-settings works because require_settings_admin returns early when auth is disabled (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:136). Gotcha The font rule is method based: every POST or DELETE under /api/v1/ppt/fonts/ is admin only. That includes POST /api/v1/ppt/fonts/check, which only analyzes a PPTX. The custom template hook calls it (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/hooks/useTemplateCreation.ts:150), so a non-admin user running that flow receives a 403 from this call. Middleware order also matters. Starlette wraps the most recently added middleware outermost, so for a request

Method Path Handler Source Access Purpose GET /api/v1/auth/status get_status servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:58 Public Returns configured, authenticated, username, user_id, role for the session cookie. With auth disabled it always answers username: "electron", role: "admin". GET /api/v1/auth/verify verify_session servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:81 Public (handler requires principal) Resolves cookie or API key, 401 if none. If X-Original-URI is present it applies the /app_data ownership rule (403 on mismatch). This is nginx's auth_request target. POST /api/v1/auth/setup setup_credentials servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:110 Public Creates the first account as is_superuser=True, admin_slot="primary". 409 once any user exists. Does not log in (authenticated: false). POST /api/v1/auth/login login servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:155 Public Case-insensitive username lookup, password verify with transparent rehash, sets the presenton_session cookie (30 days, httponly, samesite=lax). 428 before setup. POST /api/v1/auth/logout logout servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:191 Public Deletes the session cookie and returns {"success": true}.

docs.t: Step 9: Paths the Presenton Cloud proxy intercepts
docs.x: When an administrator links Presenton Cloud and selects LLM=presenton, SessionAuthMiddleware forwards certain requests to the cloud instead of the local handler, through maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:407). The matching rule is should_proxy_presenton_cloud (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:105): Set Paths CLOUD_GENERATION_PATHS /api/v1/ppt/files/upload, /api/v1/ppt/files/decompose, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare CLOUD_EDIT_PATHS /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update CLOUD_SMART_PATHS /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate-html/init, /api/v2/ppt/presentation/update CLOUD_API_PATH_PREFIXES /api/v1/async-tasks, /api/v1/ppt/outlines/, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/, /api/v1/ppt/template/, /api/v1/ppt/community/presentations, /api/v1/ppt/chat/, /api/v2/ppt/presentation/stream/ CLOUD_PRIVATE_ASSET_PATH_PREFIXES /app_data/images/, /app_data/exports/, /app_data/uploads/, /app_data/pptx-to-html/, /app_data/pptx-to-json/ Gotcha CLOUD_SMART_PATHS and the /api/v2/ppt/presentation/stream/ prefix name paths that have no local FastAPI route in this snapshot. They only exist upstream on Presenton Cloud. With any other provider selected, a request to them falls through to the router and returns 404. Do not count them as local endpoints. The community prefix is GET-only through the proxy (_READ_ONLY_CLOUD_PREFIXES). How the cloud proxy rewrites and persists results is outside this index; see Configuration and LLM providers.

The Next.js server exposes its own /api/* routes, separate from FastAPI. All of them pass through proxy.ts first (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:97), whose matcher covers every path except _next/static and favicon.ico. For /api/*, proxy.ts requires a session unless the path is exempt: servers/nextjs/proxy.ts (excerpt) It also rewrites /api/v1/*, /api/v2/*, /app_data/* and /static/* to FastAPI (rewriteToFastApi, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:43). In Docker nginx catches those paths first, so the rewrite matters in Electron and in direct next dev setups. A request carrying Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... to a non-FastAPI path gets 403 "API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API". servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py builds an MCP server with FastMCP.from_openapi over the static openai_spec.json. It runs on 127.0.0.1:8001 with transport http (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:457), forwards every tool call to FastAPI at http://127.0.0.1:8000 with a 600 s read timeout and 15 s connect timeout, and exposes only an allowlist of routes. Everything else is excluded by the final RouteMap(mcp_type=MCPType.EXCLUDE) (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:124). MCP tool name Generated name it renames HTTP route Enabled when PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE is start_standard_presentation generate_presentation_async_api_v1_ppt_presentation_generate_async_post POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async standard, both list_templates template_list GET /api/v1/ppt/template/all standard, both upload_template_assets mcp_template_upload POST /api/v1/ppt/template/mcp-upload standard, both start_template_generation create_template_api_v1_ppt_template_async_post POST /api/v1/ppt/template/async standard, both start_smart_presentation generate_smart_presentation_async POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart/async smart, both upload_files mcp_files_upload POST /api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload always get_job_status check_async_task_status_api_v1_async_tasks_status__id__get GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id} always The default mode is both (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:24), so a stock deployment advertises all seven tools. Authentication works as follows. When auth is enabled, create_mcp_auth_provider returns a PresentonTokenVerifier (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:285) that accepts only tokens starting with sk-presenton-, verifies them with the same verify_api_key the REST API uses, and mints an internal session JWT with MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60. attach_request_auth_header (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:365) then sends that JWT to FastAPI as the presenton_session cookie and adds X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, so the long-lived API key never reaches a REST handler. The MCP header makes absolute_mcp_result_links qualify path, edit_path and preview_url with PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL or the forwarded host. Gotcha The MCP server is disabled entirely when PRESENTON_ELECTRON is truthy (is_mcp_server_enabled, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:319). It also enforces a host allowlist (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) and origin protection. That is why nginx rewrites the Host header to

nginx.conf defines one server listening on port 80 with client_max_body_size 100M at the http level. The map blocks at nginx.conf:16 and nginx.conf:20 preserve an outer proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host, falling back to nginx's own scheme and Host. location Line Target Auth Notes / nginx.conf:29 http://localhost:3000 (Next.js) Next.js proxy.ts and layouts WebSocket upgrade headers, Host $http_host, 30 min read and connect timeouts. Also catches /api/* routes that are not v1 or v2, and /redoc. /api/v1/ nginx.conf:45 http://localhost:8000 FastAPI middleware client_max_body_size 110M; 413 handled by @request_entity_too_large; 30 min timeouts. /api/v2/ nginx.conf:59 http://localhost:8000 FastAPI middleware Inherits the 100M body limit; no custom 413 page. @request_entity_too_large nginx.conf:71 none none Returns 413 {"detail":"File size must be less than 100MB."} as JSON. /mcp/ nginx.conf:77 http://localhost:8001/mcp/ FastMCP bearer verifier client_max_body_size 145M; Host localhost:8001. /mcp nginx.conf:94 http://localhost:8001/mcp FastMCP bearer verifier Same settings for the path without a trailing slash. /docs nginx.conf:110 http://localhost:8000/docs FastAPI protected non-API path Swagger UI; needs a session because /docs is in _PROTECTED_NON_API_PATHS. /openapi.json nginx.conf:120 http://localhost:8000/openapi.json FastAPI protected non-API path The live schema (not the static openai_spec.json). = /_auth_check nginx.conf:133 http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/verify internal only Subrequest with X-Original-URI, Cookie and Authorization passed through; body dropped. /static/ nginx.conf:153 alias /app/servers/fastapi/static/ public expires 1y, Cache-Control: public, immutable. Reads: the whole repository at snapshot 571461f · Builds on: Repository tour · Time: reference, skim as needed This appendix is an annotated map of roughly 320 source and configuration files, grouped by directory, chosen because they carry behavior you will meet when reading or changing Presenton. Each row gives the file's line count at the snapshot, a one-line statement of its responsibility written after reading it, and the chapter that explains it in depth. Use it as a lookup table: find the file behind a stack trace, an endpoint, or a concept, then jump to the chapter.

docs.t: Step 1: How the core terms fit together
docs.x: Most of the vocabulary hangs off one chain: a request produces an outline, the outline is matched to layouts of a template to form a structure, each structure entry becomes a slide whose content is generated against a layout's JSON Schema, and the slide's ui is the template layout with that content applied. Smart mode skips the template chain and stores raw HTML in html_content. How to read an entry The bold-free first line is the term exactly as it appears in code or in this book. The definition gives the meaning, then the source location in inline code, then the chapter. Where two names exist for one thing (for example "block" in the UI and "merged component" in the code), both are listed and cross-referenced.

Admin A user whose is_superuser is true. Admin-only routes are decided in SessionAuthMiddleware (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:100 to servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:114): everything under /api/v1/admin/ and /api/v1/ppt/codex/auth/, POST and DELETE on /api/v1/ppt/fonts/, and five discovery or test paths. An admin must also be using a browser session (method == "jwt"); an admin's API key gets 403 Admin browser session required. See Auth and multi-user. admin_slot A unique, nullable String(32) column on user (servers/fastapi/models/sql/user.py:27). The bootstrap and first-run setup write the value "primary" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:116, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:132), so the unique constraint guarantees at most one primary admin. See Auth and multi-user. Alembic migration Schema change scripts in servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/, driven by servers/fastapi/migrations.py. They run at startup unless MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP is set to something other than true or True; the default is "true" (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:41, servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:454). Right after migrate_database_on_startup, create_db_and_tables always creates any missing tables (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:57, servers/fastapi/services/database.py:117). See Data model. API key A user-scoped bearer token of the form sk-presenton-<16 hex id>.<secret> (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:19, servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:35). The secret must be at least 32 characters (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:58). Default expiry is 90 days, maximum 365 (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:20, servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:21). Rows live in api_keys; the full token is stored Fernet-encrypted with a key derived (SHA-256) from the auth secret so an admin can reveal it (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:39). Next.js forwards Bearer sk-presenton-* requests only to FastAPI paths (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:147). See Auth and multi-user. app_data (APP_DATA_DIRECTORY) The writable data root. start.js refuses to start without APP_DATA_DIRECTORY (start.js:50); the Docker image sets it to /app_data (Dockerfile:82); Python falls back to /tmp/presenton (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:24). It holds fastapi.db (default SQLite database, servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:58), userConfig.json, mem0/, and the asset roots images,

Decompose Turning uploaded documents into plain text files before generation. POST /api/v1/ppt/files/decompose (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:133) runs DocumentsLoader (servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py:163) over the temp files and returns DecomposedFileInfo items (name, file_path). See Document ingestion. decorative A required boolean on the Template v2 element models that carry content (text, image, text-list, table, chart, infographic; for example servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:218). Only elements with decorative: false become fields in the layout's content schema (_is_editable_element, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:53); decorative elements are drawn as-is and never rewritten by the LLM. See From template to schema to slide. Default template (built-in template) One of the 16 folders under templates/ (civic to verdant) with a template.json. They are discovered at import time and ordered momentum, dynamic, executive, general, modern, standard, swift first (servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:25), then imported into template_v2 with is_default=True on every startup by import_default_templates_on_startup (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:22). Default rows have owner_id null and are visible to everyone (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:88). The REST default template name is general (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:30). See Template v2 format. Derive / Edit (presentation) Two one-shot API operations: POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/edit replaces slide content in an existing deck and re-exports it, and POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/derive copies a deck first and then applies the changes (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3301, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3352). Request models are in servers/fastapi/models/presentation_from_template.py. See REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP. Desktop guard The Electron-only transport check applied before any auth logic. When PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true, every request must arrive with a Host among PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS, a matching Origin if present, and the x-presenton-desktop-token header or presenton_desktop_session cookie equal to PRESENTON_DESKTOP_TOKEN (compared with hmac.compare_digest) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/desktop.py:25). A token shorter than 32 characters, or no

Layout (slide layout) One slide design inside a template. In the stored template it is a SlideLayout(id, description, components) (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py:98). For generation it is reduced to a SlideLayoutModel(id, name, description, json_schema) (servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:11) by _build_template_layout_model (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:410). On a slide row, slides.layout holds the layout id (servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:24). See From template to schema to slide. Layout (presentation layout column) presentations.layout (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:65) stores a copy of the template's layouts JSON with name, template_id, icon_type and icon_weight added (_copy_template_layout_payload, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:232). Copying it decouples a deck from later edits to its template. See Data model. Layout group (layout_group) Required string on slides (servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:23) naming the family a slide's layout belongs to. Values in this snapshot: the template id for template slides (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1815), "blank" for blank decks, and "smart-html" for Smart slides (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2062). See Data model. LiteParse @llamaindex/liteparse, the Node document parser used for PDFs and other documents. LiteParseService (servers/fastapi/services/liteparse_service.py:67) runs liteparse_runner.mjs with node as a subprocess, with a 600-second default timeout and LITEPARSE_DPI (clamped 72 to 600) and LITEPARSE_NUM_WORKERS settings (servers/fastapi/services/liteparse_service.py:68 to servers/fastapi/services/liteparse_service.py:78). See Document ingestion. llmai The provider-agnostic LLM client library Presenton depends on (llmai==0.3.15 in servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml). It supplies GenerationDefaults, GenerationProfile, prepare_generation and model capabilities (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/generation.py:2). Per-provider client configuration is built in servers/fastapi/utils/llm_config.py. The library source is not part of this repository; its internals are not covered here. See Configuration and LLM providers. LLM provider The selected text model backend, stored in config key LLM. The enum lists 16: ollama, deepseek, openai, google, vertex, azure, bedrock,

pdf-maker The Next.js page /pdf-maker?id=<presentation id> (servers/nextjs/app/(export)/pdf-maker/page.tsx) that the export runtime opens in a headless browser. It renders every slide at print size; the export runtime then produces the PDF or PPTX from it. The proxy treats /pdf-maker specially: an exportSession query parameter is turned into a presenton_session cookie and stripped by redirect (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:114). See PPTX and PDF export. Phosphor icons The icon set bundled with Presenton: servers/fastapi/assets/icons.json declares the set label "Phosphor Icons", and servers/fastapi/static/icons/<weight>/ holds the SVGs (1,512 files in bold/ alone, named like acorn-bold.svg). A missing icon path returns static/icons/placeholder.svg instead of 404 (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:107). See Images, icons, web search. Prepare (presentation) POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1840): the step after outline editing that resolves the chosen template layout, computes the structure (including TOC slides) and saves both on the presentation, returning only presentation_id. The UI then opens /presentation?id=...&stream=true. See Standard generation pipeline. Presentation version (v1-standard, v2-standard) PresentationVersion enum stored in presentations.version (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:16). v2-standard is every deck created by this snapshot, Standard and Smart alike (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1747). v1-standard is the value the migration back-fills for decks made before Template v2 (servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/6e4a1b2c3d5f_add_template_v2_and_presentation_version.py:22). The UI refuses to open v1 decks ("This deck was created in an older Presenton version", servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:33). See Data model. Presenton Cloud (presenton provider) Optional hosted service at https://api.presenton.ai (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:7). An admin links an account through an OAuth device flow under /api/v1/auth/presenton/*; the encrypted token sits in the presenton_cloud_provider singleton. When provider settings have LLM == "presenton", maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request forwards selected generation, edit, Smart and asset paths to the cloud and persists results locally

SessionAuthMiddleware The FastAPI middleware that owns authentication (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:29). Order of checks: desktop guard, DISABLE_AUTH short circuit, public paths (/api/v1/auth/status, verify, setup, login, logout, plus /app_data/fonts/ and /app_data/templates/), 428 Login setup is required when no user exists, principal resolution, admin-only rules, owner context, Presenton Cloud proxy, and /app_data ownership. See Auth and multi-user. Slide A row in slides (servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:9): presentation (FK, cascade), layout_group, layout, index, content, html_content, speaker_note, properties, ui, owner_id. See Data model. Slide content (content) The JSON object the LLM produces for one slide by filling the layout's JSON Schema (slides.content, servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:26). It may contain image prompts and icon queries for hydration and the reserved __speaker_note__ key, which is moved to speaker_note (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2388). For Smart slides it is just {"title": ...} (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2064). See Prompts and schemas. slides_markdown Optional list on GeneratePresentationRequest (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:10): one Markdown string per slide, used instead of LLM outline generation. When present it also fixes the slide count (_requested_slide_count, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:190). See REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP. Smart mode / Smart slide The template-free generation path. The LLM writes each slide directly as a 1280 by 720 HTML <section> that is sanitized (no scripts other than vetted Chart.js initializers, no event handlers or javascript: URLs) and stored in html_content with layout_group and layout both "smart-html". Defaults: 8 slides, maximum 50, up to 8 generation attempts (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py:45 to servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py:49). REST entry points are POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart and .../generate/smart/async. See Smart mode. speaker_note Optional text column on slides (servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:28), filled from the __speaker_note__ property that generate_slide_content adds to every slide schema (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py:217). See Prompts and

Table of contents (TOC) Optional generated slides listing the deck's sections, enabled by include_table_of_contents (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:70). The number of TOC slides depends on the total (get_no_of_toc_required_for_n_outlines, servers/fastapi/utils/outline_utils.py:52), and the layout is found by regex over layout names (select_toc_or_list_slide_layout_index, servers/fastapi/utils/ppt_utils.py:59). See Standard generation pipeline. Template v2 The current template format and its table template_v2 (servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16): string UUID id, name, description, raw_layouts, components, merged_components, layouts, theme, assets, is_default, owner_id. Built-in template.json files carry id, name, description, thumbnail, merged_components, layouts, fonts, theme. Custom templates are produced from a PPTX by the multi-pass generator in servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py and servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py. A template name of the form custom-<id> is accepted and stripped to <id> (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:200). See Template v2 format. Template schema (get_template_schema) The JSON Schema derived from a template layout that the LLM must fill, built by get_template_schema (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257) from the non-decorative elements of each component, with table text capacity and repeated-group arrays handled specially. See From template to schema to slide. Temp files Uploaded documents live in owner-scoped temporary directories managed by TEMP_FILE_SERVICE (servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py:191), rooted at TEMP_DIRECTORY or, when unset, /tmp/presenton (servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py:14); the Docker image sets TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton (Dockerfile:83). See Document ingestion. Theme Colors and fonts for a presentation: PresentationThemeData with colors (PresentationThemeColors: roles primary, background, card, stroke, background_text, primary_text, graph_0 to graph_9) and fonts.textFont (name, url) (servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py:4, servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py:31). Template themes are derived from layout colors by servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py (LLM or deterministic role selection with contrast repair). Stored in presentations.theme and template_v2.theme. See Themes and fonts. Tone and verbosity

Gotcha trigger_webhook exists on GeneratePresentationRequest (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:44) but nothing in the FastAPI code reads it. The success and failure webhooks are scheduled unconditionally in generate_presentation_handler (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3133, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3150); filtering happens only by subscription event. Gotcha "Layout" means three different things: a template SlideLayout (components), a generation SlideLayoutModel (id plus JSON Schema), and the presentations.layout column (a copied template payload). The slides.layout column is only the layout id string. Read the type, not the name. Gotcha presenton is a valid value of the LLM setting but not a member of LLMProvider (servers/fastapi/enums/llm_provider.py:4). get_llm_provider answers 500 Invalid LLM provider for it (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_provider.py:47), so any request that reaches local LLM code instead of being intercepted by the cloud proxy fails. When you add a route that calls the LLM, check whether it also needs a cloud proxy rule. Gotcha owner_id is null in two very different situations: built-in templates (shared with everyone because is_default is true) and every row created in auth-disabled mode, including Electron. If you turn auth on for a database created with DISABLE_AUTH, those rows are not visible to any user until ownership is backfilled (the bootstrap's legacy backfill in servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py exists for this reason). Gotcha All SSE messages share the event name response. A client that registers addEventListener("chunk", ...) receives nothing; it must listen for response and switch on data.type.

Reads: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts, servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py · Builds on: Part VIII landing, Part VII landing · Time: ~15 min Presenton turns a sentence into a slide deck. The goal of this part is bigger: the same "type what you want, get finished content" experience as one reusable component that any surface can host. Today that surface is Superset text; tomorrow a Superset dashboard; the day after, a page in a Tiptap editor. This part explains how to extract that capability from Presenton into a frontend-first kit, and how to plan the frontend work so each new host is an integration, not a rebuild.

The end objective is to create, the way Presenton creates a PPT slide from normal text, a common functionality that can be plugged into any host. Today it might be for Superset text, tomorrow for a Superset dashboard, the next day for pages with the Tiptap editor. We want to automatically create pages based on the user's natural language input. How can we extend Presenton into an AI component that is easy to integrate from a frontend perspective, and how should we plan it from a frontend perspective?

Presenton's value is not its slide screens. It is a pipeline: Natural language plus context becomes a plan (Presenton's outline). The plan becomes structured content that must fit a schema derived from what the output can hold (Presenton's Template v2 layouts). The content streams to the browser and is shown progressively (Presenton's SSE streams). A renderer turns structured content into the final format (Presenton's slide renderer and PPTX export). Generalize each step and the kit falls out: Presenton today Generative Content Kit Slide outline Target-neutral plan with sections Template v2 layout schema (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py) A target manifest that declares which blocks, layouts and limits an output supports; the engine builds the model's response schema from it Slide JSON One intermediate representation, the Artifact Spec, shared by every output Presenton-specific SSE frames, read with EventSource (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:107) A versioned run protocol: JSON Patch events over fetch-based streaming, resumable, with a human-review step Next.js pages wired to Redux A headless core plus a thin React kit and a web component One output: slides Pluggable targets: slides, Tiptap documents, Superset dashboards, text One app Pluggable hosts: Superset extension, Tiptap extension, Presenton, any page Chart values written by the model Data bindings to Superset charts, datasets and saved metrics, resolved as the viewing user and refreshed after generation The recommendation in one sentence: the language model never writes host-native formats; it writes the Artifact Spec, constrained by the target's manifest, and deterministic adapters convert it into slides, ProseMirror JSON, Superset position_json or Markdown. Numbers never come from the model either: every number is a binding to Superset data, and every target shows it live. The host stores the binding definition, and the value is fetched again as the person viewing it, on open, on "Refresh data", on an interval and when a dashboard filter or a parameter changes. Outputs that can only hold static text (an exported Markdown file, an email, a downloaded PPTX) carry a "Data as of" stamp and a link to the live version, and no target ever shows a screenshot of a chart.

docs.t: How this part relates to the others
docs.x: Part VII designed the data-bound document model for Superset. The Artifact Spec here is a smaller, frontend-friendly version of it, with the same rule: numbers come only from data bindings. Part VIII builds AI Slides by embedding Presenton in an iframe. That is the right first step for slides. Part IX does not change it. It defines what to extract once AI Slides works, so the next surfaces do not each need their own Presenton fork. AI Slides moves onto the kit last (phase P4 in the Roadmap and tracker), once the kit is proven on the text, Tiptap and dashboard targets. GCK decks keep Part VIII's behavior for data: the slides target writes real slide_data_bindings rows, so a generated deck refreshes on open and refreshes before export exactly like a Part VIII deck.

Architecture: layers, packages, the three main flows, and the key decisions. Artifact Spec and targets: the intermediate representation and the four target adapters. Live Superset data: binding sources, scope and parameters, refresh policies, the resolve APIs and how every target stays live as the viewer. Run protocol and client: how the frontend talks to the engine. React SDK and UI kit: hooks, state machine and components. Host integrations: Superset dashboard, Superset text, Tiptap, Presenton, and the web component. Extracting the engine from Presenton: what to reuse, generalize or drop. Frontend engineering and quality: packaging, theming, accessibility, security, testing. Roadmap and tracker: phases, work packages, effort and exit criteria.

Reads: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts, servers/nextjs/package.json · Builds on: Part IX landing · Time: ~30 min This chapter lays out the Generative Content Kit (GCK) end to end: the layers, the packages and their dependency rules, the three interactions every host needs (generate, transform, edit), how a run flows through the system, and the decisions that shape everything else. Later chapters zoom into each layer.

Every "type a sentence, get content" feature mixes four concerns. Presenton mixes them inside one Next.js app and one FastAPI service. The kit separates them so each can change independently. Concern Question it answers GCK layer Presenton today Host Where is the user, and how is the result inserted? Host adapters: context providers plus a HostApi (@gck/host-superset, the Tiptap extension GckGenerate shipped in @gck/target-tiptap, @gck/element) The Presenton web app itself Target What kind of content is produced, and what can it hold? Target adapters with manifests (@gck/target-*) Slides only, shaped by Template v2 layouts Run How does a request become streamed, structured content? @gck/protocol, @gck/client, @gck/core, GCK Engine Outline, structure and content steps (for example generate_ppt_outline, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:252) streamed with Presenton-specific SSE Data Where do numbers come from, and how are they kept current after generation? Data providers (@gck/data-superset) for the catalog and live refresh, a binding store and refresh controller in @gck/core; the engine resolves bindings during a run and on demand (/v1/data/resolve), always as the viewing user The LLM invents chart values; Part VIII adds bindings that refresh on open and before export The rule that makes this work: hosts and targets are plugins, the run layer is shared, and the only thing the model produces is the Artifact Spec (Artifact Spec and targets). The data concern has one more rule: an applied artifact stores binding definitions, never frozen numbers presented as current. Every target fetches live Superset data as the person viewing it, on open, on demand, on an interval or when a filter or parameter changes, and a host that can only store static text (an exported Markdown file, an email, a downloaded PPTX) gets a stamped snapshot ("Data as of ...") plus a link to the live version. Live Superset data is the full contract. Data sources covered A binding's source is a discriminated union on type. Protocol 1.0 has superset_chart (a saved chart, through its stored query context). Protocol 1.1 adds superset_dataset (metrics and dimensions of a dataset the user can read, no saved chart needed) and superset_metric (one saved metric, with an optional period comparison). Protocol 1.2 adds superset_sql (a saved SQL Lab query, off by default

Dependency rules, enforced in CI: @gck/protocol has no runtime dependencies. The engine shares its JSON Schemas, so the frontend and backend cannot drift apart. @gck/core has no DOM and no React, not even as a type (its runtime dependencies are @gck/protocol, @gck/client, jsonrepair and d3-format). It runs in a browser, a web worker, Node, or a test. A target's main entry (manifest, toNative, apply) depends only on @gck/core and @gck/protocol, plus its host library as a peer dependency, for example @tiptap/core. A Tiptap host must never get a second copy of Tiptap. React node views and previews live in the target's /react subpath. Host packages may depend on React and targets, never the other way round. Renderers that are heavy (the slides renderer and its Chart.js runtime) are lazy-loaded through the target's loadPreview, so a Tiptap-only host never downloads them.

Every host needs the same three interactions. The protocol carries them as an intent (Run protocol and client). Intent User story Context sent Apply mode generate "Create a QBR page for EMEA from the Sales dashboard." context.surface, host ids (for example dashboardId), locale, theme; chart ids in data.allowedChartIds, dataset ids in data.allowedDatasetIds and the dashboard's current filter state in data.scope (protocol 1.1) replace, append or insert_at_cursor transform Select three paragraphs, "turn this into a chart and a summary." context.selection, converted to Artifact blocks by the target's fromHost replace the selection edit "Make section 2 shorter and add a revenue KPI." context.document: the artifact applied earlier, read back with fromHost patch All three intents run end to end through one call. The run controller in React SDK and UI kit takes them in submit({ prompt, intent, selection, baseArtifact, apply }): transform requires a selection and defaults to replace, edit requires a baseArtifact and defaults to patch. For an edit the engine streams artifact.patch ops against the base (the stream starts from the base as version 0), and the controller hands the target a block diff (added, removed and changed block ids) that it also exposes as run.diff for review UI. The Tiptap and text targets implement the patch apply mode (Artifact Spec and targets); the slides and dashboard targets do not list it in v1 and apply "patch" as replace with a patch_unsupported warning. Gotcha: patch needs ids that survive in the host A patch finds content in the host by block id. The Tiptap target stores every top-level node's block id in a gckBlockId global attribute, so an edit can replace, delete and insert single blocks in one undo step. Content the user pasted from another generated page carries that page's ids, and content typed by hand has none; both are handled by fromHost, which stamps fresh ids before it reads the document back, so always build baseArtifact with fromHost, never from a cached copy of the last run. A fourth, non-AI interaction is refresh: re-resolve data bindings as the viewing user without calling a model, on open, on demand ("Refresh data"), on an interval of at least 60 seconds, when the tab becomes visible again, or when a host filter or an artifact parameter changes. The browser calls the engine's POST {engine}/v1/data/resolve with binding

docs.t: Step 4: Follow one run end to end
docs.x: The run ends with the content in the host, but the data is not finished: from then on the host owns refresh. This is the same for every target that a browser renders (Tiptap pages, kit-rendered text, and later slides through the Presenton transport). It is target-neutral and mirrors Part VIII's "open a deck" flow (Architecture and contracts): Two targets do not use this path. The superset-dashboard target writes native Superset charts, and Superset's own frontend queries them as the viewer on open, on native filter change, on dashboard refresh and on the dashboard's json_metadata.refresh_frequency (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/schemas.py:215, read by the frontend at apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/dashboard/actions/hydrate.ts:411). The slides target in Presenton keeps Part VIII's deck routes (slide_data_bindings rows, refresh on open and before export) until phase P4 moves it onto the kit with a Presenton transport. What runs where: Step Runs in Why Context capture Host adapter (ContextProviders collected by @gck/core), browser Only the host knows the selection, cursor and current page Data catalog (allowedChartIds, allowedDatasetIds) Browser asks (DataProvider.catalog in @gck/data-superset); the engine answers from Story 8's catalog and dataset metadata as the user (GET {engine}/v1/data/catalog) Only charts and datasets the user can see are offered to the model; charts that cannot be snapshotted stay listed as embed entries with a reason Schema assembly from the manifest and data catalog Engine (build_response_schema) The engine must enforce it on the model response Planning and content generation Engine Secrets, provider keys and model choice stay server-side Validation of the Artifact Engine first (validate_artifact), then the browser again (validateArtifact, same issue codes) The browser treats model output as untrusted Binding resolution during the run Engine (resolving_data, sent as binding.resolved) Goes through Story 8's refresh endpoint with the user's identity; snapshots live in an overlay beside the artifact, so a later refresh never forks the engine's version line Refresh after the run (on open, Refresh data, interval, tab return, filter or parameter change) Browser: the host's RefreshController (@gck/core) calls POST {engine}/v1/data/resolve through @gck/data-superset; the engine calls Story 8. Dashboard target: Superset's

Decision Choice Alternatives considered Reason Integration style Headless SDK plus thin UI kit, with a web component and an iframe fallback Embed Presenton everywhere as an iframe An iframe cannot insert into a host editor's undo history, read its selection, or match its theme What the model produces The Artifact Spec, constrained by a schema built from the target manifest Host-native formats directly (HTML, ProseMirror JSON, position_json) One validation path, one safety model, many outputs; adapters are deterministic and testable Schema source Target manifest per run Fixed global schema Matches how Presenton builds a schema from each Template v2 layout (get_template_schema, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257), and lets each host restrict blocks and limits Streaming Own versioned run protocol (GCK-Protocol: 1), JSON Patch over fetch-based SSE, with an optional AG-UI adapter (toAgUi) EventSource, as Presenton uses now (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:107); What the kit does not do: It does not own the host's document. It proposes content and applies it through the host's own API. It does not store artifacts long-term by default. Hosts persist what they apply, and for data that means binding definitions, not values; the engine keeps the run event log for resume and audit, and never persists refresh results. It does not bypass host permissions. Data comes through the user's identity (Story 8), and dashboard creation uses the user's own Superset rights. It does not replace Presenton's PPTX export. The slides target hands its output to Presenton's existing export path (PPTX and PDF export). Gotcha: Tiptap is already inside Presenton Presenton depends on @tiptap/* 3.30.5 (servers/nextjs/package.json:40-44) for inline slide text editing (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx). The Tiptap target must declare Tiptap as a peer dependency and support the host's major version. Otherwise Presenton, or any other Tiptap host, ends up with two copies of ProseMirror, and nodes created by one copy fail schema checks in the other.

Reads: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/utils/schema_utils.py, apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/dashboard/util/constants.ts, apache/superset: superset/dashboards/schemas.py, apache/superset: superset/daos/dashboard.py, apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py, apache/superset: superset-frontend/plugins/plugin-chart-handlebars/src/, apache/superset: superset/dashboards/filter_scope.py · Builds on: Architecture · Time: ~90 min This chapter defines the one data structure every part of the Generative Content Kit agrees on, the Artifact (Artifact Spec v1), and the four adapters that turn it into host-native content: Presenton Template v2 slides, Tiptap (ProseMirror) documents, Apache Superset dashboards, and plain text, Markdown or HTML. You will see the full TypeScript types, the JSON Schema and Pydantic equivalents, the invariants the engine and the client both enforce, how a target manifest becomes the LLM response schema for a run, and complete adapter code for each target. Every target shows live Superset data: a DataBinding is a refreshable definition (a saved chart, a dataset query or a saved metric), resolved as the viewing user on open, on demand, on an interval and on filter change, and each adapter documents what stays live in its host and what becomes a stamped snapshot. A worked example takes one prompt through one refreshable Artifact into all four outputs, and the chapter closes with the test strategy that keeps adapters deterministic. All new code in this chapter (the gck/ packages, the gck_engine/ modules, and one proposed Presenton endpoint) is marked "(new)" in its block title; everything else is quoted from source. Types marked "protocol 1.1" are additive to gck.artifact/1 and ship as a minor bump of @gck/protocol. Presenton code is quoted from the source snapshot used throughout this site (commit 571461f); Superset paths, prefixed apache/superset:, refer to a clone of apache/superset master at cabd8d4 (2 November 2026), so line numbers can differ on the 6.1 release. The resolution side of live data (the refresh endpoint, the binding store, the refresh controller, identity and caching) is the subject of Live Superset data; this chapter covers the data model and what

There are two ways to make a model produce "a page" for a host. Direct emission. Ask the LLM for the host's own format: ProseMirror JSON for Tiptap, a position_json tree for a Superset dashboard, Template v2 layout JSON for a slide. IR plus adapters. Ask the LLM for a small, target-neutral document (the Artifact), constrained by a JSON Schema derived from the target's capabilities, and convert it to the native format with a deterministic adapter. GCK uses the second design everywhere. The table records why. Concern Direct emission IR + deterministic adapters Validation Every host format needs its own schema for the LLM; most are not designed for it (position_json is an id-keyed graph with parents back-references; ProseMirror needs a live schema to validate) One schema family, assembled per run from a manifest; validated with the same JSON Schema in the browser and in the engine Safety The model can emit any node, mark, URL, chartId or HTML the format allows The model can only choose block types the manifest lists and bindingIds from an enum; URLs and numbers pass validators before an adapter sees them Numbers The model writes chart values and KPI figures, frozen at generation time Numbers come only from DataBinding snapshots through tokens (Part VII number discipline, Data-bound slide model), and a binding is a query definition, so every number can be re-resolved after generation Multi-target One prompt engineering effort per host format One generation pipeline; a new host is a new adapter, not a new prompt Editing "Change the second chart" requires the model to understand the host format fromHost imports existing content into an Artifact; the model edits the IR; the adapter re-serializes Streaming Partial native JSON is often invalid for the host (a ProseMirror node without its children) artifact.patch events add whole blocks; each patch is renderable (Run protocol and client) Testability Model output must be checked against a running host Adapters are pure functions: golden files and round-trip tests without an LLM Token cost Host formats are verbose (styling, geometry, ids) The IR carries content only; styling and geometry are added by the adapter

docs.t: Step 2: The Artifact Spec v1 in TypeScript
docs.x: The types live in @gck/protocol, which has no runtime dependencies. They are the blueprint's types, with the supporting aliases spelled out, plus the protocol 1.1 data additions (parameters, refresh, dataContext, the embed block, and the data types of 2.3, which live in src/data.ts and are re-exported here). gck/packages/protocol/src/artifact.ts (new)

Id Pattern Assigned by Stable across Artifact.id ^art_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$ (ULID) engine, at run.started every later edit of the same artifact Section.id ^sec_[a-z0-9]{4,24}$ engine, after validating LLM output patches, edits, host round-trips Block.id ^blk_[a-z0-9]{4,24}$ engine, same patches, edits, host round-trips binding key ^b_[a-z0-9_]{1,48}$ (same as Part VII) engine, from the data catalog before the LLM call the artifact's life The LLM never writes id fields. Ids are stamped after validation (Step 6.3), so the model cannot collide them, and an edit run receives existing ids in its input and must return them unchanged. Ids are the anchor for three things: RFC 6902 patches address blocks by array index, but the client resolves index paths to block ids after each patch (Run protocol and client); every top-level Tiptap node the target creates carries a gckBlockId attribute (data nodes also keep gckId) and Superset components get ids derived from block ids, so fromHost can map content back and a patch apply can find the node to change (Step 8.6); and golden-file tests diff by id.

RichText is a flat list of segments. A segment is plain text with optional marks, or a token: a reference to one value of one binding. Tokens are the only way a number enters prose. Binding kind Token field Value metric value, previous, delta, delta_pct numbers from MetricSnapshot; delta_pct is (value - previous) / abs(previous) chart total:<series>, last:<series>, max:<series> numbers over one series (first series only when the name is empty, as in total:) chart argmax:<series>, last_category category labels (strings) table cell:<row>:<column>, row_count one cell by row index and column (raw result name first, then display label); the row count any (protocol 1.1) period the effective time range of the last resolve, from snapshot.meta.time_range (label, else from to to formatted with format.date) period exists so that a sentence about live data does not carry a frozen calendar label. "Revenue in Q3 2026 was ..." is wrong one quarter later even though the number refreshed; "Revenue for {period} was ..." stays true. Plain calendar labels next to data tokens raise the I16_PERIOD_LABELS warning (Step 4). format is a d3-format specifier such as ,.3s or .0%, or one of Superset's SMART_NUMBER and SMART_NUMBER_SIGNED formatter ids, the same notation Superset uses for number formats and that Part VIII's format.number holds. @gck/core ports SMART_NUMBER from createSmartNumberFormatter (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/number-format/factories/createSmartNumberFormatter.ts:54), so a binding that has no explicit format renders the way the same metric renders in Superset. Resolution order is token.format, then the column's spec in binding.format.columns (a plain string, the Part VIII shape, for cell: fields), then binding.format.number, then SMART_NUMBER; the effective prefix and suffix (or currency.symbol at currency.symbolPosition) wrap the result. delta_pct uses binding.format.delta (default +.1%) unless the token overrides it, and never takes the binding's currency prefix. Because the prefix is added outside d3, a token spec must not repeat it ($,.3s on a binding with prefix: "$" would print $$591k). An invalid spec never throws: it falls back to "," and the validator rejects it in authored tokens (I14_FORMAT). A token segment's text is not a value store. The engine blanks it in every artifact it sends to a host, hosts persist it as ""

docs.t: 2.3 DataBinding: a live definition plus runtime state
docs.x: A DataBinding is two things, and the split is what keeps every target live: A definition: kind, source, mapping, format, params and refresh. It says which Superset data to fetch and how to turn the result rows into a chart, a metric or a table. Hosts persist definitions only. Runtime state: snapshot, snapshotAt, status and error. It is the result of the last resolve as the current viewer. It lives in a binding store in the browser (or in the engine during a run), is refreshed after generation, and is persisted only as an offline fallback (redacted for other viewers, 2.2). The definition keeps the field names of Part VIII's slide_data_bindings row (Architecture and contracts), minus the slide coordinates, so one snapshot JSON serves both stores. Protocol 1.1 widens it in four ways: source becomes a discriminated union over Superset's data sources, mapping and format get real types, and params and refresh say how the binding reacts to viewer inputs and when it re-resolves. gck/packages/protocol/src/data.ts (new, protocol 1.1) The snapshot shapes are normative per kind, so adapters can read them without knowing where they came from: a chart snapshot's {categories, series} is exactly what Presenton's Chart element stores (categories: Optional[list[str]], series: Optional[list[ChartSeries]], servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:361), and Part VIII's slide_data_bindings.snapshot stores the same JSON. Tables keep raw values plus labels, and every adapter formats at render time through resolveToken, so a refreshed table never carries strings formatted for someone else's locale or currency. Data sources covered source.type What it reads How it resolves (inside Superset, as the viewer) Version superset_chart a saved chart: its query, viz type and saved filters the chart's saved query context, with dashboard filters, parameters and pinned overrides merged into extra_form_data (the keys Superset accepts there are listed in apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-234) v1 superset_dataset any physical or virtual dataset the user can read; saved metrics or SIMPLE aggregates, up to 3 groupby columns, a temporal x axis a query context built from the source and loaded through ChartDataQueryContextSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1677); pivot adds Superset's pivot post-processing (ChartDataPivotOptionsSchema, schemas.py:972) 1.1

Change Allowed in gck.artifact/1? How New optional field on an existing type yes minor bump of @gck/protocol; readers ignore unknown fields only when the reader's protocol minor is older New token field grammar yes minor bump; resolveToken returns n/a for unknown fields New block type or mark yes, as a minor bump adapters must apply the unknown-block rule below New source.type (1.1: superset_dataset, superset_metric; 1.2: superset_sql) yes minor bump, engine first; a reader that does not know the type marks the binding error with code source_unsupported and renders its fallback, never a guess Renaming or removing a field, changing a meaning no gck.artifact/2 plus an upgrade_1_to_2 function shipped in @gck/protocol and the engine Protocol 1.1 is entirely additive: Artifact.parameters, refresh and dataContext, the embed block, the source union, typed mapping and format, params, refresh, generatedAgainst and error on bindings, and meta on snapshots. A 1.0 artifact is a valid 1.1 artifact. The engine ships first, so a 1.0 client never receives a field it cannot ignore. The unknown-block rule: an adapter that meets a block type it does not support renders it through @gck/target-text as a paragraph if the block has text or items, otherwise drops it and records a warning in its result. Validation is strict on write (the engine rejects unknown fields with extra="forbid") and tolerant on read (adapters accept newer minors). This asymmetry keeps old hosts working while preventing the model from inventing structure.

docs.t: Step 3: The JSON Schema and the Pydantic models
docs.x: @gck/protocol publishes schemas/artifact-1.schema.json (draft 2020-12). It is the contract artifact both codebases test against (Step 12). An excerpt: gck/packages/protocol/schemas/artifact-1.schema.json (new, excerpt) The other block variants and the remaining $defs (datasetSource, sqlSource, filterContext, overrides, filterClause, bindingFormat, paramBinding, artifactParameter, hostDataScope) follow the same pattern and mirror the TypeScript types of 2.3 field for field. oneOf is safe here because every block variant and every source variant pins type with const, so at most one can match. (The per-run LLM schema in Step 6 uses anyOf instead, for a different reason.) The binding's snapshot stays an open object in the artifact schema: snapshots are runtime state written by the resolver, validated by gck_data's own models, and never authored. The engine's models mirror the schema. Field names match the JSON exactly, camelCase included, so there is no alias layer to drift: gck_engine/spec/artifact.py (new) The data models live in their own module so that Presenton's backend can import the same source and snapshot models through the shared gck_data package (Part VIII's mappers, moved and extended) without importing the whole Artifact: gck_engine/spec/data.py (new, protocol 1.1, excerpt) The engine's old Source model had a single superset_chart variant, mapping: dict = {} and an untyped overrides: dict. All three were the frozen-data gaps of v1: an empty mapping cannot be resolved by Part VIII's mappers, and an untyped override is a SQL surface. Protocol 1.1 types the overrides, requires a mapping (Step 6.3 derives it), and caps every list the resolver will turn into a query. Field(discriminator="type") is the same construction Presenton uses for its element union (SlideElement, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, chapter 16), with one deliberate difference: GCK sets extra="forbid" on every model. Presenton's element models do not (only a few infographic data sub-models set extra, elements.py:458), which is why unknown keys in template bundles are silently dropped (Template v2 format).

Schema validation catches shape errors. The invariants below need cross-references or rendering, so they live in a validator that runs in the engine after every LLM response (feeding a repair retry) and in @gck/core before toNative (validateArtifact(artifact, manifest, { allowedChartIds, allowedDatasetIds }), feeding a warning UI). Both implementations share issue codes. Code Invariant Severity I1_VERSION version == "gck.artifact/1" error I2_IDS Section and block ids are unique within the artifact and match their patterns error I3_BINDING_REF Every block bindingId and every token.bindingId is a key of bindings error I4_BINDING_KIND chart blocks reference chart bindings, metric to metric, table to table, embed to embed; token fields are valid for the binding's kind (period for any kind, no tokens on embed); mapping is non-empty except for embed error I5_NUMBERS_IN_TOKENS Plain segments contain no digits, except allowlisted calendar labels (years 19xx/20xx, Q1 to Q4, H1/H2, FY plus two or four digits) error I6_MANIFEST_BLOCKS Block types and section kinds are in the target manifest error I7_LIMITS Section count, blocks per section, and rendered characters per block (tokens counted by their display) are within manifest limits error I8_LAYOUT_HINT layoutHint, when set, is an id in the manifest's layoutCatalog error I9_LINKS href is present if and only if the segment has the link mark; scheme is https, http or mailto error I10_ALLOWED_SOURCES Every binding's source is allowed for the run: superset_chart.chart_id in data.allowedChartIds; superset_dataset and superset_metric dataset_id in data.allowedDatasetIds; superset_sql only when the run's data scope grants SQL sources error I11_IMAGES An image block has prompt or url; url is https error I12_PARAMS (1.1) Every binding.params[].param exists in artifact.parameters; as and column fit the parameter type and the source dataset; no column is both pinned in overrides and parameterized error I13_REFRESH_POLICY (1.1) intervalSec >= 60 whenever interval is a mode; on_schedule only with a schedule and only for headless surfaces error I14_FORMAT (1.1) token.format, format.number, format.delta and every format.columns value parse as d3 specs or SMART_NUMBER[_SIGNED] error I15_OVERRIDES (1.1) Filter columns are filterable columns of the source dataset, operators are in the allowlist, time_range is at most 100 characters,

docs.t: Step 5: Target manifests and the adapter interface
docs.x: A target describes what it can render (the manifest) and implements a deterministic serializer (the adapter). These types refine the blueprint's: the manifest is unchanged, the host context and patch types reuse the run protocol's (RunContext and JsonPatchOp from run.ts, Run protocol and client), and the adapter's preview is lazy and React-free (below). gck/packages/protocol/src/target.ts (new) gck/packages/core/src/adapter.ts (new) @gck/core never imports React, not even as a type, so the core bundle stays React-free and DOM-free. Preview is a type parameter that @gck/react narrows to ComponentType<PreviewProps> (PreviewProps = { artifact: Artifact; streaming: boolean }), and each target supplies its preview through loadPreview from its /react subpath, never as an eager import in the target's main entry (React SDK and UI kit). ApplyResult and ApplyMode live in @gck/protocol and are re-exported by @gck/core. After every apply the run controller calls host.emit?.("gck.applied", { result, artifact }), so a host can react without wrapping the adapter.

docs.t: 5.1 Intents, diffs and the patch apply mode
docs.x: The run controller's submit takes the run's intent (React SDK and UI kit): submit({ prompt, intent?, selection?, baseArtifact?, apply? }), with RunIntent = "generate" | "transform" | "edit" from @gck/protocol. The adapter supplies the inputs for the two non-generate intents through fromHost: Intent Input from the target Sent as Default apply mode generate none (context only) RunRequest.context none: the mode chosen in the apply bar transform selection: the target's fromHost output for the user's selection RunRequest.context.selection (as Artifact blocks) replace edit baseArtifact: the artifact previously applied, re-read with fromHost RunRequest.context.document patch For edit, the engine streams artifact.patch ops against the base artifact (the stream starts from baseArtifact as version 0), and run.completed carries the final version. The controller keeps the base and computes an ArtifactDiff (the ids of added, removed and changed blocks), which it exposes as run.diff for review UI and passes to the adapter. The adapter interface has two apply entry points, and the controller picks one. When the mode is "patch" and the adapter has applyPatch, it calls adapter.applyPatch(native, diff, artifact, host) as a method, where native is toNative of the final artifact. Every other case goes through apply(native, host, mode). A target that does not list "patch" in manifest.applyModes never gets applyPatch called; if it still receives "patch" through apply (a host that passes a mode through without checking the manifest), it applies as replace and adds a patch_unsupported warning. The streaming patches themselves never reach an adapter: the run store applies them to the Artifact, and the preview re-runs toNative. Target applyModes applyPatch slides append, replace none; "patch" falls back to replace with a warning (Step 7.3) tiptap-doc replace, insert_at_cursor, append, plus patch when GckBlockIds is registered one ProseMirror transaction over the changed blocks (Step 8.6) superset-dashboard append, replace none; "patch" falls back to replace with a warning (Step 9.4) text replace, append, insert_at_cursor, patch re-renders the whole text: patch equals replace (Step 10) The well-known capability names the adapters in this chapter read are presenton.api (Step 7), tiptap.editor (Step 8), and superset.http and superset.positionLimit (Step 9). docs.t: Step 6: From manifest to the per-run response schema
docs.x: The engine turns (manifest, data catalog) into the JSON Schema it hands the LLM. This is the general form of _template_layout_schema: Presenton derives fields from a layout's editable elements; GCK derives them from the manifest's block list and the catalog of bindings the user may use.

Before the LLM call, the engine turns the run's data scope (data.allowedChartIds, data.allowedDatasetIds and the host's filter state, Run protocol and client) into candidate bindings. A candidate is a complete binding definition, so whatever the model picks is refreshable the moment it is stamped. Candidates come from three places, all read as the user who submitted the run: Candidate Read from Key Kind a saved chart Part VIII Story 8's catalog (GET /api/v1/ai_slides/catalog, Story 8): the charts the user can see, each with Story 8's refreshable flag, reason and Presenton chart type b_c<chart_id> from the viz type: chart, metric (big_number_total, big_number, pop_kpi), table (table, ag-grid-table, pivot_table_v2); a non-refreshable chart becomes embed a saved metric of an allowed dataset (protocol 1.1) GET /api/v1/dataset/<pk>, whose show columns include metrics.metric_name, metrics.verbose_name, metrics.d3format and metrics.currency (apache/superset: superset/datasets/api.py:380-389) b_m<dataset_id>_<metric> metric with a superset_metric source; compare: {time_offset: "1 year ago"} when the dataset has a temporal column a metric over time (protocol 1.1) the same dataset response: columns.column_name, columns.filterable, columns.groupby, columns.is_dttm (api.py:360-369) and main_dttm_col b_d<dataset_id>_<metric> chart with a superset_dataset source: the metric by month over main_dttm_col Non-refreshable charts (maps, deck.gl, Sankey and the other viz types Story 8 cannot map to rows) are kept as embed entries rather than dropped: the model may place them as live Superset charts, but it cannot read numbers from them, and the engine sends one run.warning with code data_source_unsupported naming each such chart and Story 8's reason. How each target renders an embed is in Steps 7.5, 8.7, 9.5 and 10. Each candidate is then resolved once, through the same Story 8 call a refresh uses (row_limit 25, force: false), and its mapping and format are derived from the actual result columns, using the chart's form data only to decide roles. The model never writes a mapping: Source (Story 8 kind) mapping format time series bar, line, area, scatter, step, smooth x = form data x_axis (or granularity_sqla); series = numeric result columns minus x, or ["*"] when the chart has a groupby (the series set changes with the data); series_labels from the dataset's verbose names; sort:

gck_engine/schema/response_schema.py (new) What each manifest field and catalog fact becomes: Input Schema output blocks the anyOf list of block variants; data block types without a candidate are dropped sectionKinds kind enum limits.maxSections sections.maxItems limits.maxBlocksPerSection blocks.maxItems limits.maxCharsPerBlock maxLength on every segment's text (the validator checks the sum, I7) layoutCatalog[].id layoutHint enum, nullable catalog keys one data-block variant per candidate (bindingId as a const); token.bindingId enum over every key except embeds compatible_kinds chartType enum for that candidate: bar, horizontal bar and the stacked bars are mutually compatible (stacked kinds only with two or more series), line with area, pie with donut and polar area (one series), scatter and radar alone. The default is the candidate's own chart type. The dashboard target ignores chartType (it renders the saved chart) supports_compare compare exists only for candidates that can produce a previous value (big_number, pop_kpi, a superset_metric with compare); for the others it is null filterable columns and sample values the optional per-block scope (time range preset, up to 3 IN filters over enum columns and values) and the top-level parameters (at most 3) promptHints not schema: appended to the system prompt Three choices make the schema acceptable to strict structured-output modes. Every object lists all of its properties as required and sets additionalProperties: false, with optional fields expressed as nullable unions; that is the same normalization Presenton applies in ensure_strict_json_schema (servers/fastapi/utils/schema_utils.py:92), which forces required to every property key. Unions use anyOf, because that normalizer walks anyOf (schema_utils.py:159) and has no oneOf branch. And ids, binding definitions, snapshots and provenance are absent: the model chooses content, a candidate key, a chart kind from that candidate's list and, at most, a scope from enums; the engine writes everything else. Gotcha: the model's scope is never prose "Revenue for EMEA last quarter" must not be a sentence over an unfiltered binding: on refresh it would show the global number under an EMEA label. The only way the model can narrow data is the scope field, whose columns and values are enums from the sample resolve, and the engine also checks the reverse: when prose names

stamp copies each used candidate's complete definition into the Artifact. The old version wrote {"type": "superset_chart", "chart_id": ...} with mapping: {}, which Part VIII's mappers cannot resolve, so every binding it produced was frozen at whatever the run resolved. The new one copies source, mapping and format, adds the host's captured filter context, turns a block's scope into pinned source.overrides on a scoped copy of the binding, attaches the model's parameters, and sets the target's default refresh policy: gck_engine/schema/stamp.py (new) catalog_columns (omitted) returns the filterable columns of the source's dataset from the catalog. Every binding leaves stamp with status: "pending" and a non-empty mapping (except embeds), so I4 and I10 to I15 run on the stamped artifact before the first patch is streamed. When the engine then resolves the bindings, it records generatedAgainst: {snapshot_hash, snapshotAt} on each, which is what lets a view say later that the prose was written against older data (Live Superset data). Null optionals are then dropped (exclude_none when dumping the Pydantic model), so the stored Artifact matches the TypeScript types, where optional means absent. The Tiptap target converts between Artifacts and ProseMirror JSON, both ways. Built-in content uses StarterKit's node and mark names; data blocks use four custom nodes. In Tiptap 3, StarterKit includes the doc, paragraph, text, heading, bulletList, orderedList, listItem, blockquote, horizontalRule, codeBlock and hardBreak nodes and the bold, italic, code, strike, underline and link marks (StarterKit docs). Presenton itself pins @tiptap/core, @tiptap/react and @tiptap/starter-kit at 3.30.5 (servers/nextjs/package.json:40-44).

Artifact ProseMirror JSON Reverse (fromHost) title (only with includeTitle; the adapter leaves it off) heading {level: 1} first in the doc first H1 becomes title section.title heading {level: 2} each H2 starts a new section heading level 1, 2, 3 heading level 3, 4, 5 H3 to H5 back to 1 to 3; H6 to 3 paragraph paragraph same list bulletList or orderedList with listItem > paragraph same; nested lists are flattened into the parent item quote blockquote > paragraph same callout blockquote whose first text is a bold Note:, Warning: or Success: label pattern restores the tone divider horizontalRule same chart, metric, table gckChart, gckMetric, gckDataTable atoms, each with a binding attribute holding the binding definition (no snapshot) same; binding attributes rebuild Artifact.bindings embed (protocol 1.1) gckEmbed atom: a live Superset chart (8.7) same token segment inline atom gckToken with text: "" and the binding definition same marks bold, italic, code, link with attrs.href same; other marks (strike, underline) are dropped image image node if the host schema has one, else a paragraph with a link same Block.id, Section.id, Artifact.id attrs.gckBlockId on every top-level node the target creates (block node, section H2, title H1) gckBlockId restores the id; H2 ids starting with sec_ restore the section id Every top-level node the target creates carries the block id in a gckBlockId attribute. StarterKit nodes do not declare such an attribute, so the target ships a small extension, GckBlockIds, that adds it with Tiptap's addGlobalAttributes to exactly the node types the target emits (8.2). The cost is a schema change in the host: one optional attribute with a null default, so existing documents still load unchanged. The gain is that ids survive the round trip through the host document: fromHost returns the same block ids the engine stamped, an edit run's patches refer to blocks the user can still see, and applyPatch (8.6) finds the node for each changed block by id instead of by position. The data nodes keep their own gckId attribute as well, for documents written before GckBlockIds existed. Without the extension, applyPatch is not offered (the manifest omits "patch") and fromHost assigns fresh blk_h ids, as before.
