docs.t: 3.5 A semantic view metric (protocol 1.2, master only)
docs.x: datasource_type: "semantic_view" targets Superset's semantic layer. It needs SEMANTIC_LAYERS (default False, apache/superset: superset/config.py:776) and the headless POST /api/v1/datasource/<type>/<id>/query route (apache/superset: superset/datasource/api.py:790), which is not in 6.1.0. A 1.1 reader that meets it reports source_unsupported.

superset_sql The model never writes sql. A superset_sql source comes only from a saved query the user selected or the text of their current SQL Lab tab. It accepts no parameters or overrides (validator I15_OVERRIDES): the only injection point would be Jinja, and ENABLE_TEMPLATE_PROCESSING defaults to False (apache/superset: superset/config.py:995).

docs.t: 3.7 An embed (live, but not redrawn by the kit)
docs.x: embed for a chart the kit cannot redraw Step 13 explains what each target does with it.

For each binding the resolver computes one effective scope, lowest layer first: Merge rule for L1 to L3: a higher layer replaces lower-layer filters on the same column and replaces time_range and time_grain_sqla. Superset ANDs extra filters, so appending region IN [APAC] to a pinned region IN [EMEA] would return nothing; replacement is the only useful semantics. Validator I12_PARAMS rejects a binding that both pins and parameterizes one column. For superset_chart, the merged extras meet L0 exactly as a dashboard native filter would: filters are appended with isExtra: True and the time range is overridden (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:379-408).

The Superset dashboard host reads dataMask and nativeFilters from the dashboard Redux state (both on the root state type, superset-frontend/src/dashboard/types.ts:275-277) and produces a HostDataScope. At submit it also creates a dashboard permalink (POST /api/v1/dashboard/<pk>/permalink, apache/superset: superset/dashboards/permalink/api.py:48), so the selection is durable and reproducible. The engine stores the scope as Artifact.dataContext and gives every binding created in that context filter_context: { dashboard_id, mode: "captured", data_mask, permalink_key }. The host sends the native filters' own extraFormData, never a re-derivation from the filter type: Superset already publishes filters, time_range, time_grain_sqla and granularity_sqla in the mask, the same keys that EXTRA_FORM_DATA_APPEND_KEYS and EXTRA_FORM_DATA_OVERRIDE_REGULAR_MAPPINGS declare (apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-224). filter_context.mode Values used at resolve time captured (default) the data_mask stored on the binding; the narrative and every refresh use the same selection follow_host the viewer's live mask when the viewing host is the same dashboard and the policy includes on_filter_change; else captured defaults the dashboard's saved defaults (active_data_mask omitted) none no dashboard filters

docs.t: 4.3 Which filters apply to which binding
docs.x: On master, Superset already answers this: get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id, chart_id, active_data_mask=...) (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272) loads the native filter configuration, keeps the filters in scope for the chart, and resolves each value. Its rules, read from the source: In scope means one of the chart's layout parents is in the filter's scope.rootPath and the chart is not in scope.excluded. The persisted chartsInScope is deliberately ignored because it is a frontend cache that can be stale (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:78-100). An entry in the active mask wins; an empty active value means "cleared" and does not fall back to the default (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:205-227). Without an active entry, a filter applies only when it has a static default; defaultToFirstItem filters are reported as not_applied_uses_default_to_first_item_prequery (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:173-202). It raises ValueError when the chart is not on the dashboard, and handles native filters only. On 6.1.0 the module does not exist (Story 8). The extension below ports the same three rules into a local resolver, and uses it for dataset and metric sources on both versions, where "in scope" means a filter targets[].datasetId equals the source's dataset_id. Gotcha: cross filters are not propagated Cross-filter entries in the mask are keyed by chart id, not native filter id, and neither master's module nor the local resolver maps them. A captured mask that contains any raises warning cross_filter_not_applied. Users see the native filter selection, not the cross filter, until a later version maps chart_configuration scopes.

gck/packages/protocol/src/data.ts (new, excerpt) Options from a dataset column are loaded as the viewer through Superset's column-values route (GET /api/v1/datasource/<type>/<id>/column/<column>/values/, apache/superset: superset/datasource/api.py:225-227), so a viewer only sees values RLS allows. The viewer's choice lives in view state (host state or ?gck_p_region=EMEA), never in the artifact. Changing it re-resolves exactly the bindings whose params reference it.

gck/packages/protocol/src/data.ts (new, excerpt) Effective policy for a binding is binding.refresh over artifact.refresh over the target default over the host's provider prop. Target Default modes Interval Who triggers slides in Presenton on_open, manual, before export opt-in, at least 60 s while presenting Story 4 useDeckRefresh, later the kit controller with the Presenton transport tiptap-doc on_open, manual, on_filter_change opt-in host RefreshController superset-dashboard Superset's own: open, native filter change, dashboard refresh json_metadata.refresh_frequency, opt-in, at least 60 s Superset frontend text rendered by the kit on_open, manual, on_filter_change opt-in RefreshController text exported (Markdown, HTML, email) snapshot, or on_schedule per send n/a scheduler, as the schedule's executor
Six flows cover every way a number gets onto a screen. All of them end in the same Superset call; only the trigger, the identity source and the receiver differ.

Resolution starts once the outline is final and emits in section order, so resolving_data can overlap generating. A data error never fails the run: the binding ends error, stale or forbidden, and run.failed data_forbidden is reserved for a target that requires data where every binding is forbidden.

Two cases. Inside a generated dashboard target, nothing in the kit runs: data blocks are native Superset charts and re-query on their own. For a kit view next to a dashboard (an embedded dashboard with a Tiptap page, or a kit panel inside Superset) with follow_host bindings: The Embedded SDK publishes the mask through getDataMask() and observeDataMask(cb) when dashboardUiConfig.emitDataMasks is set (superset-embedded-sdk/src/index.ts:44, 164-165, 239, 594-614).

No model call happens here: the stored definitions are re-resolved and re-rendered. The executor follows Superset's report rules: ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS (default [ExecutorType.EDITOR] on master, apache/superset: superset/config.py:2838), per-schedule "Run As" behind ALERT_REPORT_DYNAMIC_EXECUTOR (apache/superset: superset/config.py:741), and lookup through get_executor (apache/superset: superset/tasks/utils.py:58). Never a shared service account.

docs.t: Step 7: The Superset side: extending the Story 8 refresh API
docs.x: Story 8's POST /api/v1/ai_slides/refresh already runs a saved chart's query inside a Flask blueprint, under override_user(token_user), through ChartDataCommand.validate() (RBAC) and .run() (RLS in the generated SQL). Protocol 1.1 keeps that endpoint and its legacy flat items, and adds source-typed items.

POST /api/v1/ai_slides/refresh (protocol 1.1 items) param_scope is the L2 layer: the engine converts the viewer's parameter values into an extra_form_data fragment before calling, because only the engine knows the viewer's current values. Every filter in it still passes Story 8's column and operator allowlist.

Gotcha: the engine cache key must include the viewer Superset's own data cache is RLS-safe because get_rls_cache_key adds the user's RLS clauses to the key (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313). The engine's 60-second cache sits in front of Superset and knows nothing about RLS, so its key starts with the viewer key. Dropping it would serve one user's rows to another for up to a minute.

docs.t: 9.1 Binding error codes: the honest fallbacks
docs.x: A data problem never fails a run or a refresh; it ends one binding in a status with a code. The engine reports a transient failure (the retryable codes below) as stale with the code in reason and no snapshot, the same rule as Part VIII's binding_stale; the browser's BindingStore keeps the snapshot it already holds, so the old value stays visible with its "as of" time and a Retry action instead of disappearing. A viewer who holds no snapshot sees the unavailable panel with Retry. Every other code arrives as error or forbidden with retryable: false. error.code Status Retryable What the viewer sees forbidden, chart_forbidden, datasource_forbidden forbidden no nothing (no value, no stored snapshot), data.forbidden chart_not_found, datasource_not_found error no data.chartNotFound unsupported_viz, unsupported_viz_type, multi_query, source_unsupported error no data.unsupportedViz plus "Open in Superset" no_query_context error no "Open and save this chart in Superset once" mapping_invalid, mapping_changed error no data.mappingChanged invalid_override, param_invalid error no "This filter is not valid for the data" sql_not_permitted, sql_mutation_rejected forbidden, error no data.forbidden, or the generic error query_failed, cache_load_failed, invalid_query, analytics_error, missing_result, internal_error stale (code in reason) yes the kept snapshot with a stale badge and Retry, or data.error plus Retry when the viewer holds none timeout, analytics_unavailable stale (code in reason) yes, with backoff as above rate_limited unchanged yes, after retryAfterMs "Too many refreshes, retrying shortly" data_token_expired unchanged yes, after re-authentication silent no_data_identity error no data.noIdentity element_missing (slides) error no binding listed as orphaned run.failed with data_forbidden is reserved for a target that requires data where every requested binding is forbidden; there is no run-level data_unavailable.

Two Story 1 changes feed it: binding_data gains snapshot, so the kit's store gets the normative shape rather than the element patch, and refresh_started gains viewer_key, computed by Presenton BE with the shared GCK_VIEWER_KEY_SECRET (Step 14.3). Without viewer_key the redact policy hides every deck snapshot, because none matches an empty viewer key (it fails closed, never open). artifact_key is a new nullable column on slide_data_bindings written by the slides apply path (Step 12.1); rows created by Part VIII's own planner have none and are keyed by row id. readPresentonFrames is a small wrapper over createSseParser that keeps only event: response frames. Only manual (the "Refresh data" button and Retry) sends it, the engine honors it once per binding per viewer per 30 seconds, and every other trigger uses force: false. With the default DATA_CACHE_CONFIG of NullCache (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1532) every request hits the warehouse anyway; configure a real cache before turning on intervals.

docs.t: 14.3 Shared artifacts never leak the author's data
docs.x: meta.resolved_by is base64url(HMAC-SHA256(GCK_VIEWER_KEY_SECRET, superset_user_id))[:16], computed by the engine and by Presenton BE with one secret. sharedSnapshotPolicy defaults to redact: a stored snapshot is shown only when resolved_by equals the current viewerKey; anyone else sees a skeleton until their own refresh lands. show is allowed only when the host asserts that the document's audience equals the dataset's audience. Hosts persist stripRuntime(artifact); the engine blanks token text in every artifact it sends. Only the owner's results are persisted into Presenton slides; the engine never persists refresh results. The run event log replaces binding.resolved payloads with {snapshot_hash} 24 hours after the run completes.

The model never writes numbers in prose (I5_NUMBERS_IN_TOKENS), and calendar labels next to tokens raise I16_PERIOD_LABELS (use the period token). The engine stamps generatedAgainst = { snapshot_hash, snapshotAt } per binding; when a later refresh returns changed: true, views show "Text was written against data as of {date}. Regenerate?", which starts an edit run that re-resolves every referenced binding. Gotcha: not_found versus forbidden Story 8 looks charts up with skip_base_filter=True so a viewer without access gets forbidden rather than not_found; the dataset loader in Step 7.3 does the same. The views need the distinction (a forbidden binding must render nothing, not "deleted"), and the price is that a caller learns an id exists. If policy forbids that, use the base-filtered lookup and accept not_found for both.

Gotcha: the row cap applies before pivoting A superset_dataset with pivot: true and 10 regions over 12 months returns 120 long-format rows before the pivot. A row_limit of 50 silently drops points. The engine sets row_limit from x buckets x expected series at catalog time, and meta.truncated makes the remaining cases visible (data.truncated).

Shared mapper parity. A recorded Story 8 refresh response (chart, metric with previous, table with raw cells) goes through gck_data.map_result, then into Part VIII's write_value and GCK's resolveToken; the displayed strings must be identical. Snapshot v1 to v2. Fixture pairs run through every adapter: the output changes and no author value remains anywhere (getHTML(), Markdown, position_json, slide content). Status fixtures per adapter for pending, stale, error and forbidden: no template sample data, nothing under forbidden, stamps present on frozen outputs. Drift. A renamed series yields mapping_changed, never the first series. Limits. 101 bindings return 413; an interval under 60 s fails I13_REFRESH_POLICY; a second forced refresh within 30 s is downgraded and reports meta.force_throttled: true; the 61st request in a minute returns 429. Token exchange. Wrong client assertion, expired subject token, inactive user and missing AISlides permission each return the documented error, and the data token never appears in an engine event or log line.

docs.t: Part VIII · AI Slides delivery plan
docs.p: Part VIII · AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Reads: the architect's story backlog, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts · Builds on: Part VII landing, Template v2 format · Time: ~15 min Part VII describes a long-term, Superset-native design. Part VIII is the plan the team is actually building first. It forks Presenton, embeds it inside the Superset-based analytics platform as a feature called AI Slides, and makes every chart and metric in a generated deck a live binding to Superset data that refreshes when the deck is opened. This part takes the architect's nine stories and turns each one into an implementation guide, with architecture diagrams, the exact code changes in the Presenton fork and in the analytics backend, UI component code, tests and rollout steps.

docs.p: Part VIII · AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Three ideas hold the plan together: One identity. The user is signed in to Superset only. The host page exchanges the Superset session for a short-lived signed assertion. Presenton turns that into its own session, and every data call afterwards runs as that same Superset user, so roles and row-level security apply unchanged (Story 2, Story 8). Bindings, not numbers. A chart on a slide stores a reference to a saved Superset chart plus a mapping, never typed-in values. The planner only proposes charts that Superset can refresh and the user can see (Story 7). The refresh service resolves them on open (Story 1), and the editor fills them in progressively (Story 4). Same origin. Presenton is served under /ai-slides/ on the analytics domain. That keeps cookies, Content Security Policy and API calls simple, and it is why Next.js basePath and prefix-aware routing matter so much (Story 5, Story 9).

Public path Served by Notes https://analytics.example.com/ Superset web (Flask and React) Unchanged /ai-slides/launch Superset, new host view (Story 5) Renders the iframe and the postMessage bridge; needs an exact-match ingress rule ahead of /ai-slides /ai-slides/ Presenton FE (Next.js, basePath: "/ai-slides") Story 5 makes the app prefix-aware /ai-slides/api/v1/, /ai-slides/api/v2/ Presenton BE (FastAPI), prefix stripped to /api/v1/... and /api/v2/... Story 9 ingress rule; other /ai-slides/api/* paths are Next.js route handlers /ai-slides/app_data/ Presenton BE assets, auth-checked Replaces the nginx alias blocks of the stock image /api/v1/ai_slides/* Superset, new ai_slides blueprint (Story 8) Handoff, JWKS, refresh, catalog http://superset-mcp:5008/mcp Superset MCP service, internal only Used by the harness http://ai-harness:8080 Harness, internal only Runs the presentation-planner skill Why same-origin is the default: Cookies just work. Presenton's session cookie is set with samesite="lax" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:47-55). Inside a same-site iframe a Lax cookie is sent normally. On a separate subdomain that is still same-site, but on a different registrable domain the cookie becomes third-party and needs SameSite=None; Secure, plus partitioned cookies for browsers that block third-party cookies. Framing is already allowed. Superset's default TALISMAN_CONFIG content security policy sets default-src 'self' and no explicit frame-src (apache/superset: superset/config.py:3116-3160), so a same-origin iframe is permitted without changing Superset's CSP. A different origin would need frame-src added there. No CORS. The browser talks to one origin, so neither Superset nor Presenton needs CORS for the embedded flow. Gotcha: cookie path on a shared origin Stock Presenton sets presenton_session with path="/" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:54). On a shared origin that cookie would also travel with every Superset request. Set Path=/ai-slides in the fork. Story 2 changes both _set_login_cookie and the fastapi-users cookie transport (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:188-192). Gotcha: base path everywhere Presenton assumes it owns /. Its Next.js proxy rewrites /api/v1, /api/v2, /app_data and /static to FastAPI (see Next.js

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: One identity, owned by Superset, flows into Presenton and back out to every data call. Token Issued by Audience Lifetime Holder Used for Superset session cookie Superset Superset Superset config Browser Calling the handoff endpoint Handoff assertion (JWT, RS256) Analytics BE presenton 60 s, single use Browser, briefly Creating a Presenton session presenton_session Presenton BE Presenton Presenton session TTL Browser cookie All Presenton API calls Data token (JWT, RS256) Analytics BE analytics-data, scopes ai_slides:refresh superset:chart:read superset:dashboard:read superset:dataset:read 15 min Presenton BE only Refresh API and harness/MCP calls as the user Assertion claims: iss, aud, sub (Superset user id), username, email, first_name, last_name, org_id, roles, jti, iat, exp. The data token carries the same sub and username, plus scope. Gotcha: per-user MCP needs Superset master Superset's MCP service maps JWT claims to a Superset user (by preferred_username, username, email, then sub) and checks superset:* scopes only on master; Superset 6.1.0 runs every MCP tool as one configured user. On 6.1 the harness must use the analytics catalog and refresh endpoints instead of MCP for anything user-specific (Story 7, Story 8). That is also why the data token carries a username claim and read-only superset:* scopes. Why a separate data token Presenton BE must call Superset as the user long after the handoff. Storing the user's Superset session cookie would be fragile and over-privileged. A narrow token with its own audience and scope is easy to verify in Superset and to revoke by rotating keys. When it expires, the FE asks the parent page for a fresh handoff (ai-slides:handoff-request).

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Presenton's Template v2 already has a chart element with real data fields. It has chart_type drawn from the ChartType enum (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:76-88), plus categories: list[str] and series: list[ChartSeries], where each series is {name, values: list[float]} (elements.py:176-178, elements.py:361-393). Today the language model invents those numbers. A binding replaces invention with a reference. The source and mapping for one chart binding: Resolution produces an element patch that the existing renderer already understands: Three binding kinds cover v1: Kind Target element Mapping Result written into chart Template v2 chart x, series, labels, sort, top-N categories, series metric Text element (a KPI) metric, optional compare Text run, formatted with format table Template v2 table columns, max_rows Table rows and header Statuses: pending (never resolved), ok, stale (snapshot older than AI_SLIDES_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS, default 3600), error, forbidden (the viewer may not see this data). Refreshable means resolvable In v1, "refreshable" has one precise meaning: the source is a saved Superset chart that the analytics refresh API can execute, for the current user, with a viz_type that maps onto a Presenton ChartType. The planner (Story 7) and the catalog (Story 8) use exactly this rule.

You will run a three-day spike that picks how chart data is refreshed, then build the slide_data_bindings table (SQLModel model and Alembic migration), hook binding creation into the generation pipeline, and write the BindingRefreshService with its four endpoints. docs.t: Step 1: The story, its owners and its acceptance criteria
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: The architect's backlog row, transcribed exactly: # Story What it does Owners 1 [Presenton BE] Dynamic data: refresh spike, binding storage and refresh service Stores a Superset data binding for each chart or metric and refreshes values on open, after a spike picks the refresh approach. Srini, Sourav, Nitesh Goal. Every chart, metric and table that the planner (Story 7) binds to a saved Superset chart keeps a durable link to that chart. When a deck is opened, exported or explicitly refreshed, Presenton re-runs the chart's query as the current user, maps the result into the Template v2 element, and stores the latest snapshot so the next open renders instantly. Suggested split of work. Srini owns the spike and the refresh service, Sourav owns binding creation in the generation pipeline and export integration, Nitesh owns the migration and the contract with Story 8 (refresh API). This split is a recommendation, not part of the backlog. Relationship to Part VII. Part VII's DataBinding (Data-bound slide model) becomes one slide_data_bindings row here, and Part VII's Binding Resolver becomes the refresh service of this chapter plus the analytics refresh API of Story 8. Native PPTX refresh in place is out of scope: Part VIII refreshes on open in the browser and bakes the latest snapshot into exports.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: A. Presenton FE calls the Superset chart data API from the iframe. Same-origin routing means the iframe already carries Superset's session cookie, so the Presenton frontend can call GET /api/v1/chart/{pk}/data/ directly. That endpoint loads the chart's saved query context (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:89), applies dashboard native filters when filters_dashboard_id is passed (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:193) and runs ChartDataCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:36). It fails with "Chart has no query context saved" for charts that were never re-saved (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:180). The POST /api/v1/chart/data variant (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:271) needs a CSRF token because WTF_CSRF_ENABLED = True by default (apache/superset: superset/config.py:387). B. Presenton BE refresh service calls the analytics BE refresh API with the user's data token (recommended default). The Presenton backend sends POST /api/v1/ai_slides/refresh with up to 25 items, authenticated by the 15-minute data token from the handoff (see Architecture and contracts). Story 8 runs ChartDataCommand per item as the token's user, so RBAC and RLS apply, and returns rows. Presenton maps rows into elements, persists snapshots, and streams patches to the browser. C. Refresh through the harness and the Superset MCP service. The Presenton backend asks the harness to call the MCP get_chart_data tool per chart. The tool is designed for an agent to inspect samples, not for bulk deterministic refresh.

Gotcha: charts without a saved query context Both A and B depend on query_context stored on the chart. Charts created before query contexts were persisted, or never re-saved, fail. Add it to _STRICT_OWNER_MODELS (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:56) so selects are owner-scoped exactly like slides. Story 2 later replaces owner scoping with require_presentation_access for all three tables together (Story 2). Add a local column deck_plan (nullable JSON) to PresentationModel (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:21). The REST path in Story 7 runs the planner and builds slides in one request and hands the DeckPlan over in memory; the editor's streaming path prepares in one request and streams in another, so it needs the plan stored on the row in between. The DeckPlan shape is owned by Story 7; the column is a local addition not listed in the contracts table. Gotcha: JSON columns are not mutation-tracked The JSON and JSONB column types do not use MutableDict, so binding.snapshot["series"] = ... or slide.ui["components"][0] = ... is invisible to the unit of work. Always build a new dict and reassign (slide.ui = new_ui). Presenton's own code does this, for example slide.ui = _apply_template_content_to_ui(slide.ui, slide.content) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2396).

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: A bound element is found by its Template v2 name. Only elements with decorative: false and a name receive generated content; the hydrator checks both before applying a value (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:666-672), and the set of value-bearing types includes chart, text and table (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:503-511). The Chart model carries the data the binding replaces: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) and Chart has chart_type, categories: Optional[list[str]], series: Optional[list[ChartSeries]], decorative and name (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:361-393). Pie and donut charts keep only the first series (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:395-403), so a pie binding with two series silently loses the second. A metric binds to a Text element (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:203-221) and a table binding to Table (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:302-318). The kind-to-type rule is strict: chart needs type == "chart", metric needs type == "text", table needs type == "table". A slide's ui is a copy of the layout: {"components": [{"id", "position", "elements": [...]}], ...} (see Template v2 format). Elements nest through child (container) and children (flex, grid, group). The element_path is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into slides.ui, for example /components/3/elements/0 or /components/1/elements/2/child. servers/fastapi/services/data_bindings/elements.py (new) Gotcha: names are unique per layout, not per slide Names inside repeated flex and grid regions are duplicated or renumbered when the hydrator expands an array (_normalize_repeated_names, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:813). find_element therefore refuses elements inside repeated regions and refuses ambiguous names. docs.t: Story 2: Platform integration, Postgres, access control, pod-ready API
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Reads: servers/fastapi/services/database.py, servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py, servers/fastapi/migrations.py, servers/fastapi/alembic/env.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/context.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py, servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py · Builds on: Architecture and contracts, Data model, Auth and multi-user · Time: ~60 min This chapter turns Story 2 into code. You will move Presenton's metadata into a dedicated presenton schema of the analytics Postgres, replace username and password login with the Superset handoff from the contracts chapter, add organizations and collaborators with a single access dependency, and remove the assumptions that keep stock Presenton from running as several stateless pods. Every change starts from the code that exists today, with file and line references, and every new file is labeled as new.

docs.t: Step 0: The story, its owner and its acceptance criteria
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owner 2 [Presenton BE] Platform Integration: Postgres, access control, pod-ready API Moves metadata to the analytics Postgres, enforces owner, org and collaborator access with platform identity, and makes the API fit the analytics pod. Nitesh Story 2 and Story 5 (menu, iframe, handoff) unblock any production use. Story 1 (bindings) and Story 3 (prompt library) add tables to the schema created here, so the Postgres and Alembic work in Step 1 and Step 2 should land first. Acceptance criteria: Given the analytics Postgres with an empty presenton schema, when the presenton-migrate Job runs alembic upgrade head, then every Presenton table and presenton.alembic_version exist in schema presenton, and nothing is created in public. Given a BE pod with MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=false, when it starts, then it issues no DDL and /readyz returns 503 until the database revision equals the image's expected head. Given a valid handoff assertion and data token, when the FE posts them to POST /api/v1/platform/session, then the BE upserts the user by platform_subject, sets presenton_session (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ai-slides) and returns {user, org_id, data_token_expires_at} without echoing the data token. Given an assertion that was already used, expired, signed by an unknown key, or carries the wrong aud or iss, when it is posted, then the response is 401 and no cookie is set. Given AI_SLIDES_LOCAL_LOGIN_ENABLED=false, when anyone calls /api/v1/auth/setup or /api/v1/auth/login, then the response is 404. Given user B in the same org as owner A and no share, when B lists or opens A's deck, then the list omits it and the open returns 404. When A shares it with B as viewer, then B can open, refresh and export but every edit, share and delete endpoint returns 403. Given two BE replicas behind one Service, when a session cookie issued by replica 1 is presented to replica 2, then it is accepted (shared signing key, no local state). Given a rolling update, when a pod receives SIGTERM, then it fails readiness, finishes in-flight requests up to the grace period, and does not mark other pods' running async tasks as failed.

docs.x: All URL handling lives in get_database_url_and_connect_args (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:57). With no DATABASE_URL it falls back to sqlite:///<APP_DATA_DIRECTORY>/fastapi.db (:58-60). A postgresql:// URL is rewritten to postgresql+asyncpg:// (:66-67). If the URL has a query string, the function inspects only sslmode (turning it into an ssl.create_default_context() connect argument, :84-86) and then rebuilds the URL with an empty query (:88-96). The engine is created once at import time in servers/fastapi/services/database.py:34-42, with pool settings only for non-SQLite URLs: servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py (excerpt) Migrations run synchronously. _run_migrations (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:52) takes the same URL, converts it with to_sync_sqlalchemy_url to postgresql+psycopg:// (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:114-116), repairs orphan revisions and stamps legacy databases, then calls command.upgrade(config, "head") (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:69). alembic/env.py configures the context with only connection, target_metadata and compare_type (servers/fastapi/alembic/env.py:86-90), so the version table lands in the connection's default schema. The Data model chapter walks the full revision chain. Gotcha: every query parameter in DATABASE_URL is dropped Because the query string is rebuilt as empty (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:88-96), you cannot pass options=-csearch_path=presenton, prepared_statement_cache_size=0 or application_name in the URL. They silently disappear. Also, migrations.py:59 discards the connect_args, so the Alembic connection never receives the ssl context: psycopg's default sslmode=prefer still negotiates TLS if the server offers it, but without certificate verification. Every setting below therefore goes through code or role defaults, not the URL.

(servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:29), and SQLite tests in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_owner_isolation.py create tables in an unqualified in-memory database. search_path keeps both working. Gotcha: PgBouncer in transaction mode SQLAlchemy's asyncpg dialect prepares statements, and asyncpg caches them per connection. Behind PgBouncer in transaction mode, consecutive transactions may land on different server connections, which yields prepared statement "__asyncpg_stmt_1__" does not exist. Set DB_PGBOUNCER_TRANSACTION_MODE=true (above) and, because the URL query is stripped, also pass SQLAlchemy's prepared_statement_cache_size=0 through create_async_engine(..., connect_args=...) rather than the URL. Two more traps: PgBouncer rejects unknown startup parameters, so server_settings={"search_path": ...} fails unless search_path is in track_extra_parameters (set DB_SET_SEARCH_PATH=false and rely on the role default), and SET statements do not survive across transactions. PgBouncer 1.21+ with max_prepared_statements > 0 removes the first problem. Session mode removes all of them at the cost of pooling efficiency.

docs.x: Each BE pod owns one engine. The worst case connection count is replicas x (DB_POOL_SIZE + DB_MAX_OVERFLOW). With the stock defaults (5 + 10) and an HPA maximum of 6, that is 90 connections from one service, which is too many to share a database with Superset. Recommended defaults: Variable Stock default Recommended for pods Why DB_POOL_SIZE 5 5 One uvicorn worker per pod; most requests hold a connection briefly DB_MAX_OVERFLOW 10 5 Caps a pod at 10 connections DB_POOL_TIMEOUT 30 10 Fail fast and let the ingress retry on another pod DB_POOL_RECYCLE 1800 1800 Below typical firewall idle timeouts DB_POOL_PRE_PING true true Survives a Postgres failover Gotcha: long SSE streams hold sessions Endpoints that receive sql_session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_session) keep that session open for the life of the request. For the streaming endpoints (GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id}, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2281) that can be minutes. A connection is only checked out while a transaction is active, but a stream that awaits an LLM between two queries inside one transaction holds it. Add the idle_in_transaction_session_timeout from 1.2 and watch the pool metric from Story 9.

Three additions make that clean in Kubernetes: A preStop sleep of 10 seconds plus setting SHUTTING_DOWN (via a signal handler installed in the lifespan) so /readyz returns 503 and endpoints are removed before connections are refused. The fork adds runner_id (the pod name from POD_NAME) and heartbeat_at to async_tasks, has the running task update heartbeat_at every 30 seconds, and changes the startup sweep (and a periodic reaper) to fail only PENDING tasks whose heartbeat_at is older than AI_SLIDES_TASK_STALE_SECONDS (default 180). docs.t: Step 1: The story, the owner and the acceptance criteria
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owners 3 [Presenton BE] Prompt library and custom templates backend Provides APIs for curated prompts and bundled templates and async generation, with custom template upload on hold pending a decision. Srini Acceptance criteria (written for this guide; each maps to a test in Step 10): GET /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library returns active prompts visible to the caller: global curated prompts (org_id IS NULL) plus prompts of the caller's org. Supports category, q, page, page_size, and returns category facets. GET /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library/{slug} returns one prompt including its variables JSON Schema, or 404 prompt_not_found (also for another org's prompt). POST /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library/{slug}/render validates variables against the schema and returns the rendered content, static instructions, generation defaults and the recommended template. Invalid input returns 422 invalid_variables with a list of JSON paths. GET /api/v1/ppt/templates/bundled returns a curated subset of the 16 built-in templates with thumbnails, layout counts and chart layout counts, and marks the recommended one when prompt_slug is given. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate-from-prompt/async creates an async_tasks row and returns it; the task is pollable at GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id} and ends with data.presentation_id and data.edit_path. When the harness planner is enabled and the prompt declares a dashboard variable, the task calls presentation-planner first and generates slides from its DeckPlan (fixed layouts, outlines from the plan). Curated prompts live in servers/fastapi/assets/prompt_library/*.json; startup import is idempotent, bumps version on change, writes an audit revision, and deactivates removed prompts. With AI_SLIDES_CUSTOM_TEMPLATES_ENABLED unset or false, every custom-template creation or editing route returns 403 with detail.code = "custom_templates_disabled"; listing and reading templates still work. A decision record for custom template upload exists, with the open questions in Step 7.3 answered before the flag is turned on. Scope boundaries Story 3 does not store data bindings (Story 1), does not authenticate users or resolve orgs (Story 2), and does not implement the planner (Story 7). It calls the seams those stories provide. Where this chapter needs one of those seams, it names a recommended function and says which story owns it.

A change is a pull request to a JSON file; code review is the approval step, and git log is the human-readable history. version increases by one for every effective change (insert is 1, edit or deactivation is +1). The async task payload (Step 6.5) records prompt_slug and prompt_version, so a generated deck can always be traced to the exact text that produced it. prompt_library_revisions stores a full snapshot per version with change_kind and changed_by. It is append-only; nothing in the API updates or deletes it. Org prompts (source="org", org_id set) are a recommended follow-up, not v1. When added, an org admin endpoint writes the row and a revision with change_kind="admin_update" and changed_by set to the platform subject from Story 2.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: The rendered text becomes GeneratePresentationRequest.content, which Presenton places in the user message of the outline prompt (Prompts and schemas). The variables come from a browser and, through deep links, from URLs that a third party could craft. Three things must therefore hold: No code execution. Rendering must not evaluate expressions, attribute access or filters. Jinja2 is present only as a transitive dependency, and even a SandboxedEnvironment still exposes loops, filters and attribute lookups that a prompt author does not need. A 30-line placeholder substitution has no such surface. Values are data. A value cannot introduce new placeholders, new lines, or structural markers that read like instructions. Free text is short, single line and pattern-restricted; numbers and enums cannot carry text at all. Authorization is not the renderer's job. A valid dashboard_id is just an integer. Whether the user may see dashboard 37 is decided by Superset when the planner (Story 7) and refresh API (Story 8) run under the user's data token.

docs.p: Story 4: Native charts and refresh UX
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: This chapter implements the frontend half of refresh-on-open. You will see how Presenton draws charts today in three places (editor canvas, HTML preview, export page), why the recommended design keeps the vendored Chart.js runtime, and how live data reaches the screen by patching element JSON in the Redux store while a per-element overlay shows loading, stale, error and forbidden states. You get the full TypeScript for the refresh hook, the bindingsSlice, the overlay components and the autosave changes, plus ordering, cancellation, backoff and the test plan.

docs.t: Step 1: The story and its acceptance criteria
docs.p: Story 4: Native charts and refresh UX
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owners 4 [Presenton FE] Native charts and async refresh UX Renders charts with a charting library from stored bindings and fills them in progressively with loading, error and stale states. Srini, Sourav, Nitesh A suggested split: Sourav owns the hook, slices and autosave integration, Srini owns overlays and visual states, Nitesh owns the contract tests against the Story 1 stream. This split is a recommendation. ID Given When Then AC1 A deck whose bindings all have snapshots younger than AI_SLIDES_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS The user opens it Charts render immediately from the stored slide JSON, no skeletons appear, the refresh stream runs in the background AC2 A deck with a binding that has no snapshot The user opens it That element shows a shimmer skeleton until binding_data arrives, then the real chart AC3 The user is on slide 5 The deck opens Slide 5's bindings are requested first (first_slide) and fill before other slides AC4 A binding's refresh fails transiently and it has a snapshot Refresh completes The element shows the last data and a chip "Data as of 3 h ago" AC5 A binding fails without a snapshot Refresh completes An error panel with a Retry button covers the element; Retry refreshes only that binding AC6 The user lacks access to the chart's data Refresh completes The element shows "You don't have access to this data" and no numbers AC7 Data patches arrive Autosave runs No slide update request is sent for data-only changes, and no undo entry is created AC8 The user is typing in a text box on the active slide A patch for that slide arrives The patch is held until the text box loses focus AC9 The user leaves the page mid-refresh Navigation happens The fetch is aborted and no further Redux updates happen AC10 The deck is exported /pdf-maker renders Charts show the latest snapshot and no overlay, badge or skeleton is in the DOM AC11 A screen reader user opens a deck Refresh starts and ends One polite announcement at start and one summary at the end, no per-chart chatter

The analytics platform's own library is ECharts (apache/superset: superset-frontend/package.json:167 pins echarts ^6.1.0), so the question is whether AI Slides should switch. Criterion Keep Chart.js 4.5.1 (recommended) Switch to ECharts Export fidelity Unchanged: /pdf-maker already draws canvas[data-presenton-chart]; whatever export-core does with those canvases keeps working Every chart in the export DOM changes shape; export-core's handling of charts cannot be verified from this repository (PPTX and PDF export), so PPTX output is at risk Editor TemplateV2ChartJsElement and the chart editor (components/slide-editor/charts/) already speak Chart.js Konva integration, hit-testing and the chart editor need a rewrite Template v2 chart types All 11 ChartType values are mapped today New mapping for every type Visual parity with Superset dashboards Different look (fonts, axis styles) Closer to dashboards Delivery cost None for rendering; work goes into data and states Weeks, across three renderers License MIT (public/vendor/chart-4.5.1-LICENSE.md) Apache-2.0 Decision: keep Chart.js. "Native" in the story means drawn from data, never a screenshot, which Chart.js already does in all three render paths. Parity with Superset styling is handled by theme colors in the binding's element, not by swapping libraries. ECharts stays the documented alternative if the product later demands pixel parity with dashboards.

docs.x: servers/nextjs/store/slices/bindingsSlice.ts (new) Register it as bindings: bindingsReducer in servers/nextjs/store/store.ts. Every run-scoped action carries runId, and reducers ignore stale runs, which is what makes cancellation safe: an aborted stream's last frames cannot overwrite a newer run. The UI status is derived, not copied. The server knows five statuses (ok, stale, error, forbidden, pending); the browser adds idle and loading and recomputes stale from snapshot age, because a snapshot that was ok when written becomes stale simply by time passing. The transitions: A forbidden binding is re-queried by every full refresh (the server does not skip it), so access granted in Superset shows up on the next open or the next Refresh data click. It never gets a per-element Retry button, because retrying a permission error immediately only produces the same answer. A data_token_expired error is not a state at all; it sets needsReauth, leaves the binding loading, and the hook retries after a new handoff.

docs.t: Step 6: Autosave must not save data patches as edits
docs.p: Story 4: Native charts and refresh UX
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Autosave ignores changes that arrive while it is paused and treats them as already persisted: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/useAutoSave.tsx (excerpt) Refresh patches are also server-originated. For the deck owner they are already persisted (Story 1 writes them into slides.ui); for editors and viewers they are deliberately not persisted, because the stored snapshot is always the owner's RLS view. Either way the browser must not save them as edits. Pausing autosave for the whole refresh would block saving real edits for several seconds, so instead re-acknowledge exactly the patched slides, and only if they had no unsaved user edit before the patch. servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/autoSaveDiff.ts (addition) servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/useAutoSave.tsx (change) Returning before dispatch(addToHistory(...)) (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/useAutoSave.tsx:163-166) keeps data patches out of app-level undo. Gotcha: undo can bring old numbers back History entries recorded before a refresh still hold the old values, and a dirty slide saved by an editor carries that editor's live values. Neither may reach the database. Story 1 makes the slide update endpoints call reapply_binding_snapshots before saving, so stored bound values always equal the owner's last snapshot (Story 1). In the browser, Undo after a refresh still shows old numbers on screen until the next refresh; that is cosmetic, not a data problem. Gotcha: hand-edited bound data is overwritten The chart editor (components/slide-editor/charts/ChartEditorContent.tsx) lets users type values into a chart. For a bound chart those values are replaced on the next refresh. Show a "Values come from Superset" notice in the chart editor when selectBindingsForSlide contains the chart's name, and disable value editing for bound charts in v1.

docs.t: Step 8: Ordering, cancellation, backoff and concurrency
docs.p: Story 4: Native charts and refresh UX
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Progressive fill. The hook sends first_slide=<active slide id>. Story 1's service puts that slide's bindings into their own first batch, then the rest in deck order in batches of up to 25 (see Story 1). Charts already showing snapshot data stay visible while they refresh, so in practice the user sees skeletons only for never-resolved bindings. Navigation inside the deck. Moving to another slide does not restart the stream. The first slide's batch is a head start, not a priority queue; restarting would waste work already in flight on the server. Cancellation. Unmount or a new presentationId aborts the AbortController; fetch rejects with AbortError, the reader stops, and pending animation frames are cancelled. The backend sees the disconnect and cancels unstarted batches (safe_sse_stream handles CancelledError, servers/fastapi/utils/sse.py:21-23). Late frames from an aborted run are ignored by runId checks in every reducer. Backoff. Network errors, non-2xx responses and streams that end without refresh_complete retry up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, capped at 8 s, plus or minus 20 % jitter). Retries ask only for unsettled bindings with repeated binding_id parameters. data_token_expired first triggers a new handoff through the parent page (contract message ai-slides:handoff-request, owned by Story 5), then retries. Concurrency. One stream per open deck in the browser. Fan-out happens server-side: at most 4 concurrent analytics calls per refresh, 25 items each. A single-binding Retry uses the non-streaming POST .../refresh with binding_ids and force: true, so it never opens a second stream. Gotcha: one deck in two tabs refreshes twice Each tab runs its own stream. Story 1's per-user TTL cache absorbs the duplicate within 60 s, but both tabs write the same values, and each tab's autosave re-acknowledges independently. Do not add cross-tab coordination in v1; it is cheap to tolerate. Presentation mode. The hook keeps running (it is called before the present-mode return), overlays render without buttons, and the active slide is presentSlideFromUrl. The audience sees a skeleton only for elements that never had data, and a small "Data as of" chip for stale ones, which is honest in a live meeting. Export. /pdf-maker never mounts useDeckRefresh or BoundDataLayer; it fetches slides from the database

docs.p: Story 4: Native charts and refresh UX
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: These are the situations that come up in review and in bug reports. Each one has a defined behavior so the team does not rediscover it. The user reorders slides during a refresh. Patches address slides by slideId and elements by pointer plus name, never by index, so a reorder in the middle of a stream is harmless. The reorder itself triggers a structural autosave; Story 1 changes update_presentation to upsert so the binding rows survive it (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2568-2574 is the block that must change). The user deletes a bound slide. The slide disappears from presentationData.slides; any later binding_data for it finds no slide and applyBindingElementPatches skips it. When the structural autosave deletes the slide row, the database cascade removes the binding. The bindings slice still holds the entry until the next GET bindings; selectBindingsForSlide returns nothing for a slide that no longer renders, so no stray overlay appears. The user deletes or retypes a bound element. applyElementPatch first tries the pointer, then the unique name; if neither matches, it returns false and nothing changes. On the server, write_value raises element_missing and the binding becomes error with an "orphaned" message. Show orphaned bindings in a small list under Refresh data (a v1.1 follow-up) so users can remove them. The user duplicates a bound element on a slide. The copy carries the same name, which makes the name ambiguous; findNamedElement refuses ambiguous names, so only the pointer lookup can match. That keeps the original bound and leaves the copy static. This mirrors the backend rule in Story 1. The deck is huge. Twenty slides with 12 bindings is the planner's ceiling (Story 7 limits). At that size there is one stream, at most one batch for the first slide plus one batch of 11, and at most 12 Konva resets spread over two animation frames. If product later lifts the limits, keep the per-frame batching and consider coalescing patches per slide in the reducer. The theme or template changes after binding. Patches only touch data keys (categories and series, runs, columns and rows). Colors, fonts, axis styles and positions remain whatever the slide JSON says, so a theme change or a manual restyle survives every refresh. The browser is offline or the backend restarts. fetch rejects, the hook backs off three times, then dispatches

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owner 5 [Presenton FE] Analytics menu and iframe hardening Adds the "AI Slides" menu item and makes the embedded Presenton iframe reliable (sizing, deep links, session handoff, base path). Sourav Acceptance criteria (written for this chapter; the architect's row lists the four themes, these make them testable): A user with the can_access on AISlides permission sees AI Slides in the Superset navbar; a user without it does not, and a direct request to /ai-slides/launch returns Superset's normal access-denied response. Clicking the item opens /ai-slides/launch, which shows the Superset navbar on top and Presenton below it, filling the remaining viewport with no double scrollbars at 1280x720 and 1920x1080. The user lands in Presenton signed in as themselves without seeing any Presenton login form. No token ever appears in a URL, in browser storage, or in Presenton JavaScript-readable cookies. Every Presenton request (pages, /api/v1, /api/v2, Next.js route handlers, /app_data, /static, /vendor, /_next) is served under /ai-slides. Nothing requests a root-relative Presenton URL. /ai-slides/launch?path=/presentation?id=<uuid> opens that deck directly. Navigating inside Presenton updates the parent URL (shareable), and browser Back/Forward keep both in step. When the Presenton session or data token expires, the iframe obtains a new handoff silently. When the Superset session itself has expired, the top window goes to the Superset login page and returns to the same deck afterwards. Presentation mode can enter browser fullscreen from inside the iframe; PPTX and PDF exports download from inside the iframe. Presenton pages cannot be framed by any origin other than the analytics origin, and both sides reject postMessage traffic from unexpected origins or windows. An automated end-to-end suite covers launch, deep link, expiry, export and fullscreen, and the manual QA matrix below is signed off for the supported browsers.

docs.x: Height. The host computes height: calc(100dvh - var(--ai-slides-nav-height)) and a ResizeObserver on #app-menu keeps the variable current (Step 3.4). The navbar's height is not constant: the environment tag, a long brand text or a narrow window can change it, so measuring beats hard-coding 56 px. 100dvh avoids the mobile URL-bar jump; the 100vh line before it is the fallback. Inside the frame nothing changes: Presenton's h-screen layouts now mean "the iframe's viewport", which is exactly the space left under the navbar. Set overflow: hidden on the host body so only the iframe scrolls. Focus. Presentation mode reads arrow keys inside the iframe. The host calls frame.focus() on load, and Presenton should keep its own focus handling. Fullscreen. Presenton enters fullscreen on #presentation-mode-wrapper, falling back to document.documentElement: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationNavigation.ts:68-82 requestFullscreen() inside an iframe needs the frame to be allowed the fullscreen feature, hence allow="fullscreen" plus the legacy allowfullscreen attribute on the iframe. The element that goes fullscreen is inside the iframe, so the Superset navbar disappears with it, and Escape returns to the framed view. The call still needs a user gesture inside the iframe; keyboard shortcuts work once the iframe has focus. Gotcha: a Permissions-Policy header can silently veto fullscreen allow="fullscreen" only delegates what the top document itself has. If an ingress or a future Talisman setting sends Permissions-Policy: fullscreen=() on the Superset host page, requestFullscreen() rejects and Presenton's catch handler just leaves isFullscreen false. Include fullscreen in the QA matrix and check response headers of /ai-slides/launch when it fails.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: All messages are plain objects with v: 1 and a type starting with ai-slides:. Receivers drop anything else. Type Direction Payload Receiver checks ai-slides:handoff-request iframe to host request_id (uuid), reason (launch, unauthorized, data_token_expiring, retry) host: event.origin === presentonOrigin, event.source === frame.contentWindow, request_id length at most 64 ai-slides:handoff host to iframe request_id, assertion, data_token, expires_in iframe: event.origin === parentOrigin, event.source === window.parent, request_id matches the pending request ai-slides:handoff-error host to iframe request_id, code (superset_session_expired, forbidden, handoff_<status>) same as above ai-slides:session-ready iframe to host none host origin and source checks ai-slides:session-error iframe to host code host origin and source checks; host shows a banner ai-slides:navigate iframe to host path, optional title host checks plus the safe-path rule ai-slides:route host to iframe path iframe checks plus isSafeAppPath ai-slides:open-superset iframe to host path (a Superset path, for example /dashboard/37/) host checks, safe-path rule, must not start with /ai-slides Senders always pass an explicit targetOrigin (cfg.presentonOrigin on the host, getParentOrigin() in the iframe). The contract's ai-slides:handoff message is extended here with request_id, data_token and expires_in; it is still the only message that carries tokens.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Framing. Two different headers protect two different documents. The Superset host page is a top-level document; Talisman's default frame_options is SAMEORIGIN (flask-talisman talisman.py, default argument of init_app), which prevents other sites from framing the host page that holds the handoff bridge. Presenton's own responses need Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (same-origin topology) or frame-ancestors https://analytics.example.com (subdomain topology), set in Next.js headers() and in FastAPI middleware. The exact configuration is in Story 8, Step 9. The bridge's top-level redirect adds a third layer: even a page that loads Presenton top-level gets sent to Superset. postMessage rules, all enforced in the code above: Check both event.origin and event.source. Origin alone is not enough in the same-origin topology, because every Superset page and every Presenton page share that origin; event.source === frame.contentWindow (host) and event.source === window.parent (iframe) pin the conversation to the two windows that should be talking. Never use "*" as targetOrigin. If the iframe were navigated somewhere else (for example by an open redirect), a wildcard would deliver tokens to it. Correlate request and response with a random request_id, and accept a handoff only while a request is pending. Keep tokens in memory for the duration of one POST /api/v1/platform/session call. The assertion lives 60 seconds and is single-use (jti, checked by Presenton BE), and the data token is stored server-side by Presenton BE and never returned to the browser. Validate every path on receipt, on both sides and on the server. Gotcha: same-origin means a cross-site scripting bug anywhere on the origin reaches the bridge In the same-origin topology, script injected into any Superset page could open /ai-slides/launch in a hidden frame and call the handoff endpoint itself; origin checks cannot help because the attacker is the origin. The mitigations are Superset's nonce-based CSP, the CSRF requirement on the handoff, the 60-second single-use assertion, and the data token's narrow scope (Story 8). The subdomain topology isolates Presenton's DOM from Superset's, at the price of the cookie settings in Story 8.

docs.t: Step 10: Downloads, popups and the sandbox question
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Downloads. The export flow ends with a synthetic anchor: link.href = path; link.download = fileName; link.click() (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationHeader.tsx:426-434). The file route answers with Content-Disposition: attachment (servers/nextjs/app/api/export-presentation/file/route.ts:55, 89-91). In an iframe without a sandbox attribute this behaves exactly as at top level, provided the href carries the base path (Step 4.7). Popups. Presenton opens a few external pages with window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer"), for example in Codex settings (servers/nextjs/components/CodexConfig.tsx:134). These work from an unsandboxed iframe. Hide provider and account settings in AI Slides mode anyway (Story 2 and Story 6), because users should not configure LLM keys inside the analytics platform. Sandbox. Recommended default: no sandbox attribute in the same-origin topology. A sandbox that keeps allow-scripts and allow-same-origin for same-origin content is not a security boundary (the framed document can reach into its parent and remove the attribute), while every missing token breaks a feature. If a security review insists, this is the minimum set that keeps Presenton working: Token Needed for allow-scripts the whole app allow-same-origin cookies, fetch to /ai-slides/api, localStorage allow-forms file uploads and form posts allow-downloads PPTX and PDF export downloads allow-popups, allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox external links opened in new tabs behave like normal pages allow-modals window.confirm and alert if any remain Never add allow-top-navigation; the bridge's ai-slides:open-superset message lets the host perform the few top-level navigations Presenton needs.

docs.x: Check Chrome (latest) Edge (latest) Firefox (latest, ETP standard) Safari 17+ macOS (ITP on) Navbar item and access denied First launch without login form Height correct, single scrollbar, window resize Deep link, in-app navigation, Back/Forward Silent re-handoff after deleting presenton_session Superset logout then return Fullscreen presentation and Escape PPTX and PDF download Clipboard copy inside editor Safari and third-party cookies. In the recommended same-origin topology the iframe is first-party, so Safari's Intelligent Tracking Prevention and Firefox's Enhanced Tracking Protection do not affect presenton_session. A sibling subdomain under the same registrable domain (slides.analytics.example.com framed by analytics.example.com) is still same-site, so SameSite=Lax cookies are sent. Only a cross-site deployment (Presenton on a different registrable domain) makes the iframe cookie third-party: Safari blocks those by default, and Chrome expects SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned. Whether a given Safari version honors partitioned cookies, or requires the Storage Access API (document.requestStorageAccess() after a user gesture), was not verified for this chapter; test it on the exact versions in the matrix before committing to a cross-site topology.

docs.t: Step 1: The story, the owner and the acceptance criteria
docs.p: Story 6: Prompt library and template UI
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owners 6 [Presenton FE] Prompt library and template UI Lets users browse and use curated prompts and select templates, with template upload on hold. Radhika Acceptance criteria: The upload page offers a Prompt library tab next to the free-text prompt. It lists prompts from GET /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library with search, category filters, loading, empty and error states. Selecting a prompt shows a form generated from its variables JSON Schema. A field marked x-ai-slides-widget: "dashboard" renders a dashboard picker fed by the analytics catalog (GET /api/v1/ai_slides/catalog). Server validation errors appear on the matching fields. A template picker shows the bundled templates from GET /api/v1/ppt/templates/bundled with thumbnails, a selected state and a Recommended badge; the recommended template is preselected. Generate calls POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate-from-prompt/async, polls GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id}, shows progress, and navigates to /presentation?id=... on completion. Failures are shown with a retry. Review outline first renders the prompt and continues through Presenton's existing outline page with the recommended template suggested. With AI_SLIDES_CUSTOM_TEMPLATES_ENABLED off, no custom template entry point is visible (upload page, outline template stage, template library, template editor) and /custom-template redirects away. /upload?prompt=<slug>&dashboard_id=37 opens the library with that prompt selected and the dashboard prefilled. An unknown slug falls back to Presenton's existing free-text behavior. Everything is operable by keyboard, has visible focus, and announces async progress to screen readers.

docs.x: upload/components/prompt-library/PromptLibraryPanel.tsx (NEW) How the panel's effects fit together, in the order they run after a prompt is chosen: selectPrompt sets slug and clears templateId, which triggers two fetches in parallel: usePromptDetail(slug) and useBundledTemplates(slug) (the latter passes prompt_slug so the backend marks the recommended template). When the bundled list arrives, the preselection effect keeps the current template if it is still in the list and otherwise picks the recommended one, falling back to the first. A user's explicit choice therefore survives a refetch, while switching prompts resets to the new recommendation. When the detail arrives, schemaToFields derives the field list and the initialization effect computes values: schema defaults, overlaid once with deep-link values. The appliedDeepLink ref guarantees that URL values are applied to the first prompt only; choosing a different prompt later starts from that prompt's defaults. If the deep-link slug returns 404, the fallback effect hands the slug text back to UploadPage, which switches to the free-text tab. On Generate, the button runs validate (client-side checks plus "a template is selected"), posts, polls and finally calls onNavigate. On Review outline first, the panel renders the prompt on the server (so the outline sees exactly the text the backend validated) and delegates the Redux hand-off to UploadPage. Values are kept as typed JavaScript values (numbers for integers, the original enum value rather than its string form), because the backend validates with JSON Schema types: sending "37" for an integer field fails with invalid_variables even though it looks right in the form.

docs.t: Story 7: Harness presentation-planner skill and refreshable-only data selection
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/chart/tool/get_chart_data.py, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/chart/schemas.py · Builds on: Architecture and contracts, Generation flow · Time: ~60 min This chapter turns Story 7 into an implementation guide. You will build the presentation-planner skill that the team's harness runs: it reads the user's request, a summary of the chosen template's layouts and the catalog of Superset charts the user may refresh, and returns a validated DeckPlan that fixes every slide's layout, outline and data bindings. You will also see exactly where the plan plugs into Presenton's generation handler, which Presenton LLM steps it replaces, how every chart choice is checked by deterministic code before anything is saved, and how an eval set of 40+ cases keeps the planner honest in CI.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owners 7 [Harness] presentation-planner skill and refreshable-only data selection Plans decks and picks only charts and metrics that Superset can refresh and the user can access, with validation, limits and an eval set. Srini, Nitesh A sensible split: Srini owns the skill (SKILL.md, tools, validators, eval set), Nitesh owns the analytics side it depends on (the catalog endpoint and MCP authentication from Story 8) and the Presenton BE client that consumes the plan.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: POST http://ai-harness:8080/v1/skills/presentation-planner:run accepts {prompt, template_id, layout_catalog, dashboard_id?, chart_ids?, n_slides, language} with the user's data token as Authorization: Bearer, and returns a DeckPlan that validates against the JSON Schema in Step 4. Every binding in a returned plan references a chart that appears in the analytics BE catalog for that user with refreshable: true. Refreshable-violation rate and access-violation rate on the eval set are both exactly 0. Every layout_id and element_name exists in the supplied layout_catalog, and each binding's kind matches the slot type (chart slot, metric-capable text slot, or table slot). Every mapping column exists in the columns returned by the MCP get_chart_data sample for that chart, and the chart's viz_type is compatible with the slot's chart_type according to the compatibility table in Step 6. Limits hold: at most 20 slides, 12 bindings in total, 3 bindings per slide, 100 sample rows per chart, 30 tool calls and 90 seconds of wall time per run. Outlines contain no raw numbers outside a small allowlist (Step 8). Values shown on slides come only from bindings. Invalid plans are repaired with at most 2 feedback rounds; after that the harness either returns a plan with offending bindings moved to excluded, or fails with a typed error. Presenton BE, when given a plan, skips its free outline and layout-selection LLM steps, keeps its per-slide content step for text only, and writes pending bindings through the Story 1 binding storage. An eval set of at least 40 cases runs in CI on every change to the skill and blocks merges when a threshold in Step 13 is missed. How this maps to Part VII The planner here is the near-term version of the Planner in Generation flow. Part VII's "Data Digest" and "Binding Registry" collapse into two simpler things in Part VIII: the analytics BE catalog (Story 8) and the deterministic validators in this chapter.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: The harness is the team's agent runtime, in the style of an Agent SDK: it runs an LLM in a tool-use loop, and it packages capabilities as skills. A skill is a directory with a SKILL.md (the instructions the model follows, with a short front-matter header), the tool code the model may call, and configuration (model, limits, timeouts). The harness exposes each skill over HTTP as POST /v1/skills/<name>:run, enforces the configured budgets, and returns the skill's final structured output. Nothing in this chapter depends on a particular vendor SDK; the skill only needs four things from the runtime: tool calling, a token and tool-call budget, a wall clock, and a "final answer must match this JSON Schema" hook. The planner does not own data access. Its tools call two systems, both as the user: the analytics BE catalog endpoint GET /api/v1/ai_slides/catalog (Story 8, new), which is the single authority on "refreshable and accessible"; the Superset MCP service at http://superset-mcp:5008/mcp, for chart metadata and small data samples (list_charts, get_chart_info, get_dashboard_info, get_chart_data).

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: The end-to-end run, in one list: Presenton BE resolves the template, builds the layout catalog, and calls the harness with the data token. The skill fetches the user's catalog, drops unrefreshable rows into excluded, and discovers context through get_dashboard_info and get_chart_info. For each data slide, the ranker returns the top candidates whose viz_type fits the slot; the model samples at most 12 charts through get_chart_data with limit: 100. The model drafts the DeckPlan; the validators check it; at most two repair rounds follow, then the removal-only fallback. Presenton BE re-checks catalog membership, builds outlines and structure from the plan, runs slide content generation with bound fields removed, saves pending bindings, and triggers the refresh that fills real values.

docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Gotcha: prompt injection through chart names and descriptions Chart slice_name, description, column names and even sample values are written by other users. Wrap them in a clearly labeled DATA section in tool results, strip control characters, truncate descriptions to 300 characters, and never place them in the system prompt. More importantly, the defenses that matter are structural: the gateway refuses non-catalog charts, and the validators reject any binding outside the user's catalog regardless of what the model was persuaded to do. Group E of the eval set exists to prove this. Gotcha: stale catalog A chart can be deleted, have its dataset permission revoked, or lose its query_context between the catalog read and the refresh. The 300 s cache makes this window larger. Mitigations: invalidate the cache on any NotFound, AccessDenied or DatasetNotAccessible from MCP; re-validate the plan in Presenton BE with a fresh catalog read; and rely on Story 1's refresh to mark such bindings forbidden or error instead of failing the deck. Gotcha: RLS makes samples differ across users The author's sample reflects the author's row-level security. A viewer with narrower RLS (Story 2 sharing) sees different numbers on refresh, which is correct, but any outline sentence derived from the author's sample ("EMEA leads every month") can leak information the viewer could not query, or simply be false for them. That is why outlines carry no numbers and SKILL.md asks for neutral framing; the judge's "no fabricated facts" criterion scores it. Also keep eval fixtures per role: the same case can have different expected chart ids for admin and analyst_emea. Gotcha: big number charts do not equal their rows For big_number, the rows are the trend series and the displayed number is an aggregation over it; MCP exposes it as headline (ChartData docstring in apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/chart/schemas.py). A metric binding to a big_number chart must tell the refresh API (Story 8) to compute the same aggregation, not to take the last row. Map metric to the numeric column but record viz_type in source so Story 1's refresh can apply the right rule. Gotcha: the planner's n_slides is not Presenton's n_slides Presenton may add a table of contents and treats include_title_slide separately. The plan path forces include_table_of_contents=False and counts the title slide as one of the plan's

docs.t: Story 8: Analytics refresh APIs, MCP catalog, user-context enforcement, CSP and cookies
docs.p: Story 8: Analytics refresh APIs and MCP
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: Reads: apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py, apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py, apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py, apache/superset: superset/config.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py · Builds on: Architecture and contracts, Story 5, Security, RLS, auth · Time: ~45 min Story 8 is the analytics-platform half of AI Slides. This chapter builds the Superset-side ai_slides blueprint: the handoff that turns a Superset browser session into a signed assertion and a short-lived data token, the JWKS that Presenton and the MCP service verify those tokens against, a decorator that runs each Bearer request as the token's Superset user, the batch refresh API that re-executes saved charts through Superset's own chart-data command (so RBAC and row-level security apply unchanged), and the catalog that tells the planner which charts can be refreshed at all. It then configures Superset's MCP service so the harness acts as the same user, and sets the Content Security Policy and cookie attributes that the embedded iframe from Story 5 needs. Code marked new is written by the team in a Python package installed into the Superset image, ai_slides_superset (the same package that holds the Story 5 host page). Every Superset function it calls is cited from apache/superset master (2026-11-02); differences from the 6.1.0 release are flagged where the source or UPDATING.md shows them.

docs.p: Story 8: Analytics refresh APIs and MCP
docs.b: Part VIII: AI Slides delivery plan
docs.x: # Story What it does Owner 8 [Analytics BE/MCP] Refresh APIs, MCP catalog, user-context enforcement, CSP and cookies Lets Presenton and the harness discover and refresh Superset data per user, with RBAC enforcement and the iframe CSP and cookie settings. Nitesh Acceptance criteria: POST /api/v1/ai_slides/handoff returns {assertion, data_token, expires_in} only for an authenticated Superset browser session with a valid CSRF token and can_access on AISlides; it returns 401 for anonymous and 403 for users without the permission. GET /api/v1/ai_slides/.well-known/jwks.json publishes every active verification key with a stable kid; a key rotation needs no Presenton or harness deploy. Every Bearer endpoint rejects tokens with a wrong signature, aud, iss, expired exp or missing scope, and runs the request as exactly the user in sub. POST /api/v1/ai_slides/refresh accepts at most 25 items, returns one result per item in the contract shape, and returns forbidden (not data) for a chart the user cannot access. Row-level security filters for the user appear in the executed SQL. overrides (time_range, extra_filters) change the result; filters on columns that are not dataset columns are rejected. GET /api/v1/ai_slides/catalog lists only charts the user can access, marks unsupported visualization types (deck.gl, maps, multi-query) as not refreshable with a reason, and filters by dashboard and text. The harness, holding the user's data token, can call the read-only Superset MCP tools and list_refreshable_charts as that user, and cannot call any mutating tool. Superset can frame /ai-slides/ and nothing else can; Presenton responses carry frame-ancestors; cookies carry the attributes in Step 9. Integration tests (Superset pytest style) cover RLS on refresh, forbidden charts, overrides, token validation and the CSRF behavior.
