The six boxes in the diagram are not six objects. They are views over UDM fields, and every field is optional and target-neutral unless it was required in 1.2. Facet Already in gck.artifact/1 (1.0 to 1.2) Added in 1.3 Prototype evidence (383 layouts) Content heading, paragraph, list, callout, quote, divider, chart, metric, table, image, embed; marks bold, italic, code, link; tokens blocks code, math, diagram; marks underline, strike, math; "\n" as a hard line break; static binding source 4,041 blocks: paragraph 2,445, heading 783, image 607, chart 113, diagram 51, list 35, table 7 Sections id, title, kind, layoutHint, blocks role, level, summary, notes, ext 354 of 383 slides got a detected title Structure section and block order; heading levels 1 to 3; flat lists nested ListItem; Block.group (same id = one visual region) groups present in 310 slides (they are what Markdown drops) Semantics block types, callout.tone, metric.compare, tokens, binding definitions, parameters Block.role (subtitle, takeaway, kpi, caption, citation, label); diagramKind; sources plus TextSegment.cite; meta.audience roles inferred: label 750, kpi 600, subtitle 77, takeaway 5 Media image {prompt, url, alt}, embed image.kind (photo, icon, illustration, logo), image.caption, image.assetId, assets registry with attribution and a generated flag 607 images, icons and photos told apart by is_icon Metadata id, version, title, language, target, provenance profile, plannedFor, meta (description, tags, authors, timestamps, revision, classification, audience), generalized provenance every imported UDM carries provenance.importedFrom

Content is the block union plus RichText. Two content rules matter for every adapter: Marks are semantic, not styling. bold, italic, underline, strike, code, link and math say what the text means. Font family, size and color never enter the UDM. When Presenton text is read, marks are recorded only as differences from the element's own font (runsToRichText, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/from-presenton.mjs:29), so a slide title that is bold by template style does not carry a bold mark. Data lives in bindings. Chart, metric, table and embed blocks reference a bindingId; the values sit in Artifact.bindings (Step 10). The only number-bearing structure inside a block is the diagram block's items[].value and range, which Step 10 discusses as an open point. RichText is canonical: marks sorted in vocabulary order, no empty segments, bold and italic never covering boundary whitespace, and adjacent equal segments merged (normalizeRichText, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:49). The whitespace rule was forced by the conformance kit: Markdown cannot express ** bold**, so without it the round trip changed text.

A section is the unit an adapter paginates: one slide for Presenton, a titled region (an H2 boundary) for Tiptap, a row for a dashboard. The UDM never says which. role gives the section's purpose (title, agenda, content, summary, closing, appendix), level gives outline depth without nesting section objects, summary holds the short abstract (Presenton's per-slide outline Markdown), and notes holds non-body annotation (speaker notes on a slide, an aside in a document). An adapter whose manifest has features.notes: false drops notes and summary with a loss entry.

Structure is order plus three hints. Heading levels stay 1 to 3 (an adapter maps them: Tiptap writes H3 to H5 because H1 and H2 are the document title and section boundaries). ListItem is either a plain RichText or {text, children}; readers without nesting flatten. Block.group says that several blocks form one visual region, for example a card holding a heading, a price and a bullet list. Presenton's groups come from Template v2 group elements (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/walk.mjs:36-39), and a target that cannot show regions drops the group with a groups_dropped loss.

Block.role is the smallest useful vocabulary that survived the corpus: subtitle, takeaway, kpi, caption, citation and label. The Presenton reader infers roles from element names and font size (classifyText, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/from-presenton.mjs:45), and the inference is a heuristic measured only on the bundled templates. diagramKind is a neutral vocabulary for infographics (progress, gauge, timeline, process, steps, funnel, pyramid, cycle, matrix, hierarchy, comparison, other); the 27 Presenton infographic types map onto it (DIAGRAM_KIND, from-presenton.mjs:9-19) and the exact original type is kept in ext.

An image block keeps url, the generation prompt, alt (required), kind and caption. assetId points into Artifact.assets, a registry keyed by asset id that holds the MIME type, URL, optional hash and size, attribution and a generated flag, so that one picture used three times is stored once and its license travels with it. Video, audio and file attachments are deferred until a target needs them; they would arrive as a new media block in a minor bump.

Document identity and origin: id, version, profile, title, language, plannedFor, meta and provenance. Step 8 covers provenance. Presenton-only generation settings (tone, verbosity, table of contents, template id) are not metadata; they go to ext["presenton.slides"].

The UDM holds content and meaning. Each adapter keeps geometry and styling in its own host: positions, sizes, rotation, z-order, fonts, colors, fills, shadows and theme values (Presenton slides.ui and presentations.theme, the Tiptap host's CSS, a dashboard's position_json); data values of live sources (the binding store, resolved as the viewer); host ids, except as opaque values inside that adapter's ext bag. The prototype measured what this rule throws away on the Presenton side: 1,644 decorative images, 718 unnamed vectors, 39 decorative texts and 15 decorative vectors were skipped as non-content, and 3 empty text elements were ignored. None of them is lost on a Presenton round trip, because patch-mode serialization edits a copy of the original ui (PPT adapter, Step 9).

The production types replace gck/packages/protocol/src/artifact.ts from Part IX. They are the prototype's core/udm.ts merged with every 1.0 to 1.2 field the prototype left out for brevity (metric.compare, table.columns and maxRows, parameters, refresh, dataContext, and the full DataBinding with mapping and format). gck/packages/protocol/src/artifact.ts (new, protocol 1.3 UDM profile) The data module gains one source type, static, and one relaxation: a static binding has mapping: {}, because its payload is already in snapshot shape. gck/packages/protocol/src/data.ts (new, protocol 1.3 additions) Gotcha: the prototype's types are a subset tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm.ts:89 declares DataBinding as { kind, source } with no mapping, format, refresh or runtime state, and its MetricBlock has no compare; the fixtures even spell a live source as { type: "superset_chart", chartId: 42 } (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/fixtures.mjs), not Part IX's chart_id. That was enough to prove the content mapping, because the prototype covers only static data. Production code imports the types above, and the conformance kit's live-data fixtures use the real 1.1 source shapes.

The engine's models mirror the TypeScript field for field, camelCase included, with extra="forbid" (strict on write). This excerpt shows only what 1.3 changes in gck_engine/spec/artifact.py from Part IX Step 3. gck_engine/spec/artifact.py (new, protocol 1.3 excerpt) Artifact.ext and the other bags run through the same _check_ext with their own cap. Four engine invariants change or appear with these models (the invariant codes are Part IX's, Step 4): Code 1.2 behavior 1.3 behavior I6_MANIFEST_BLOCKS block types and Section.kind checked against the manifest block types, marks and chart kinds checked against the manifest; kind ignored I8_LAYOUT_HINT layoutHint must be in manifest.layoutCatalog ext[manifest.id].layout, when present, must be in the same manifest's layoutCatalog; an opaque membership check that names no target I10_ALLOWED_SOURCES only allowed Superset source types also rejects static in model output of a generate run; static is legal only from deserialize, fromHost or a user edit I17_EXT (new) n/a namespace pattern and size caps on every ext bag; the LLM never writes ext (it is excluded from build_response_schema) The prototype's structural validator checkUdm (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:147) enforces the field allowlists, id prefixes, duplicate ids, vocabularies and binding references, and it reported a valid UDM for 383 of 383 layouts. It does not enforce the ext size caps; that is new in production.

docs.t: Step 6: One canonical format: the field mapping
docs.x: This table is the contract between Part IX and Part X. Every Artifact 1.2 field appears once; nothing exists in two places. Artifact 1.2 UDM 1.3 Change Artifact.id (ULID) id unchanged pattern; deserializers mint a deterministic ULID-shaped id (Step 7) version version unchanged (gck.artifact/1) (none) profile new, "udm/1.3" title (required) title (optional) widening; the engine still always writes it language language unchanged target (required, closed union) plannedFor (optional, open) widening; target read as an alias and mapped through the registry sections sections unchanged bindings bindings unchanged; static source added provenance {runId, model?, createdAt, prompt} provenance {origin, runId?, model?, prompt?, createdAt?, importedFrom?} generalized; generated artifacts carry all four 1.2 fields plus origin: "generated" parameters, refresh, dataContext (1.1) same unchanged (none) meta, assets, sources, ext new Section.id, title, blocks same unchanged Section.kind (required) kind (optional, deprecated) engine writes "section"; adapters ignore it Section.layoutHint ext["<adapter-id>"].layout moved; read as alias (engine-only SPEAKER_NOTE) Section.notes moved into the IR (none) Section.role, level, summary, ext new Block.id, type same unchanged (none) Block.role, group, ext new heading, paragraph, callout, divider, embed same unchanged list.items: RichText[] items: ListItem[] widening; a flat 1.2 list is a valid 1.3 list quote {text} quote {text, attribution?} additive chart {bindingId, chartType, title?} + axes?, caption?; chartType + bubble additive metric {bindingId, label, compare?} same unchanged table {bindingId, columns?, maxRows?} + caption? additive image {prompt?, url?, alt} + kind?, caption?, assetId? additive (none) code, math, diagram blocks new Mark bold, italic, code, link + underline, strike, math additive TextSegment {text, marks, href, token} + cite? additive TargetManifest AdapterManifest superset; see Adding any new target ArtifactDiff, BlockDiff UdmDiff one name engine TARGET_REFRESH[target] manifest.defaultRefresh moved out of the engine Readers apply the aliases once, at the edge, so the rest of the code sees only 1.3 fields: gck/packages/protocol/src/compat.ts (new) The same function exists in Python (gck_engine/spec/compat.py) and both are tested against one shared fixture folder of 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 artifacts, the way Part IX tests

Id Pattern Generated artifact Deserialized document Survives a round trip through Artifact.id ^art_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$ engine, ULID at run.started deterministic hash of the native identity (deck id, or template and slide keys) Tiptap (stored in the section boundary's udmMeta.artifact) Section.id ^sec_[a-z0-9]{4,24}$ engine stamp hash of the slide id, or index and layout (from-presenton.mjs:74-75) Tiptap (udmId on the boundary node) Block.id ^blk_[a-z0-9]{4,24}$ engine stamp hash of the slide key and element path (from-presenton.mjs:105) Tiptap (udmId on every top-level node) Block.group ^grp_[a-z0-9]{4,24}$ (new) engine, when it plans a region hash of the slide key and group path (from-presenton.mjs:109) Tiptap (udmGroup) binding key ^b_[a-z0-9_]{1,48}$ engine, from the data catalog hash of the slide key and element path (from-presenton.mjs:128, :136) Tiptap (dataBlock.bindingId, table udmMeta) asset id ^ast_[a-z0-9]{4,24}$ (proposed) engine or host upload content hash targets with assets support Three rules keep ids useful: deserialize is pure, so its ids are deterministic. No clock, no randomness: converting the same deck twice gives the same ids, which is what lets a document edit find its slide again and what makes golden files possible. The prototype hashes with 32-bit FNV-1a and writes 7 base36 characters (hashId, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:19), which yields ids like art_1acm3z3. That fits the section and block patterns but not the artifact's ULID pattern, and 32 bits can collide in a large workspace. Production uses a 128-bit hash (sha256 truncated) rendered as 26 Crockford base32 characters for artifact ids and as 16 base36 characters for the others; checkUdm already rejects duplicate ids, so a collision fails loudly. The LLM never writes ids (Part IX, unchanged). An edit run receives existing ids and must return them. Id survival is a declared capability. manifest.features.ids says whether ids survive serialize then deserialize. The conformance kit compares ids only for adapters that declare it. Tiptap's page profile does; Markdown and a StarterKit-only editor do not, and for those the reverse direction is positional (PPT adapter, Step 9).

provenance answers where the whole document came from. A deck read from Presenton: tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/2-udm.json (excerpt) nativeRef (the presentation id) is added when the deck has one; the corpus slides come from template files and have none. A hand-written Tiptap page gets "importedFrom": {"adapter": "tiptap", "adapterVersion": "0.1.0"} (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/doc-to-slides/2-udm.json). When a run edits an imported document, stamp sets origin: "edited", adds runId, model and prompt, and keeps importedFrom. Per-block origin is target-specific, so it is not a core field. The Presenton adapter records it in its own bag on every block, and that is what lets an edit in a document land in the right slide slot: tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/2-udm.json (excerpt) The section carries the layout and the title slot in the same namespace: tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/2-udm.json (excerpt) Two production adjustments: the layout key is spelled layout (the name I8_LAYOUT_HINT reads; the prototype used layoutId), and slot paths become RFC 6901 pointers (/components/2/elements/0/children/0/children/2) so they equal the element_path that Part VIII's slide_data_bindings rows already store (Story 1). Per-block slots replace the section-level slots map an earlier draft proposed, because a per-block bag survives reordering and Tiptap stores it on the node it belongs to.

ext is the only place target data may live. It exists on the artifact, on sections and on blocks, never on text segments (that keeps RichText small and canonical). Rule Enforced by 1. An adapter reads and writes only ext[manifest.id]. conformance check C11 (isolation) 2. An adapter with features.extPassThrough carries every other namespace through serialize then deserialize unchanged; one without it gets foreign namespaces removed by negotiate, with an ext_dropped loss per bag. negotiate rule 1; C11 (pass-through) 3. The engine never interprets ext (its only access is the opaque I8_LAYOUT_HINT membership check), the LLM never writes it, and stamp copies it from the base artifact on edit. build_response_schema excludes it; I17_EXT 4. Nothing in ext may change meaning: removing every bag leaves a valid, renderable UDM. Content always lives in core fields. C8 (deserialized UDM is valid and neutral) 5. Size caps: 4 KB per block, 16 KB per section, 64 KB per artifact, so ext cannot become a shadow document. I17_EXT (new; not enforced by the prototype) Rule 2 is what makes Presenton to Tiptap to Presenton exact. The Tiptap page profile stores each node's bags in a udmExt global attribute, so presenton.slides provenance survives a trip through the editor; the corpus run reports a byte-identical ui for 383 of 383 layouts through Tiptap. Markdown has nowhere to put the bags, so negotiation drops them and reports it: the simple-cards-with-list loss file lists six ext_dropped entries for Markdown and none for Tiptap (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/5-loss.json). The shared fixture kitchen-sink carries a foreign acme.crm namespace precisely to prove that adapters which have never heard of it still pass it through.

docs.t: Step 10: Data bindings and number tokens
docs.x: Part IX's data model is unchanged: blocks reference bindings by key, a binding is a definition (kind, source, mapping, format, params, refresh) plus runtime state (snapshot, snapshotAt, status, error) that lives in the binding store and is resolved as the viewer, and tokens are the only way a number enters prose. Two things are new.

An imported deck has charts whose numbers were written by an LLM at generation time, and a person can type a table into a document. Those numbers have no Superset query behind them. Three options were considered: Option Why it was rejected or chosen inline categories and series on the chart block rejected: a second data path that bypasses resolveToken and invites the model to write numbers drop the numbers on import rejected: the deck would lose its charts source.type: "static" whose payload is a snapshot chosen: one data path, existing snapshot shapes, existing adapters The chart from the chart-and-table example, read from a Presenton chart element: tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/chart-and-table/2-udm.json (excerpt) And the table a person typed into a Tiptap page, which is origin: "user": tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/doc-to-slides/2-udm.json (excerpt) Rules for static bindings: data uses the normative snapshot shapes (ChartSnapshot, TableSnapshot, MetricSnapshot) without meta. Imported table cells are strings exactly as they appeared ("10K+", "$1.2M"); coltypes is omitted because the reader cannot know the type. mapping is {}. The binding store treats a static binding as permanently resolved: withBindingState sets snapshot = source.data and status = "ok", with no snapshotAt. Views show a "Static data" badge, never "Data as of", and refresh modes ignore it. I10_ALLOWED_SOURCES rejects static in the output of a generate run, so the model still cannot invent numbers. An edit run may offer "make this live" by replacing the source with a catalog candidate of the same kind. An older reader that does not know static marks the binding error with source_unsupported and renders the block's fallback (Part IX 2.4). In the prototype, the 113 corpus charts and 7 tables kept their categories, series and cells exactly through every target that can show them; Markdown renders a static chart as a GFM table and the Presenton reader finds the chart slot again by shape (PPT adapter, Step 9).

docs.t: 10.2 Tokens, live data and imported prose
docs.x: Token grammar and resolution are Part IX's (2.2): value, previous, delta, delta_pct for metrics; total:, last:, max:, argmax:, last_category for charts; cell: and row_count for tables; period for any kind. Token text is blanked by the engine and persisted as "", and every adapter renders through resolveToken. A token may reference a static binding; it then resolves from source.data. Imported prose is not tokenized. A Presenton card that says "$1 / Month" stays a text segment with digits in it. The deserializer does not guess which digits are data, because a wrong guess would turn a sentence into a live number. I5_NUMBERS_IN_TOKENS on imported or user-authored text is therefore a warning, exactly as Part IX already treats user text in edit intents. Live bindings survive every adapter as definitions only. The Tiptap page profile stores the definition in the dataBlock node's binding attribute; the Presenton adapter turns definitions back into slide_data_bindings rows (PPT adapter, Step 4.4). The prototype does not cover live tokens or the binding store; the conformance kit has live-binding fixtures, but no live data was resolved. Gotcha: diagram values are numbers outside bindings A diagram block stores range.value (a progress bar's 96 out of 100) and items[].value inline, because Presenton's infographic data holds them inline and the structure (labels, order, hierarchy) is the content. That is acceptable for imported and user-authored diagrams, but a model-generated diagram must not carry invented numbers. Until a bindingId on diagram is designed, I5 treats range and items[].value like prose digits: allowed from deserialize and user edits, rejected in generate output.

The UDM evolves under Part IX's rules (2.4), plus one consequence of the generic design: Change How new optional field, mark, token grammar, source.type minor bump of gck.artifact/1 (1.4, 1.5, ...) new block type minor bump and a fallback chain in core negotiate, so every existing adapter degrades it deterministically without a code change new adapter (a module) no protocol change at all; register the adapter new diagramKind, BlockRole or SectionRole value minor bump; negotiation maps unknown values to other, no role, and content respectively rename or remove, change a meaning gck.artifact/2 plus upgrade_1_to_2 The block-type row is the one place where a UDM change touches the core: the fallback chain belongs to the block, not to any target. The prototype's chains (DEGRADE, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/negotiate.mjs:15) are, for example, chart to table (from static data, title and axes kept as the caption) to list to paragraph, and callout to quote with a bold "Note:" label to paragraph. Two candidates for the next minor bump came out of the corpus run: highlight mark. 44 Presenton text elements use a second color or size inside one element. RichText has no mark for that, so an edit to one of those elements flattens it to the slot's base style (0 of 44 kept). A neutral highlight mark (meaning "emphasized by color", with the color itself left to the host) would close the gap. Not in the prototype. math on Tiptap. The math mark and block exist in 1.3, and Presenton carries LaTeX as latex runs, but the Tiptap page profile maps math to the code mark until @tiptap/extension-mathematics is added. The corpus has no LaTeX, so this path is checked only by the shared fixtures.

docs.t: Step 12: A worked example from slide to UDM
docs.x: The chart-and-table example is the modern template's title_description_chart_table layout. The UDM the prototype produced has one section with the title "Company Traction", three blocks in reading order (a line chart, a paragraph and a table), two static bindings and the Presenton provenance: tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/chart-and-table/2-udm.json (excerpt) (The paragraph text is shortened here.) Everything about the slide's look (the 1280 by 720 canvas, fonts, the chart's colors and legend, the card backgrounds) stayed in slides.ui. Negotiating this UDM for Tiptap produced no loss entries; for Markdown it produced one block_degraded (chart to table) and five ext_dropped entries plus a section_role_dropped (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/chart-and-table/5-loss.json). After an edit in the Tiptap document (one bold run in the paragraph, doubled values in the first series), the Presenton serializer rewrote exactly two slots, the chart and the paragraph, and left two unchanged (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/chart-and-table/8-edit-result.json).

Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/walk.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/from-presenton.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/to-presenton.mjs · Builds on: Unified Document Model, From template to schema to slide · Time: ~60 min

This chapter builds presenton.slides, the first adapter of the generic contract: Presenton slide JSON in, a UDM out (the deserializer), and a UDM back into Presenton slides (the serializer). You will see which of the three JSON layers that hold a slide's content the adapter reads and writes, how a Template v2 ui tree is walked into reading order, how headings, roles and element types are detected, and how a UDM section returns to a slide in two modes: patch (an existing slide, slot by slot, everything unchanged left byte-identical) and content (a new slide, with layout selection reused from Presenton's structure step, slots filled by element name and hydration through Presenton's own templates/v2/content.py). The chapter ends with Smart HTML slides, what stays Presenton-only, and the file-by-file port from the prototype to production. Code is the prototype's, adapted, and every Presenton function it calls is cited by path:line. Nothing in this adapter is special to Tiptap: the same UDM goes to Markdown or any later module.

"Presenton already deals with JSON" is true, but a deck's slide content lives in three JSON layers (the Feasibility analysis counts four forms, adding the outline, which the adapter reads only as Section.summary), and only one of them is safe to read. Layer Where Shape Role for the adapter slides.content servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:26 object keyed by component key, then element name, shaped by the layout's content schema (get_template_schema, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257) written in content mode (new slides); never read, because it goes stale slides.ui servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:30 the hydrated Template v2 layout tree: components, elements, positions, runs read by the deserializer; written in patch mode editor Deck adaptGeneratedTemplateV2PresentationToDeck, servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/importing/template-v2-import.ts:135 the Konva editor's view model untouched; it keeps adapting ui exactly as today ui is the source of truth after generation. The canvas editor writes ui through PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2585), and the chat tools edit ui directly, so content can describe text the user already changed. The deserializer therefore reads ui, plus speaker_note (slide.py:28) and the deck's outline. Smart-mode slides carry an HTML string in html_content (slide.py:27) instead of a ui tree (Step 10). Version 1 decks are refused by the frontend and need no support. The existing "presentation adapter" the team refers to, template-v2-import.ts, adapts ui into the editor's model. It stays as it is. The UDM adapter sits next to it and converts ui into a target-neutral document; the two never call each other.

docs.t: Step 2: The adapter at a glance
docs.x: The prototype adapter is four files and 590 lines of code: walk.mjs (tree walker), from-presenton.mjs (deserializer), to-presenton.mjs (serializer and validator) and index.mjs (manifest). Its manifest (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/index.mjs:11-22) declares what a Template v2 slide can hold natively; everything else is degraded by the core negotiate before serialize sees it. The production manifest adds the live-data and metric capabilities that Part IX's slides target already had: gck/adapters/presenton-slides/src/manifest.ts (new) Three declarations carry most of the design: orderPreserved: false: a layout decides where blocks go, so the conformance kit compares this adapter's round trip as a multiset of blocks, not a sequence. ids: false and extPassThrough: false: Template v2 elements have no place for UDM ids or other adapters' bags. Ids are re-derived on every read (deterministically, see Unified Document Model, Step 7), and the adapter's own provenance lives in ui itself (the slot path is where the content is). liveData.tokensInText: "snapshot": a token in a text slot is written once with an "(as of ...)" stamp until Part VIII gains text bindings (Part IX, Step 7.6). negotiate applies that rule generically from the manifest. limits.maxBlocksPerSection is a production addition (the prototype had none); 12 is a starting value, not a measured one. The codec is TypeScript. Code titles in this chapter use the Part IX package path gck/adapters/presenton-slides/; the first delivery places the same files in servers/nextjs/lib/udm/adapters/presenton-slides/ and moves them into the package later (Code changes in Presenton, Step 4; Plan and tracker, work package F1). It runs in the browser and in the Next.js server's Node runtime, the same places the Tiptap adapter runs. FastAPI does not run the codec; it supplies inputs (slides, layouts, binding rows) and applies outputs through its existing hydrator. That split follows from the Tiptap research: Tiptap's schema check and @tiptap/html are JavaScript-only, so conversions between two targets must happen in TypeScript anyway.

docs.t: Step 3: Deserializer, part 1: walking the ui tree
docs.x: A Template v2 slide is a 1280 by 720 canvas. Components have positions; elements are positioned relative to their parent; group children are absolutely positioned inside the group; flex and grid children usually have no position and are laid out by flow. The walker computes an absolute box for every content leaf and then orders leaves for reading. tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/walk.mjs (excerpt, lines 29-55) Four decisions are encoded here: What is content. A leaf is content when its type is one of text, text-list, table, chart, image, infographic or math and it is not decorative: true (isContent, walk.mjs:13-17). That is Presenton's own rule for what becomes a schema field (CONTENT_TYPES, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:15, and _is_editable_element, schema.py:53), plus math. Vectors, SVGs and containers are never content. Groups are regions. The innermost group path becomes the UDM group of every leaf inside it, which is how a card's heading, price and bullet list stay together. Flow is approximated. flowPositions (walk.mjs:91-121) lays out flex rows and columns (with wrap and gaps) and grid cells, using each child's size. The approximation only needs to be good enough to order leaves; flex and grid children keep their index order regardless. Reading order is a recursive XY-cut. xyCut (walk.mjs:124-142) splits a set of boxes by horizontal whitespace bands first, then by vertical gutters, and falls back to top-then-left. It runs over components and over unordered groups, so a two-column slide reads the left column before the right one. Every leaf keeps its path (for example components.2.elements.0.children.0.children.2). In production the path is written as an RFC 6901 pointer (/components/2/elements/0/children/0/children/2), the same element_path that Part VIII's slide_data_bindings rows store (Story 1), so a slot path and a binding row can be compared directly. Gotcha: the renderer knows types the Pydantic model does not The HTML renderer accepts svg, list-view and grid-view (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:321, :334, :337), and the hydrator writes a math element (presentation.py:913), but none of them is in the SlideElement union (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:624). The walker accepts all four. Do not validate ui with SlideLayout.model_validate before deserializing; it would reject real slides.

Template v2 element UDM block Data Corpus count text (elements.py:203) heading or paragraph, possibly with a role; or the section title runs to RichText 3,582 elements: 354 titles, 783 headings, 2,445 paragraphs text-list (elements.py:265) list, ordered when marker == "number" each item's runs to RichText 35 table (elements.py:302) table static binding: header columns and rows, cell text from runs 7 chart (elements.py:361) chart with chartType, title, axes, caption from source static binding: categories, series (or a live binding, 4.4) 113 image (elements.py:240) image, kind: "icon" when is_icon, else "photo"; url from data, prompt none 607 infographic (elements.py:549) diagram with a neutral diagramKind, items, range inline items; extra fields to ext 51 math (hydrated, not modeled) math latex 0 in the corpus decorative leaves, vector, svg none none skipped: 1,644 decorative images, 718 unnamed vectors, 39 decorative texts, 15 decorative vectors Every content element in the corpus was represented: 3,582 of 3,582 text, 607 of 607 images, 113 charts, 51 infographics, 35 lists and 7 tables. Three text elements were empty and produced no block.

docs.t: 4.2 Marks as differences from the slot's font
docs.x: Template v2 text is a list of runs, each with a font (TextRun, elements.py:181; LatexTextRun, elements.py:193). The UDM must not learn that a title is bold because its template made it bold, so marks are recorded only where a run differs from the element's own font: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/from-presenton.mjs (lines 29-39) Paragraph breaks inside an element are "\n" in run text, which the UDM keeps as a hard line break. Run-level color and size are not marks. The corpus has 44 text elements that use a second color or size inside one element; they read correctly, but an edit to one of them flattens it to the slot's base style on the way back (Step 8). A neutral highlight mark would fix that (Unified Document Model, Step 11).

docs.t: 4.3 Headings, roles and the section title
docs.x: Template v2 has no heading level. Heading-ness is inferred from the element name (snake_case and semantic in every bundled template) and from font size relative to the slide's median body size: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/from-presenton.mjs (lines 23-26 and 45-54) The section title is the largest ungrouped heading; when a slide has none, the largest ungrouped text of at least 28 px that has no role (from-presenton.mjs:84-88). It is removed from the blocks and stored as Section.title, and its path is kept as titleSlot in the section's ext. Headings inside a group get level 2, others level 1. The section role comes from layout id tokens (agenda, toc, closing, thank, cover, title_slide; sectionRole, from-presenton.mjs:56-62), defaulting to content. On the corpus this found a title for 354 of 383 slides and assigned roles label 750, kpi 600, subtitle 77 and takeaway 5. These are heuristics measured only on the 16 bundled templates; a custom template imported from a PPTX file (convert_pptx_to_json, servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:687) may use names the word lists do not know. That only lowers semantic quality (a heading becomes a paragraph); it never loses content, and it does not affect the round trip, which goes by slot.

docs.t: 4.4 Data: static values and live bindings
docs.x: A chart's categories and series, and a table's cell text, become static bindings keyed by a hash of the slide and element path (from-presenton.mjs:127-145). The prototype stops there. Production must also read Part VIII's slide_data_bindings rows, because a chart generated against Superset data is a live binding whose values in ui are only the last snapshot. A row matches a leaf when its element_path equals the leaf's pointer (or, for repeated metric grids, by element_name plus element_index): gck/adapters/presenton-slides/src/deserialize/bindings.ts (new) A row of kind metric is bound to a text element, so that leaf becomes a metric block instead of a kpi paragraph, with label taken from the element name (card_large_value becomes "card large value") until a better label source is designed. The row's snapshot, status and error are runtime state and go to the binding store, never into the UDM.

speaker_note becomes Section.notes and the slide's outline Markdown (from presentations.outlines, servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:51) becomes Section.summary. Infographic fields that have no neutral meaning (gantt columns and rows, matrix criteria, colors) are kept in ext["presenton.slides"].data with a diagram_extra_to_ext loss, so a Presenton round trip restores them and other targets ignore them (from-presenton.mjs:166-168).

docs.t: Step 5: Deserializer, part 3: provenance in ext
docs.x: Every block records where it came from, in the adapter's own namespace: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/from-presenton.mjs (lines 90-106, excerpt) ext["presenton.slides"] key On Used by templateId, layout (prototype: layoutId) section patch mode (which layout); content mode skips layout selection when present slideId section patch mode (which row in slides) titleSlot section where Section.title goes back slot, name, element block slot lookup, pass 1 (Step 8); content mode matches name against the chosen layout infographicType, data diagram block restoring the exact infographic templateId, settings (tone, verbosity, table of contents) artifact regeneration with the deck's own settings These bags reach Tiptap and come back because the Tiptap page profile stores them in udmExt (Tiptap adapter). That is the whole reason the Presenton to Tiptap to Presenton round trip is exact for 383 of 383 layouts while the same trip through Markdown is not (Step 8).

serialize receives a UDM that negotiate has already reduced to the manifest. For each section it decides how the section reaches Presenton: Mode When Native output Applied through patch the section's ext has a slideId that exists in the deck and the slide has a ui the slide's ui with only changed slots rewritten, plus speaker_note and binding row changes new apply service behind PUT /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/udm and POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/slides/apply, with the patch guard (Step 8) content no linked slide (a document became slides, a new section was added, or the user asked to re-layout) layoutId plus content JSON keyed like get_template_schema, plus binding rows the same apply service, hydrated by _apply_template_content_to_ui (presentation.py:575) smart patch the linked slide is a Smart HTML slide edited html_content Step 10 gck/adapters/presenton-slides/src/serialize/index.ts (new) Both modes obey the rules that Part IX found for Template v2 (Artifact Spec and targets, Step 7): never leave a slot holding the template's sample content, clip to every maximum the adapter itself writes, warn on every minimum it cannot meet, never pad.

docs.t: Step 7: Layout selection, reused from the structure step
docs.x: A section that came from a document has no layout. Presenton already has a step that picks one: generate_presentation_structure (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:157) takes a PresentationOutlineModel (one Markdown string per slide, servers/fastapi/models/presentation_outline_model.py:24) and the template's PresentationLayoutModel (built by _build_template_layout_model, presentation.py:410) and returns one layout index per slide. The generation pipeline calls it at presentation.py:2895, or uses the template's fixed order when layout_model.ordered is set. The adapter reuses that step instead of writing a second layout picker, in three stages that run before serialize, so serialize stays pure: Provenance. A section with ext["presenton.slides"].layout keeps its layout (I8_LAYOUT_HINT checks it exists in the catalog). Structure step. The remaining sections are written as an outline with the registered markdown adapter on the TypeScript side (one section, one Markdown string; the same registry any conversion uses), sent with the apply request, and passed to generate_presentation_structure. This keeps Presenton's prompt, its instructions handling and its model configuration. Capacity check, then deterministic fallback. The structure step chooses by layout description, not by slot capacity, so its answer is checked against the hard rule from Part IX: the layout's chart and table slot counts must equal the section's chart and table blocks, or the template's sample chart shows through. A layout that fails, and every section when no LLM is configured, goes to the deterministic picker. servers/fastapi/services/udm/layouts.py (new) The deterministic picker is the prototype's chooseLayout (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/to-presenton.mjs:43-59): it reads every layout's own sample content as a UDM, compares block-type counts, charges 10 per missing or spare chart, table or diagram slot, 3 per missing other slot and 1 per spare one, and subtracts 2 when the section has a title and the layout does not (or the reverse). Ties keep the first layout, so the result is stable. In production it is merged with Part IX's score (chooseLayout, Part IX Step 7.2), which adds the metric-grid rule and the image-placeholder penalty. How good is a content-only choice? The prototype measured it by throwing away the layout id and asking the picker

docs.t: Step 8: Patch mode: an existing slide, slot by slot
docs.x: Patch mode is the prototype's serializer, and it is what made the round trip exact. The steps are in udmToPresenton (to-presenton.mjs:66-144). 1. Start from the slide as it is. Copy its ui, deserialize the same ui to get the base blocks, and index the base by slot. Gotcha: the prototype patches the layout, production patches the slide The prototype clones the catalog layout (const ui = clone(layout), to-presenton.mjs:76) and compares against the layout's own content (baseOf, to-presenton.mjs:37-40). That equals the slide only because every corpus slide is a layout with its sample content. Production clones the current slides.ui and builds the base by deserializing that same ui, so "unchanged" means unchanged since the user last saved, and any manual geometry edits in the canvas editor survive. 2. Map blocks to slots, in four passes, each taking only free slots (to-presenton.mjs:99-120): Pass Rule Why 1 the block's own provenance slot (ext.slot), if the element type still fits exact return for every target that kept ext 1b a table block to a table or chart slot of exactly the same shape a chart that Markdown turned into a table finds its chart slot again 2 the next free slot whose base block has the same type, in reading order positional fallback for targets without ext 3 any compatible slot (SLOT_TYPES, to-presenton.mjs:9-12) last resort, reported as block_retyped 3. Write only what changed. A block whose content equals its base block (ids, ext, group and role ignored; static data resolved) leaves the slot untouched, byte for byte: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/presenton/to-presenton.mjs (lines 30-33 and 121-131) A changed text slot is rewritten from the slot's first run's font, with marks applied on top of the element's own font (runsFrom and writeText, to-presenton.mjs:146-165); a mark the slot's style already has is reported as mark_absorbed_by_slot_style. Lists, tables, charts, images and diagrams write their own fields (writeBlock, to-presenton.mjs:167-235), and chart writes keep chart_type, title, axis titles and the source caption. 4. Clear what no block claimed. A slot that held content but received no block is blanked: text gets a single space, lists and table rows are emptied, charts lose their categories and series (blankSlot, to-presenton.mjs:237-243). Images and infographics keep their asset. A single space is deliberate: Presenton's text

docs.t: Step 9: Content mode: a new slide, filled by element name
docs.x: Content mode produces exactly what Presenton's own generation produces at presentation.py:2370-2396: a layout id and a content object, which _apply_template_content_to_ui turns into a ui. Doing it this way means repeated cards, the centering of fewer items than template children (repeated_child_source_index, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py:43-54), Markdown emphasis and image fitting all behave exactly as in a generated deck. The content object's shape comes from the layout's content schema: the top-level key is the component key (component id, deduplicated by _template_component_content_keys, presentation.py:538-572), then one property per editable element name, and a repeated flex, grid or group becomes an array of item objects (_array_schema_for_repeated_children, schema.py:426). The prototype never produced content JSON (it wrote ui directly and could not add or remove cards). Production adapts Part IX's fillSection (Step 7.3) with one new first pass, matching by element name: gck/adapters/presenton-slides/src/serialize/content.ts (new, excerpt) Text crosses the hydrator as Markdown. Presenton parses only ** and __ (bold) and * and _ (italic) (_template_text_runs_from_markdown, presentation.py:1157, and _parse_template_markdown_text, :1224), plus LaTeX tags that parse_latex_tags recognizes. So in content mode underline is dropped with a mark_dropped loss (patch mode keeps it, because it writes runs). Text longer than a slot's maxLength is clipped at a word boundary with an ellipsis and a text_clipped loss whose droppedText holds the cut, which keeps the conformance kit's "no silent text loss" check true. Patch mode never clips user text; it reports max_length warnings from validateNative instead (the scripted edit produced 2,477 such warnings because it appended 9 characters to every slot). Fitting edited text to a slot is the slide editor's decision, not the adapter's. The doc-to-slides example shows the behavior on a hand-written page with no UDM attributes. The deterministic picker chose General's title_table_description for a section holding a paragraph, a three-item bullet list and a table. That layout has no list slot, so the list was reported, not hidden: tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/doc-to-slides/4-report.json In production the 34-character title would be clipped (content mode), and the no_slot loss is the cue for the UI to offer

Smart mode stores no ui tree. Each slide is a complete HTML string in slides.html_content, normalized by normalize_smart_slide_html (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py:417): scripts are stripped except inline Chart.js initializers that pass the safety checks (_sanitize_script, :378), event handlers and javascript: URLs are removed, and the root must be a 1280 by 720 section. content holds only {"title"} (presentation.py:2060-2067). None of this was prototyped; the design below reuses the patch idea with DOM paths in place of ui paths. Deserialize. Parse html_content with an HTML parser in Node (no script execution) and map elements in document order: h1 to h6 to headings (the first h1 or largest heading becomes Section.title), p to paragraphs, ul and ol to lists with nesting, table to a static table, img to an image (src, alt), blockquote to a quote; strong, em, u, s, code and a to marks. Each block records ext["presenton.slides"].dom (an element path such as section>div:2>ul:0) and the slide's htmlSha256. A canvas with a Chart.js initializer is not parsed: its data is inside a script, and the adapter never evaluates scripts. It produces a smart_chart_opaque loss and no block, so a Smart slide's charts do not reach other targets. Serialize (smart patch). If the HTML's hash still matches, rewrite only the text of elements whose blocks changed, at their DOM paths, keeping tags and classes; add or remove list items by cloning a sibling li, the way the hydrator clones repeated children. Structural changes the DOM path cannot express (a new table, a new chart) are not written; they produce a smart_structure_unsupported loss, and the UI offers Presenton's own LLM edit, POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit-html (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:135-170), with an instruction built from the section's Markdown. That call is non-deterministic and is never made by serialize; it is a user action. The rewritten HTML must pass normalize_smart_slide_html again before it is saved. Until this is built and measured, the manifest stays as above and Smart sections are handled read-only: deserialize works, serialize returns the slide unchanged with a loss entry when the section changed.

The UDM carries content and meaning; everything below stays in Presenton, in the place it already lives. "In ext" means kept in the adapter's bag only so that a Presenton round trip can restore it. Presenton data Stays in In the UDM positions, sizes, rotation, flips, z-order slides.ui no fonts, colors, fills, strokes, shadows, opacity, alignment slides.ui, presentations.theme, presentations.fonts no; only marks that differ from the element font decorative images, vectors, SVGs, backgrounds slides.ui no (skipped, counted) flex, grid and group arrangement, gaps, padding slides.ui only as group and reading order chart colors, legend, axis and grid flags, data labels slides.ui no; chartType, title, axis titles and source caption are image fit, crop, focus, clip path, icon_type slides.ui no; url, prompt and kind are table cell fills, borders, per-cell fonts slides.ui no; cell text is infographic visual type and extra data slides.ui diagramKind and items; exact type and extras in ext slot limits (max_length, min_items, ...) the layout no; used by validateNative and content mode template id, layout id, slide id, slot paths slides.layout_group, slides.layout, slides.id in ext tone, verbosity, instructions, table of contents presentations columns in artifact ext outline per slide presentations.outlines Section.summary speaker note slides.speaker_note Section.notes live chart, metric and table definitions slide_data_bindings bindings (definitions only) Export is unchanged. A .pptx or PDF is still made by Presenton's DOM-based export from slides.ui (export_presentation, servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:43); the "PPT serializer" in the team's diagram is this adapter plus that export, not a new PPTX writer.

validateNative checks what Presenton would accept, and reports slot limits as warnings (validatePresenton, to-presenton.mjs:246-283): known element types, runs arrays with string text, list items as run arrays, table rows as wide as the header, chart series as finite numbers with one value per category, plus max_length and max_items warnings. It deliberately checks less than the Pydantic SlideElement union (see the gotcha in Step 3). On the corpus it found no errors in any serialized slide; the only findings were the 2,477 over-length warnings from the scripted edit. Production adds two server-side checks at the apply endpoint: assert_content_only_patch for patch mode (Step 8) and the layout id lookup for content mode. The conformance kit runs the adapter against the shared fixtures; the prototype passed 45 of 45 checks.

Reads: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/extensions.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/to-tiptap.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/from-tiptap.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/validate.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/, servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx, servers/nextjs/package.json, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts · Builds on: Unified Document Model, PPT adapter (Presenton JSON) · Time: ~60 min

This chapter is the Tiptap side of the Unified Document Model: how a UDM becomes tiptap.json and how a tiptap.json document, including one a person has edited or written from scratch, becomes a UDM again. The Tiptap adapter is the first implementation of the generic adapter contract described in Adding any new target; nothing in it is special-cased in the core. You will see the node and mark mapping for Tiptap v3.30.5 (the version Presenton ships), how the adapter derives its capabilities from the host editor's schema so it only emits nodes that editor has, the one custom node for charts, metrics, infographics, live tables and embeds with full Tiptap v3 extension code, stable block ids, validation with the real ProseMirror schema, the server-side conversion options, the reverse direction for edited documents, live data nodes, worked examples quoted from the prototype, and the prototype's measured results for this adapter. Code labeled "(prototype)" is quoted from tutorial/prototypes/udm/, which was run on all 383 bundled Presenton layouts. Code labeled "(new)" is proposed production code; the parts of it that were executed against Tiptap 3.30.5 while writing this chapter say so, and the rest is marked unverified. Production files use the layout of Code changes in Presenton (Step 4): the Tiptap codec lives in Next.js under servers/nextjs/lib/udm/, because that is the runtime that owns the real ProseMirror schema.

Presenton already uses Tiptap, but not as a page editor. It pins @tiptap/core, @tiptap/extension-underline, @tiptap/pm, @tiptap/react and @tiptap/starter-kit at 3.30.5 (servers/nextjs/package.json:40-44) and uses them to edit the text inside one slide element: TiptapInlineTextEditor turns StarterKit's block nodes off (headings, lists, blockquote, code block, horizontal rule; servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx:266-281), so a document is always doc > paragraph > (text | hardBreak | latexRun)*. Styling travels as a custom runStyle mark (TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx:49) and LaTeX as a custom inline atom latexRun (TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx:86). textRunsToTiptapContent (TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx:751) and tiptapContentToTextRuns (TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx:798) convert Presenton TextRun[] to and from that JSON. That is an inline-run profile: the same JSON format as a page, but a schema with almost nothing in it. A Tiptap page is a different schema profile of the same format: headings, lists, tables, images and data blocks. The adapter in this chapter is written for any profile. It is given an extension list (or a live editor), builds the schema, and derives from the schema what it can emit. The existing inline editor and its converters stay as they are: they edit styled runs inside one slot, which the UDM deliberately does not model (styling stays in the host).

Tiptap's JSON is ProseMirror's Node.toJSON(), typed as JSONContent in @tiptap/core: Four facts shape the adapter: The root is always { "type": "doc", "content": [...] } and doc requires at least one block. Formatting is marks on text nodes, not wrapper elements. An empty text node is illegal and makes Node.fromJSON throw. The schema decides what is valid. A node type the schema does not know throws Unknown node type. An attribute it does not know is silently dropped on load. A heading with level: 9 passes check() unless the attribute declares a validator. The editor's fallback for invalid content is not a partial repair. In Tiptap 3.30.5, a JSON document containing one unknown node is replaced by an empty paragraph as a whole, with or without enableContentCheck; in Node without a DOM that fallback path crashes. So the adapter validates its own output before any editor sees it, and never relies on the editor to clean up. These were observed by running 3.30.5 in Node for the Part X research, and the prototype's negative controls (Step 7) re-check them.

udmToTiptap (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/to-tiptap.mjs:12-35) emits a flat sequence of top-level nodes. Sections do not become wrapper nodes, because a flat document is what a person edits in Tiptap; instead, every section starts with a boundary node that carries the section's identity: UDM tiptap.json (page profile) Reverse (tiptapToUdm) title heading level 1 with udmKind: "doc-title" title; in a document without UDM attributes, an H1 as the very first node document id, provenance, meta, assets, sources, ext udmMeta.artifact on the first node restored from the first node titled section heading level 2 with udmKind: "section", udmId (the section id), udmMeta {role, level, summary}, udmExt new section; in a foreign document, every H2 (and every H1 after the first node) starts a section untitled section horizontalRule with udmKind: "section" new untitled section; in a foreign document, every bare horizontal rule starts one Section.notes blockquote with udmKind: "notes" at the end of the section notes of the current section heading level 1, 2, 3 heading level 3, 4, 5 level minus 2, clamped to 1 to 3 paragraph paragraph; a "\n" in text becomes hardBreak same; hardBreak becomes "\n" list bulletList or orderedList (start: 1) of listItem > paragraph, nested items as a nested bulletList same; a non-list block inside a list item is flattened to text with list_item_block_flattened quote blockquote > paragraph, udmKind: "quote", attribution in udmMeta same callout blockquote with udmKind: "callout" and udmMeta: {tone} callout with its tone divider horizontalRule with a udmId and no udmKind divider code codeBlock with language same table with static data table > tableRow > tableHeader / tableCell > paragraph; first row is the header; udmMeta: {bindingId, origin, caption} table plus a static binding; no header row gives table_no_header, uneven rows give table_ragged chart, diagram, metric, embed, live table dataBlock atom (Step 5) the block and its binding, restored from the node's attributes image image {src, alt, title}; kind, prompt, caption, assetId in udmMeta same math not in the page manifest: negotiation turns it into a paragraph with a math mark, then the mark into code paragraph with a code mark block id, group, role, ext udmId, udmGroup, udmRole, udmExt same unknown node (foreign document) n/a paragraph with its text and native_node_degraded Marks

docs.t: Step 4: Schema negotiation with the host editor
docs.x: The adapter never assumes which extensions the host has. createTiptapAdapter builds the schema with getSchema(extensions) (no DOM, no editor) and derives the manifest from it: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs (prototype, excerpt) The prototype registers the same code twice with two extension packs (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/extensions.mjs:52-54): Profile Extensions Derived capabilities tiptap (page) StarterKit, TableKit, Image, DataBlock, UdmAttrs every UDM block except math; all marks except math; ids, ext pass-through, notes, captions, groups, roles; patch tiptap.basic StarterKit only paragraph, heading, list, quote, code; six marks; no ids, no ext, no tables, images or data blocks The basic profile stands in for "somebody else's Tiptap app". Nothing in the adapter knows it is basic: negotiation reads its manifest and degrades. Over the 383-layout corpus that produced ext_dropped 4,807 times, block_degraded 891, section_role_dropped 383, groups_dropped 310 and roles_dropped 303, while the page profile produced no loss entries at all (tutorial/prototypes/udm/REPORT.md). Both profiles produced a valid document for 383/383 layouts. In production the host is a live editor, so the adapter should be built from it rather than from a list the integrator has to keep in sync: servers/nextjs/lib/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.ts (new, excerpt) createTiptapAdapterFromSchema(schema, id, overrides) is the prototype's createTiptapAdapter (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs:40-52) split so that it accepts a ready schema and lets the caller narrow the derived manifest. Gotcha: an allowed heading level is not the same as a node in the schema The prototype checks only that a heading node exists. Tiptap's Heading extension renders a level that is not in its levels option as the first allowed level (renderHTML in @tiptap/extension-heading, heading.ts:80-81 in 3.30.5), and the attribute has no validator, so check() accepts it. An editor configured with levels: [1, 2, 3] would load an H5 block heading and display it as an H1. The production derivation above reads the levels option; it has not been run.

Presenton slides carry charts, infographics (here called diagrams, with a neutral vocabulary: progress, gauge, timeline, process, funnel, matrix and so on) and KPI values. Part IX planned one custom Tiptap node per kind (gckChart, gckMetric, gckDataTable, gckEmbed; Artifact Spec and targets, Step 8). The prototype uses one node instead, dataBlock, whose kind attribute is the UDM block type. Adding a sixth kind of data block later is a UDM change and a renderer, not a new schema node that every editor holding old documents must also register. KPI values deserve a note. In Presenton slides, a KPI such as $1 / Month is a text element, so the Presenton adapter produces a paragraph with role: "kpi", not a metric block. It reaches Tiptap as a normal paragraph with udmRole: "kpi" and stays editable as text. The metric block is for a number that comes from a binding (a Superset metric, or a static value): that is what goes into a dataBlock.

tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/extensions.mjs (prototype, excerpt) It is enough for the corpus run: 113 charts and 51 infographics serialize, validate, load in an editor, and come back unchanged.

The production node adds what the prototype skipped: attribute validators, so node.check() rejects a bad kind, a malformed binding id, or a binding that carries runtime state; a renderHTML with a readable caption, so generateHTML produces something meaningful without a node view; and renderText, so copying the node as text gives a summary instead of nothing. servers/nextjs/lib/udm/adapters/tiptap/extensions.ts (new, DataBlock excerpt) A JavaScript copy of this node was run against Tiptap 3.30.5 in Node with getSchema([StarterKit, DataBlock]): a valid metric node passed nodeFromJSON().check(); kind: "infographic", bindingId: "Chart 1" and a binding with a snapshot field were each rejected by check() with the messages above; getText returned [metric: Active users]. The parseHTML and renderHTML paths need a DOM or @tiptap/html and were not exercised. Gotcha: an attribute validator only runs in check() ProseMirror runs attribute validate functions in Node.check() (prosemirror-model 1.25 calls checkAttrs there), not in nodeFromJSON. A document built with nodeFromJSON alone accepts any attribute value. The adapter's validateNative always calls both, and the editor runs check() when enableContentCheck is on.

The node view is editor-only: it never changes the JSON, generateHTML output or the static renderer. It picks a renderer by kind, and gets its data either from the node (static data) or from a live binding resolver (Step 10). The resolver is injected through a React context, because Presenton does not read live bindings into documents yet (Code changes in Presenton, exception E8); until it does, the default resolver returns nothing and every data block in a Presenton document is static. servers/nextjs/lib/udm/react/DataBlockView.tsx (new) The editor attaches it without changing the schema, as the document editor in Code changes in Presenton (Step 7.2) does: DataBlock.extend({ addNodeView: () => ReactNodeViewRenderer(DataBlockView) }). The node's name and attributes stay the same, so the manifest derived from the editor's schema equals the serializer's. DATA_BLOCK_RENDERERS (servers/nextjs/lib/udm/react/renderers.tsx, new) maps each kind to a component. For charts and infographics the natural renderers are the ones slides already use: the HTML renderer builds a Chart.js configuration in chartConfig (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:2261) and draws each infographic type with its own function (renderInfographic, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:1212). Both are module-private today, and Part VIII Story 4 already owns the chart rendering decision, so the node view follows that choice rather than making its own. This node view has not been rendered in a browser. Gotcha: every editor that opens the document must register the node A document saved with dataBlock nodes and opened in an editor without DataBlock is not partially loaded: in Tiptap 3.30.5 the whole document is replaced by an empty paragraph. Read-only viewers, server-side generateHTML and any second editor in the product need the extension too. Load DataBlock where there is no React and the extended node with DataBlockView in the browser; both have the same schema.

All of these were produced by the prototype's serializer (to-tiptap.mjs:73-76), from the Presenton corpus or from the shared fixtures. A line chart from the modern title_description_chart_table layout (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/chart-and-table/3-tiptap.json): tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/chart-and-table/3-tiptap.json (prototype, excerpt) A progress infographic from the mosaic hero_panel_with_progress_cards_6136 layout, part of a card (udmGroup), with the Presenton infographic type kept in ext only: dataBlock for a progress infographic (prototype output) A timeline infographic from the landmark branded_header_centered_title_connected_timeline_3792 layout (two of its five items shown): dataBlock for a timeline infographic (prototype output, excerpt) A metric and a live embed, from the kitchen-sink conformance fixture (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/fixtures.mjs:27, 40): dataBlock for a metric and a live embed (prototype output) The live embed holds only the definition (superset_chart, chart 42). No number from it is ever written into the document.

Ids are what let an edited page find its way back: the Presenton slot path rides in udmExt next to udmId, and the edit test in Step 9 depends on both surviving. The prototype adds six attributes to every top-level node type with one extension: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/extensions.mjs (prototype, excerpt) This is the same technique as Part IX's GckBlockIds (addGlobalAttributes with a null default, so documents without the attributes still load), widened from one id to the six UDM fields that have no StarterKit home. Each attribute is optional; the derived manifest turns ids, extPassThrough, groups, roles, notes, captions, callout, divider and patch on only when udmId is in the schema. Gotcha: splitting a paragraph duplicates its id and its slot Tiptap copies a node's attributes when the user presses Enter in the middle of it. Run against 3.30.5 with the prototype's page extensions, splitting "Hello world" (with udmId: "blk_a" and a Presenton slot in udmExt) produced two paragraphs that both carry blk_a and the same slot, and the deserialized UDM failed checkUdm with dup_id. Declaring the attributes with keepOnSplit: false fixed only the case where Enter is pressed at the end of the paragraph; a split in the middle still copied them. The prototype's scripted edit test only appends text, so it did not catch this. The fix below was run against the same split and produced a valid UDM in which the first half keeps the id and the slot and the second half is a new block. servers/nextjs/lib/udm/adapters/tiptap/from-tiptap.ts (new, excerpt) deserialize calls it first, so the guarantee holds for documents from any editor, including ones without a plugin. In Presenton's own page editor, the UniqueID extension (@tiptap/extension-unique-id, MIT in v3) can additionally keep ids unique while the user edits: configured with attributeName: "udmId", the TOP_LEVEL types, and a generateID that returns a blk_ id, it would assign ids to blocks the user creates and repair copies on split and paste. It then replaces udmId in UdmAttrs, since both would declare the same attribute. This configuration was not installed in the prototype and is unverified; the research probe found that UniqueID assigns ids through a plugin transaction, which a headless server-side Editor did not run, so server code should use its generateUniqueIds(doc, extensions) helper or rely on

validateNative is the adapter's own guarantee that a document is valid before an editor sees it: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs (prototype, excerpt) Three layers, each catching what the previous one cannot: nodeFromJSON rejects unknown node and mark types and empty text nodes. check() rejects invalid content (text directly in doc, a listItem that starts with a heading), invalid mark sets (a code mark combined with bold), and any attribute whose validate function throws. The dropped-attribute diff compares the input with node.toJSON(). Tiptap drops unknown attributes silently, so without this diff a udmExt written for an editor that lacks UdmAttrs would vanish with no error, and the slot links with it. The prototype checks the validator with seven negative controls, all rejected (tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/validate.mjs:241-252): an unknown node type, text directly in doc, a listItem starting with a heading, an attribute not in the schema, a code mark combined with bold, an empty text node, and a heading of level 9. It then loads every generated document in a real headless editor, new Editor({ element: null, extensions, content, enableContentCheck: true, onContentError }), and requires that no content error fires and that getJSON() equals the input as the schema reads it, nodeFromJSON(doc).toJSON(), which adds default attribute values but, after the dropped-attribute diff, loses nothing (validate.mjs:147-152). Both profiles passed for 383/383 layouts. Gotcha: the editor will not tell you about a dropped attribute enableContentCheck catches what check() catches. It does not report an attribute the schema does not declare, because ProseMirror drops it before checking. Only a diff against the input does.

Once a document is valid tiptap.json, Tiptap's own utilities can turn it into other things on the server. The Part X research ran each of them against 3.30.5 in plain Node 22; none is used by the prototype. Pass the same extensions as the editor (the React-free DataBlock): an unknown node throws. Node views are not used, so dataBlock needs an explicit mapping. Markdown, HTML and email exports should come from adapters that read the UDM directly (the prototype's Markdown adapter is one; see Adding any new target). They then do not depend on an editor schema, and negotiation reports what they lose. Tiptap's converters are for content that already is tiptap.json: a page a person edited, rendered for a reader. Run them where Node runs. In Presenton's Next.js app that is a route handler or server action in the Node runtime, not the Edge runtime. The

docs.t: Step 9: The reverse direction, including edited documents
docs.x: tiptapToUdm (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/from-tiptap.mjs:8-105) walks the top-level nodes once and handles two kinds of input with the same code: Documents this adapter wrote. udmKind, udmId, udmMeta and udmExt restore section boundaries, ids, roles, groups, callout tones, notes, the document's metadata and every ext bag. Table cells are read back into a static binding under the original binding id from udmMeta; data blocks restore their block fields and binding definition from their attributes. Documents nobody annotated. A page written by hand, or by another Tiptap app. H1 as the first node becomes the title, H1 and H2 start sections, a bare horizontal rule starts an untitled section, H3 to H6 become block headings, unknown nodes become paragraphs with native_node_degraded, unknown marks are dropped with native_mark_dropped, and non-text inline nodes (a mention, for example) become their text with inline_node_degraded. Edited documents are the first kind with changes. The prototype's edit test applies a scripted edit to every generated tiptap.json (append [edited] to every heading, paragraph, list item and table cell; change every static chart's categories and values; validate.mjs editTiptap), converts back to the UDM, then into the same Presenton layout, and checks each slot: Edited content Landed in the right slot Text elements 3,228/3,228 Section titles 354/354 Lists 35/35 Tables 7/7 Charts 113/113 Edited slots keeping the slot's base font (family, size, color) 3,582/3,582 Edited elements keeping a second color or size inside one element 0/44 Edits land because each block still carries its Presenton slot in udmExt, and the Presenton adapter writes a block to its provenance slot first (PPT adapter (Presenton JSON)). Unchanged blocks leave their slots byte-identical, which is what gives a document edit patch semantics on the slide. The 44 flattened elements are the one systematic loss. Some template text elements mix two colors or sizes inside one element (for example a headline with one highlighted word). The UDM records only marks that differ from the element's base font (bold, italic, underline), so after an edit the Presenton adapter rewrites the element with the slot's first-run font, and the second color is gone. A neutral highlight mark in the UDM would close this; it is a UDM change for all adapters, not a Tiptap change. Gotcha: an

Part VIII and Part IX make one rule non-negotiable: a document stores binding definitions, never numbers presented as current; values are resolved as the viewer and held in a binding store (Story 1: Dynamic data and refresh, Artifact Spec and targets Steps 2 and 8). The data block follows it by construction: Binding source What is in dataBlock.attrs.binding Where the node view gets values Refresh static (imported Presenton chart, a table typed by hand) the data itself, source.data the node n/a: editing the chart edits the attribute, and the edit goes back to the slide (113/113 charts in the edit test) live (superset_chart, superset_dataset, superset_metric) the definition only: source, mapping, format, refresh policy the hook in LiveBindingContext: Part IX's useGckBinding(bindingId), inside a GckBindingsProvider built from the document's definitions Part IX refresh controller: on open, manual, interval, filter change; as the viewer The production validate on binding (Step 5.2) rejects snapshot, snapshotAt, status and error, so a document that accidentally captured runtime state fails check() instead of saving someone's numbers into a shared page. A saved page becomes live exactly as Part IX describes for its Tiptap target: the host collects the definitions from the document, wraps the editor in GckBindingsProvider, and every data block's view re-renders when a binding.resolved event lands, without changing the ProseMirror document. What the prototype does not cover, and what is therefore design only: Bindings that start on a slide. Part VIII stores a slide's bindings as slide_data_bindings rows keyed by an RFC 6901 element_path into slides.ui. The Presenton adapter would read those rows on deserialize and put the definitions into the UDM's bindings; the Tiptap adapter then needs no change, since a live binding is just another binding value. Not built: until it is, a live chart reaches the UDM as static with its last snapshot, and the loss report says so (Code changes in Presenton, exception E8). Live numbers inside text. A token segment (Part IX: a number in prose that is a reference to a binding field) is dropped today with token_unsupported. The design is an inline atom, udmToken, with attrs: { bindingId, field, format } and no text, whose view calls useGckToken. It mirrors Part IX's gckToken and needs "token" support declared in the manifest. Not built.
The prototype writes three examples into tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/ with npm run examples.
