It names every file in the Presenton repository that the Unified Document Model (UDM) work adds or touches, the existing function and line each change hooks into, what changes there, and the code for the new modules. You will learn why every codec runs in TypeScript while FastAPI keeps the database, the hydrator and the LLM steps, how six new routes plug into the existing /api/v1/ppt router without growing the 3,393-line presentation.py route table, how a "page" output target reuses the outline step and the slide content choke point while skipping layout selection, which tests and fixtures move over from the prototype, and where the work needs more than an adapter. The framing is the same as in the rest of Part X: the UDM plus one adapter contract is the product, and Presenton slides and Tiptap pages are the first two adapters. Line numbers refer to the Presenton checkout read on 11 November 2026. New code is marked "(new)" in its block title; none of it is merged, and only the prototype in tutorial/prototypes/udm/ has run. Statements that depend on behavior not run here say "(unverified)".

docs.t: Step 1: Start from the rule and its exceptions
docs.x: The team's direction was "only the adapter layer should change". The feasibility analysis showed that this holds for the conversion itself: the prototype converts all 383 bundled layouts to a valid UDM, every Tiptap document passes the real Tiptap schema check, and an edit made in tiptap.json lands back in the right slide slot for every text, title, list, table and chart. What the rule does not cover is the host glue: an endpoint has to expose the conversion, a menu has to offer it, a write has to be applied safely to the database, and a generation run that should produce a page instead of slides has to be told so. This chapter keeps that glue thin and target-neutral, so that the user's second requirement also holds: "today it is for Tiptap, tomorrow it might be for other modules". The change list therefore has three layers, and only the middle one grows when a new target arrives. Layer What it contains Changes when a new target is added? UDM core Types, validation, negotiate, registry, conformance kit (TypeScript); Pydantic models and a registry client (Python) No. The prototype froze its core with file hashes (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core.lock.json) and then wrote the plain-text adapter without touching it Adapters presenton.slides, tiptap, tiptap.basic, markdown, plain-text, all TypeScript Yes: one new adapter, registered in one setup file Host glue Endpoints, apply service, migration, generation branch, export menu, document page No. Endpoints and the export menu are driven by the registry list, never by a target name

docs.t: Step 2: Decide where each piece lives
docs.x: Production Presenton has two servers. The rule this chapter adopts, consistent with PPT adapter (Presenton JSON) (Step 2) and the runtime risk in the feasibility analysis: every codec runs in TypeScript, once; FastAPI supplies inputs and applies outputs. Piece Lives in Why UDM core: types, negotiate, registry, conformance kit servers/nextjs/lib/udm/core/ (new) One implementation of negotiation, so a preview, an export and an edit of the same document can never degrade differently. Python has no copy of negotiate All adapters, including presenton.slides servers/nextjs/lib/udm/adapters/ (new) Tiptap's schema check is JavaScript-only: the adapter validates its own output with getSchema(extensions) and nodeFromJSON(doc).check() because Tiptap silently drops attributes it does not know (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs:47-74). Any conversion that involves Tiptap therefore runs in TypeScript, and putting the Presenton codec next to it makes slides to Tiptap one in-process call Pydantic UDM models and a registry client servers/fastapi/udm/ (new) FastAPI validates every UDM that enters the database and calls the TypeScript registry; it never converts formats itself Apply, guard, content sync, layout choice, page generation servers/fastapi/services/udm/ (new) Only Python owns the database transaction, the Template v2 hydrator _apply_template_content_to_ui (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:575) and the LLM structure step generate_presentation_structure (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:157) Cross-language fixtures servers/fastapi/tests/fixtures/udm/ (new) Node tests write some of them and Python tests read them (Step 8). Tests are not part of either Docker image Three alternatives were considered and rejected. Codecs in Python. Porting the prototype's serializers is easy, but validating Tiptap output is not: without the real ProseMirror schema the server could emit a document the editor rejects or silently changes. Two of the prototype's seven negative controls (tutorial/prototypes/udm/REPORT.md) only the real schema catches: an attribute the schema does not declare, which Tiptap drops without an error, and a code mark combined with bold. A Python codec for slides plus a TypeScript codec for Tiptap would also need two copies of negotiate kept identical by golden files, which Adding any new target
servers/fastapi/udm/ and servers/fastapi/services/udm/ (new)

The models validate a UDM before it is stored or applied; Python never turns one into a target format. Wire names stay camelCase to match the TypeScript side. servers/fastapi/udm/models.py (new, abridged) The block above is abridged; the full module declares all 14 block classes, DataBinding (a static source must carry origin and data), Provenance and nested list items. The reference check repeats a subset of the TypeScript checkUdm (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:147). Both run against the same fixtures (Step 8); TypeScript is the reference.

The Python registry has the same shape as the TypeScript one and the prototype's core/adapter.ts contract. In the first delivery it holds no local adapter: every id resolves to the Next.js registry, which it asks for manifests the first time. Local registration stays available for server-side materializers that never run in a browser (a scheduled email, a DOCX export; see Adding any new target). servers/fastapi/udm/registry.py (new) servers/fastapi/udm/__init__.py (new) Importing the private _get_next_public_url from servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:18-19 is deliberate: it is the URL the export runner already uses to reach Next.js, so any base-path fix for exports applies here too. A follow-up can rename it to a public helper. httpx is already a dependency (servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:26). The routes map a ValueError from convert to 422 and an httpx connection error to 503.

docs.t: 3.3 Apply, guard, content sync and layout choice
docs.x: These four modules are where Python does what only Python can. Two of them are specified in PPT adapter (Presenton JSON) and are only placed here: services/udm/layouts.py (73, Step 7) runs generate_presentation_structure for sections that have no layout and keeps a choice only if the layout's chart and table slot counts match the section; services/udm/patch_guard.py (73, Step 8) refuses a patched ui that differs from the stored one anywhere outside content keys (runs, items, columns, rows, categories, series, chart_type, title, axis titles, source, data, prompt, latex). apply.py is 73's apply endpoint sketch (Step 9) turned into a service, so that two routes can share it: the server-orchestrated PUT /presentation/{id}/udm and the lower-level POST /presentation/{id}/slides/apply for clients that serialized on their own. servers/fastapi/services/udm/apply.py (new) clear_unresolved_charts comes from Part IX's slides sketch; it is needed because _apply_template_chart_content copies categories and series only when they are non-empty (73, Step 9). Importing _apply_template_content_to_ui and _template_slide_ui from the endpoint module is how 73's sketch calls them too. It works because presentation.py does not import services/udm/apply.py; if it ever needs to, the two helpers move to a module of their own. content_sync.py closes the gap that 73 flags as a gotcha in Step 8 and this chapter lists as exception E3: patch mode writes ui, but several paths read slides.content. servers/fastapi/services/udm/content_sync.py (new) The shapes written back follow the content schema that get_template_schema derives for each element type (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:361-423). The content-sync test in Step 8 checks every corpus layout by hydrating the synced content and comparing the result with the patched ui; whatever shape passes that test is the one that ships.

docs.t: Step 5: Add the endpoints and wire them into the router
docs.x: All new routes go into one new module, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation_udm.py, instead of the existing presentation.py. That file has 3,393 lines and is edited by several Part VIII stories at the same time; a separate module keeps merge conflicts out of the way. Method and path Purpose Response GET /api/v1/ppt/udm/adapters List every registered adapter manifest { adapters: AdapterManifest[] } GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/udm A deck (or a stored document) as a UDM { udm, loss } GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export?format=<adapter id>&download=<bool> Any registered target's native output; download=true returns the raw file with Content-Disposition { format, native, loss } or the file POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/from-udm Create a new deck from a UDM or from any target's native document (content mode for every section) { presentation: PresentationWithSlides, loss } PUT /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/udm Apply an edited UDM to a deck (patch for linked sections, content for new ones) or replace a stored document { loss, patched, created, content_unsynced } POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/slides/apply Apply serializer output directly (73, Step 9) same report PUT and from-udm were not in the original request. PUT is what makes the edit round trip usable from the document page, and from-udm is the "document to slides" direction. servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation_udm.py (new) POST /from-udm creates the row first and then runs the same path with no current slides, so every section goes through content mode: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation_udm.py (new, continued) choose_layouts_for wraps 73's choose_layouts: sections with no linked slide and no layout in ext["presenton.slides"] are rendered as Markdown through the registry and sent to the structure step; sections it cannot place go to the adapter's deterministic picker. An edit of linked slides never calls the LLM. Gotcha: patch only for linked sections 73 sets a product rule from the prototype's numbers: through targets that drop ids and ext, text lands in the right slot only 94.3% (Markdown) or 67.81% (StarterKit-only Tiptap) of the time. The serializer therefore patches only sections whose blocks still carry ext["presenton.slides"].slot. A document that comes back without them is applied in content mode, as new slides, never as an update of the slides

Forgetting this would duplicate a document as an empty slides deck. One source of truth per row. For output_target == "presenton.slides" the slide rows are the truth and udm stays NULL; the UDM is derived on read. For any other target, udm is the truth and there are no slide rows. The response model gains output_target: str = "presenton.slides" (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_with_slides.py:10-27). _presentation_response_data dumps the model with only layout and structure excluded (presentation.py:343-344); it must also exclude udm, because a document can be large and GET /{id}/udm serves it. servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/b4d6f8a0c2e4_add_output_target_and_udm.py (new) The migration copies the defensive pattern of f3a7c1d9e5b2_add_smart_generation_fields.py, which added generation_mode the same way, and chains after the current head 026c0ba8b35c. servers/fastapi/migrations.py:36-37 gets REVISION_OUTPUT_TARGET_UDM = "b4d6f8a0c2e4" and REVISION_HEAD = REVISION_OUTPUT_TARGET_UDM; tests/unit/test_migrations.py asserts against migrations.REVISION_HEAD and follows automatically. The revision id is a placeholder: if Part VIII's Postgres work (Story 2, subtask 2.1) or binding table (Story 1, subtask 1.2) lands first, down_revision must point at their head instead.

prepare_presentation requires a template today (layout: Annotated[str, Body()], presentation.py:1844). For a page target the parameter becomes optional, and the function returns right after building the outline model (:1860): servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (changed, prepare_presentation) stream_presentation already branches once for Smart mode (presentation.py:2288-2289) before it rejects a row without a structure (:2290-2294). The page branch goes next to it: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (changed, stream_presentation)

The content step is schema-driven: get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline takes any SlideLayoutModel (id, name, description, json_schema; servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:11-15) and asks the LLM for JSON that matches its schema. _prepare_response_schema (generate_slide_content.py:203-226) strips asset-only fields and adds a __speaker_note__ field, which maps onto Section.notes. The page target therefore needs no new LLM call, only a new schema. The schema is flat (no anyOf), because the call runs JSONSchemaResponse(..., strict=True) against several providers and a flat object is the shape the current layout schemas already exercise. Whether every configured provider accepts it is unverified (work package D5). servers/fastapi/udm/section_schema.py (new) The first release generates text blocks only. Tables and charts in a generated page would put LLM-written numbers into static bindings, which Part IX's invariants reserve for imported or user data. Data blocks arrive through conversion from slides (where they are static with origin: "imported") or, later, through live bindings (Story 1: Dynamic data and refresh). servers/fastapi/services/udm/document_generation.py (new) This sketch generates sections one by one for readability; the production version batches the calls with asyncio.gather, as generate_presentation_handler does in batches of 10 (presentation.py:2985-3005). The safe_sse_stream call mirrors the one at the end of stream_presentation (presentation.py:2516-2525), which also passes on_error to roll the session back; its logger and error_detail arguments are keyword-only (servers/fastapi/utils/sse.py:10-17). markdown_inline_to_rich_text is a small new helper: the slide path has its own Markdown-emphasis parser (_parse_template_markdown_text, presentation.py:1224) that writes Template v2 runs, so it is not reusable as is. Prompt wording The system prompt says "Make slide as concise as possible" and similar (generate_slide_content.py:126-137), and the user prompt carries a "Slide Number" section (:152-155). Section content still validates against the schema with this wording. A unit_noun parameter ("slide" or "section") is a small, target-neutral change scheduled with the provider tests (work package D5); it is not required for correctness.

The request named PresentationActions for the export menu item. Reading the code shows the menu is not there: PresentationActions.tsx (2,485 lines) holds the insert palette and action side panel (textItems at :234, chartTypeItems at :289) and has no export code. The export menu is ExportOptions in servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationHeader.tsx:469-500, with the PDF and PPTX buttons calling handleExportPdf (:308) and handleExportPptx (:226) and the download helper at :426. The change goes there. The new entries come from GET /api/v1/ppt/udm/adapters, so a new adapter shows up in the menu without a frontend change. presenton.slides is filtered out because it is the deck itself. servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationHeader.tsx (changed) UdmApi (new, services/api/udm.ts) follows DashboardApi.getPresentation (services/api/dashboard.ts:70-88). downloadBlob sits next to downloadLink (PresentationHeader.tsx:426) because the adapter path returns content, not a file path. The header also gets an "Edit as document" item that opens /document?id=<presentation id>.

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/document/ (new) servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/document/components/DocumentEditor.tsx (new) In the browser, the document page needs only the Tiptap adapter; the Presenton adapter runs on the Next.js server when FastAPI calls the convert route. A browser bundle that imported registry-setup.ts would pull in every adapter, so the page imports registry-browser.ts, which registers tiptap alone. DocumentPage debounces onChange and saves with PUT /presentation/{id}/udm, sending the updated_at it loaded as if_unmodified_since. For a slides deck this patches the slots that changed; for a document row it stores the UDM. Replacing the dataBlock node view only adds rendering; the node's name, attributes and atom: true are unchanged, so the manifest derived from the extension list equals the serializer's. That rests on deriveManifest reading only the schema (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs:13-40); a unit test pins it. DataBlockView and its renderers are specified in Tiptap adapter (tiptap.json). Charts follow Part VIII Story 4, subtask 4.1 ("Chart rendering decision") rather than making a separate choice.

You will learn the six phases and 29 work packages, their effort in person-days and their dependencies, the acceptance criteria for each one (most are the prototype's measured numbers, now enforced in CI), how the plan fits next to the AI Slides delivery plan (Part VIII), what it replaces or reorders in the Generative Content Kit roadmap (Part IX), and which risks need watching. Owners are left blank on purpose; the team assigns them. The plan keeps the framing of the rest of Part X. The deliverable is the Unified Document Model (UDM) plus one adapter contract, a registry, capability negotiation and a conformance kit. Presenton slides and Tiptap pages are the first two adapters. Markdown and plain text ship with them because they cost little and prove that the contract holds for a third and a fourth target.

docs.t: Step 4: Fit the plan next to Part VIII
docs.x: The AI Slides delivery plan schedules 9 stories and 129 d over trains R1 (Fri 13 Nov 2026) to R11 (Fri 5 Feb 2027), with named owners. No Part VIII story depends on Part X, and Part X must not take capacity from that plan's critical path. Five touchpoints need care. Part VIII item Touchpoint What Part X does Story 1, subtask 1.2: slide_data_bindings model and migration Both add an Alembic revision after 026c0ba8b35c D1's down_revision points at whatever head exists when D1 starts; F2 reads the binding rows (Story 1: Dynamic data and refresh) Story 2, subtask 2.1: Postgres schema; subtask 2.4: require_presentation_access on every endpoint The migration must run on Postgres; the six new routes need the access check D1 tests on Postgres once 2.1 lands; B4, C2 and E2 adopt the access dependency once 2.4 lands Story 4, subtask 4.1: chart rendering decision The document page renders charts too C4 follows that decision instead of making its own Story 5, subtask 5.3: Next.js basePath /ai-slides and prefix fixes, including the export route The /document route, the /api/udm/* routes, and the URL FastAPI uses to reach Next.js Every new path goes through the same prefix helpers; the registry client reuses the export runner's base URL, so it should inherit 5.3's fix (verify when 5.3 lands) Stories 1 and 3 edit presentation.py Merge conflicts in a 3,393-line file Part X keeps its edits there to the create flag, two branches and one excluded field; every new route lives in presentation_udm.py Story 7 (the presentation planner) produces the outline that a page run also uses. Nothing in Part X changes the outline, so the planner serves both targets without extra work.

docs.x: Part IX plans 44 work packages and 210 d in phases P0 to P4, starting "after the AI Slides pilot is stable, or in parallel". docs.t: Step 8: Record what is out of scope and what needs a decision
docs.x: Out of scope for this plan, each with the reason: Writing to Smart-mode HTML slides. 73 designs a DOM-path reader and writer; until it is built and measured, Smart decks are reported as losses. Live-data tokens inside text. Part VIII's bindings cover charts, tables and metrics; tokens in prose belong to Part IX's run protocol. Collaborative editing of documents. The document page is single-user, with the conflict check from C2. Images in generated pages. The first section schema has text blocks only; image prompts need the asset pipeline and a placement rule (a later work package, not estimated). Python measurements of the prototype's findings. The prototype ran in Node only. Because every codec stays in TypeScript, its numbers carry over; the acceptance criteria re-measure them in CI. Decisions the team needs to take before phase B starts: Accept that every codec runs in TypeScript and that FastAPI orchestrates and applies, as in 73 and 75. Accept that document rows store a UDM, not tiptap.json, so that any adapter can open them. Accept text-only generated pages until live bindings are available. Confirm that Part IX's @gck/target-slides is replaced by the presenton.slides adapter (Step 5). Name the feature flags and decide who can turn them on in staging.

Reads: tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/adapter.ts, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/registry.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/negotiate.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/conformance.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/fixtures.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/markdown.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/plaintext.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/setup.mjs, tutorial/prototypes/udm/REPORT.md · Builds on: Unified Document Model, Tiptap adapter (tiptap.json) · Time: ~45 min

Today the request is Tiptap. Tomorrow it might be a Superset dashboard, a Word file, a Confluence page or an email. This chapter shows that each of those is one new adapter and nothing else. You will read the generic adapter contract in TypeScript and Python, the registry that plugs adapters in, the capability negotiation that degrades any UDM to what a target can hold, the rules for namespaced extension fields, and the shared conformance kit every adapter must pass. Then you will follow a step-by-step recipe, study the prototype's Markdown adapter as a worked example with its measured results, read short design sketches for four more targets, and finish with a checklist that proves a new target needed no change to the UDM core or the generation engine. Presenton slides (PPT adapter (Presenton JSON)) and Tiptap pages (Tiptap adapter (tiptap.json)) are the first two adapters. Nothing in this chapter is specific to either of them. Code labeled "(prototype)" is quoted from the runnable prototype in tutorial/prototypes/udm/, which was run against all 383 bundled Presenton layouts (npm ci && npm run all). Code labeled "(new)" is proposed production code that the prototype did not run. Anything not measured is marked as unverified. Paths under gck/ and gck_engine/ are the Part IX package layout used in Unified Document Model; the first delivery inside Presenton places the same code under servers/nextjs/lib/udm/ and servers/fastapi/udm/ (Code changes in Presenton, Steps 3 and 4).

docs.t: Step 1: The rule, and how it is enforced
docs.x: The rule has two halves: The core never names a target. The UDM types, the adapter contract, the registry, negotiation and the conformance kit contain no if (target === "..."), no table keyed by target name and no import of an adapter. An adapter never changes the core. It declares what it can hold (its manifest), converts in both directions, validates its own output with its host's rules, and stores anything only it needs under its own namespace in ext. The prototype checks both halves mechanically, not by review: Claim How it is checked Result (tutorial/prototypes/udm/REPORT.md) The core names no target in code tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/validate.mjs:273-274 strips comments from every core file and searches it for presenton, tiptap, markdown, prosemirror and plaintext "Core files naming a target in code: none" A new adapter needs no core change core.lock.json holds sha256 hashes of every core file, taken after the Markdown adapter and before the plain-text adapter; validate recomputes them "Core files changed after the freeze: none" Only one file knows which adapters exist tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/setup.mjs:27-35 is the only file that imports adapters by construction The Markdown adapter is written only against the contract validate lists its imports marked and ../core/udm-runtime.mjs only The core was not frozen from day one While the first three adapters (Presenton, Tiptap, Markdown) were being built, the conformance kit and the 383-layout corpus forced five changes in the core. None of them names a target: a negotiation rule that drops section role and level when a target cannot hold them, whitespace canonicalization at bold and italic edges (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:45-56), keeping a chart's title and axes as the caption when a chart degrades to a table (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/negotiate.mjs:24-26), the structure.orderPreserved flag, and an optional trace on serialize results. The freeze was taken after those settled. Plan for the same with the first production adapters: each core change must be target-neutral, or it does not go in.

docs.t: Step 2: The adapter contract in TypeScript
docs.x: The whole contract is 69 lines. This is the part every adapter author reads: tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/adapter.ts (prototype, excerpt) Four members, and each has one job: Member Job Rules manifest Says what this target can hold Validated at registration (checkManifest, Step 4). Prefer deriving it from the host (the Tiptap adapter derives it from the editor schema, tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/tiptap/index.mjs:13-38) over writing it by hand serialize UDM to native Pure and deterministic: no I/O, no clock, no randomness. Its input has already been negotiated, so it never sees a block type its manifest does not list. It reports anything it still could not express as a LossEntry deserialize Native to UDM Pure. Required unless roundTrip is "write-only". Must accept native documents the adapter did not write (a hand-written page, a file from another tool) and degrade unknown native content to paragraphs with a loss entry validateNative Checks the output against the host's own rules Uses the host's real validator where one exists (the Tiptap adapter runs schema.nodeFromJSON(doc).check(); see Tiptap adapter (tiptap.json) Step 7). Errors fail the conversion; warnings (such as a slot's max_length) are surfaced to the user Talking to a live host and fetching data are deliberately not in the pure contract. As in Part IX (Artifact Spec and targets, Step 5), host binding is an optional second layer that calls the pure functions, and live values reach a host through the binding store at render time. That is what makes the pure layer testable without a browser, a server or an LLM. The production contract keeps these signatures and adds the optional host layer in its own file, so the pure contract never changes for it: gck/packages/protocol/src/host.ts (new) UdmDiff is the one diff type for edit runs. It replaces the two names Part IX used for the same thing (ArtifactDiff and BlockDiff); see Unified Document Model.

docs.t: Step 3: The same contract in Python
docs.x: The engine (FastAPI) needs the contract too, for two reasons. It builds each run's LLM response schema from the target's manifest, and some targets are written on the server by Python code that never runs in a browser (a scheduled email, a DOCX export). The Python mirror holds the same fields with the same JSON names, so a manifest serialized by either side validates on the other. gck_engine/adapters/base.py (new) Two Protocols instead of one optional method keep the "required unless write-only" rule checkable with isinstance(adapter, ReversibleAdapter) at registration. Gotcha: one negotiation, two languages Negotiation must give the same result in the browser and in the engine, or a preview and an export of the same document will differ. The prototype implements negotiation once, in JavaScript (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/negotiate.mjs). If the engine needs its own copy (gck_engine/adapters/negotiate.py, new), treat the TypeScript one as the reference: generate golden files of negotiate(fixture, manifest) for every shared fixture and every registered manifest, and make the Python port pass them byte for byte in CI. This is the same discipline Part IX uses for its JSON Schema and Pydantic mirrors. The Python port has not been written or measured.

A registry maps an id (or an alias) to an adapter, refuses invalid adapters at registration (checkManifest, tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/registry.mjs:7-18), and offers one convert call that always negotiates before it serializes: tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/registry.mjs (prototype, excerpt) Three details matter: paragraph is mandatory (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/registry.mjs:14). It is the last step of every fallback chain, so a manifest without it could leave negotiation with nowhere to put text. The manifest may only use the core vocabularies (BLOCK_TYPES, MARKS, CHART_KINDS in tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:5-9). A target cannot invent a block type; it can only choose which existing ones it supports. A genuinely new concept is a UDM change (Step 11). Aliases keep old ids working. Part IX used the closed union "slides" | "tiptap-doc" | "superset-dashboard" | "text" as target ids. The UDM makes ids open strings in the namespace form, and the old names are registered as aliases: tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/setup.mjs (prototype, excerpt) The Python registry mirrors it; the Presenton version (servers/fastapi/udm/registry.py, Code changes in Presenton Step 3.2) also resolves remote adapters whose codec runs in Next.js, such as Tiptap. To remove even the one wiring line from the change set of a new target, the engine can discover adapters through package entry points, so installing a package registers its adapter: gck_engine/adapters/discovery.py (new)

docs.t: Step 5: Capability negotiation and the degradation chain
docs.x: Negotiation is the reason a new adapter can be small. Every target receives a UDM that contains only what its manifest says it can hold, and every change made on the way is reported. The adapter never decides on its own how to degrade a chart or a callout; the core does, in one fixed order, the same way for every target: Rule Applies when the manifest says What happens Loss codes 1. Extensions features.extPassThrough: false Foreign ext namespaces are removed; the target keeps only its own ext_dropped 2. Annotations features.notes: false Section.notes and Section.summary are removed, their text recorded notes_dropped, summary_dropped 3. Section titles features.sectionTitles: false The title becomes a leading heading block section_title_to_block 4. Blocks block type not in blocks The block follows its fallback chain until supported block_degraded, block_dropped, text_reduced 5. Chart kinds chartType not in chartKinds Fixed chain to the nearest kind; none left means rule 4 chart_kind_fallback 6. Marks mark not in marks math falls back to code; others are dropped (a link keeps its text, the href is recorded) mark_dropped 7. Nesting above maxHeadingLevel or maxListDepth Heading levels clamped, deep lists flattened heading_clamped, list_flattened 8. Structure structure.groups, structure.roles, features.captions false group, block role, section role and level removed; a caption becomes a paragraph after its block groups_dropped, roles_dropped, section_role_dropped, caption_to_paragraph, caption_dropped 9. Limits limits set Text clipped to maxCharsPerBlock; sections split at maxBlocksPerSection; content is never padded text_clipped, section_split The block fallback chains (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/negotiate.mjs:15-65) form a graph that always ends at paragraph or at nothing: Chart kinds have their own chain (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/negotiate.mjs:7-10): horizontal_stacked_bar to stacked_bar to bar; horizontal_bar to bar; donut and polar_area to pie; radar to bar; scatter to line; bubble to scatter; area to line; pie and line to bar. When no kind is left, the chart degrades as a block (rule 4). Three properties make this safe to share across all targets: Deterministic. Same UDM and manifest, same output, byte for byte (conformance check C4). Generated ids in degraded blocks are derived from the original id (blk_x_cap, blk_x_1), never random. Complete. Every

Some information matters only to one target: the Presenton slot path an element came from, the layout id, a Notion block id, a dashboard component id. It cannot go into the UDM's core fields (they must stay target-neutral) and it must not be thrown away (or an edit cannot find its way back). It goes into ext: tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm.ts (prototype, excerpt) Udm.ext, Section.ext and every block's ext may hold one bag per namespace. The rules: The namespace is the adapter id. An adapter writes only ext[manifest.id]. Check C11 fails an adapter whose deserialize writes a namespace that was not already in its input. Foreign namespaces pass through or are reported. An adapter that declares features.extPassThrough: true must carry every other namespace through serialize and deserialize unchanged (C11 compares them). An adapter that cannot (Markdown, plain text, a StarterKit-only editor) declares false, and negotiation removes the foreign bags before serialize with an ext_dropped entry. Nothing in ext may change meaning. Removing every ext bag must leave a valid UDM that renders the same content. Content always lives in core fields. The engine never interprets ext, and the LLM never writes it. ext is excluded from the response schema of a run; on an edit run the engine copies it from the base document. The one engine access is I8_LAYOUT_HINT, an opaque check that ext[manifest.id].layout is in the same manifest's layoutCatalog (Unified Document Model, Step 5). Bags stay small (proposed: 4 KB per block, 64 KB per document), so ext cannot turn into a second document. The prototype does not enforce a size cap; this is unverified. What a Presenton bag looks like on a block, taken from the prototype example (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/2-udm.json): tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/2-udm.json (prototype, excerpt) The measured effect of rule 2 is the strongest argument for carrying ext wherever a target can. When the Presenton bags survive (the Tiptap page profile stores them in a node attribute), a document edited in Tiptap returns to the right Presenton slot for 100% of 3,582 text slots. When they do not survive, the Presenton adapter must place blocks back by position, and fidelity drops: Target, back into the same Presenton layout Text slots correct Layout found again from content alone tiptap (ext kept)

Every adapter runs the same checks on the same fixtures. Passing them is the definition of "done" for a new target: Check What it verifies Runs for C0 The manifest is valid (checkManifest) every adapter, once C1 The fixture is a valid UDM every fixture C2 The negotiated UDM is valid and uses only blocks the manifest lists every fixture C3 Negotiation is complete: every text atom is still present or in a droppedText every fixture C4 Negotiation is deterministic every fixture C5 serialize is deterministic and does not mutate its input every fixture C6 validateNative reports no errors on the output every fixture C7 Every loss entry has a string code and path every fixture C8 The deserialized UDM is valid and neutral reversible adapters C9 The round trip loses no text silently reversible adapters C10 The round trip equals the negotiated input apart from declared losses; ids compared when features.ids, order when structure.orderPreserved reversible adapters C11 ext passes through (when declared) and stays isolated reversible adapters With four fixtures, a reversible adapter runs 1 + 4 x 11 = 45 checks and a write-only adapter 1 + 4 x 7 = 29. The fixtures (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/fixtures.mjs:9-69) are target-neutral and deliberately hostile: Fixture What it contains minimal One section, one paragraph kitchen-sink Every block type and every mark, a link whose URL has & and parentheses, a three-level nested list, an ordered list, notes and a summary, a group of three blocks forming a card, block roles, static chart, table and metric bindings, a live superset_chart embed, and ext bags under a foreign namespace (acme.crm) on the document, a section and a block non-latin Hindi, Bengali and Arabic text, including bold inside Devanagari and an emoji edge An empty section, an untitled section, a line break inside a paragraph, a paragraph that starts like a numbered list and is full of Markdown metacharacters (asterisk, underscore, brackets, angle brackets, hash, pipe, tilde, backslash, backtick), a level-3 heading, a 1,200-character paragraph, a bubble chart and a table of empty cells The kit itself is target-blind (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/conformance.mjs:50-124). C3 builds the set of text atoms in the negotiated UDM plus every droppedText, and fails if any atom of the input is in neither. docs.t: Step 8: Recipe for adding a module
docs.x: Follow these steps in order. Each produces something you can check. Pick the id. Lowercase, dot-separated, matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z0-9-]+)*$ (tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:12). The id is also the ext namespace, so pick the name of the host, not of a feature: superset.dashboard, docx, notion, confluence, email. Variants of one host with different capabilities get a suffix (tiptap.basic). Write the manifest from the host's real capabilities. List only blocks and marks the native format can express and read back. If capabilities vary per instance (an editor's schema, a workspace's enabled macros), derive the manifest from the instance, as deriveManifest(schema, id) does for Tiptap. Set roundTrip honestly. Write serialize. Walk sections and blocks; emit native content; push a LossEntry for anything the native format cannot express even after negotiation (for example image_meta_dropped in Markdown). Do not degrade blocks yourself: negotiation already did. Do not read the clock, generate random ids or fetch anything. Write validateNative with the host's own validator. Use the strictest check the host offers: a schema check, a re-parse, an official SDK validator. If the host silently drops data (Tiptap drops unknown attributes), add a check that detects the drop. Write deserialize, or declare write-only. Accept documents the adapter did not write; unknown native content becomes a paragraph plus a native_node_degraded loss. Generate ids deterministically (hashId in tutorial/prototypes/udm/core/udm-runtime.mjs:19-26) and record provenance: { origin: "imported", importedFrom: { adapter, adapterVersion } }. Put target-only data in ext[manifest.id]. Ids the host assigns, layout choices, native style names. Nothing else. Register it. One line in the registry wiring (or an entry point in Python). Add an alias only if an older id must keep working. Run the conformance kit until it is green. Expect C3 and C10 to find real bugs in escaping and whitespace. Run a corpus. At minimum the 383-layout Presenton corpus, plus real native documents from the host if there is a reverse direction. Commit golden examples (input UDM, native output, loss report) so changes to the adapter show up in review as diffs. Add the host layer only if needed. apply and applyPatch for interactive hosts; "patch" in applyModes only when ids survive the round trip. Document the

docs.t: Step 9: Worked example: the Markdown adapter
docs.x: The Markdown adapter was the first one written only against the contract, after the Presenton and Tiptap adapters existed. It is 181 non-blank, non-comment lines in one file and imports two things: marked (17.0.5, for parsing) and the shared UDM helpers.

tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/markdown.mjs (prototype, excerpt) Each false is a decision with a consequence. No chart, diagram, metric or embed, so negotiation turns charts into GFM tables and diagrams into lists before serialize runs. No underline, because GitHub-flavored Markdown has no underline syntax. No ids and no extPassThrough, because plain Markdown has nowhere to put them that survives a round trip through other tools. No "patch", because without ids an edit cannot be applied in place.

The serializer maps UDM sections to ## headings (or a --- break for an untitled section), block headings 1 to 3 to ### to #####, and each block to its GFM form. The interesting code is all about making sure the output parses back to the same thing: Escaping. Every Markdown metacharacter in text is escaped (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/markdown.mjs:20), and line starts that would turn into a list item, a numbered item or a setext underline are escaped too (markdown.mjs:22). The edge fixture's 1. not a list * _x_ [y] <z> # | ~ \ paragraph exists to catch this. Flanking rules. CommonMark does not treat ** as bold when the delimiter touches punctuation on the wrong side, so **Presenter:**Lorem is not bold. Where the emphasized text starts or ends with punctuation, the adapter writes <strong>, <em> or <del> instead (markdown.mjs:35-37), and the parser maps those tags back to marks (markdown.mjs:105-112). Adjacent lists. Two consecutive lists merge into one in Markdown. The adapter writes an empty HTML comment between them (markdown.mjs:93) and the parser skips it (markdown.mjs:155). Code spans. A code span is fenced with one more backtick than the longest run inside it (markdown.mjs:28-29). What it produced for the simple card slide (tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/4-markdown.md): tutorial/prototypes/udm/examples/simple-cards-with-list/4-markdown.md (prototype) The card's grouping, the kpi and subtitle roles and the Presenton slot paths did not survive, and the loss report says so (groups_dropped, roles_dropped, ext_dropped).

deserialize lexes with marked in GFM mode, with autolinking turned off so a bare URL stays text (markdown.mjs:102-103). An H1 before any section becomes the document title; H1 and H2 start sections; H3 and deeper become block headings; --- starts an untitled section while *** is a divider; a paragraph that is a single image becomes an image block; a GFM table becomes a table block with a static binding whose origin is "imported". Anything else becomes a paragraph with a native_node_degraded loss (markdown.mjs:142-195). validateNative checks that the output is a string that marked can lex (markdown.mjs:198-203). That is a weak check on its own. The real test for Markdown is the round trip: conformance checks C9 and C10 and the corpus run re-parse the output and compare it with what went in.

Check Result Conformance kit 45/45 UDM to Markdown valid, 383 layouts 383/383 Text atoms surviving UDM to Markdown to UDM 5,211/5,211 Back into the same Presenton layout: text slots 3,378/3,582 (94.3%) Charts, tables, images back into their slots 113/113, 7/7, 607/607 Infographics back into their slots 0/51 (they became lists or paragraphs) Whole slide byte-identical after the round trip 278/383 (72.58%) Original layout found again from content alone 254/383 (66.32%) Negotiation losses over the corpus ext_dropped 4,807, section_role_dropped 383, groups_dropped 310, roles_dropped 303, block_degraded 164, caption_to_paragraph 29, mark_dropped 1 Serializer losses over the corpus image_meta_dropped 607 (image kind and prompt), line_break_in_title 39 Time per layout 0.044 ms negotiate, 0.028 ms serialize, 0.063 ms deserialize Lines of code 181 Charts come back into their chart slots because the Presenton adapter matches a returning table to a chart slot by shape (a chart that a target turned into a table finds its chart slot again); that logic lives in the Presenton adapter, not in the core and not in the Markdown adapter.

The plain-text adapter (tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/plaintext.mjs, 33 lines) was written after core.lock.json was taken. It is write-only (an email body, an SMS digest, a text-to-speech script), declares no marks and six block types, and relies entirely on negotiation for everything else: tutorial/prototypes/udm/adapters/plaintext.mjs (prototype, excerpt) It passes 29/29 conformance checks, keeps 5,211/5,211 text atoms from the corpus in its output, and no core file hash changed. That is the claim of this chapter, measured once.

docs.t: Step 10: Design sketches for the next targets
docs.x: None of these adapters exists. Each sketch lists what its manifest would declare, what negotiation would degrade, and where its target-only data would live. Library and API details are from their public documentation and have not been exercised in this project; treat them as unverified until each adapter's corpus run.

Part IX designed this target in detail (Artifact Spec and targets, Step 9). Under the UDM it becomes an adapter like any other. Manifest field Value Why nativeFormat application/vnd.superset.dashboard+json position_json plus json_metadata blocks heading, paragraph, list, quote, code, table, image, divider, chart, metric, embed HEADER, MARKDOWN (text, lists, quotes, code, static tables, images), DIVIDER, CHART components marks bold, italic, strike, code, link Markdown component structure maxHeadingLevel: 3, groups: true (a ROW), roles: false, orderPreserved: true grid order is reading order features notes: false, sectionTitles: true (a TAB or HEADER), ids: false, extPassThrough: false component meta has no free field for UDM ids (unverified) applyModes append, replace Part IX: patch falls back to replace roundTrip lossy reverse reads the layout tree and saved charts Degradations: diagram and callout follow the core chains (list, quote). The important adapter-local rule is about data: a chart or metric with a live Superset binding becomes a CHART component; a chart with static data (an imported Presenton chart) cannot become a Superset chart without a dataset, so the adapter writes it as a Markdown table and reports static_chart_as_table. Today's negotiation has no rule keyed on features.staticData; if a second target needs the same treatment, that is a candidate target-neutral rule for the core (Step 11). Target-only data: ext["superset.dashboard"] = { tabId, componentIds } on sections and blocks, so a later replace keeps tab ids, as Part IX requires.

Manifest field Value Why nativeFormat application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document blocks heading, paragraph, list, quote, code, table, image, divider built-in heading, list, quote styles; tables; inline pictures marks bold, italic, underline, strike, code, link run properties and hyperlinks; code as a monospace character style structure maxHeadingLevel: 3, maxListDepth: 8, groups: false, roles: false, orderPreserved: true features notes: false (or true if notes are written as comments; a decision), captions: true, ids: true only if block ids are kept as bookmarks (unverified), extPassThrough: false applyModes replace a file, not a live host roundTrip lossy or write-only for the first version Degradations: charts become tables (the chain), unless the chosen writer library supports native Word charts, in which case chart and chartKinds are added to the manifest and nothing else changes; callouts become quotes with a bold label; diagrams become lists. Writing could use the docx npm package on the Node side or python-docx in the engine; reading would need a parser that preserves heading styles. Both choices are unverified. Live data: a .docx file is a frozen output, so every data block is written from its current snapshot with a "Data as of" stamp, following the Part IX live-data rules.

These two are close: both are block-structured wikis with an API, native callouts, code blocks, tables and stable server-side block ids. They are two adapters with two manifests. Manifest field notion confluence nativeFormat Notion block objects (JSON) Confluence storage format (XHTML with macros) blocks heading, paragraph, list, quote, callout, divider, code, math, table, image, embed heading, paragraph, list, quote, callout, divider, code, table, image marks bold, italic, underline, strike, code, link, math bold, italic, underline, strike, code, link structure.maxHeadingLevel 3 (Notion has three heading levels) 3 (UDM headings start below section titles) features.ids true: Notion returns block ids, kept in ext["notion"].blockId true if macro or anchor ids are kept in ext["confluence"] (unverified) applyModes append, replace, patch (update a block by id) replace, append roundTrip lossy lossy Degradations: chart and diagram become tables and lists through the chains; callout tones map to the host's own callout types (Confluence info, note, warning, success panels; a Notion callout with an icon), so callouts keep their tone in these targets rather than degrading to quotes. API request limits belong in limits or in batching inside apply; check the current API reference for the numbers. Live data: frozen snapshot with a "Data as of" stamp and a link to the live version, unless the host can embed a live Superset chart (an embed block), which is a host capability the adapter derives at construction.

HTML is a separate adapter from Tiptap even though Tiptap can produce HTML: an HTML adapter consumes the UDM directly, so it does not depend on an editor schema, and it can produce markup for consumers that never load Tiptap (a public share page, a static export). Manifest field html email nativeFormat text/html text/html (sanitized email profile) blocks every block type except chart, diagram, metric, embed in the static profile; all of them when a chart renderer is bundled paragraph, list, quote, divider, table marks all seven, math only with a math renderer bold, italic, underline, strike, link structure.maxHeadingLevel 3 0 (headings become bold paragraphs) features notes: false, captions: true, ids: true via data-udm-id attributes, extPassThrough: true via a data-udm-ext attribute (both unverified) all false roundTrip lossy write-only The email row follows the Part IX finding that the report-email sanitizer's allowed tags include no headings and no images (Artifact Spec and targets, Step 10): declaring maxHeadingLevel: 0 and leaving heading and image out of blocks lets negotiation produce bold paragraphs and link paragraphs, and the adapter writes no special code for it. Charts become tables with a "Data as of" stamp and a link to the live document; Part IX rules out screenshots of charts.

docs.t: 10.5 What the sketches have in common
docs.x: Each needs a new manifest and its own serialize and deserialize; none needs a new UDM field. The only possible core addition is a rule for static data written against features.staticData, usable by any target.

docs.t: Step 11: Checklist: proving no core change was needed
docs.x: Run this before merging a new adapter. Every line has a mechanical check. # Check How 1 No core file changed The core hashes still match core.lock.json (the corpus run prints "Core files changed after the freeze: none"), or git diff --stat shows nothing under the core package 2 No core file names the new target Add the new target's name to the scan in tutorial/prototypes/udm/scripts/validate.mjs:274; the corpus run still reports "Core files naming a target in code: none" 3 The manifest uses only existing vocabulary checkManifest passes at registration (C0) 4 The adapter imports only the shared helpers and its own libraries List its imports; for the prototype Markdown adapter: marked and ../core/udm-runtime.mjs 5 Target-only data lives only in ext[manifest.id] C11 passes; a grep of the adapter for writes to other namespaces finds none 6 All conformance checks pass 45/45 (reversible) or 29/29 (write-only) on the shared fixtures 7 The corpus runs clean Native output valid for 383/383 layouts; text atoms surviving 100% 8 The engine did not change No new branch on the target id in the run pipeline; the run's response schema is built from the manifest alone 9 No other adapter changed git diff touches only the new adapter's folder and the registration line (or no registration line with entry points) 10 Losses are documented The loss codes the corpus produced are listed in the adapter's README When check 1 cannot pass, stop and decide which of two cases you are in: The UDM lacks a concept. The prototype found one: a second color or size inside one text element is flattened when the element is edited (44 of 3,582 elements), because the UDM has no neutral highlight mark. Adding it is a UDM change: a new mark in the vocabulary, a minor protocol bump, a fixture that uses it, and every adapter re-running the kit (those that do not support it get a mark_dropped entry automatically). It is made once, for all targets, never inside one adapter. Negotiation lacks a target-neutral rule. Like the five rules the prototype needed. The test is simple: can the rule be written using only manifest fields? If yes, it belongs in the core with a fixture. If it needs the target's name, it belongs in the adapter.

docs.t: Presenton internals, Parts I to VI
docs.p: Presenton internals, Parts I to VI
docs.x: Reads: README.md, start.js, nginx.conf, servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts · Builds on: Home · Time: ~8 min This is the entry point for the Presenton half of the book. It shows the whole running system on one diagram, then lists every chapter in Parts I to VI with a one-line description so you can jump straight to the subsystem you need. If you read nothing else before opening the code, read the diagram and the four chapters of Part I.

docs.t: The whole system on one page
docs.p: Presenton internals, Parts I to VI
docs.x: Presenton ships as one container (or one desktop app) that runs several cooperating processes. In the Docker image, node start.js supervises everything (start.js:720), nginx is the only listener reachable from outside, and every other server binds to the loopback interface. How to read it: nginx (nginx.conf:25) routes by path prefix. Pages and the Next.js-owned /api/* routes go to Next.js, the REST API goes to FastAPI, /mcp goes to the MCP server, and /app_data/... files are served straight from disk. Images, exports, uploads and the two PPTX conversion folders first pass an auth_request subrequest to FastAPI; fonts and template assets are served without one (nginx.conf:159-211). Next.js renders the UI. Its request middleware (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:97) and server layouts ask FastAPI whether the caller is signed in, over the loopback URL in FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL (start.js:485). FastAPI (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:65) owns the data model, the LLM calls, image and icon resolution, authentication, and API keys. The MCP server (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:346) is generated from a static OpenAPI document and forwards tool calls to FastAPI at http://127.0.0.1:8000. The export runtime is a Node script (presentation-export/runner.mjs, copied from scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs) that drives headless Chromium through @presenton/export-core. It opens the /pdf-maker page and writes PPTX or PDF files into app_data/exports. app_data is the only persistent state: the SQLite database (unless DATABASE_URL is set), userConfig.json, generated images, uploads, fonts, template assets, exports and Mem0 memory. The Electron desktop app runs the same FastAPI and Next.js code without nginx and without the MCP server. Runtime topology contrasts the two in detail.

docs.p: Presenton internals, Parts I to VI
docs.x: Start here. These chapters give you the mental map that every later chapter assumes. What Presenton is: the product surface (inputs, Standard and Smart modes, templates, editing, export, providers, deployment shapes, workspaces), a 30,000-foot walk from prompt to PPTX, and the core vocabulary. Repository tour: every top-level directory and FastAPI/Next.js subpackage with its key files, verified size statistics, the technology stack with exact versions, and a "where do I look for X" index. Runtime topology: the process tree under start.js, readiness and shutdown, the app_data layout and permissions, every nginx location block, and four request sequence diagrams. Running it locally: docker run, the four Compose services, a minimal .env, first-run admin setup, running from source without Docker, Electron dev, Swagger, API keys with curl, tests and troubleshooting.

docs.p: Presenton internals, Parts I to VI
docs.x: The FastAPI server, from process start to every generation path. FastAPI app and startup: the app object, router mounting, the middleware stack and the lifespan hook (migrations, admin bootstrap, template import). Configuration and LLM providers: how environment variables, userConfig.json and the provider-settings row combine, and how each LLM provider client is built. Data model: every SQLModel table, ownership columns, and the Alembic migration chain. docs.x: Source citations look like servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:29. Paths are relative to the repository root and line numbers refer to snapshot 571461f. Code excerpts are verbatim apart from elisions marked # ... or // .... Blocks titled Gotcha flag behavior that is easy to break or misread.
