Reads: README.md, VISION.md, docs/presentation-generation-modes.md, docs/template-v2.md, servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/constants/llm.py · Builds on: Part I landing · Time: ~25 min This chapter describes Presenton as a product, but every claim is pinned to the code that implements it. You will learn what goes in (prompts, documents, PPTX designs), the two generation modes and how PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE gates them, what ships as templates, how editing and export work, which model providers are supported, and which deployment shapes exist. The chapter ends with a 30,000-foot walk through one Standard generation, naming the function at each step, and a vocabulary table used by the rest of the book.

Presenton is an open-source (Apache 2.0) AI presentation generator. A user gives it a prompt, optionally with reference documents, chooses a design, and gets back a deck that is fully editable in the browser and exportable as an editable PPTX or a PDF. It runs self-hosted as a Docker web app or as an Electron desktop app, it exposes the same generation as a REST API and as an MCP server, and it lets you bring your own text and image model providers, including local ones such as Ollama and LM Studio (README.md:40-46). VISION.md frames the project as "an open source document engine, not a closed design platform", and the code reflects that: almost every behavior is configurable through environment variables or a Settings page, and nothing requires a hosted service except the optional Community gallery and the optional Presenton Cloud provider (README.md:356-369, README.md:563-582). The rest of this chapter goes through the product surface one feature at a time.

Presenton accepts three kinds of input. Each maps to concrete endpoints. Input How the user supplies it Where it enters the backend A prompt Text box on the upload page, or content in the API body POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1681) or POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate (presentation.py:3169) Pre-written slides slides_markdown, one Markdown string per slide (API only) GeneratePresentationRequest.slides_markdown (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:10); skips outline generation (presentation.py:2710-2711, presentation.py:2836-2844, see Standard generation pipeline) Reference documents File picker on the upload page, or files in the API body POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:79) stores files in a temp directory and returns their paths; DocumentsLoader (servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py:163) extracts text Your own PowerPoint design Custom template wizard The template endpoints under /api/v1/ppt/template (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:96), which convert a PPTX into a Template v2 design (see Custom templates from PPTX) The one-shot API accepts any combination of content, slides_markdown and files, but at least one must be non-empty. The check lives in check_if_api_request_is_valid (presentation.py:2620): servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES is 50 (servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:4). Each outline is capped at MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS words, read from the MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS environment variable and 100 by default (constants/presentation.py:5-23). Gotcha content is declared as a required field (content: str = Field(...), servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:9). A body that omits content entirely fails Pydantic validation with HTTP 422 before the check above runs, even if slides_markdown is present. Send "content": "" when you only want to supply slides_markdown or files. Generation can be tuned with tone (default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch, from servers/fastapi/enums/tone.py), verbosity (concise, standard, text-heavy, from servers/fastapi/enums/verbosity.py), language, instructions, include_title_slide, include_table_of_contents and web_search. Gotcha The README says language defaults to "English"

Presenton has two different generation engines that share the same database, editor and export path. Standard Smart Layouts Fixed layouts from a Template v2 design; the LLM only fills schema fields Adaptive HTML slides written by the LLM for the content Outline review Yes: outlines stream to an outline page where the user edits them and picks a template No: generation streams straight into the editor Templates Built-in and custom templates Not used (no template workflow) Stored slide SlideModel.content (JSON) plus SlideModel.ui (layout tree) SlideModel.html_content, with layout_group and layout set to "smart-html" (presentation.py:2062-2066) One-shot API POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate and /generate/async POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart and /generate/smart/async (servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:229, servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:264) Covered in Standard generation pipeline Smart mode In the browser both modes start from the same upload page. UploadPage.tsx creates the presentation row with generation_mode set, then routes to /outline for Standard or straight to /presentation for Smart (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx:517-525). On the server, stream_presentation checks the stored mode and hands Smart presentations to a separate streamer: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)

An operator chooses which modes users see with one environment variable. FastAPI parses it like this: servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py (excerpt) Next.js has a twin, normalizePresentationGenerationMode (servers/nextjs/utils/presentationGenerationMode.ts:7-21), with the same fallback to "both". The effect of each value: Value Web UI MCP tools exposed both (default, and any unknown value) Mode selector shown; Standard is selected first (getInitialGenerationMode, presentationGenerationMode.ts:30-34) Standard, template-generation, Smart and shared tools standard Selector hidden, always Standard; template pages available Standard, template-generation and shared tools smart Selector hidden, always Smart; /templates, /custom-template and /template-preview redirect to /dashboard (for example servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/templates/page.tsx:7-14) Smart tools plus the shared tools The "shared" tools are file upload (/api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload) and async task status (/api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id}), which every mode needs (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:88-99). The MCP side is implemented by choosing which OpenAPI routes become tools: servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py (excerpt) Gotcha PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE is a UI and MCP filter, not an access control. The REST endpoints for both modes stay mounted regardless of the value (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:68-74), and docs/presentation-generation-modes.md says so explicitly. If you need to forbid a mode, you must add a check in the endpoints. Gotcha The variable is read from the process environment of both servers at request time. In Docker both inherit it from the container, but if you run Next.js and FastAPI separately you must set the same value in both, and restart both after changing it.

A template is a Template v2 design: a JSON document of slide layouts on a 1280 by 720 canvas, each layout made of components, each component made of typed elements. Elements marked decorative: true are fixed artwork; the rest become fields in a JSON schema the LLM fills (docs/template-v2.md:116-117). Template v2 format covers the format. Sixteen built-in designs live in the top-level templates/ directory, one folder each with a template.json and a static/ folder of fonts and images. At startup, import_default_templates_on_startup (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:22) upserts each one into the TemplateV2 table with is_default=True and copies its static assets into app_data/templates/<id>/static (default_templates.py:295-301). Layout counts at this snapshot, counted from each template.json: Template Layouts Template Layouts civic 29 modern 10 dynamic 32 momentum 28 editorial 24 mosaic 34 executive 32 nova 28 general 12 pulse 28 horizon 28 signal 24 landmark 27 standard 11 verdant 27 swift 9 That is 383 layouts in total. The API default is general (generate_presentation_request.py:29-31). Custom templates are created from an uploaded PPTX: the export runtime converts the deck to raw element JSON, a vision-capable model certifies each slide into components and editable fields, and the result is stored as a private TemplateV2 row (docs/template-v2.md:7-14). See Custom templates from PPTX.

After generation the user lands in the editor at /presentation?id=.... Three editing paths exist: Direct manipulation. Template v2 slides render on a Konva canvas (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/surface/TemplateV2KonvaSlide.tsx) with drag, resize, alignment guides, and inline rich-text editing through Tiptap (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/TiptapInlineTextEditor.tsx). Changes flow into Redux and are saved with PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update or PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update (presentation.py:2527, presentation.py:2585). See Slide editor. AI slide edit. The user types an instruction for one slide. Standard slides go to POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:38), Smart slides to POST /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit-html (slide.py:135). Chat assistant. A conversational panel backed by POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message and POST /api/v1/ppt/chat/message/stream (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:105, chat.py:124), with tools and memory implemented under servers/fastapi/services/chat/. See Editing and chat assistant.

The deck exports as an editable PPTX or as a PDF. Both formats are produced the same way: a Node process runs presentation-export/runner.mjs, which calls runTask from the @presenton/export-core package (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:3, scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:116-119). That package drives headless Chromium against the /pdf-maker?id=... page of the Next.js app and writes the file into app_data/exports. The package version is pinned by "presentationExportVersion": "v1.0.51" in the root package.json and installed by scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs. PPTX and PDF export covers the details.

LLM selects the text provider. The accepted values are the members of LLMProvider (servers/fastapi/enums/llm_provider.py:4-20). Defaults come from servers/fastapi/constants/llm.py and are applied in get_model (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_provider.py:126-175): LLM Default model when the *_MODEL variable is unset openai gpt-4.1 deepseek deepseek-chat google models/gemini-2.5-flash vertex gemini-2.5-flash azure AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL, then AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT, then gpt-4.1 bedrock us.anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0 openrouter openai/gpt-4o fireworks accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3p1-8b-instruct together openai/gpt-oss-20b cerebras llama-3.3-70b anthropic claude-sonnet-4-20250514 litellm gpt-4.1 lmstudio openai/gpt-oss-20b ollama none (OLLAMA_MODEL must be set) custom none (CUSTOM_MODEL must be set; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) codex gpt-5.6-luna unless CODEX_MODEL is one of the supported Codex models (constants/llm.py:18-27) Two more provider paths exist outside that enum. LLM=presenton selects the optional Presenton Cloud provider, in which case maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request forwards generation requests to the hosted API instead of calling a model locally (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:407-460). And codex uses an OAuth sign-in with a ChatGPT account, which is why the Compose services publish host port 1455 for its callback (docker-compose.yml:11-12). Gotcha The README's provider table lists models/gemini-2.0-flash as the Google default and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 as the Anthropic default (README.md:392, README.md:426). The code defaults are models/gemini-2.5-flash and claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (constants/llm.py:6, constants/llm.py:14). When in doubt, trust constants/llm.py. An unset or unknown LLM fails at the first LLM call, not at startup, with HTTP 500 and the detail "Invalid LLM provider. Please select one of: ..." (utils/llm_provider.py:47-58). This is deliberate: the lifespan docstring says provider availability is checked when used, so account setup still works on an unconfigured instance (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:46-53). Provider configuration chapters: Configuration and LLM providers for text, Images, icons, web search for images and search.

IMAGE_PROVIDER selects how __image_prompt__ fields become pictures. Values come from ImageProvider (servers/fastapi/enums/image_provider.py:4-13): IMAGE_PROVIDER Kind Credentials pexels Stock search PEXELS_API_KEY pixabay Stock search PIXABAY_API_KEY gemini_flash Generation (Google) GOOGLE_API_KEY nanobanana_pro Generation (Google) GOOGLE_API_KEY gpt-image-2 Generation (OpenAI) OPENAI_API_KEY, quality from GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY gpt-image-1.5 Generation (OpenAI) OPENAI_API_KEY, quality from GPT_IMAGE_1_5_QUALITY comfyui Self-hosted generation COMFYUI_URL, COMFYUI_WORKFLOW open_webui Self-hosted generation OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_URL, OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_API_KEY openai_compatible Any /v1/images/* gateway OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_BASE_URL, _API_KEY, _MODEL The dispatcher is ImageGenerationService.generate_image (servers/fastapi/services/image_generation_service.py:187). Image generation can be turned off with DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION. Icons are not generated: __icon_query__ fields are matched against a bundled FastEmbed vector index of Phosphor icons (servers/fastapi/services/icon_finder_service.py:26-28, data in servers/fastapi/assets/icons-vectorstore.json).

Optional web grounding uses either the provider's native search (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic) or an external provider. WebSearchProvider lists auto, native, searxng, tavily, exa, brave and serper (servers/fastapi/enums/web_search_provider.py), although the README notes that Brave and Serper are hidden until tested (README.md:451).

Shape What runs Entry point Chapter Docker web app nginx, FastAPI, MCP, Next.js, optional Ollama in one container CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"] (Dockerfile:153), image ghcr.io/presenton/presenton Runtime topology, Docker build and deployment Electron desktop app FastAPI and Next.js on loopback ports chosen at launch, inside a desktop window; no nginx, no MCP electron/app/main.ts Electron desktop app REST API The same FastAPI routes, called with an sk-presenton-... API key POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate and friends REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP MCP server A FastMCP Streamable HTTP server at /mcp whose tools are generated from the OpenAPI document servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP The MCP tool names are fixed by a mapping from OpenAPI operation IDs (mcp_server.py:101-111): start_standard_presentation, start_smart_presentation, list_templates, upload_template_assets, start_template_generation, upload_files and get_job_status. Generation tools all return an async task ID that the client polls with get_job_status. Gotcha External REST and MCP access are server features. In Electron, PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true makes mcp_server.py exit immediately (mcp_server.py:319-321, mcp_server.py:419-424), and both HTTP servers reject any request that does not carry the per-launch desktop credential (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/desktop.py:25-48).

Presenton keeps a user table and scopes every owned row to a user. The first account created through /api/v1/auth/setup becomes the primary administrator (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:110-152); administrators create, reset and delete other accounts and issue API keys under /api/v1/admin (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:41). Isolation is enforced in three places: Request context. SessionAuthMiddleware resolves the caller from the presenton_session cookie or a bearer API key and stores the user ID in a context variable (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:94-128). Database. SQLAlchemy event hooks add owner_id == <current user> to every ORM SELECT on owned models and stamp owner_id on new rows (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:66-108). Built-in templates stay visible to everyone because the template filter also admits rows with owner_id IS NULL AND is_default (database.py:86-94). Files. Generated files go to per-user folders such as app_data/images/users/<user-id>/ (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23-30), and /app_data/... URLs are authorized per path segment (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:106-123). The Electron app runs auth-disabled and single-user. Auth and multi-user covers all of this in depth.

docs.t: Step 10: One generation, prompt to PPTX, at 30,000 feet
docs.x: Here is one Standard generation from the browser, with the module and function that does the work at each step. Each later chapter zooms into one or more of these steps. Collect the request. The upload page (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx) gathers prompt, slide count, language, tone, verbosity and toggles. If files were attached it first calls PresentationGenerationApi.uploadDoc (POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload). It then calls PresentationGenerationApi.createPresentation (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/presentation-generation.ts:82). Details: User journey. Create the row. create_presentation (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1682) validates the inputs and inserts a PresentationModel row with generation_mode="standard". Nothing has been generated yet. Details: Data model, Standard generation pipeline. Stream the outline. The outline page hook useOutlineStreaming opens GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/{id} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:108). stream_outlines (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:85) loads any documents, then iterates generate_ppt_outline (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:252), forwarding LLM chunks as server-sent events through safe_sse_stream (servers/fastapi/utils/sse.py:10). Details: Prompts and schemas, Streaming (SSE), Document ingestion. Review and prepare. The user edits outlines and picks a template. usePresentationGeneration calls presentationPrepare with {presentation_id, outlines, layout: <template id>} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/usePresentationGeneration.ts:107-111). prepare_presentation (presentation.py:1841) loads the template and converts it to per-layout JSON schemas through get_template_schema (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257, called from presentation.py:416), then asks the LLM to pick a layout index for each outline with generate_presentation_structure (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:157) and stores the result as presentation.structure. Details: From template to schema to slide. Stream the slides. The editor opens with stream=true, and usePresentationStreaming calls GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id}

These terms are used with exactly these meanings in the rest of the book. Term Meaning Where it lives Presentation One deck: the prompt, settings, outlines, chosen layout payload, structure, theme and fonts PresentationModel (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py) Outline Audience-facing Markdown for one slide, at most MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS words SlideOutlineModel.content (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_outline_model.py:8-21); stored in presentation.outlines Structure The list of layout indexes, one per slide PresentationStructureModel.slides: List[int] (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_structure_model.py:5-6); stored in presentation.structure Layout One slide design inside a template: an ID, a description and a list of components SlideLayout (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py:98); at generation time a SlideLayoutModel with a json_schema (presentation.py:450-456) Slide content The JSON the LLM returns for one slide, conforming to the layout's schema, including fields such as __speaker_note__, __image_prompt__ and __icon_query__ SlideModel.content (servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py:26) Template v2 A complete design: layouts, merged components, theme, fonts and assets TemplateV2 table (servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16); built-ins in templates/<name>/template.json Component A positioned group of elements with an ID and description, the unit the certification passes reason about Component (templates/v2/models/layouts.py:54-58) Element A typed visual primitive: text, image, container, text list, table, vector, chart, infographic and others servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py Decorative flag decorative: bool on an element; false turns the element into an LLM-filled schema field, true keeps it fixed for example Text.decorative (elements.py:218) Smart slide A slide produced in Smart mode: sanitized HTML in html_content, with layout_group and layout set to "smart-html" presentation.py:2062-2066; prompts in servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py Export runtime The presentation-export/ directory: runner.mjs plus node_modules/@presenton/export-core, driven by headless Chromium installed by scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs; checked by ExportTaskService._ensure_runtime_ready (export_task_service.py:202-220) app_data The persistent data root named by APP_DATA_DIRECTORY (/app_data in Docker):

Reads: start.js, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, nginx.conf, package.json, servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml, servers/nextjs/package.json, electron/package.json, .github/workflows/README.md · Builds on: What Presenton is · Time: ~30 min This chapter walks the repository directory by directory and names the two to five files in each place that you will actually open. It also records verified size statistics for the snapshot, the full technology stack with exact versions, and a "where do I look for X?" index you can come back to whenever you need to find code. Treat it as a map; the later chapters are the guided walks.

Everything in this book refers to one commit. You can re-derive every number below with the commands in the collapsible block. Fact Value Commit 571461f969beb1daa52cc68c5aaa9ba019530a35, dated 2026-11-01 Commits on that line 2,952 App version 0.9.12-beta (root package.json:3, electron/package.json:4) Export runtime pin v1.0.51 (root package.json:4) Python files in servers/fastapi, excluding tests/ 233 files, 58,185 lines Python test code in servers/fastapi/tests 114 test_*.py files, 31,899 lines in all .py files Alembic migrations 24 files in servers/fastapi/alembic/versions TypeScript in servers/nextjs (app, components, lib, store, utils, types) about 113,900 lines Built-in templates 16, with 383 layouts in total Commands that reproduce these numbers The FastAPI line count breaks down as api 10,204, services 17,559 (of which services/chat is 11,201), templates 14,283, utils 11,598 (of which utils/llm_calls is 2,255), alembic 1,801, models 1,222, constants 521, enums 84 and scripts 75, plus the top-level modules. The largest single Python files are servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (4,633 lines, PPTX template certification), servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py (4,131) and servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (3,393).

docs.t: Step 2: The root of the repository
docs.x: File What it is start.js (738 lines) The container entry point (CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"], Dockerfile:153). Creates app_data directories, verifies the export runtime, writes userConfig.json from environment variables, starts nginx, then spawns FastAPI, the MCP server, Next.js and optionally Ollama. Runtime topology walks it line by line. Dockerfile (153 lines) Four stages: fastapi-builder (Python 3.11 venv via uv, spaCy model, FastEmbed cache warm-up), nextjs-builder (npm ci, next build), assets-builder (LiteParse dependencies and sync-presentation-export.cjs --force), and runtime (Debian trixie with pinned Chromium, nginx, Noto fonts, Tesseract, Node 22). See Docker build and deployment. Dockerfile.dev (93 lines) A single-stage development image that installs the same system packages, installs Python dependencies into the system interpreter, and runs node /app/start.js --dev (Dockerfile.dev:93). It expects the repository to be bind-mounted at /app. docker-compose.yml (534 lines) Four services: production, production-gpu, development, development-gpu, plus three named volumes for the development services. Each service forwards about 110 environment variables. See Running it locally. nginx.conf (213 lines) The only external listener (port 80). Routes / to Next.js, /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ to FastAPI, /mcp to the MCP server, and serves /app_data/... and /static/ from disk. Copied to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf by Dockerfile:150. layouts.json (247 KB) A Template v2 layout sample: {"layouts": {"layouts": [...]}} with 14 layouts (IDs such as business_proposal_cover_layout), each with id, description and components. Its image URLs point at http://127.0.0.1:8000/app_data/pptx-to-json/..., so it is the output of a PPTX conversion. No code at this snapshot references the file by name. package.json (26 lines) Root Node project: version 0.9.12-beta, presentationExportVersion v1.0.51, dependencies @llamaindex/liteparse and sharp, and the scripts sync:presentation-export, check:presentation-export, convert:template, convert:presentation-template and test. package-lock.json Lock file for the root project; also fingerprinted by scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs to decide whether the LiteParse runtime must be reinstalled. test-local.sh (83 lines) Runs the same three check groups as the test-all.yml workflow: repository tooling, the FastAPI pytest suite, and Next.js tests,

The backend is one Python package named presenton-backend (servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:6) with requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.12". Setuptools packages api, enums, models, services, constants, utils and templates (pyproject.toml:48-58). The server is always started with the working directory set to servers/fastapi, because get_resource_path resolves bundled assets relative to os.getcwd() (servers/fastapi/utils/path_helpers.py:15-17).

File Role server.py 29-line launcher: parses --port (required), --reload ("true" or not) and --log-level, then runs uvicorn.run("api.main:app", host="127.0.0.1", ...) (server.py:21-29). mcp_server.py 480 lines. Builds a FastMCP server from openai_spec.json and serves it with the Streamable HTTP transport on 127.0.0.1:8001 (mcp_server.py:457-466). migrations.py 329 lines. Runs Alembic on startup when MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP is "true" or "True" (migrations.py:42-45), with special handling for databases created before Alembic was introduced. openai_spec.json A static OpenAPI document (despite the name, it has nothing to do with OpenAI) consumed by the MCP server. Regenerate it with scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py. server.spec PyInstaller spec used by npm run build:fastapi in electron/ to freeze the backend for desktop builds. alembic.ini Alembic configuration; scripts live in alembic/. uv.lock, pyproject.toml Dependency pins.

The HTTP layer. api/main.py creates the app and mounts seven routers (api/main.py:68-74), mounts /app_data/<root> and /static file servers (api/main.py:77-86), and adds CORS, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware and SessionAuthMiddleware (api/main.py:94-103). api/lifespan.py runs migrations, admin bootstrap and template import at startup. Path Prefix Key files api/v1/ppt/ /api/v1/ppt endpoints/presentation.py (create, prepare, stream, generate, export), endpoints/outlines.py, endpoints/slide.py, endpoints/template.py, endpoints/chat.py, endpoints/files.py, endpoints/images.py, endpoints/icons.py, endpoints/fonts.py, plus provider helpers (openai.py, google.py, anthropic.py, ollama.py, openrouter.py, codex_auth.py) api/v1/auth/ /api/v1/auth router.py (status, verify, setup, login, logout), principal.py, users.py, assets.py, bootstrap.py, desktop.py, presenton_oauth.py api/v1/admin/ /api/v1/admin router.py (API keys, users, provider settings) api/v1/async_tasks/ /api/v1/async-tasks router.py (task status polling) api/v1/webhook/ /api/v1/webhook router.py (subscribe, unsubscribe) api/v1/mock/ /api/v1/mock router.py (sample webhook payloads) api/v2/ppt/ /api/v2/ppt endpoints/presentation.py (Smart /generate/smart and /generate/smart/async) api/middlewares.py (all) SessionAuthMiddleware, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware

models/ holds Pydantic request and response models: generate_presentation_request.py, presentation_outline_model.py, presentation_structure_model.py, presentation_layout.py, sse_response.py, user_config.py and others. models/sql/ holds 15 table modules: 13 SQLModel tables plus user.py and presenton_cloud_provider.py, which use a plain SQLAlchemy DeclarativeBase (models/sql/user.py:12-19) so they work with fastapi-users. They include presentation.py, slide.py, template_v2.py, user.py, api_key.py, async_task.py, provider_settings.py, image_asset.py, chat_history_message.py and webhook_subscription.py. See Data model.

Stateful or I/O-heavy components. database.py: engine, async_session_maker, owner-scoping event hooks (services/database.py:66-108), create_db_and_tables. export_task_service.py: spawns the Node export runtime with a 300-second timeout (services/export_task_service.py:122). image_generation_service.py: one method per image provider (services/image_generation_service.py:132). icon_finder_service.py: FastEmbed vector search over Phosphor icons. documents_loader.py and liteparse_service.py: document text extraction. chat/: the assistant (service.py, tools.py, memory_layer.py, prompts.py). Also: api_keys.py, async_tasks.py, webhook_service.py, provider_settings.py, mem0_presentation_memory_service.py, presenton_cloud_proxy.py, concurrent_service.py, temp_file_service.py.

Pure helpers and configuration readers. The ones you will open most: get_env.py: one getter per environment variable. user_config.py: merges userConfig.json into the environment. llm_config.py and llm_provider.py: build LLM client configurations and resolve model names. process_slides.py: resolves __image_prompt__ and __icon_query__ into URLs. sse.py: safe_sse_stream. export_utils.py: export_presentation. asset_directory_utils.py: per-user directories and path resolution. web_search.py: grounding. utils/llm_calls/ holds one module per LLM task: generate_presentation_outlines.py, generate_presentation_structure.py, generate_slide_content.py, generate_smart_presentation.py, edit_slide.py, edit_slide_html.py, select_slide_type_on_edit.py and generate_web_search_query.py. Prompts live inside these modules. See Prompts and schemas.

Gotcha There are two directories named templates. The top-level templates/ holds the 16 design folders (data). servers/fastapi/templates/ is a Python package (code) that loads, previews and converts templates. The production Compose service bind-mounts the code package read-only from the host (docker-compose.yml:15), which replaces the image's copy of that Python code; it does not affect the design folders. The Python package contains default_templates.py (imports the built-in designs at startup), pptx_font_utils.py (font catalog; the Docker build asserts it is non-empty, Dockerfile:22), fonts_and_slides_preview.py, presentation_layout.py, preview.py and assets/fonts.json. Its v2/ subpackage is the Template v2 engine: schema.py: turns layouts into JSON schemas (get_template_schema, templates/v2/schema.py:257). generation.py and certified_generation.py: the PPTX-to-template pipeline. theme.py: theme roles. content.py and tools.py: content helpers. models/layouts.py and models/elements.py: the Pydantic models of layouts, components and elements. See Template v2 format.

enums/ has eight small enums: LLMProvider, ImageProvider, WebSearchProvider, Tone, Verbosity, AsyncTaskStatus, WebhookEvent and LLMCallType. constants/ has llm.py (default models), presentation.py (MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES = 50, outline word limit, default template order), documents.py (accepted upload types) and supported_ollama_models.py.

alembic/env.py, script.py.mako and 24 revision files under alembic/versions/, from 00b3c27a13bc_init.py to the head 026c0ba8b35c_add_async_task_payload_and_unified_api_.py (REVISION_HEAD, migrations.py:36-37). See Data model.

114 test_*.py files: 95 in tests/unit, 6 in tests/integration, 1 each in tests/regression and tests/edge_cases, the rest at the top level, plus conftest.py and shared mocks/. pyproject.toml:72-73 sets testpaths = ["tests"]. See CI, tests, security.

static/ is served at /static/: icons/ (Phosphor icons in six weights, bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin, with 1,512 SVGs in bold alone, plus placeholder.svg), images/ (placeholder.jpg, replaceable_template_image.png) and vendor/ (Chart.js 4.5.1, chartjs-plugin-datalabels 2.2.0 and the Tailwind browser runtime 4.3.3, each with its license). assets/ holds icons.json (9,072 icon entries with tags) and icons-vectorstore.json, the prebuilt embedding index loaded by IconFinderService. scripts/ has generate_openapi_spec.py (rewrites openai_spec.json from app.openapi()) and warm_fastembed_cache.py (downloads FastEmbed weights during the Docker build).

A Next.js 16.4.1 app with output: "standalone" and distDir: ".next-build" (servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:8-11). Its request middleware is proxy.ts at the project root, which Next.js 16 runs for every request matched by config.matcher (proxy.ts:174-176).

Route group or folder URLs What it holds app/page.tsx / Shows AuthGate (setup or sign in) or the home screen (app/page.tsx:7-26) app/(presentation-generator)/upload /upload Prompt, settings, document upload, mode selector app/(presentation-generator)/outline /outline Outline streaming, editing and template selection app/(presentation-generator)/presentation /presentation The editor and its streaming hooks app/(presentation-generator)/documents-preview /documents-preview Review extracted document content before generation app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template /custom-template PPTX to Template v2 wizard app/(presentation-generator)/template-preview /template-preview Preview a template's layouts app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/... /dashboard, /templates, /community, /settings, /admin Dashboard shell pages app/(export)/pdf-maker /pdf-maker The page the export runtime renders app/api/... /api/export-presentation, /api/export-presentation/file, /api/export-presentation-data/[id], /api/user-config, /api/runtime-config, /api/has-required-key, /api/read-file, /api/upload-image, /api/update-svg, /api/telemetry-status, /api/github-stars Next.js route handlers (Node runtime) The (presentation-generator) layout calls requireAppSession() before rendering any child (app/(presentation-generator)/layout.tsx:6-13), which redirects to / when there is no session.

components/: shared React components. slide-editor/ (about 48,000 lines) is the Konva-based Template v2 editor, with its own README.md. Auth/ holds AuthGate.tsx and LogoutButton.tsx. OnBoarding/ holds the onboarding steps. ui/ holds Radix-based primitives. runtime/ holds the Tailwind browser runtime used for Smart slides. Provider configuration forms such as LLMSelection.tsx and OpenAIConfig.tsx sit at the top level. lib/: server-side helpers. run-bundled-presentation-export.ts spawns the export runtime. template-v2-json-to-html.ts (4,145 lines) renders layouts to HTML. desktop-auth.ts holds the Electron guard. fastapi-internal.ts resolves the FastAPI URL. Also server-auth-role.ts and runtime-provider-config.ts. store/: Redux Toolkit. store.ts combines four slices: presentationGeneration, pptGenUpload, userConfig and undoRedo (store/store.ts:7-14). utils/: browser and server utilities. api.ts provides getApiUrl and the same-origin rule. serverAuth.ts provides getServerAuthStatus and requireAppSession. auth.ts provides isAuthDisabled. Also presentationGenerationMode.ts and providerConstants.ts. types/: global.d.ts (the window.env and window.electron shapes) and llm_config.ts. tests/: 27 node --test files (*.test.mjs) run by npm test ("test": "node --test"). cypress/: component-test support (support/), fixtures and security specs (security/). Seven *.cy.tsx component specs live next to the components they test. See Next.js architecture.

Each of the 16 folders contains template.json and static/ (fonts and images referenced by relative paths such as static/Montserrat Bold.ttf). The top-level keys of every template.json are id, name, description, thumbnail, merged_components, layouts, fonts and theme, and most also have icon_type (for example civic uses regular, standard uses bold). fonts maps a family name either to a bundled file (civic) or to a Google Fonts CSS URL (general, standard). Template Layouts Template Layouts civic 29 modern 10 dynamic 32 momentum 28 editorial 24 mosaic 34 executive 32 nova 28 general 12 pulse 28 horizon 28 signal 24 landmark 27 standard 11 verdant 27 swift 9 constants/presentation.py:25-56 discovers these folders and orders them momentum, dynamic, executive, general, modern, standard, swift, then the rest alphabetically. templates/default_templates.py:58-59 resolves the folder as three levels above the Python package, so in Docker it is /app/templates (Dockerfile:131).

app/main.ts (547 lines) is the main process: finds two free ports, generates a per-launch desktop token, starts FastAPI and Next.js, and opens the window. app/utils/servers.ts spawns the servers; in development it runs uv run python server.py --port <n> --reload true and npm run dev -- -H 127.0.0.1 -p <n> (electron/app/utils/servers.ts:137-139, servers.ts:207-211). app/utils/desktop-auth.ts holds the desktop credential. app/ipc/export_handlers.ts handles exports over IPC. app/preloads/ holds the preload scripts. resources/document-extraction/liteparse_runner.mjs is the LiteParse runner shared with Docker (Dockerfile:65). scripts/ holds build helpers: sync-export-runtime.cjs, prepare-export-chromium.cjs, build-nextjs-resources.cjs, copy-templates.cjs and others. build.js is the electron-builder driver. version.json is the release message and download links. package.json pins Electron 42.11.16 and electron-builder 26.15.0 and defines setup:env, dev, build:all and dist. See Electron desktop app.

File Purpose sync-presentation-export.cjs Downloads presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz from the presenton/presenton-export GitHub releases and installs it into presentation-export/ (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:170-172). Flags: --force, --check-only, --allow-version-override. run-presentation-export.mjs Copied to presentation-export/runner.mjs. Reads a task JSON, calls runTask from @presenton/export-core, fixes permissions, writes <task>.response.json. export-permissions.cjs finalizeExportPermissions: gives export artifacts the nginx group and strips world access. sync-document-dependencies.cjs Installs and fingerprints the LiteParse runtime in document-extraction-liteparse/. user-config-env.cjs buildUserConfigFromEnv, used by start.js to write userConfig.json. presenton-terminal-banner.mjs, presenton-ascii.txt The startup banner. run-node-script.mjs fork wrapper used by start.js. convert-template.mjs, convert-presentation-template.mjs Convert template or presentation JSON into the packaged template format. rebuild_notice_all.py Regenerates NOTICE. *.test.mjs, glob-security-checks.cjs Tests run by root npm test.

docs/ contains presentation-generation-modes.md, template-v2.md, amazon-bedrock.md, multi-docker-build.md (manual multi-architecture image release), presenton-resource-usage.md (a k6 load-test report of the five-call Standard workflow) and macos/dev/* (signing and notarization guides). .github/workflows/ contains: test-all.yml: three jobs, test-repository-tools, test-fastapi and test-nextjs, on push and pull request to main. codeql.yml: CodeQL for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions. export-runtime-regressions.yml: repository tools on a matrix of operating systems. docker-release.yml: multi-architecture image on release. electron-linux-ubuntu22.yml: test release build. sync-releaes-to-r2.yml: uploads release assets to R2. The misspelling is in the file name. docs-pages.yml: publishes this tutorial. It is not part of upstream Presenton. .github/workflows/README.md documents how to run each group locally. See CI, tests, security.

Reads: start.js, nginx.conf, servers/fastapi/server.py, servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts, scripts/export-permissions.cjs, electron/app/main.ts · Builds on: Repository tour · Time: ~35 min

This chapter is about what is running once a Presenton container has started, not how the image is built (that is Docker build and deployment). You will follow start.js from its first line to the point where it parks forever, learn exactly which process listens on which port and how readiness and shutdown work, map every directory under app_data to the code that writes it, read every nginx location block, and trace four representative requests end to end: a page load, an authenticated API call, a protected image fetch, and an MCP tool call.

docs.t: Step 1: The process tree at a glance
docs.x: In the production image the container command is CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"] (Dockerfile:153). The development image runs CMD ["node", "/app/start.js", "--dev"] (Dockerfile.dev:93). start.js is a small supervisor: it prepares the filesystem, starts nginx as a system service, and spawns four kinds of children. Process Bind address Started at Watched by start.js? Logs nginx 0.0.0.0:80 (listen 80, nginx.conf:26) start.js:696-718 No (only the service command's exit code) /var/log/nginx/error.log (nginx.conf:4) FastAPI (uvicorn) 127.0.0.1:8000 (servers/fastapi/server.py:21-28) start.js:521-536, 601-606 Yes forwarded to container stdout/stderr MCP server (FastMCP) 127.0.0.1:8001 (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:457-465) start.js:608-620 No discarded (stdio: "ignore") Next.js 127.0.0.1:3000 start.js:538-566, 622-627 Yes forwarded Ollama (optional) Ollama's default start.js:661-670 Yes (no restart) inherited Only port 80 is meant to be reachable from outside the container. FastAPI hard-codes host = "127.0.0.1" (servers/fastapi/server.py:21), Next.js is told -H 127.0.0.1 or HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1, and FastMCP runs on host="127.0.0.1". The Compose files also publish 1455:1455 for the Codex OAuth callback (docker-compose.yml:12), which is unrelated to the four servers above.

docs.t: Step 2: What happens before main() runs
docs.x: start.js does real work at module load time, before main() is called.

process.umask(0o022) (start.js:28) makes every file and directory created by the supervisor and its children default to group/other read but not write. Then: start.js (excerpt) The ports are constants (start.js:46-48); there is no environment variable to change them. Both Dockerfiles set APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/app_data and TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton (Dockerfile:82-83, Dockerfile.dev:10-11).

ensureAppDataDirectories() runs at start.js:103. It creates the data root and seven asset directories with mode 0755, then tightens the three directories that hold export output: start.js (excerpt) chmodBestEffort (start.js:73-82) swallows EPERM and EACCES, so a volume owned by another UID (the comment mentions Kubernetes/OpenShift PVCs) does not crash startup. Immediately afterwards userConfig.json and userConfig.json.bak are forced to 0600 if they exist (start.js:104-106). ensureReadableExportFiles calls finalizeExportPermissions(dirPath, [appDataDirectory], { recursive: true, legacy: true }) from scripts/export-permissions.cjs:37-64. When the process runs as root it looks up the www-data (or nginx) group in /etc/group (scripts/export-permissions.cjs:4-16), chowns each path to that group, sets files to 0640, and for directories in legacy mode keeps the existing mode but strips the "other" bits (stat.mode & 0o7770, scripts/export-permissions.cjs:27-30). It walks upward from the export directory to the boundary root (app_data itself), so app_data, exports, pptx-to-html and pptx-to-json end up group-readable by the nginx worker user but not world-readable. Gotcha nginx runs its workers as user www-data (nginx.conf:1) and serves /app_data/... straight from disk with alias. If you change the nginx user, or run the container as a non-root UID without a www-data group, exported files may become unreadable to nginx and downloads fail with 403/404 from nginx even though FastAPI produced the file. The export runtime calls the same helper after each export (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:123, servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:269-280).

docs.t: 2.3 Environment variables start.js sets for its children
docs.x: start.js (excerpt) Variable Value Consumers USER_CONFIG_PATH /app_data/userConfig.json FastAPI utils/get_env.py:63-64 (provider settings, auth secret), Next.js lib/fastapi-internal.ts:27, user-config route handlers FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 unless already set Next.js proxy.ts:10-23, utils/serverAuth.ts:17-30, lib/fastapi-internal.ts:3-13 HOSTNAME, PORT 127.0.0.1, 3000 only for the standalone Next.js server (start.js:557-562) Every child is spawned with env: process.env, so all container environment variables (provider keys, PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE, DATABASE_URL and the rest) reach FastAPI, MCP and Next.js unchanged.
start.js (excerpt)

Skipped when ENSURE_PRESENTATION_EXPORT_RUNTIME === "false" or when scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs is absent. Otherwise it runs node scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --check-only. The check (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:253-286, 359-366) verifies that presentation-export/runner.mjs, node_modules/@presenton/export-core/package.json and presenton-export-version.json exist, that the installed version equals presentationExportVersion in the root package.json (v1.0.51 at this snapshot), that the sharp native runtime is valid, and that export-permissions.cjs was copied in. Production: a failed check throws presentation-export runtime is missing in this container image. Rebuild the image so the runtime package is installed. (start.js:457-461). Because main() is not awaited with a catch, the unhandled rejection terminates Node and the container exits. Development: it warns and runs the same script with --force, which downloads presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz from GitHub releases (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, 382-394).

If START_OLLAMA is truthy (anything except empty, 0, false, no, off, start.js:418-426) and neither /usr/bin/ollama nor /usr/local/bin/ollama exists, it runs curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh. The production image sets START_OLLAMA=false (Dockerfile:91).

With --dev (or -d, start.js:43): npm ci inside servers/nextjs (start.js:171-195), then scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs (start.js:225-227), which installs the LiteParse document-extraction dependencies.

start.js (excerpt) readUserConfig() falls back to userConfig.json.bak when the main file is missing or corrupt (start.js:126-127). readUserConfigEnv picks only the keys in USER_CONFIG_ENV_KEYS (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:20-116), ignoring empty strings. buildUserConfigFromEnv merges env over the existing file, converts boolean-like and integer values, and picks a default IMAGE_PROVIDER when none is given (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:186-222). writeUserConfig is crash-safe: it copies the current file to .bak, writes a unique temp file opened with wx and mode 0600, fsyncs it, then renames it over the target (start.js:140-168). The details of the merge and how FastAPI consumes it belong to Configuration and LLM providers. Gotcha On the first FastAPI startup, migrate_provider_settings_from_file copies userConfig.json into a ProviderSettings database row. On every later startup the database row is mirrored back over the file, keeping only AUTH_* keys from the file (servers/fastapi/services/provider_settings.py:85-127). So editing provider variables in docker-compose.yml after the first boot does not reliably change the active provider: start.js writes them, then FastAPI's lifespan replaces them with the stored settings. Change providers in the Settings UI instead.
In dev only, copies the bind-mounted /app/nginx.conf to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf, so nginx changes in your working tree take effect on container restart without rebuilding.

Runs service nginx start. The init script daemonizes nginx and exits; the promise resolves true on exit code 0 and false otherwise. It never rejects. Gotcha nginx is not in the supervisor's managed set. If nginx fails to start, start.js only logs Nginx failed to start with exit code: ... and keeps running FastAPI and Next.js, so the container looks healthy while port 80 refuses connections. If nginx dies later, nothing notices.

Spawn order: FastAPI, MCP, Next.js, then optional Ollama. Command lines: Child Command Working dir FastAPI python server.py --port 8000 --reload false (true in dev) servers/fastapi MCP python mcp_server.py --port 8001 servers/fastapi Next.js, production node servers/nextjs/server.js with HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 PORT=3000 (only if server.js exists, start.js:539) servers/nextjs Next.js, dev or no standalone build node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next dev --webpack -H 127.0.0.1 -p 3000 (or start instead of dev --webpack) servers/nextjs Ollama ollama serve / server.py simply parses --port, --reload and --log-level (default info) and calls uvicorn.run("api.main:app", host="127.0.0.1", ...) (servers/fastapi/server.py:6-28). Everything about the FastAPI app itself (lifespan, migrations, admin bootstrap, routers, middleware) is in FastAPI app and startup.

start.js (excerpt) Next.js readiness (both modes) is a regex match on any stdout or stderr line (start.js:269-330). FastAPI readiness in production is an HTTP probe: GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/status, 1 second per attempt, retried every 250 ms, giving up after 60 seconds (start.js:332-416). Any HTTP response counts as ready, whatever its status code (start.js:373-376). /api/v1/auth/status is listed in SessionAuthMiddleware._PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:30-36), so it answers before any admin exists. In dev, FastAPI readiness is uvicorn's Application startup complete. line, which appears only after the lifespan (migrations, template import) finishes. Promise.all([fastApi, nextjs, nginx]) gates only the startup banner (start.js:681-690). On failure it logs Skipping startup banner: .... Readiness never kills anything. In production forwardProcessOutput(..., { suppressStartupUrls: true }) hides lines such as Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (start.js:229-234, 644-656) so users are not misled into opening internal loopback ports; the banner prints the public URL instead.

start.js (excerpt) Situation Behavior Production, FastAPI/Next.js/Ollama exits (any code) shutdown(exitCode): kill every managed child, process.exit(exitCode); the container stops Dev, FastAPI or Next.js exits with code 0 restart after 1 s; the new child gets stdio: ["ignore", "inherit", "inherit"] (start.js:602-605, 623-626) Dev, non-zero exit or killed by a signal same as production: whole container exits Ollama exits (any mode) no restart function is passed (start.js:670), so shutdown MCP server exits nothing happens; the process is not watched SIGINT / SIGTERM to Node shutdown(0) (start.js:518-519) Gotcha The MCP server is spawned with stdio: "ignore" and no exit watcher (start.js:608-620). If mcp_server.py crashes on startup (for example because openai_spec.json is missing or malformed), /mcp returns nginx 502 forever and there are no logs anywhere. Run python mcp_server.py --port 8001 by hand inside the container to see its DEBUG: and ERROR: output. After startServers returns its spawn work it awaits a never-resolving promise (start.js:692), which keeps the Node event loop alive.

APP_DATA_DIRECTORY (/app_data in Docker, a bind mount ./app_data:/app_data in every Compose service) is the only persistent state.
