normally empty because the bundled servers/fastapi/assets/icons-vectorstore.json is used (servers/fastapi/services/icon_finder_service.py:53-58) FastAPI Per-user subfolders come from _owned_directory (asset_directory_utils.py:23-30): when a request has an owner (set by the auth middleware), files go under <root>/users/<owner_id>/. Files left in the root by pre-multi-user versions are "legacy" and only the admin may read them

nginx.conf has one server on port 80. Global settings: worker_connections 1024, client_max_body_size 100M (nginx.conf:7, 13), and two maps that keep X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host from an outer proxy, falling back to $scheme and $http_host (nginx.conf:16-23). Location Upstream / target Auth Body limit Timeouts Notes / (:29) http://localhost:3000 (Next.js) none at nginx; Next.js layouts and proxy.ts 100M read 30m, connect 30m WebSocket Upgrade/Connection headers (Next dev HMR); Host $http_host keeps the port /api/v1/ (:45) http://localhost:8000 (path kept) FastAPI SessionAuthMiddleware 110M read/send/connect 30m error_page 413 = @request_entity_too_large /api/v2/ (:59) http://localhost:8000 FastAPI 100M (inherited) 30m no custom 413 body @request_entity_too_large (:71) returns 413 n/a n/a n/a body {"detail":"File size must be less than 100MB."} /mcp/ and /mcp (:77, :94) http://localhost:8001/mcp/ and /mcp bearer API key checked inside FastMCP 145M read/connect 30m forces Host: localhost:8001, forwards public host in X-Forwarded-Host /docs (:110) http://localhost:8000/docs FastAPI (protected path) 100M 30m uses $host and $scheme, not the forwarded maps /openapi.json (:120) http://localhost:8000/openapi.json FastAPI (protected path) 100M 30m same as /docs = /_auth_check (:133) http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/verify internal only body dropped defaults sends X-Original-URI, Cookie, Authorization /static/ (:153) alias /app/servers/fastapi/static/ none n/a n/a expires 1y, Cache-Control: public, immutable /app_data/images/, exports/, uploads/, pptx-to-html/, pptx-to-json/ alias /app_data/<root>/ auth_request /_auth_check n/a n/a disable_symlinks on, Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000 /app_data/fonts/, /app_data/templates/ alias none n/a n/a same caching; matches SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS (assets.py:17) nginx picks the longest matching prefix, so /api/v1/... never reaches Next.js and /app_data/images/... never reaches FastAPI in Docker. There is no location for /redoc; it falls to / and Next.js answers 404.

nginx.conf (excerpt) This is the classic nginx "alias traversal" misconfiguration: with location /static plus alias .../static/, nginx substitutes the matched prefix and the rest of the URI (../server.py) is appended verbatim. Ending both the location and the alias with / closes it. Gotcha When you add a new alias location (for example a new asset root), always end both the location prefix and the alias path with a slash, keep disable_symlinks on for user-writable roots, and add the root to PRIVATE_APP_DATA_ROOTS or SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS in servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:10-17. Otherwise /_auth_check returns 403 for every file in it, because _namespace_authorized rejects unknown roots (assets.py:111-112).

docs.t: Step 7: Sequence (a), a browser page load
docs.x: Take GET /dashboard with a valid session cookie. nginx matches location / and forwards to localhost:3000 (nginx.conf:29-43). proxy.ts runs for every path except _next/static and favicon.ico (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:174-176). For page paths it first runs desktopRequestDenied (a no-op unless PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true, servers/nextjs/lib/desktop-auth.ts:14-15), then returns NextResponse.next() (proxy.ts:103-105). The (presentation-generator) layout calls requireAppSession() (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/layout.tsx:6-7), which fetches ${FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL}/api/v1/auth/status with the incoming cookie (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:37-58). It redirects to / when FastAPI is unreachable or no admin exists, and to /?reason=unauthorized when not signed in (serverAuth.ts:93-107). The response to /api/v1/auth/status looks like this (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:71-78): Page-level guarding is covered in Settings, onboarding, auth UI.

docs.t: Step 8: Sequence (b), an authenticated API call
docs.x: Browser code builds FastAPI URLs with getApiUrl(), which in the Docker web runtime returns a same-origin relative path such as /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:123-141, resolveBackendPathForRuntime at api.ts:88-98). So the request goes to nginx, not to Next.js. The middleware stack, outermost first, is: the static_icon_fallback_middleware function middleware, SessionAuthMiddleware, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, then CORSMiddleware (Starlette runs the last-added middleware first, servers/fastapi/api/main.py:94-118). SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:55-152) does, in order: Desktop guard (desktop_request_denied), then the auth-disabled branch for Electron. Pass through OPTIONS, public auth paths, and paths that do not require auth (_requires_auth, middlewares.py:44-53: everything under /api/, /app_data/ except fonts and templates, plus /docs, /openapi.json, /redoc). 428 when the user table is empty (middlewares.py:83-94). resolve_request_principal (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22-57): cookie JWT first, then Authorization: Bearer <token> checked as an API key. Failure gives 401. Admin-only paths (/api/v1/admin/, Codex auth, font POST/DELETE, model listings, /api/v1/ppt/images/test) require a browser JWT from an admin, otherwise 403 Admin browser session required (middlewares.py:100-119). Store the principal on request.state, mint an internal JWT for API-key callers (used later by the exporter), set owner context variables, and call the route.

In Docker, /api/v1/* and /api/v2/* never reach Next.js because nginx routes them first. Next.js's own route handlers do reach it: servers/nextjs/app/api/ contains export-presentation, export-presentation-data/[id], read-file, runtime-config, telemetry-status, update-svg, upload-image, user-config, has-required-key and github-stars. For those, proxy.ts:138-171 applies: Condition Result DISABLE_AUTH truthy pass through (continueRequest) OPTIONS, or path is /api/v1/auth/*, /api/telemetry-status, /api/update-svg, /api/export-presentation-data/* pass through Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... if FastAPI path, rewrite to FastAPI, else 403 API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API cookie valid per GET {FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL}/api/v1/auth/status pass through no admin configured 428 {"detail":"Login setup is required","setup_required":true} otherwise 401 {"detail":"Unauthorized"} continueRequest rewrites /api/v1 and /api/v2 paths to the FastAPI base URL and lets other paths fall to the Next.js handler (proxy.ts:51-55). The rewrite branch matters when Next.js is reached without nginx (local next dev and Electron). getAuthStatus treats any fetch failure as {configured: true, authenticated: false} (proxy.ts:65-85), so a down FastAPI produces 401, not 428. Gotcha API keys are rejected by Next.js route handlers on purpose (proxy.ts:146-156). A script that calls /api/export-presentation with Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... gets 403. Use the FastAPI endpoints such as POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export instead; see REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.t: Step 9: Sequence (c), a protected image under /app_data/images
docs.x: Generated images are stored as files and referenced in slide JSON by URL, for example /app_data/images/users/6f1c.../a1b2.png. In Docker the filesystem path and the URL path coincide because APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is /app_data. verify_session (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:81-107) is public at the middleware level (it is in _PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS) and does its own check. It calls is_app_data_path_authorized(original_uri, ...) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:78-103), which: Decodes the path up to 8 times until stable, failing closed on deeper nesting, and rejects NUL bytes, backslashes, empty, . and .. segments (assets.py:47-75). Allows fonts and templates for everyone; for the five private roots requires users/<caller-id>/<file> (at least three segments) or, for legacy root-level files, an admin (assets.py:106-123). Re-checks the canonical realpath target relative to the root, so a symlink cannot alias another user's folder (assets.py:89-103). Gotcha nginx auth_request treats only 2xx as allow and 401/403 as deny; any other status from /api/v1/auth/verify (for example a 500 while the database is locked) becomes a 500 to the browser. Broken images during heavy SQLite contention usually come from this subrequest, not from the file itself. Outside Docker, the same URL is served by FastAPI's own _OwnerScopedStaticFiles mounts (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:20-44, mounted in servers/fastapi/api/main.py:77-82), with SessionAuthMiddleware returning 404 Asset not found for unauthorized paths (middlewares.py:138-148). The response code for "not yours" therefore differs: 403 behind nginx, 404 without it.

docs.t: Step 10: Sequence (d), an MCP client call to /mcp
docs.x: mcp_server.py builds a FastMCP server from the checked-in OpenAPI spec servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json and exposes only a short allowlist of routes as tools (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:54-125). It proxies each tool call to FastAPI over HTTP. Key code points: nginx forces Host: localhost:8001 because FastMCP's DNS-rebinding guard only accepts localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:41, nginx.conf:85-87). The browser-visible host travels in X-Forwarded-Host. Allowed Origins are local origins plus PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL when set (mcp_server.py:128-140). nginx deliberately does not use /_auth_check for /mcp (comment at nginx.conf:79-81): the asset ownership check would reject the non-asset path. PresentonTokenVerifier.verify_token accepts only tokens starting with sk-presenton- (mcp_server.py:285-316). Browser cookies are never accepted as MCP credentials. In normal operation attach_request_auth_header never forwards the long-lived API key to FastAPI (the only bearer fallback is for auth-disabled development and old tests, per its docstring). It sends the minted internal session as Cookie: presenton_session=..., adds X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, and copies X-Forwarded-Host/X-Forwarded-Proto (mcp_server.py:365-414). That header makes FastAPI turn path, edit_path and preview_url into absolute URLs (servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py:9-52). The internal JWT lives for one hour (MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS, mcp_server.py:39) because the same session is reused by the exporter at the end of a long generation. Upstream reads time out after 600 s, connects after 15 s (mcp_server.py:31-34). Which tools exist depends on PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE (get_mcp_route_maps, mcp_server.py:113-125). The full tool list and naming are in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP. Gotcha The MCP server reads the database directly (async_session_maker for API-key verification) but serves everything else by calling FastAPI at the hard-coded http://127.0.0.1:8000 (MCP_API_BASE_URL, mcp_server.py:31). It must run in the same network namespace as FastAPI, with the same DATABASE_URL and USER_CONFIG_PATH; splitting them into separate containers needs code changes.

docs.t: Step 11: One more hop, the export runtime calling back into the app
docs.x: When FastAPI exports a deck, export_presentation builds a URL "{NEXT_PUBLIC_URL or http://127.0.0.1}/pdf-maker?id=..." and hands it to the export runtime (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:18-40). In Docker NEXT_PUBLIC_URL is not set, so headless Chromium loads http://127.0.0.1/pdf-maker, which is nginx on port 80, then location /, then Next.js. The caller's cookie travels two ways: the task's cookieHeader is installed as browser cookies for the page origin by the runner (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:43-56), and it is also appended as a #exportCookie=... URL fragment that PdfMakerPage reads (export_utils.py:35-36, servers/nextjs/app/(export)/pdf-maker/PdfMakerPage.tsx:146-152). The browser export path built by Next.js additionally sets an exportSession query parameter (servers/nextjs/lib/run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:162-165), which proxy.ts:114-136 converts into a presenton_session cookie before redirecting to the clean URL. The whole export path is the subject of PPTX and PDF export. Gotcha Because the exporter goes through nginx on 127.0.0.1:80 from inside the container, an nginx that failed to start (Step 3.6) breaks exports even if you were reaching the UI some other way, and a custom nginx config that drops location / or binds a different port breaks every PPTX/PDF download.

docs.t: Step 12: Electron, the same code without nginx
docs.x: The desktop app runs the same FastAPI and Next.js with a different topology. Details are in Electron desktop app; the contrasts that matter here: Concern Docker Electron Reverse proxy nginx on port 80 none Ports fixed 8000, 3000, 8001 first two free ports scanning upward from 40000 (findUnusedPorts, electron/app/utils/index.ts:39-65, called at electron/app/main.ts:468-470) How the browser reaches FastAPI same origin through nginx NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API=http://127.0.0.1:<port> set by setupEnv (electron/app/utils/index.ts:5-22), plus proxy.ts rewriting /app_data and /static (proxy.ts:107-112) and /api/v1, /api/v2 (continueRequest, proxy.ts:51-55) to FastAPI at request time Auth enabled; admin account required DISABLE_AUTH defaults to "true" unless ELECTRON_DISABLE_AUTH/DISABLE_AUTH says otherwise (electron/app/main.ts:150-160, 455-459); FastAPI and Next.js short-circuit to an "electron" admin Request guard none beyond auth desktop token cookie or header plus exact host and origin checks (servers/nextjs/lib/desktop-auth.ts:14-44) MCP port 8001 behind /mcp disabled when PRESENTON_ELECTRON is truthy (mcp_server.py:319-321) CORS * fallback (same origin anyway) exact NEXT_PUBLIC_URL origin with credentials (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:92-100)

Reads: README.md, docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile.dev, start.js, scripts/user-config-env.cjs, scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs, test-local.sh, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py, servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py, servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, electron/package.json · Builds on: Runtime topology · Time: ~40 min

This is the hands-on chapter. You will start Presenton from the published image, then from source with each of the four Compose services, then with FastAPI and Next.js as two plain processes on your machine, and finally as the Electron app. Along the way you will create the first administrator (both through the UI and unattended), open Swagger, mint an API key and generate a deck with curl, and run the same test suites CI runs. The chapter ends with a troubleshooting table built from error strings that actually exist in the code.

The quickest start, straight from README.md:328: Port 80 inside the container is nginx; nothing else is reachable from the host (see Runtime topology). ./app_data on the host becomes APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/app_data (Dockerfile:82). Everything that must survive a restart lives there: userConfig.json, fastapi.db, images, exports and so on. Open http://localhost:5001. With no account yet, the first screen is the account setup form (Step 4). To preconfigure a text and image provider, pass them as environment variables (README.md:679): start.js copies the recognized variables into app_data/userConfig.json before FastAPI starts (start.js:490-497, key list in scripts/user-config-env.cjs:20-116). Gotcha Provider variables are authoritative only on the first boot. FastAPI's lifespan imports userConfig.json into a ProviderSettings database row the first time, and on every later start mirrors that row back over the file (servers/fastapi/services/provider_settings.py:85-127). Changing OPENAI_MODEL in your docker run command after the first boot therefore may not change anything. Use Settings in the UI, which writes the database row. Configuration precedence is detailed in Configuration and LLM providers.

docker-compose.yml defines four services. They are services, not Compose profiles: there is no profiles: key in the file, so you name the service you want, for example docker compose up production. Running a bare docker compose up starts all four, which collide on the same host port. Service Dockerfile Ports Volumes Command in container GPU production Dockerfile (multi-stage) ${PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT:-5001}:80, 1455:1455 ./app_data:/app_data, ./servers/fastapi/templates:/app/servers/fastapi/templates:ro node /app/start.js no production-gpu Dockerfile same ./app_data:/app_data only node /app/start.js 1 NVIDIA device (docker-compose.yml:136-142) development Dockerfile.dev same .:/app, named volumes for /app/node_modules, /app/document-extraction-liteparse, /app/presentation-export, ./app_data:/app_data node /app/start.js --dev no development-gpu Dockerfile.dev same same as development node /app/start.js --dev 1 NVIDIA device Line references: production at docker-compose.yml:2-128, production-gpu at :130-262, development at :264-393, development-gpu at :395-520, named volumes at :530-534. Every service sets MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=true, PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE=${...:-both}, PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium, and forwards about a hundred provider, search, Mem0 and auth variables with empty defaults. Port 1455 exists for the Codex OAuth callback, because OpenAI redirects the browser to localhost:1455 (docker-compose.yml:11-12).

docs.t: 2.1 What the development image does differently
docs.x: Dockerfile.dev is a single stage on python:3.11-slim-trixie (Dockerfile.dev:2). It installs nginx, Chromium (pinned to 149.0.7827.196-1~deb13u1), fonts, Tesseract and Node 22, runs the LiteParse and export-runtime sync scripts, installs FastAPI dependencies into the system interpreter with uv pip install --system (Dockerfile.dev:73-76), warms the FastEmbed caches, and ends with CMD ["node", "/app/start.js", "--dev"] (Dockerfile.dev:93). The comment at Dockerfile.dev:68-69 explains the system-wide install: the .:/app bind mount hides any .venv you may have under servers/fastapi, so dependencies must live outside the source tree. The three named volumes do the same job for Node: they stop your host's node_modules (built for macOS, say) from shadowing the Linux ones. With --dev, start.js (see Runtime topology) additionally: Runs npm ci in servers/nextjs (start.js:171-195). On the first start this takes several minutes. Re-syncs the export runtime with --force if the check fails, instead of exiting (start.js:456-465). Copies your working-tree nginx.conf into /etc/nginx/nginx.conf (start.js:468-479). Starts uvicorn with --reload true and next dev --webpack, and restarts either one after a clean exit (start.js:521-536, 538-566, 582-590). Gotcha Python dependencies are baked into the dev image. If you change servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml, rebuild with docker compose build development; uvicorn's reloader will not install new packages. Node dependencies in servers/nextjs are reinstalled by npm ci at every container start. Gotcha The host port is controlled by PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT (the port mapping), while the container receives PRESENTON_HOST_HTTP_PORT (only used by the startup banner, scripts/presenton-terminal-banner.mjs:98). The names differ by word order. The banner reads PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT first, but Compose does not pass that variable into the container, so in practice it uses PRESENTON_HOST_HTTP_PORT (scripts/presenton-terminal-banner.mjs:95-99). Both GPU services default the banner variable to 5000 (docker-compose.yml:152, docker-compose.yml:419) while mapping 5001, so their banner can print the wrong URL.

Compose substitutes ${VAR:-default} from a .env file next to docker-compose.yml. A minimal working setup needs one text provider and, optionally, one image provider: .env start.js's config writer knows these LLM values: ollama, openai, deepseek, google, vertex, azure, bedrock, openrouter, fireworks, together, cerebras, anthropic, litellm, lmstudio, custom, codex (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:1-18). The list is applied only to the value already in userConfig.json, which is dropped when it is not in the set (sanitizeExistingConfig, scripts/user-config-env.cjs:224-230); a value coming from the environment is copied as is and is only rejected later, by FastAPI, at the first LLM call. Note that presenton (the Presenton Cloud provider) is not in this set, so a rewrite by start.js drops an LLM=presenton from the file; the database-backed provider row is mirrored back over the file when FastAPI starts (Step 1). Image providers are the ImageProvider enum: pexels, pixabay, gemini_flash, nanobanana_pro, gpt-image-2, gpt-image-1.5, comfyui, open_webui, openai_compatible (servers/fastapi/enums/image_provider.py:4-13). If you omit IMAGE_PROVIDER, normalizeImageConfig picks one in this order (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:194-219): openai_compatible if its base URL, key and model are all set; open_webui if OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_URL; comfyui if COMFYUI_URL; pexels or pixabay if their keys exist; gpt-image-1.5 (quality medium) when LLM=openai with a key; gemini_flash when LLM=google with a key; otherwise it sets DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true. A legacy IMAGE_PROVIDER=dall-e-3 is rewritten to gpt-image-2 (:187-192).

Every /api/ route except the public /api/v1/auth/status, verify, setup, login and logout paths is behind SessionAuthMiddleware (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:30-36). Until a user exists it answers 428 {"detail":"Login setup is required","setup_required":true} (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:82-93). There are two ways to create the first account.

Open the app. The root page's AuthGate asks GET /api/v1/auth/status; when configured is false it shows setup mode (servers/nextjs/components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:39). Submit username, password and confirmation. The client checks the two passwords match, then posts to /api/v1/auth/setup (AuthGate.tsx:199-235). setup_credentials (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:110-152) returns 409 if any user already exists, validates the body (AuthCredentialsRequest: username 3 to 128 non-whitespace characters, password 8 to 128, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/schemas.py:28-34), creates a User with is_superuser=True and admin_slot="primary", writes a recovery copy of the hash and a signing secret to userConfig.json (persist_admin_credentials, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/config.py:95-107), and responds: Setup does not sign you in (authenticated: false). The UI shows "Account created" and asks you to sign in, which calls POST /api/v1/auth/login; that sets the presenton_session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 30 days, Secure only when the request or X-Forwarded-Proto is HTTPS, router.py:39-55, config.py:11-12).

bootstrap_database_admin() runs in FastAPI's lifespan on every start (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:58). Its logic (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:43-125): State at startup Variables Result No users, AUTH_USERNAME and AUTH_PASSWORD set (no flags) creates the primary admin with that password; password must be at least 8 characters, username at least 3 No users, legacy AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH in userConfig.json no flag migrates the legacy account (pre-multi-user installs); AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD from the environment are ignored No users, legacy credentials present RESET_AUTH=true or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true plus AUTH_PASSWORD creates the admin from the environment values instead of the legacy ones (bootstrap.py:91-106) No users, nothing set none does nothing; UI setup is required Admin exists RESET_AUTH=true or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true plus AUTH_PASSWORD replaces password (and username if given), bumps auth_version so old sessions die, deletes all API keys, rotates the signing secret Admin exists a flag without AUTH_PASSWORD raises RuntimeError("RESET_AUTH and AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV require AUTH_PASSWORD ..."), FastAPI fails to start Users exist but none is superuser any raises User accounts exist but no bootstrap administrator is configured Gotcha Leaving RESET_AUTH=true or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true in your .env rotates the admin on every container restart, which also deletes every API key (bootstrap.py:61-74). Remove the flag after one successful start, as the README advises. Gotcha Do not delete AUTH_* fields from app_data/userConfig.json to "reset" login. AUTH_SECRET_KEY there signs every session JWT and derives the Fernet key that encrypts stored API keys (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:39-43). Losing it invalidates sessions and makes existing keys impossible to reveal again.

docs.t: Step 5: Run FastAPI and Next.js without Docker
docs.x: For fast iteration on one side you can run both servers directly. There is no nginx, so Next.js's proxy.ts takes over the routing role (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:43-55, 107-112).

Python 3.11 exactly (requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.12", servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:11) and uv. Node 22 (the Docker images use NodeSource 22.x, Dockerfile:113-114) and npm. A Chrome or Chromium for exports, pointed to by PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH (the images use /usr/bin/chromium). Whether the export package can fetch its own browser when the variable is unset is not verified here.

From the repository root: The sync downloads presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz for the version pinned by presentationExportVersion in package.json from github.com/presenton/presenton-export releases into presentation-export/ (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, 155-172, 359-394). Use npm run sync:presentation-export:force to reinstall, or set EXPORT_CORE_ARCHIVE=/path/to/file.tgz to install from a local archive (:381-388). FastAPI finds the runtime at ../../presentation-export relative to servers/fastapi, or wherever EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT points (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:128-147).

Why each variable: Variable Required? Reason in code APP_DATA_DIRECTORY yes lifespan calls os.makedirs(get_app_data_directory_env(), ...) and fails on None (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:55); asset mounts are only added when it is set (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:77-82); exports raise 500 without it (export_task_service.py:155-161) USER_CONFIG_PATH effectively yes the JWT secret is created and saved there; without it _save_auth_config raises ValueError("USER_CONFIG_PATH is not set") on the first login or bootstrap (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/config.py:32-35) TEMP_DIRECTORY no defaults to the system temp dir plus presenton (export_task_service.py:164-166) MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP no defaults to "true" when unset (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:453-454); Alembic runs only when the value is exactly true or True (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:40-42); create_db_and_tables still runs either way DATABASE_URL no defaults to sqlite:///$APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/fastapi.db, rewritten to sqlite+aiosqlite://; postgresql:// and mysql:// become asyncpg/aiomysql (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:57-67) NEXT_PUBLIC_URL yes for exports the exporter opens {NEXT_PUBLIC_URL or http://127.0.0.1}/pdf-maker (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:18-40); without nginx on port 80 the default points nowhere. It also narrows CORS to that origin (api/main.py:92-100) server.py accepts --port (required), --reload ("true" enables it) and --log-level (default info) and always binds 127.0.0.1 (servers/fastapi/server.py:6-28). The lifespan steps that run next are described in FastAPI app and startup. Gotcha update_env_with_user_config() runs on every request (UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:23-26). When USER_CONFIG_PATH is set and the file has no LLM key, it removes LLM from os.environ (servers/fastapi/utils/user_config.py:378-383). An export LLM=openai in your shell can therefore vanish after the first request. Configure the provider through Settings, which persists it, rather than relying on shell variables.

Variable Used by Default when unset FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL proxy.ts rewrites and auth checks, server layouts NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, then http://127.0.0.1:8000 (proxy.ts:10-23, utils/serverAuth.ts:17-30) NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API browser and server code that needs an absolute backend origin none; leave it unset in this setup so browser calls stay same-origin and go through proxy.ts (utils/api.ts:88-98) USER_CONFIG_PATH app/api/user-config, lib/fastapi-internal.ts none APP_DATA_DIRECTORY app/api/export-presentation/*, app/api/upload-image those routes throw APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is required ... NEXT_PUBLIC_URL the browser export route builds {NEXT_PUBLIC_URL}/pdf-maker?... for the export runtime (servers/nextjs/lib/run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:159-160) http://127.0.0.1, which is nothing without nginx on port 80 PRESENTON_APP_ROOT, EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT where the browser export route finds presentation-export/runner.mjs the repository root two levels above servers/nextjs (run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:20-25) PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE which generation UI is offered both (see What Presenton is) Open http://127.0.0.1:3000. A browser request to /api/v1/... hits Next.js, proxy.ts asks FastAPI /api/v1/auth/status with your cookie, then rewrites the request to http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/... (proxy.ts:138-171, 51-55). Requests to /app_data/* and /static/* are rewritten unconditionally and FastAPI's own owner-scoped static mounts enforce access (proxy.ts:110-112, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:20-44). Gotcha Because each /api/v1 call in this mode costs an extra auth/status round trip from proxy.ts to FastAPI, it is slower than Docker, where nginx routes /api/v1 straight to FastAPI. Do not benchmark from this setup.

In dev mode Electron starts FastAPI with uv run python server.py --port <port> --reload true and Next.js with npm run dev -- -H 127.0.0.1 -p <port> (electron/app/utils/servers.ts:137-143, 208-212). Ports are the first two free ones from 40000 upward, auth is disabled by default, and MCP is off. The full lifecycle is in Electron desktop app.

docs.t: Step 7: Swagger and the OpenAPI document
docs.x: nginx proxies /docs and /openapi.json to FastAPI (nginx.conf:110-128). Both are in SessionAuthMiddleware._PROTECTED_NON_API_PATHS (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:42), so sign in through the UI first; the browser then sends presenton_session and Swagger loads. In the no-Docker setup, sign in through the UI at http://127.0.0.1:3000, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs. Browser cookies are scoped to the host name, not the port, so the presenton_session cookie set on 127.0.0.1:3000 is also sent to 127.0.0.1:8000. Use the same host name for both (localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different cookie hosts). The MCP server does not read the live /openapi.json. It uses the checked-in servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json, regenerated by servers/fastapi/scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py. After adding or renaming an endpoint the MCP layer depends on, regenerate that file.

docs.t: Step 8: An API key and a generation with curl
docs.x: API keys are created by an admin with a browser session, then used by scripts. The full API surface is in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP; this step is the shortest working path.

docs.t: 8.1 Log in and capture the session cookie
docs.x: The handler is login (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:155-188); the user fields come from serialize_user (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:227-233). IDs and timestamps above are placeholders. Wrong credentials give 401 Unauthorized; no account gives 428 Login setup is required.

AdminCreateApiKeyRequest requires user_id; label defaults to "API client" (1 to 120 characters) and expiry_days to 90 (1 to 365) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/schemas.py:56-59). The endpoint (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:60-82) returns 201 with ApiKeyCreated: The token format is sk-presenton-<16 hex id>.<secret> where the secret is secrets.token_urlsafe(40) (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:19-22, 79-104). Only a hash of the secret is used for verification, plus a Fernet-encrypted copy so an admin can reveal it again with GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{id}/token. Gotcha /api/v1/admin/* accepts only a browser JWT from an admin (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:100-119). Calling it with an API key, even an admin's, returns 403 Admin browser session required. That is why this step logs in with a cookie first.

GeneratePresentationRequest (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:8-46): Field Type Default content string, required (none) slides_markdown list of strings null instructions string null tone default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch default verbosity concise, standard, text-heavy standard web_search bool false n_slides int null (model decides) language string null (model decides) template string "general" include_table_of_contents bool false include_title_slide bool true files list of uploaded file paths null export_as pptx or pdf pptx trigger_webhook bool false check_if_api_request_is_valid (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2620-2681) returns 400 when content, slides_markdown and files are all empty, when n_slides is not positive or exceeds MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES = 50 (servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:4), when slides_markdown has more than 50 items, when a table of contents is requested with fewer than 3 slides, or with Template not found. Please use a valid template. The 16 bundled names are the folder names under templates/ (civic, dynamic, editorial, executive, general, horizon, landmark, modern, momentum, mosaic, nova, pulse, signal, standard, swift, verdant). The synchronous endpoint (presentation.py:3169-3195) blocks until export finishes and returns PresentationPathAndEditPath: The file name is derived from the generated presentation title, so the values above are illustrative. path is the filesystem path returned by the export service after it moves the file into the owner's folder (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:449-455, 773-805); in Docker it is also the nginx URL. Download it with the same bearer key, since nginx's /_auth_check forwards Authorization (nginx.conf:141): For long decks use POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async, which returns an AsyncTaskModel immediately, then poll GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/status/{id} until status is completed; data.path and data.edit_path carry the same values (presentation.py:3240-3298, completion data at :3113-3127). Gotcha The README example shows a path like /app_data/<id>/<name>.pptx. In this snapshot, authenticated exports land in exports/users/<owner-id>/. Always use the path the API returns rather than building it yourself.

test-local.sh reproduces .github/workflows/test-all.yml and runs three checks, counting failures instead of stopping at the first one (test-local.sh:15-30, 73-83). It needs uv, npm and node on PATH (:63-68). Check Commands (test-local.sh lines) Repository tooling npm ci && npm test && npm run sync:presentation-export && npm run check:presentation-export at the root (:32-38) FastAPI uv sync --locked --dev, then uv run --locked python -m pytest --verbose --tb=short with APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/app-data, TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/temp, DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/presenton-tests/test.db, DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING=true, DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true (:40-50) Next.js npm ci && npm test && npm run lint && NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API=http://localhost:8000 NEXT_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm run build && npx cypress run --component --browser electron (:52-61) Per suite, run the same commands by hand. The root npm test runs the template converter tests and seven node --test files under scripts/ (package.json, "test" script). In servers/nextjs, npm test is plain node --test, which discovers the *.test.mjs files in servers/nextjs/tests/, and component tests live in servers/nextjs/cypress/. Electron has its own npm run test:security (electron/package.json:41). CI wiring is covered in CI, tests, security.

Reads: servers/fastapi/server.py, servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/context.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py, servers/fastapi/services/database.py · Builds on: Running it locally · Time: ~35 min This chapter follows the FastAPI process from python server.py to the first request it serves. You will see every router and its full URL prefix, the /app_data and /static mounts, the CORS rule, the middleware stack in the order it really executes, each lifespan step, and the SessionAuthMiddleware decision tree. It ends with the request-scoped owner context that makes multi-user isolation automatic, and a worked example of adding an endpoint the way the codebase expects. All paths below are relative to the repository root. Unless stated otherwise, servers/fastapi/ is the Python package root and the working directory of the process.

The whole backend is started by a 29-line script, servers/fastapi/server.py. It parses three flags and hands a module path string to Uvicorn. Flag Type Default Effect --port int required TCP port (server.py:7) --reload str "false" Only the exact string "true" enables Uvicorn auto-reload (server.py:11, server.py:20) --log-level str "info" Passed to uvicorn.run(log_level=...) (server.py:13) The bind host is hard-coded: servers/fastapi/server.py (excerpt) FastAPI therefore only listens on loopback. In Docker, nginx is the public face and proxies /api/v1/, /api/v2/, /docs and /openapi.json to localhost:8000 (nginx.conf:45, nginx.conf:59, nginx.conf:110). Two launchers call this script: start.js spawns python server.py --port 8000 --reload <isDev> with cwd set to servers/fastapi (start.js:521, start.js:532, with fastapiDir defined at start.js:33). Electron runs either uv run python server.py --port <port> --reload true in development or a PyInstaller binary with --port <port> (electron/app/utils/servers.ts:139, electron/app/utils/servers.ts:143). See Electron desktop app. Gotcha server.py imports from api.main import app at line 3, before uvicorn.run receives the string "api.main:app". With --reload true, the Uvicorn supervisor process has therefore already executed all of api/main.py (Sentry init, directory creation, mounts) even though only the reloaded child serves requests. The lifespan (Step 8) runs only in the serving process. The working directory matters. utils/path_helpers.py:15 resolves bundled read-only assets with os.path.join(os.getcwd(), relative_path), so static/ and assets/ are found only when the process starts inside servers/fastapi.
Everything in api/main.py runs when the module is imported, before any request and before the lifespan.

init_sandbox_safe_mimetypes() is the first statement (api/main.py:29). It re-initializes the stdlib mimetypes table with files=[], so Python never reads OS databases such as /etc/apache2/mime.types, then registers 15 explicit types (utils/mime_types.py:4). The docstring explains why: macOS App Store sandboxed builds can be denied access to those files, and Starlette's FileResponse calls mimetypes.guess_type lazily (utils/mime_types.py:23). Extension Media type .avif, .gif, .jpeg/.jpg, .png, .svg, .webp image types (.svg is image/svg+xml) .otf, .ttf, .woff, .woff2 font/otf, font/ttf, font/woff, font/woff2 .pdf, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx application/pdf and the three OOXML types

_maybe_init_sentry() runs at api/main.py:63, still at import time. servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) Env var Getter Default when unset SENTRY_DSN get_sentry_dsn_env (utils/get_env.py:457) No Sentry at all SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE get_sentry_traces_sample_rate_env (utils/get_env.py:461) 1.0; also 1.0 if not parseable as float SENTRY_SEND_DEFAULT_PII get_sentry_send_default_pii_env (utils/get_env.py:465) True; any value other than true (case-insensitive) means False If sentry_sdk cannot be imported, the function returns silently (api/main.py:37), because the SDK is optional in some build targets. Gotcha Setting only SENTRY_DSN gives you 100 percent trace sampling and send_default_pii=True. Set both companion variables explicitly in any deployment that handles real user data.

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) There are no global exception handlers, no custom OpenAPI configuration and no root path. The only startup hook is the app_lifespan async context manager covered in Step 8.

Seven top-level routers are included in this order (api/main.py:68 to api/main.py:74): servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) Two of them are aggregators: API_V1_PPT_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/ppt") includes 17 feature routers (api/v1/ppt/router.py:22 to api/v1/ppt/router.py:40), and API_V2_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v2") nests /ppt and then /presentation (api/v2/router.py:6, api/v2/ppt/router.py:6, api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:35). API_V1_AUTH_ROUTER nests the Presenton Cloud device-login router under /presenton (api/v1/auth/router.py:28). The backend declares 101 route decorators in total. Full prefix Router constant and definition Endpoints (method and path suffix) /api/v1/ppt/files FILES_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:16 POST /upload, POST /mcp-upload, POST /decompose, POST /update /api/v1/ppt/fonts FONTS_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py:18 POST /upload, GET /list, GET /uploaded, DELETE /delete/{filename} /api/v1/ppt/outlines OUTLINES_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:40 GET /{id}, PUT /{id}, GET /stream/{id} /api/v1/ppt/slide SLIDE_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/slide.py:30 POST /edit, POST /edit-html /api/v1/ppt/images IMAGES_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/images.py:31 POST /test, GET /search, GET /generate, GET /generated, POST /upload, GET /uploaded, DELETE /{id} /api/v1/ppt/icons ICONS_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/icons.py:7 GET /search /api/v1/ppt/ollama OLLAMA_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/ollama.py:13 GET /models/supported, GET /models/available, GET /models/library, POST /models/pull /api/v1/ppt/openai OPENAI_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/openai.py:9 POST /models/available /api/v1/ppt/openrouter OPENROUTER_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/openrouter.py:11 POST /providers/available /api/v1/ppt/anthropic ANTHROPIC_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/anthropic.py:9 POST /models/available /api/v1/ppt/google GOOGLE_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/google.py:6 POST /models/available /api/v1/ppt/generation GENERATION_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/generation.py:7 POST /defaults /api/v1/ppt/codex/auth CODEX_AUTH_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/codex_auth.py:48 POST /initiate, GET /status/{session_id}, POST /exchange, POST /refresh, GET /status, POST /logout /api/v1/ppt/presentation PRESENTATION_ROUTER api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:136 GET /all, GET /{id}, DELETE /{id}, POST /{id}/duplicate, POST /{id}/regenerate, POST /{id}/export, POST /create,

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) APP_DATA_DIRECTORY holds userConfig.json, the SQLite database fastapi.db, logs and browser state. The directory itself is never mounted. Instead mount_app_data_assets (api/v1/auth/assets.py:39) mounts seven subdirectories, each with its own StaticFiles instance, in sorted order: Mount path Root class Visibility /app_data/exports private (PRIVATE_APP_DATA_ROOTS, assets.py:10) owner, or legacy files for admin /app_data/fonts shared (SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS, assets.py:17) anyone (no login needed) /app_data/images private owner /app_data/pptx-to-html private owner /app_data/pptx-to-json private owner /app_data/templates shared anyone (no login needed) /app_data/uploads private owner Each mount is an _OwnerScopedStaticFiles (assets.py:20). Its lookup_path override authorizes the exact file StaticFiles resolved, after symlinks, against the current owner: servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py (excerpt) The namespace rule in _namespace_authorized (assets.py:106) is: shared roots always pass; under a private root, a path of the form <root>/users/<uuid>/<file> passes only when <uuid> equals the caller's user id; any other path under a private root is a pre-multi-user "legacy" file and passes only for an admin. Files are written to these per-user folders by _owned_directory (utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23), which appends users/<owner_id> whenever an owner is in context. In Docker, nginx serves the same directories itself and protects the private ones with auth_request /_auth_check, which calls /api/v1/auth/verify with an X-Original-URI header (nginx.conf:133, nginx.conf:159, api/v1/auth/router.py:96). The FastAPI mounts are what Electron and bare development use.

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) servers/fastapi/static/ contains icons/ (one folder per Phosphor weight: bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin, plus placeholder.svg), images/ and vendor/. This mount is plain StaticFiles, has no owner check, and /static/ is not an auth-protected path (Step 9).

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) The comment above it (api/main.py:88) gives the three cases: Deployment NEXT_PUBLIC_URL Effective allow_origins Electron (Next.js and FastAPI on separate loopback ports) the Next.js origin, for example http://127.0.0.1:40001 that exact origin, so credentialed requests are standards-compliant Docker (single origin behind nginx) usually unset ["*"], which does not matter because the browser never makes cross-origin calls Standalone FastAPI development unset ["*"] A trailing slash is stripped, so http://localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000 behave the same.

docs.t: Step 6: The middleware stack and its real execution order
docs.x: Four middlewares are registered, in this source order: CORSMiddleware (api/main.py:94) UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware (api/main.py:102) SessionAuthMiddleware (api/main.py:103) static_icon_fallback_middleware, registered with the @app.middleware("http") decorator (api/main.py:106), which internally calls add_middleware with a BaseHTTPMiddleware Starlette's add_middleware inserts each new middleware at the front of app.user_middleware, and the stack is built so that the first list entry is the outermost wrapper. The last registered middleware therefore sees the request first. The unit tests build their apps in the same relative order (tests/unit/test_desktop_security.py:69). The Starlette source is not vendored in this repository, so this ordering rule was not re-read against the locked starlette 1.6.0 (servers/fastapi/uv.lock:2842); it is the documented Starlette behavior. Layer Request phase Response phase static_icon_fallback_middleware passes through swaps a 404 on /static/icons/... for placeholder.svg SessionAuthMiddleware desktop guard, authentication, authorization, owner context, cloud proxy, /app_data check resets the owner contextvars in finally UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware calls update_env_with_user_config() (api/middlewares.py:23) nothing CORSMiddleware answers preflight OPTIONS adds CORS headers Gotcha CORSMiddleware is the innermost user middleware. Any response that SessionAuthMiddleware produces itself (the 401, 403, 404, 428 and 503 JSON bodies below) never passes through it and carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. In a cross-origin setup such as Electron, a browser reports such a rejection as a CORS failure rather than exposing the status code to JavaScript. Successful responses from routes do pass through CORS. Gotcha UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware sits inside the auth layer, so it runs only for requests that the auth layer lets through. It re-reads userConfig.json from disk on every such request. That is how a settings change made by one worker becomes visible to the next request without a restart; the precedence rules are in Configuration and LLM providers.

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt) Saved slides reference icons by URL (for example /static/icons/bold/acorn-bold.svg). When an icon set upgrade renames a file, old decks would otherwise render broken images. The fallback keeps the status at 200 and returns the placeholder SVG. It only touches 404s under /static/icons/; every other 404 is returned unchanged. Icon selection itself is covered in Images, icons, web search.

docs.t: Step 8: The lifespan, step by step
docs.x: app_lifespan (api/lifespan.py:44) runs once in the serving process before the first request is accepted, and once on shutdown. servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py (excerpt)

_configure_application_logging (api/lifespan.py:19) reads LOG_LEVEL (default INFO; unknown names fall back to INFO) and sets the root logger level. If the root logger has no handlers, it walks from the uvicorn.error logger up its propagation chain and attaches the handlers it finds to the root logger, so application logging calls appear in the same stream as Uvicorn's. Only if none are found does it call logging.basicConfig.

os.makedirs(get_app_data_directory_env(), exist_ok=True) (api/lifespan.py:55). Gotcha api/main.py guards its mounts with if app_data_dir:, but the lifespan does not. If APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is unset, os.makedirs(None) raises TypeError and the server never starts. start.js refuses to start without it as well (start.js:50), and the default template import in 8.8 raises RuntimeError without it (templates/default_templates.py:299). Treat it as required.

When MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP is "true" or "True" (the default is "true", utils/get_env.py:453), migrations.py:40 runs Alembic upgrade head in a thread via asyncio.to_thread, after repairing unknown revisions and stamping unversioned legacy databases. The full algorithm and the revision list are in Data model.

The inverse switch: only when migrations are disabled does services/database.py:117 call SQLModel.metadata.create_all for an explicit list of 15 tables. With migrations on (the default) this function does nothing. Gotcha Both checks compare against the literal strings "true" and "True". MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=1 or yes disables migrations and switches to create_all, which never alters existing tables. An upgraded deployment then runs new code against an old schema.

api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:43 guarantees one primary administrator. It looks for any user with is_superuser = True. If one exists, it sets admin_slot = "primary" and, when RESET_AUTH or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV is truthy (startup aborts with RuntimeError if either is set without AUTH_PASSWORD), replaces the username and password from AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD, bumps auth_version (invalidating every JWT) and deletes all API keys. If users exist but none is a superuser, startup fails with RuntimeError("User accounts exist but no bootstrap administrator is configured"). If no user exists, it migrates the legacy single-user credentials from userConfig.json or creates the admin from AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD; with neither, it leaves the database empty so the first request gets HTTP 428 (Step 9). Finally _backfill_legacy_ownership (bootstrap.py:128) assigns every row with owner_id IS NULL in seven owned tables to that admin, plus custom (is_default = False) templates. The full account model is in Auth and multi-user.

Background jobs run as FastAPI BackgroundTasks inside the process, so they cannot survive a restart. services/async_tasks.py:22 selects every async_tasks row whose status is pending and rewrites it: The error body is the constant INTERRUPTED_TASK_ERROR (services/async_tasks.py:13). Because no owner is in context at startup, the owner filter of Step 10 does not apply and every user's tasks are covered. Polling clients therefore get a terminal state instead of waiting forever (REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP).

services/provider_settings.py:103 reconciles provider settings between the provider_settings table (one row, id = 1) and userConfig.json. On the very first boot it imports the file into the database; on every later boot it mirrors the database back over the file. This is the single most important precedence rule in configuration and is explained in Configuration and LLM providers.

templates/default_templates.py:22 scans the repository-level templates/ directory (resolved as parents[3] of the module, default_templates.py:58) for subfolders containing template.json. At this snapshot there are 16: civic, dynamic, editorial, executive, general, horizon, landmark, modern, momentum, mosaic, nova, pulse, signal, standard, swift, verdant. For each one it: Loads template.json, rewrites every string starting with static/ to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/... (default_templates.py:257), validates layouts and merged_components, and builds a TemplateV2 row with is_default=True (default_templates.py:113). Deletes APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/templates/<id>/static and copies the bundled static/ folder over it (default_templates.py:295), so renamed assets never linger after an upgrade. Inserts the row, or overwrites name, description, layouts, components, theme and assets of the existing row, and commits. Afterwards _remove_stale_default_templates (default_templates.py:154) deletes any is_default row whose id was not imported and removes its asset folder. The template format itself is in Template v2 format. Gotcha Bundled templates are authoritative and rewritten on every boot. Editing a default template through the API or directly in the database is silently reverted by the next restart. Make changes in templates/<name>/template.json instead, or copy the template to a custom one.

The last step (utils/user_config.py:378) copies the merged configuration into os.environ, where every provider getter reads it. The same function then runs per request through UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware.
After yield, dispose_engines() (services/database.py:145) calls sql_engine.dispose() to close every pooled connection.

docs.t: Step 9: SessionAuthMiddleware as a decision tree
docs.x: SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch (api/middlewares.py:55) decides, for every request, whether it may proceed and as whom. This section follows its control flow; the account, password, JWT and API-key mechanics are in Auth and multi-user.

desktop_request_denied(request) (api/v1/auth/desktop.py:25) is a no-op unless PRESENTON_ELECTRON == "true". In Electron it requires a PRESENTON_DESKTOP_TOKEN of at least 32 characters and a non-empty PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS (otherwise 503 {"detail": "Desktop session unavailable"}), checks the raw Host header and any Origin header against those origins (403 {"detail": "Forbidden desktop origin"}; forwarded headers are deliberately ignored to defeat DNS rebinding), lets CORS preflights through, and finally compares the x-presenton-desktop-token header or presenton_desktop_session cookie with hmac.compare_digest (401 on mismatch).

With DISABLE_AUTH truthy (1, true, yes, on, via _is_truthy, utils/get_env.py:11), which is how Electron runs, the middleware only offers the request to the Presenton Cloud proxy with allow_unowned=True and otherwise calls the route directly. No owner is set, so rows are written with owner_id = NULL and reads are not filtered.

servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt) Path Needs auth /api/v1/auth/status, /verify, /setup, /login, /logout (_PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS, middlewares.py:30) no any other /api/... (including /api/v1/auth/presenton/..., because _PUBLIC_AUTH_PREFIXES is empty) yes /app_data/fonts/..., /app_data/templates/... no any other /app_data/... yes /docs, /openapi.json, /redoc yes everything else, including /static/... no OPTIONS requests always pass, so CORS preflights reach CORSMiddleware.

For protected paths the middleware opens its own AsyncSession and runs SELECT count(*) FROM user. Zero rows means no administrator has been created yet: The Next.js app uses this to route to the setup screen (Settings, onboarding, auth UI).

resolve_request_principal (api/v1/auth/principal.py:22) tries, in order, the presenton_session cookie (a JWT read by VersionedJWTStrategy, which also checks that the token's av claim equals the user's current auth_version, api/v1/auth/users.py:136) and then an Authorization: Bearer <api key> header verified by services/api_keys.py. It returns a frozen AuthPrincipal(user_id, username, is_admin, method) where method is "jwt" or "api_key". Neither present, or a bad key, yields 401 {"detail": "Unauthorized"}.

servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt) These are the endpoints that change global state (users, API keys, provider settings, the global ChatGPT token, shared fonts) or that make the server fetch an arbitrary URL supplied by the caller (OpenAI-compatible and Ollama model discovery, image provider tests). Gotcha The check requires principal.method == "jwt". An API key that belongs to the administrator still cannot reach these paths, by design: API keys are for automation, and settings changes require a browser session. Note also that /api/v1/ppt/anthropic/models/available and /api/v1/ppt/google/models/available are not in the list; they call fixed vendor hosts with the caller's key, so any signed-in user may use them.

docs.t: 9.7 Request state and the internal session token
docs.x: servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt) For API-key callers the middleware mints a short-term browser-style JWT for the same user. Some routes later need to make the server call itself as that user, most importantly the export pipeline, which opens the presentation in a headless browser. build_export_cookie_header (api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1473) prefers the incoming Cookie header and otherwise turns internal_session_token into presenton_session=<jwt>. See PPTX and PDF export.

docs.t: 9.8 Owner contextvars, cloud proxy and asset check
docs.x: servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt) Presenton Cloud proxy. For browser sessions, maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request (services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:407) forwards a fixed set of generation, editing, chat and asset paths to Presenton Cloud when the saved provider is LLM = "presenton", then mirrors results into the local database. It is described in Configuration and LLM providers. /app_data authorization. is_app_data_path_authorized (assets.py:78) decodes the URL path up to 8 times (failing closed beyond that), rejects NUL bytes, backslashes and ./.. segments, applies the namespace rule from Step 4, and then re-applies it to the realpath of the target so a symlink cannot alias another user's file. A refusal returns 404, not 403, so the response does not reveal that the file exists.

api/v1/auth/context.py defines the entire mechanism in 34 lines: servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/context.py (excerpt) ContextVar values are per asyncio task context, so concurrent requests each see their own owner. The middleware sets them before call_next and resets them with the saved tokens in finally.

Consumer Effect _scope_owned_selects, a do_orm_execute listener on every Session (services/database.py:67) adds with_loader_criteria(model, owner_id == current) for seven tables, and "own or shared default" for TemplateV2, to every ORM SELECT _stamp_new_owned_rows, a before_flush listener (services/database.py:100) sets owner_id = current owner on every new owned object before INSERT owner_id fields with default_factory=get_current_owner_id in eight SQL models (for example models/sql/presentation.py:25) fills owner_id the moment the Python object is constructed _owned_directory (utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23) writes files under <root>/users/<owner_id>/ _OwnerScopedStaticFiles.lookup_path (assets.py:25) refuses other users' files authenticated_internal_request_headers (api/v1/auth/internal.py:10) mints a JWT cookie for server-to-server calls on behalf of the owner servers/fastapi/services/database.py (excerpt)

docs.t: 10.3 Why the models default owner_id from the context
docs.x: The models declare owner_id with default_factory=get_current_owner_id and exclude=True. The default factory captures the owner at construction time, so any route can write PresentationModel(...) without threading a user id through every helper. exclude=True keeps owner_id out of every serialized API response. The before_flush listener then acts as the authoritative stamp: it overwrites owner_id on new objects even when a value was supplied, which matters for objects deserialized from request bodies, such as the slides: List[SlideModel] accepted by PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update (presentation.py:2532). A client that put another user's id in that JSON would have it replaced before INSERT. The net effect is that an endpoint written with no knowledge of users is automatically tenant-safe for reads and inserts. Asking for another user's presentation id simply returns None from session.get, which the route turns into its normal 404. Gotcha The automatic filter applies only to ORM SELECTs (execute_state.is_select). Bulk UPDATE and DELETE statements are not rewritten, which is why the code adds explicit owner predicates to them, for example delete(SlideModel).where(SlideModel.presentation == presentation.id, SlideModel.owner_id == get_current_owner_id()) (presentation.py:2568) and the chat history deletes in services/chat/sql_chat_history.py:134. Any new bulk statement must do the same. Gotcha Background work does not rely on inherited context. Every BackgroundTasks entry point receives the owner id explicitly and sets it again, for example _run_generate_presentation_task calls set_current_owner_id(owner_id) and set_current_owner_is_admin(False) and resets both in finally (presentation.py:3198). Startup code such as Step 8.6 runs with no owner, so its queries see every tenant's rows. The escape hatch for a deliberate cross-tenant query is the execution option skip_owner_scope.

docs.t: Step 11: Worked example: adding a router and endpoint the Presenton way
docs.x: Suppose you want GET /api/v1/ppt/summary/{presentation_id} returning a presentation's title and slide count. The following code is illustrative and is not in the repository. 1. Create the router module next to the others, with a short prefix and a tag: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/summary.py (new, illustrative) 2. Register it in api/v1/ppt/router.py with API_V1_PPT_ROUTER.include_router(SUMMARY_ROUTER). The full path becomes /api/v1/ppt/summary/{presentation_id}. Nothing in api/main.py changes. 3. Inherit security for free. Because the path starts with /api/, SessionAuthMiddleware requires a session cookie or API key. Because session.get is an ORM select, _scope_owned_selects limits it to the caller's rows; another user's id returns 404. The count() query selects from SlideModel through the ORM, so the loader criteria apply there too. 4. Decide on admin access. If the endpoint changes global state, either add the path to the admin_only expression in api/middlewares.py:100 or depend on require_browser_admin_principal (api/v1/auth/principal.py:67) inside the route. 5. If you add a table, follow the existing pattern: give the model an owner_id field with default_factory=get_current_owner_id, exclude=True and ForeignKey("user.id", ondelete="CASCADE"); add the class to _STRICT_OWNER_MODELS (services/database.py:56) and to the create_all list (services/database.py:124); import it in alembic/env.py; write an Alembic revision whose down_revision is the current head 026c0ba8b35c; and update REVISION_HEAD plus _infer_revision_from_schema in migrations.py. Data model explains each of these pieces. 6. If it must work with Presenton Cloud selected, decide whether the path belongs in one of the CLOUD_* path sets in services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:42. Paths that are not listed are always served locally. 7. If it is long-running, create an AsyncTaskModel row, schedule a BackgroundTasks function, and pass get_current_owner_id() into it so the task can call set_current_owner_id itself, as generate_presentation_async does (presentation.py:3241). Step 8.6 will then fail it cleanly if the server restarts.

Reads: servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py, servers/fastapi/utils/user_config.py, servers/fastapi/utils/user_config_store.py, servers/fastapi/models/user_config.py, servers/fastapi/services/provider_settings.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_config.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_provider.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/codex_auth.py, servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py, scripts/user-config-env.cjs · Builds on: FastAPI app and startup · Time: ~45 min Presenton keeps provider configuration in three places at once: process environment variables, a JSON file called userConfig.json, and a single database row. This chapter shows exactly which one wins and when, lists every environment getter, and then follows a provider name such as anthropic all the way to an llmai client making a streamed, schema-validated call. It also covers model discovery, Ollama pulls, the ChatGPT (Codex) OAuth sign-in, error normalization, and the Presenton Cloud proxy that replaces local generation when the presenton provider is selected.

docs.t: Step 1: Three places a setting can live
docs.x: Environment variables are what operators set. Every Python reader goes through utils/get_env.py. userConfig.json is a compatibility file. The Next.js server reads it for non-admin users (servers/nextjs/lib/runtime-provider-config.ts:24), the legacy auth secret lives in it, and update_env_with_user_config loads it into os.environ. provider_settings (one row, id = 1) is the source of truth for the settings UI since revision d0a2b4c6e8f1. The rest of the chapter explains each arrow.

utils/get_env.py contains 111 functions: 110 public getters plus the private helper _is_truthy. All but a few getters are one-line os.getenv wrappers that return the raw string or None. The exceptions with logic are noted in the tables. Setters with the same names live in utils/set_env.py (94 functions) and write os.environ[...] directly.
