A few modules call os.getenv directly. The ones relevant to this part of the system are: LOG_LEVEL (api/lifespan.py:21), NEXT_PUBLIC_URL (CORS, api/main.py:92), PRESENTON_DESKTOP_TOKEN and PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS (api/v1/auth/desktop.py), AUTH_USERNAME, AUTH_PASSWORD, RESET_AUTH, AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV (api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:49), the pool settings DB_POOL_SIZE, DB_MAX_OVERFLOW, DB_POOL_TIMEOUT, DB_POOL_RECYCLE, DB_POOL_PRE_PING (utils/db_utils.py:34), and MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS (default 100, constants/presentation.py:8). Memory (MEM0_*), document parsing (LITEPARSE_*) and chat (CHAT_MAX_STORED_TURNS) variables belong to their own chapters. Gotcha Booleans are parsed two different ways. _is_truthy (get_env.py:11) accepts 1, true, yes, on. parse_bool_or_none (utils/parsers.py:1), used for DISABLE_THINKING, EXTENDED_REASONING, WEB_GROUNDING, DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION and the OpenRouter flags, accepts only the word true in any case. DISABLE_THINKING=1 is therefore False if it reaches Python unchanged. Through start.js it is normalized to a JSON boolean first (Step 3.4), which hides the difference in Docker.

models/user_config.py:5 is a Pydantic model with one optional field per configurable key (92 fields). Most are Optional[str]; the typed ones are: Field Type OPENROUTER_PROVIDER_ORDER list[str], default [] OPENROUTER_ALLOW_FALLBACKS, OPENROUTER_REQUIRE_PARAMETERS, OPENROUTER_ZDR, DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION, DISABLE_THINKING, EXTENDED_REASONING, WEB_GROUNDING, CODEX_IS_PRO Optional[bool] OPENROUTER_DATA_COLLECTION Literal["allow", "deny"] LLM_GENERATION_PROFILE Literal["fast", "balanced", "deep", "model_max"] LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS int, gt=0 LLM_REASONING_MODE Literal["auto", "enabled", "disabled"] LLM_REASONING_EFFORT Literal["default", "none", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"] LLM_REASONING_BUDGET_TOKENS int, ge=0 A model_validator(mode="before") rewrites the retired IMAGE_PROVIDER = "dall-e-3" to gpt-image-2 and derives GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY (models/user_config.py:6). Unknown keys are ignored by Pydantic's default extra behavior. The AUTH_USERNAME, AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH and AUTH_SECRET_KEY keys that also live in the file are not part of this model; they are read by api/v1/auth/config.py.

Several processes touch the file: start.js, FastAPI, the Next.js server and, in Electron, the desktop shell. utils/user_config_store.py makes every write atomic and serialized. Mechanism Detail Lock userConfig.json.lock created with O_CREAT | O_EXCL, containing {"pid", "createdAt"}; retried every 50 ms for up to LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0; a lock older than LOCK_STALE_SECONDS = 30.0 is deleted (user_config_store.py:11, user_config_store.py:109) Atomic write JSON written to userConfig.json.<pid>.<ms>.<uuid>.tmp with mode 0600, fsync, then os.replace (user_config_store.py:173) Backup before each write the valid primary is copied to userConfig.json.bak (after the write the backup is only created if it does not exist yet); reads fall back to it when the primary is missing or invalid JSON (user_config_store.py:89, user_config_store.py:154) Permissions every read chmods both files to 0600 (user_config_store.py:25) Retries EACCES, EBUSY, EPERM retried up to 6 times with linear backoff (user_config_store.py:48) Read errors read_user_config_file never raises; it returns {} (user_config_store.py:202) Writers use update_user_config_file(path, update), which reads the snapshot under the lock, applies the update(dict) -> dict callback, and writes the result.

Before spawning FastAPI, start.js runs setupUserConfigFromEnv (start.js:490): start.js (excerpt) buildUserConfigFromEnv (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:232) does four things in order: sanitizeExistingConfig drops LLM from the existing file if it is not one of the 16 values in VALID_LLM_PROVIDERS (user-config-env.cjs:1). readUserConfigEnv copies every non-empty env var whose name is in USER_CONFIG_ENV_KEYS (95 names, user-config-env.cjs:20) over the existing values. Besides the UserConfig fields, the list includes USE_CUSTOM_URL, DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING and DALL_E_3_QUALITY. normalizeConfigTypes turns the nine BOOLEAN_CONFIG_KEYS into JSON booleans (accepting 1/true/yes/on and 0/false/no/off), parses LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS and LLM_REASONING_BUDGET_TOKENS as integers, and splits OPENROUTER_PROVIDER_ORDER on commas. normalizeImageConfig migrates dall-e-3, deletes DALL_E_3_QUALITY, and, if neither IMAGE_PROVIDER nor DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION is set, picks an image provider in this priority: openai_compatible (all three settings present), open_webui, comfyui, pexels, pixabay, gpt-image-1.5 with quality medium (when LLM=openai and a key exists), gemini_flash (when LLM=google and a key exists), otherwise DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION = true. For example, starting a fresh container with LLM=openai OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4.1 DISABLE_THINKING=1 OPENROUTER_PROVIDER_ORDER="groq, together" produces: APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/userConfig.json (derived from the code above)

ProviderSettings (models/sql/provider_settings.py:10) has three columns: id (integer, always 1), config (JSON, not null) and updated_at. services/provider_settings.py wraps it: Function Behavior sanitize_provider_settings (:52) Removes every key starting with AUTH_. Credentials never enter the table migrate_provider_settings_from_file (:103) Startup. No row: create it from the sanitized file. Row exists: re-sanitize it if needed. Either way, _mirror_to_legacy_file the row back to the file get_provider_settings (:130) Returns the sanitized row, creating it from the file on first use save_provider_settings (:137) Applies merge_provider_settings(existing, incoming), commits, mirrors to the file _mirror_to_legacy_file (:85) Replaces the file contents with the DB config, preserving any AUTH_* keys already in the file sync_legacy_file_to_provider_settings (:158) Synchronous reverse sync (new sync engine, upsert of row 1), used only after Codex token writes merge_provider_settings (:61) encodes the patch semantics the settings UI relies on: Rule Keys Effect Plain patch everything else incoming values overwrite existing ones; omitted keys are kept OAuth-managed CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN, CODEX_TOKEN_EXPIRES, CODEX_ACCOUNT_ID, CODEX_USERNAME, CODEX_EMAIL, CODEX_IS_PRO, PRESENTON_CONNECTED, PRESENTON_EMAIL the incoming value is always discarded; the existing value (or absence) wins Empty does not clear OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_URL, OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_API_KEY, CODEX_MODEL an empty incoming value keeps the existing one Empty resets the 12 OPTIONAL_ADVANCED_FIELDS (LLM_* overrides, DISABLE_THINKING, EXTENDED_REASONING, five OPENROUTER_* routing keys) None, "" or [] removes the key

GET /api/v1/admin/provider-settings and PUT /api/v1/admin/provider-settings (api/v1/admin/router.py:144, api/v1/admin/router.py:158) require an admin browser session (or DISABLE_AUTH). A save request from the settings UI looks like this: The handler calls save_provider_settings and then update_env_with_user_config(), so the new provider is live for the next request. The response is the merged config. GET returns the same dict plus two computed keys, PRESENTON_CONNECTED (whether a non-expired Presenton Cloud token is stored) and PRESENTON_EMAIL. The Next.js route app/api/user-config/route.ts forwards admins to these endpoints and serves non-admins a filtered view of userConfig.json; see Settings, onboarding, auth UI.

get_user_config (utils/user_config.py:197) reads the file and builds a UserConfig where each field is file value or env value: servers/fastapi/utils/user_config.py (excerpt) The booleans and LLM_REASONING_BUDGET_TOKENS use is not None checks instead of or, so a saved false or 0 is respected. OLLAMA_URL is the only string key where presence, not truthiness, decides, which allows clearing it to an empty string.

update_env_with_user_config (utils/user_config.py:378) runs at the end of startup, inside PUT /provider-settings, after Presenton Cloud logout, and on every request that SessionAuthMiddleware lets through (including public paths and auth-disabled mode) via UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware. servers/fastapi/utils/user_config.py (excerpt) After the pops, every field of the merged UserConfig is written back to os.environ with an if value: guard (or is not None for booleans and integers).

Situation Winner First boot, empty database start.js merges env over the file; FastAPI imports the file into provider_settings Any later boot provider_settings is mirrored over the file, discarding whatever start.js just merged into it Key present and non-empty in the database database value Key absent or empty in the database the process environment variable, if any LLM or one of the 12 advanced keys absent from the database removed from os.environ; the environment variable is ignored Gotcha After the first boot, changing a Docker environment variable for a key the settings UI has already saved has no effect: the database row wins at every boot. Change it in the UI, or remove the key from the row. For LLM and the advanced generation keys it is stricter: an env value is actively removed when the saved settings lack that key. Gotcha Clearing a secret in the UI does not unset it until restart. Saving "OPENAI_API_KEY": "" stores an empty string; get_user_config then falls back to os.environ, which still holds the old key written by the previous update_env_with_user_config, and the empty value is never written back. Only OLLAMA_URL, LLM and the advanced keys have explicit clearing paths. Gotcha get_user_config builds UserConfig(**file_contents) inside a bare try/except (utils/user_config.py:202). If a single key fails validation, for example "LLM_REASONING_MODE": "on" or "LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS": 0 written by hand, the whole file is ignored, only Error while loading user config is printed, and every key falls back to the process environment. Validate hand edits against models/user_config.py. Gotcha os.environ is process-global. Provider settings are therefore global to the deployment, shared by every user, and only admins may change them. A per-user provider would need a different design, not a new key.

docs.t: Step 6: From provider name to an llmai client
docs.x: Presenton does not call vendor SDKs directly for text generation. It depends on llmai==0.3.15 (servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:35), a provider-abstraction package from PyPI. Its source is not installed anywhere in this environment (no site-packages/llmai was found), so the interface described below is inferred from how Presenton calls it and from Presenton's unit tests, and is not verified against llmai's own code.

get_llm_provider() (utils/llm_provider.py:47) converts LLM into the LLMProvider enum (enums/llm_provider.py, 16 members) and raises HTTP 500 with the list of valid names for anything else. get_model() (utils/llm_provider.py:126) returns the configured model or a default from constants/llm.py: LLM Model env Default model openai OPENAI_MODEL gpt-4.1 deepseek DEEPSEEK_MODEL deepseek-chat google GOOGLE_MODEL models/gemini-2.5-flash vertex VERTEX_MODEL gemini-2.5-flash azure AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL, then AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT gpt-4.1 bedrock BEDROCK_MODEL us.anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0 openrouter OPENROUTER_MODEL openai/gpt-4o fireworks FIREWORKS_MODEL accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3p1-8b-instruct together TOGETHER_MODEL openai/gpt-oss-20b cerebras CEREBRAS_MODEL llama-3.3-70b anthropic ANTHROPIC_MODEL claude-sonnet-4-20250514 litellm LITELLM_MODEL gpt-4.1 lmstudio LMSTUDIO_MODEL openai/gpt-oss-20b ollama OLLAMA_MODEL none (returns None) custom CUSTOM_MODEL none (returns None) codex CODEX_MODEL, only if in SUPPORTED_CODEX_MODELS gpt-5.6-luna SUPPORTED_CODEX_MODELS is gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.3-codex-spark (constants/llm.py:17).

_get_llm_config (utils/llm_config.py:247) is a single match on the provider. Missing required values raise HTTP 400 with a specific message such as "Anthropic API Key is not set". LLM llmai config class Base URL passed Auth Notes openai OpenAIClientConfig none (library default) OPENAI_API_KEY api_type is COMPLETIONS, or RESPONSES when the caller asks (native web search, Smart mode) deepseek DeepSeekClientConfig DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL or none DEEPSEEK_API_KEY google GoogleClientConfig none GOOGLE_API_KEY vertex VertexAIClientConfig VERTEX_BASE_URL or none VERTEX_API_KEY, or VERTEX_PROJECT with optional VERTEX_LOCATION both styles at once is a 400 "ambiguous" error azure AzureOpenAIClientConfig AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT and/or AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL (one required) AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY plus AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION always api_type=RESPONSES; optional deployment bedrock BedrockClientConfig region = BEDROCK_REGION or us-east-1 BEDROCK_API_KEY, or access key id plus secret (optional session token, profile) openrouter OpenRouterClientConfig OPENROUTER_BASE_URL or none OPENROUTER_API_KEY routing flags go in extra_body (6.3) fireworks FireworksClientConfig FIREWORKS_BASE_URL or none FIREWORKS_API_KEY together TogetherAIClientConfig TOGETHER_BASE_URL or none TOGETHER_API_KEY cerebras CerebrasClientConfig CEREBRAS_BASE_URL or none CEREBRAS_API_KEY anthropic AnthropicClientConfig none ANTHROPIC_API_KEY litellm LiteLLMClientConfig LITELLM_BASE_URL, required, normalized to end in /v1 LITELLM_API_KEY optional lmstudio LMStudioClientConfig LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL or none LMSTUDIO_API_KEY optional ollama OpenAIClientConfig (OLLAMA_URL or http://localhost:11434) + "/v1" literal "ollama" Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint custom OpenAIClientConfig CUSTOM_LLM_URL, required CUSTOM_LLM_API_KEY or literal "null" codex ChatGPTClientConfig none OAuth access_token plus account_id refreshed on demand (Step 12) get_llm_config(use_openai_responses_api=False) (utils/llm_config.py:483) then attaches the generation defaults from Step 8 as config.generation. Every LLM call site follows the same three lines, for example utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:165: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py (excerpt) Gotcha get_model() returns None for ollama and custom when no model is configured, and that None is passed straight to the client. Configure OLLAMA_MODEL or

get_extra_body(uses_tool_choice=False) (utils/llm_config.py:489) adds vendor fields that are not part of the common interface: Provider Condition extra_body deepseek legacy DISABLE_THINKING (without explicit reasoning settings), or the call uses tools or a response schema {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}} custom legacy DISABLE_THINKING {"enable_thinking": false} openrouter any routing key set {"provider": {"order": [...], "allow_fallbacks": ..., "require_parameters": ..., "data_collection": "allow" or "deny", "zdr": ...}}

get_generate_kwargs (utils/llm_utils.py:110) builds the dict passed to client.generate(...): model, messages (llmai SystemMessage/UserMessage/AssistantMessage objects), stream, and optionally max_tokens, tools, response_format, reasoning and extra_body.

Every schema-constrained call wraps a Pydantic model's JSON schema: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py (excerpt) generate_structured_with_schema_retries (utils/llm_utils.py:310) then runs two nested loops: Parse loop: up to 3 attempts, sleeping 0.5 s and then 1.0 s between them, until the stream yields something that parses into a dict. Parsing uses extract_structured_content (utils/llm_utils.py:414), which accepts a dict, a Pydantic object, or text parsed leniently with dirtyjson. If all three fail: HTTP 400 "LLM did not return any content". Validation loop (only with validate_schema=True): up to validate_schema_max_loop_count (default 4) rounds. Each failing round appends a UserMessage listing at most 10 JSON Schema errors and the previous JSON truncated to 6,000 characters, ending with "Return corrected JSON only" (utils/llm_utils.py:276). After the last round the last response is returned with a warning, not an error. Gotcha Structured generation always streams, even when nobody consumes the chunks. The comment at utils/llm_utils.py:75 explains the reason: without an explicit max_tokens, the Anthropic SDK refuses a non-streaming request whose estimated duration exceeds ten minutes and raises before sending anything. That only affected background generation, which made it look like a provider bug. Keep new structured calls on _generate_structured_content.

llmai's client.generate(...) is consumed as a synchronous iterator. stream_generate_events (utils/llm_utils.py:458) runs it in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread and hands each event to the event loop through an asyncio.Queue: The events Presenton handles are those with type == "content" and a chunk string, type == "thinking" (or ResponseStreamThinkingChunk), and the final ResponseStreamCompletionChunk (type == "completion") carrying content, tool_calls, usage and finish_reason. When the HTTP client disconnects, the bridge stops pulling, closes the provider stream and raises CancelledError, so a closed browser tab stops token spend. build_text_generation_metrics (utils/llm_utils.py:191) turns usage into input, output and thinking token counts, estimating at four characters per token when the provider omits usage. How these chunks become SSE events for the browser is covered in Streaming (SSE).

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_config.py (excerpt) Input Mapping to llmai LLM_GENERATION_PROFILE GenerationProfile(value), default balanced; invalid value is HTTP 400 LLM_REASONING_MODE enabled sets reasoning.enabled = True; disabled sets False; empty or auto leaves it unset LLM_REASONING_EFFORT ReasoningEffortValue(value) unless empty or default LLM_REASONING_BUDGET_TOKENS reasoning.budget_tokens; negative is HTTP 400 DISABLE_THINKING (legacy) only when none of the three reasoning keys is set: reasoning.enabled = False EXTENDED_REASONING (legacy) same condition: enabled = True, effort = HIGH LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS GenerationDefaults.max_output_tokens; zero or negative is HTTP 400 How a profile becomes a concrete max_tokens value happens inside llmai (prepare_generation with the model's capabilities). Presenton's own test pins the observable behavior: with a model whose metadata reports 16,384 output tokens, both balanced and model_max resolve to 16,384; for an unknown model, balanced resolves to 8,192 and model_max to 32,768 (tests/unit/test_generation_defaults.py:21, tests/unit/test_generation_defaults.py:34).

The Advanced text-provider settings panel (servers/nextjs/components/AdvancedTextProviderSettings.tsx:214) asks the backend what those numbers would be for a given provider and model before anything is saved: resolve_generation_token_defaults (api/v1/ppt/endpoints/generation.py:27) maps Presenton names to llmai names first (PROVIDER_ALIASES: codex to chatgpt, custom and ollama to openai, together to togetherai), substitutes unknown-model for an empty model, calls get_model_capabilities, and runs prepare_generation once with BALANCED and once with MODEL_MAX. The request model limits provider to 40 and model to 300 characters.

Smart mode decides reasoning per model: get_smart_reasoning_config (utils/llm_calls/generate_smart_presentation.py:705) returns no reasoning config when legacy DISABLE_THINKING is on (and no explicit reasoning keys are set). Otherwise it asks llmai.supports_thinking(model, provider=...); if explicit LLM_REASONING_* settings exist it defers to them, and if the model supports thinking it enables reasoning, with effort LOW for openai and azure and no effort override for other providers. See Smart mode.

Every LLM call site wraps failures in handle_llm_client_exceptions (utils/llm_client_error_handler.py:35), which always returns an HTTPException: Exception Status returned Detail HTTPException unchanged unchanged, except 401/403 with codex (below) llmai.shared.errors.BaseError its status_code safe_llm_provider_error_detail(status_code, message) openai.APIError its status_code, or 500 openai_error_detail(e, operation="API request") google.genai.errors.APIError always 500 safe detail prefixed Google API error: anything else 500 safe detail of LLM API error: <e> With LLM=codex, a 401 or 403 becomes HTTP 401 with the header X-Presenton-Auth-Action: codex-reauth and a detail starting with CHATGPT_AUTH_REQUIRED:, which the UI uses to prompt a new sign-in. utils/provider_error_messages.py keeps raw provider payloads out of the UI. safe_llm_provider_error_detail (provider_error_messages.py:159) works only from the status code and the message text: It returns "Invalid API key. Please verify your API key and try again." when the status is 401 or the message matches one of the _INVALID_API_KEY_PATTERNS (provider_error_messages.py:16): "invalid api key", "incorrect api key", "api key is invalid", "no api key", or the word "authentication". An empty message becomes "The AI provider returned an error. Please try again.". A message that looks like a raw payload (starts with { or [, contains {'error', "error", Error code:, or http in any case) goes through safe_provider_error_detail("AI provider", "API request", ...) (provider_error_messages.py:104). That returns, in order of checks: the invalid-key message, a safety-system message for moderation_blocked, a quota message for code insufficient_quota, an access message for 403, "AI provider API request is temporarily rate limited. Please wait and try again." for 429, a "model is not available" message when the text mentions a model that is not found or not accessible, and otherwise "AI provider API request failed. Please try again.". Any other (plain, human-readable) message passes through unchanged. Gotcha Because any message containing the word "authentication" is reported as an invalid API key, a provider error such as "authentication service unavailable" surfaces in the UI as a bad-key message. Check the server log (handle_llm_client_exceptions always prints the traceback) before rotating keys.

The settings UI validates keys and lists models through these routes (the admin-only ones are enforced by SessionAuthMiddleware, see chapter 5): Route Body Upstream call Admin only POST /api/v1/ppt/openai/models/available {"url", "api_key"} GET <url>/models with the OpenAI SDK; api.together.ai and api.together.xyz hosts use raw aiohttp yes POST /api/v1/ppt/anthropic/models/available {"api_key"} GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models?limit=50 with anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 no POST /api/v1/ppt/google/models/available {"api_key"} genai.Client(api_key).models.list(page_size=50) no POST /api/v1/ppt/openrouter/providers/available {"model", "api_key", "base_url"} GET <root>/models/<author>/<slug>/endpoints, falling back to GET <root>/providers yes GET /api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/available?ollama_url= none GET <ollama>/api/tags (10 s timeout) yes GET /api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/supported none merges the 54 tested models with pulled ones no GET /api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/library none the static tested list no A typical exchange: The base URL is validated and normalized to end in /v1 (utils/available_models.py:96, utils/available_models.py:120); a blank key becomes the placeholder "EMPTY" because local proxies often have no auth but the SDK rejects an empty key; redirects are refused. Failures raise ModelAvailabilityError (utils/available_models.py:16), whose HTTP status is 400 for any upstream 4xx and 500 otherwise, with a safe message from Step 9. The OpenRouter route accepts only the default root https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 or the server-configured OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, and builds the outbound URL from server configuration, never from the request (api/v1/ppt/endpoints/openrouter.py:47). Its response is a sorted list of {"value", "label", "available", "context_length", "max_completion_tokens", "supported_parameters"}. Gotcha GET /ollama/models/available with an ollama_url override additionally requires an Origin or Referer from a trusted origin (the request's own origin, PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, or PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS), or Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin (api/v1/ppt/endpoints/ollama.py:27). The comment explains that SameSite=Lax cookies ride along on cross-site top-level GET navigations, so an admin cookie alone does not prove intent.

POST /api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/pull?model_name=llama3.2:3b&ollama_url= first calls list_available_ollama_models to fail fast with 503 ("Could not connect to Ollama at ... use host.docker.internal instead of localhost") if Ollama is unreachable, then returns a text/event-stream produced by pull_ollama_model (utils/ollama.py:174). That generator posts {"name": ..., "stream": true, "insecure": false} to <ollama>/api/pull with no timeout and translates Ollama's NDJSON lines into SSE frames: Ollama errors become event: error with {"detail": ...}. The URL normalizer _get_ollama_url (utils/ollama.py:46) defaults to http://localhost:11434, adds http:// when the scheme is missing, rejects control characters, backslashes, %, ?, # and dot segments, and refuses redirects. The tested catalog is SUPPORTED_OLLAMA_MODELS in constants/supported_ollama_models.py:314 (Llama 3.x, Gemma, DeepSeek, Qwen, gpt-oss, Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 families). The ollamapullstatus table exists in the schema but no code reads or writes it at this snapshot.

The codex provider uses a ChatGPT subscription instead of an API key. utils/oauth/openai_codex.py is a Python port of an existing TypeScript implementation (its docstring names pi-mono-main/packages/ai/src/utils/oauth/openai-codex.ts); PKCE helpers live in utils/oauth/pkce.py. Concrete values from utils/oauth/openai_codex.py:22: CLIENT_ID = "app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann", authorize URL https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize, token URL https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token, redirect URI http://localhost:1455/auth/callback, scope openid profile email offline_access. The authorize URL also carries id_token_add_organizations=true, codex_cli_simplified_flow=true and originator=pi (openai_codex.py:357). Endpoint (/api/v1/ppt/codex/auth) Behavior POST /initiate Creates the flow, starts the callback server, stores {verifier, state, server, server_started} in the module-level dict _sessions under a new UUID. If port 1455 cannot be bound, the instructions tell the user to paste the redirect URL into /exchange GET /status/{session_id} Non-blocking peek at the captured code. {"status": "pending"} until a code arrives; then exchanges it, closes the server, drops the session, stores tokens and returns success or failed POST /exchange Manual fallback. Body {"session_id", "code"} where code may be a bare code, code#state, a query string, or the full redirect URL. A mismatching state is a 400 "possible CSRF" here POST /refresh Refresh-token grant; 401 with the re-auth header on failure GET /status not_authenticated, expired or authenticated with profile fields decoded from the JWT POST /logout Blanks all CODEX_* env vars including CODEX_MODEL and persists the cleared values Token storage. _store_token (codex_auth.py:113) writes the access token, refresh token, expiry (Unix milliseconds) and profile (account id from the https://api.openai.com/auth claim chatgpt_account_id, email, name, and is_pro = plan_type != "free") into os.environ, then save_codex_tokens_to_user_config (utils/user_config.py:589) merges them into userConfig.json and calls sync_legacy_file_to_provider_settings to copy the file into the database row. Because the Codex fields are OAuth-managed in merge_provider_settings, a later settings save cannot overwrite them. Refresh on use. _get_codex_access_token (utils/llm_config.py:108) runs inside _get_llm_config for every Codex call. When the stored expiry is

docs.t: Step 13: The Presenton Cloud provider proxy
docs.x: Selecting LLM = "presenton" sends generation to Presenton's hosted service instead of a local model. Note that presenton is not a member of LLMProvider: local generation code would reject it with HTTP 500. It works because the requests never reach that code. Connecting. An admin runs the OAuth 2.0 device flow through /api/v1/auth/presenton/device/start and /device/poll against the issuer https://api.presenton.ai (api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:164, presenton_oauth.py:217). On success store_presenton_credentials (services/presenton_cloud.py:84) upserts the single presenton_cloud_provider row with the subject, email, expiry (default 30 days when the token response omits expires_in) and the access token encrypted with Fernet. The Fernet key is SHA-256("presenton-oauth-credentials-v1:" + AUTH_SECRET_KEY) (services/presenton_cloud.py:28), where the secret comes from get_or_create_auth_secret (api/v1/auth/config.py:71), the AUTH_SECRET_KEY stored in userConfig.json and generated on first use. Rotating AUTH_SECRET_KEY makes the stored token undecryptable and the admin must reconnect. There is no refresh token; has_cloud_credentials simply requires a non-expired token. Proxying. maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request (services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:407) runs inside SessionAuthMiddleware for browser sessions (and for the auth-disabled desktop with allow_unowned=True). It returns None, meaning "serve locally", unless all of these hold: the path is in one of the cloud path sets, the method is allowed (community paths are GET only), and the database setting LLM is presenton. If LLM is presenton but no valid token is stored, it returns 503 "Presenton is selected but the global provider is not connected". Two smaller rules sit in front of that: community paths return 404 community_disabled when PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED is off, and a request carrying presenton_cloud_only=true while LLM is not presenton gets 409 "Presenton cloud templates were requested but Presenton is not selected" (presenton_cloud_proxy.py:440). Path set (presenton_cloud_proxy.py:42) Paths Generation /api/v1/ppt/files/upload, /files/decompose, /presentation/create, /presentation/prepare Edit /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit, /presentation/update, /presentation/slide_update Smart /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate-html/init, /api/v2/ppt/presentation/update Prefixes /api/v1/async-tasks, /api/v1/ppt/outlines/,

Reads: servers/fastapi/services/database.py, servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py, servers/fastapi/migrations.py, servers/fastapi/alembic/env.py, servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/*.py, servers/fastapi/models/sql/*.py · Builds on: FastAPI app and startup · Time: ~35 min This chapter is the reference for everything Presenton keeps in its relational database. You will see how DATABASE_URL becomes an async SQLAlchemy engine, how the startup migration runner copes with old and half-migrated databases, the full Alembic revision chain, and then every table and every column of the 15 SQL models, with realistic JSON values taken from the code that writes them. It ends with ownership isolation, how presentations and slides are duplicated, and what the v1-standard / v2-standard version flag really means.

docs.t: Step 1: Pick the database URL and the async driver
docs.x: Every database connection in the FastAPI process starts from one function, get_database_url_and_connect_args() (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:57). It runs once at import time of services/database.py (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:34), so the URL is fixed for the lifetime of the process.

docs.t: 1.1 The default: SQLite under the app data directory
docs.x: servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py (excerpt) The resolution order is: DATABASE_URL (get_database_url_env, servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:40) if it is set and non-empty. Otherwise sqlite:///<APP_DATA_DIRECTORY>/fastapi.db (get_app_data_directory_env, servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:44). In Docker, APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/app_data (Dockerfile:82), so the file is /app_data/fastapi.db. If APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is unset too, /tmp/presenton/fastapi.db. _ensure_sqlite_parent_dir (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:7) creates the parent folder of a SQLite file with os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True), and strips the leading slash of Windows paths such as /C:/... before doing so.

The runtime engine is async, so plain scheme prefixes are rewritten to async dialects: Scheme in DATABASE_URL Runtime URL (async) Alembic URL (sync, to_sync_sqlalchemy_url) sqlite:// sqlite+aiosqlite:// sqlite:// postgresql:// postgresql+asyncpg:// postgresql+psycopg:// (psycopg 3) mysql:// mysql+aiomysql:// mysql+pymysql:// anything else (for example postgresql+asyncpg://... already) unchanged postgresql+asyncpg:// and mysql+aiomysql:// are also mapped; other schemes pass through to_sync_sqlalchemy_url lives at servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:103. Its docstring explains the choice of sync drivers: psycopg2 is not installed when asyncpg is the runtime driver, and PyMySQL is already pulled in by aiomysql. Gotcha postgres:// (the short form some hosting platforms emit) is not in the rewrite list. It passes through unchanged and SQLAlchemy will not find an async driver for it. Use postgresql:// in DATABASE_URL.

docs.t: 1.3 Connect arguments and the query string
docs.x: After the rewrite, the function builds connect_args: SQLite gets check_same_thread=False (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:74). For postgresql+asyncpg, a query parameter sslmode with any value other than disable produces connect_args["ssl"] = ssl.create_default_context() (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:84). Then the entire query string is dropped from the URL (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:88), because asyncpg does not accept libpq-style parameters. Any parse failure is swallowed (except Exception: pass). So postgresql://u:p@db:5432/presenton?sslmode=require becomes the URL postgresql+asyncpg://u:p@db:5432/presenton plus {"ssl": <SSLContext>}. Gotcha Every query parameter is discarded, not only sslmode. Options such as application_name or options=-csearch_path=... in DATABASE_URL silently have no effect at runtime. Alembic gets the same stripped URL because migrations.py calls the same function first (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:59).

docs.t: Step 2: Create the engine, the session factory and the listeners
docs.x: servers/fastapi/services/database.py is a module with side effects. Importing it builds the engine: servers/fastapi/services/database.py (excerpt)

get_pool_kwargs (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:34) reads five optional environment variables. Non-integer values fall back to the default through _int_env (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:23). Variable SQLAlchemy argument Default DB_POOL_SIZE pool_size 5 DB_MAX_OVERFLOW max_overflow 10 DB_POOL_TIMEOUT pool_timeout (seconds) 30 DB_POOL_RECYCLE pool_recycle (seconds) 1800 DB_POOL_PRE_PING pool_pre_ping true (anything except false, 0, no) These are not read through utils/get_env.py, so they do not appear in the environment getter inventory of Configuration and LLM providers. They apply only when the URL does not contain the substring sqlite.

SQLite ignores foreign keys unless PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is issued on every connection. The connect listener does exactly that (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:45). Without it, none of the ondelete="CASCADE" clauses in the models would fire on the default database.

async_session_maker uses expire_on_commit=False (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:53), so ORM objects stay readable after commit(). Routes receive a session through the dependency get_async_session (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:111), which opens one AsyncSession per request. Background jobs and startup code open their own with async with async_session_maker() as session.

The module also registers _scope_owned_selects on do_orm_execute and _stamp_new_owned_rows on before_flush (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:67 and :100). They are covered in Step 6 below and in depth in FastAPI app and startup.

docs.t: Step 3: Migrate or create the schema at startup
docs.x: The lifespan runs two functions back to back (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:56 and :57): MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP defaults to "true" (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:453); docker-compose.yml sets it to true and Electron sets it to "True" (electron/app/main.ts:374). Only those two spellings count; 1 or yes disable migrations.

When migrations are off, create_db_and_tables (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:117) calls SQLModel.metadata.create_all with an explicit list of 15 tables: presentations, slides, key-value, template v2, chat history, image assets, font uploads, webhook subscriptions, async tasks, legacy async generation tasks, Ollama pull status, user, API keys, provider settings and the Presenton Cloud provider. create_all creates missing tables only. Gotcha With MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=false, an existing table never gets new columns. Upgrading a deployment that runs with migrations disabled leaves, for example, presentations without generation_mode, and the first query fails. Either keep migrations on or run alembic upgrade head yourself.

migrate_database_on_startup (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:40) runs _run_migrations through asyncio.to_thread, because Alembic is synchronous. It prints Migrations run successfully or Error running migrations: ... and re-raises, so a failed migration aborts startup. _run_migrations (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:52) does four things in order: Builds an Alembic Config in code, with script_location pointing at servers/fastapi/alembic and sqlalchemy.url set to the sync URL from Step 1. alembic.ini is not read on this path. _repair_orphan_alembic_revision (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:79): if alembic_version.version_num names a revision that no longer exists in alembic/versions (an old image, a removed branch), it infers the real schema level from the live tables and overwrites version_num. _stamp_legacy_database_if_needed (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:264): if the database has application tables but no row in alembic_version (a database created by create_all, or by a pre-Alembic release), it infers the revision from the schema and runs command.stamp. command.upgrade(config, "head"). If that throws and the database is still "unversioned but populated", it stamps and upgrades once more as a safety net (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:68). "Populated" means at least one of 17 known table names exists, including legacy ones such as templates, presentation_layout_codes, template_create_infos and access_tokens (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:294).

docs.t: 3.3 Inferring a revision from the schema
docs.x: _infer_revision_from_schema (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:117) is a best-effort decision ladder that walks from the newest feature down. Rows are tested top to bottom and the first match wins; the first five rows all require that provider_settings and user exist and that every owned table present has owner_id: Evidence in the live schema Inferred revision template_v2.theme exists e4c7a9b2d6f1 else presenton_cloud_provider exists c6e8f1a3b5d7 else presentations.generation_mode exists f3a7c1d9e5b2 else user.admin_slot exists e1b3c5d7f9a2 else d0a2b4c6e8f1 user exists and ownership is ready c9f1a2b3d4e5 template_v2 exists one of a7d4c9e2f1b3, 4b7c9d0e1f2a, 3f2a1b4c5d6e, 5d7e9a1b2c3f, 2c8f4a1b9d7e, 9b2d1c4e5f6a, 8a6c4d2e1f30, 6e4a1b2c3d5f or c7b70d0f31b1, depending on font_uploads, string ids, is_default, slides.ui, presentations.fonts, chat_history_messages.template_v2_id and presentations.version async_tasks exists a7d4c9e2f1b3 chat_history_messages exists c7b70d0f31b1 template_create_infos exists 95b5127e93cd presentations.theme exists 82abdbc476a7 none of the above 00b3c27a13bc The string-id test _is_uuid_storage_column (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:253) treats a column as UUID storage when its reflected type class is uuid or its rendered type is uuid or char(32). That is how SQLAlchemy stores Uuid on SQLite and MySQL. Gotcha The inference never returns the head 026c0ba8b35c. A database that already has api_keys but no alembic_version row is stamped at e4c7a9b2d6f1, and upgrade then re-runs 026c0ba8b35c, whose op.create_table("api_keys", ...) is not guarded by an existence check (it guards only the access_tokens drop and the async_tasks.payload column). The most likely way to get there is a deployment that ran with MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=false (so create_all created api_keys) and is then switched to migrations. The retry in _run_migrations does not help, because after stamping the database is no longer unversioned. This was found by reading the code, not by running it.

servers/fastapi/alembic.ini exists for command-line use (alembic revision --autogenerate). Its sqlalchemy.url = sqlite:///placeholder (servers/fastapi/alembic.ini:7) is a sentinel. alembic/env.py recognises it in _get_url (servers/fastapi/alembic/env.py:46) and falls back to get_database_url_and_connect_args() converted with to_sync_sqlalchemy_url, so the CLI uses the same DATABASE_URL / APP_DATA_DIRECTORY logic as the app. env.py imports all 15 model modules (servers/fastapi/alembic/env.py:15 to :33) so that SQLModel.metadata is complete before autogenerate compares it. Online migrations use pool.NullPool and compare_type=True (servers/fastapi/alembic/env.py:80 to :89). User and PresentonCloudProvider are plain SQLAlchemy declarative classes, but UserBase.metadata = SQLModel.metadata (servers/fastapi/models/sql/user.py:13) puts them in the same metadata object.

The codebase convention, visible in every revision from 5 onwards, is: Write the revision by hand (or autogenerate and then edit) with down_revision set to the current head, 026c0ba8b35c. Guard every operation with _has_table / _has_column / _has_index helpers built on sa.inspect(op.get_bind()). Use op.batch_alter_table for anything that alters an existing column, because SQLite cannot ALTER COLUMN in place. Add a REVISION_... constant in migrations.py, move REVISION_HEAD to it, and teach _infer_revision_from_schema how to recognise your schema change. The test file servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_migrations.py has one test per such step, for example test_upgrade_from_template_v2_theme_adds_unified_keys_and_task_payload (line 882).

The ER diagram below shows the current model tables and their foreign keys. Legacy tables that only exist in migrated databases are omitted. Tables with no relationships at all: provider_settings, presenton_cloud_provider, font_uploads, keyvaluesqlmodel, ollamapullstatus. A note on types used below. AutoString is SQLModel's VARCHAR without a length. Uuid is SQLAlchemy's portable UUID type: native UUID on PostgreSQL, CHAR(32) hex elsewhere. JSON is native JSON on PostgreSQL and MySQL and TEXT holding serialized JSON on SQLite. Columns declared through a SQLModel Field without sa_column are NOT NULL unless the type is Optional.

Defined in servers/fastapi/models/sql/async_task.py:16. This is the table behind every .../async endpoint and the polling API. Column Type Null Default Notes id AutoString PK "task-" + token_hex(32) 69 characters owner_id Uuid yes current owner FK user.id CASCADE type AutoString no none Indexed, e.g. presentation.generate (presentation.py:137) status String no none Indexed; pending, completed or error (servers/fastapi/enums/async_task_status.py:4) message AutoString yes None Human-readable progress error JSON yes None APIErrorModel dump data JSON yes None Progress and result payload JSON yes None The original request, for resumable jobs; excluded from API output created_at DateTime(tz) no UTC now updated_at DateTime(tz) no UTC now onupdate There is no processing status: revision 16 rewrote old processing rows to pending. The field serializer at async_task.py:58 returns the plain string whether the attribute holds the enum or a raw string from the database. Lifecycle of a presentation generation task, from presentation.py:3250, :3113 and :3158: queued completed error template task payload POST /api/v1/ppt/template/async (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:1569) stores the request (minus generation_options unless explicitly set) in payload and a per-layout progress map built by _template_task_progress_data (template.py:396) in data. Values illustrative: "template.create" is ASYNC_TASK_TYPE_TEMPLATE_CREATE (template.py:100). The polling API that reads these rows is covered in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP. Gotcha The column is timezone-aware, but the background runner assigns async_status.updated_at = datetime.now() (presentation.py:3128), a naive local time. On PostgreSQL a naive value written into timestamptz is interpreted in the session time zone, and on SQLite it is stored without an offset next to UTC values written by the default. Compare updated_at values across rows with care. At startup, fail_interrupted_async_tasks turns every still-pending task into error, so a crash never leaves pollers waiting forever (FastAPI app and startup).
