Eight models carry owner_id: presentations, slides, chat history, image assets, async tasks, the legacy async generation tasks, webhook subscriptions and template_v2. All declare it identically: servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py (excerpt) The rules that follow from this, and from the two listeners in services/database.py: Rule Where Deleting a user deletes all of their rows (FK ON DELETE CASCADE) every owner_id column Deleting a presentation deletes its slides and its chat messages slides.presentation, chat_history_messages.presentation_id Deleting a template deletes its template-scoped chat messages chat_history_messages.template_v2_id Every ORM SELECT in a request with an owner gets owner_id = :owner for the seven strict models _scope_owned_selects, services/database.py:67 template_v2 is visible when owner_id = :owner or (owner_id IS NULL and is_default) services/database.py:87 New owned rows are stamped with the current owner before INSERT, overriding any supplied value _stamp_new_owned_rows, services/database.py:100 Bulk UPDATE/DELETE are not filtered, so code adds owner_id == get_current_owner_id() itself e.g. presentation.py:3328 owner_id never appears in JSON responses (exclude=True) all eight models NULL owner rows exist when auth is disabled (Electron) or for bundled templates see chapter 5 The test servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_owner_isolation.py:14 demonstrates the template rule with three rows: a shared default (owner_id=None, is_default=True), an unowned private template (owner_id=None, is_default=False) and the second user's private template. Querying as the first user, only the shared default is visible. _backfill_legacy_ownership (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:128) assigns all owner_id IS NULL rows to the bootstrap administrator when a single-user install is upgraded, except bundled templates, which stay shared. The mechanics of the contextvars, background tasks and the skip_owner_scope escape hatch are explained step by step in FastAPI app and startup; the account model behind them is in Auth and multi-user. Gotcha font_uploads, provider_settings, presenton_cloud_provider, keyvaluesqlmodel and ollamapullstatus have no owner and are shared by every user. That is intended for provider settings (admin-only routes) and for fonts, but keep it in mind before storing anything user-specific in a new global table.

Two model methods copy rows. They do not touch the database; the caller adds and commits the new objects. servers/fastapi/models/sql/slide.py (excerpt) PresentationModel.get_new_presentation (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:83) does the same for a presentation: a fresh uuid4() id, every scalar column copied, every JSON column (file_paths, outlines, layout, structure, theme, fonts, community_design_ids) deep-copied, and created_at / updated_at left to their defaults so the copy is "new". Deep copies matter because SQLAlchemy JSON columns hold mutable Python dicts; sharing one dict between two ORM objects would make an edit to one silently change the other. Note what get_new_slide does with its content override: content or self.content means an empty dict {} passed as the override falls back to the original content. Also note that both copies carry owner_id from the source row, but _stamp_new_owned_rows overwrites it with the current request's owner on flush whenever an owner is in context. The callers: Endpoint Function What it does POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/duplicate duplicate_presentation, presentation.py:1585 New presentation, title suffixed with (Copy) when it has one, one new slide per old slide in index order POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/derive derive_presentation_from_existing_one, presentation.py:3353 New presentation; slides whose index appears in the request get deep_update(old_content, new_content); every slide's ui is re-hydrated; then exported POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/edit edit_presentation_with_new_content, presentation.py:3302 Same presentation; only the edited slides are replaced by new rows with new ids, and the old rows are deleted with an owner predicate; then exported A worked duplicate, with values from the earlier examples: Gotcha /edit gives the edited slides new primary keys. Anything that cached a slide id (an open editor tab, an external integration) points at a deleted row afterwards. Chat history is keyed by presentation, not by slide, so it survives. Gotcha get_new_presentation copies owner_id, but chat history, image asset rows and async tasks are not copied. A duplicated deck shares the image files of the original (the URLs inside content are copied verbatim), so deleting files belonging to one deck can break the other.

servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py (excerpt) The column is stored as a non-native enum, that is a string column plus a CHECK constraint named presentation_version (native_enum=False, create_constraint=True, presentation.py:36 to :41), so adding a third value later requires a migration that recreates the constraint. What the two values mean at this snapshot: v1-standard is only ever written by migration 6e4a1b2c3d5f, which backfills it into every pre-existing presentation (servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/6e4a1b2c3d5f_add_template_v2_and_presentation_version.py:22 and :90). These are decks generated with the old React layout templates, before Template v2 existed. Their layout column holds the old PresentationLayoutModel shape ({"name", "ordered", "icon_type", "icon_weight", "slides": [{"id", "description", "json_schema"}]}, servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:18) instead of {"layouts": [...]}, and their slides have no ui. v2-standard is what every current code path writes: /create (presentation.py:1747), /create/blank (presentation.py:1804), the one-shot generator (presentation.py:2944) and Presenton Cloud persistence (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_persistence.py:83 and :156). Smart-mode decks are also v2-standard; the Smart/standard distinction is generation_mode, a separate column. The backend treats both the same way except for listing: GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all?version=... filters on it (presentation.py:1499). The difference is enforced in the frontend: Place Behaviour for v1-standard Dashboard (DashboardPage.tsx:427) Fetches v2-standard with first-slide previews and v1-standard with includeSlides: false, keeping legacy decks in a separate list Presentation card (PresentationCard.tsx:52) Marks the deck unsupported and shows "This deck was created in an older Presenton version. Downgrade to a compatible version to open it." Editor loader (usePresentationData.ts:33) Shows the same warning and redirects to /dashboard (All three paths are under servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/.) So v1-standard decks are kept, listed and deletable, but cannot be opened or edited in this version. Gotcha PresentationModel.get_layout() (presentation.py:113) parses layout as the old PresentationLayoutModel. Calling it on a v2-standard deck fails validation because there is no slides key. Current code checks

Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py, servers/fastapi/utils/outline_utils.py, servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py, servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py · Builds on: Data model · Time: ~45 min This chapter follows one Standard-mode deck from the moment the web UI submits a prompt to the moment slides are saved and exported. You will see the exact four HTTP calls the browser makes, every function they run in order, the database columns each call writes, how slide counts and tables of contents are enforced, and why slide text is generated one slide at a time in the web UI path but ten at a time in the one-shot API. The chapter ends with the one-shot POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate endpoint, including its asynchronous variant and the slides_markdown shortcut.

All routes below are mounted under /api/v1/ppt (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22); the presentation router adds /presentation (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:136) and the outline router adds /outlines (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:40). Order Method and path Handler Response Writes to presentations 1 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create create_presentation (presentation.py:1681) JSON PresentationModel new row: prompt, settings, version, n_slides 2 GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/{id} stream_outlines (outlines.py:84) text/event-stream outlines, title, n_slides (auto mode) 2b (optional) PUT /api/v1/ppt/outlines/{id} update_outline (outlines.py:59) JSON outline outlines, n_slides, title 3 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare prepare_presentation (presentation.py:1840) {"presentation_id": ...} outlines (with TOC), title, language="", layout, fonts, structure 4 GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id} stream_presentation (presentation.py:2281) text/event-stream replaces all slides rows, adds ImageAsset rows (servers/fastapi/models/sql/image_asset.py:12) 5 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export (or the editor's export) export_existing_presentation (presentation.py:1642) {"presentation_id", "path", "edit_path"} none The one-shot path collapses steps 1 to 5 into POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate (presentation.py:3169) and POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async (presentation.py:3240), covered in Step 6.

The upload page calls PresentationGenerationApi.createPresentation (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/presentation-generation.ts:82), which posts JSON to /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create. The handler declares each field as its own Body() parameter, so FastAPI reads them from one JSON object. Field Type Default Server-side validation content str required none (Smart mode requires prompt, files or community refs) n_slides int or null null >= 1, <= MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES (50) (presentation.py:1698-1708) language str or null null stripped, stored as "" when missing (presentation.py:1736) file_paths list[str] or null null each path must resolve inside the temp directory and exist (presentation.py:1737-1741) tone Tone enum default one of default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch (servers/fastapi/enums/tone.py:4-10) verbosity Verbosity enum standard one of concise, standard, text-heavy (servers/fastapi/enums/verbosity.py:4-7) instructions str or null null none include_table_of_contents bool false if true and n_slides < 3, 400 (presentation.py:1710-1714) include_title_slide bool true none web_search bool false none generation_mode "standard" or "smart" "standard" Smart checks at presentation.py:1716-1733 community_design_ids list[int] or null null Smart only, and only if community is enabled A typical body from the upload page (values illustrative, keys from presentation-generation.ts:116-136): The row is built and committed immediately: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) After the commit it logs which web search route is active (presentation.py:1765-1778) and returns the row as JSON. At this point outlines, layout, structure, title, fonts and theme are all null, and the slides table has no rows for this id. Gotcha The browser sends a version field, but create_presentation has no version parameter. The value is ignored and every new row is written with PresentationVersion.V2_STANDARD (presentation.py:1747). The enum's other value, v1-standard (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:17), only marks rows migrated from older databases; the web UI refuses to open such decks (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:33-41). Gotcha n_slides = 0 in the database means "let the model decide". Every later step checks presentation.n_slides > 0 before treating

docs.t: Step 2: Stream and persist the outline
docs.x: The outline page opens an EventSource on /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/{id} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:107-109). The handler loads the row (404 if missing), logs the web search routing, creates a fresh temp directory with TEMP_FILE_SERVICE.create_temp_dir() (outlines.py:110) and returns a StreamingResponse wrapping inner() in safe_sse_stream (outlines.py:268-276). Event shapes are documented in Streaming (SSE); here we follow the logic.
inner() returns immediately if the client is already gone (outlines.py:113-114), then yields the status "Preparing your presentation outline" (outlines.py:116-118).

If presentation.file_paths is set, a DocumentsLoader parses every file and the texts are joined with blank lines into additional_context (outlines.py:120-129). In the web UI the paths are already the .txt files produced by /files/decompose, so this step usually just reads text. The full ingestion story, including LiteParse and OCR, is in Document ingestion.

docs.t: 2.3 Decide how many outlines to request
docs.x: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py (excerpt) get_no_of_outlines_to_generate_for_n_slides (servers/fastapi/utils/outline_utils.py:68-81) reserves room for table-of-contents slides that /prepare will insert later. With TOC enabled it computes n_toc_1 = ceil((n - 1 if title else n) / 10), then n_toc_2 = ceil((n - n_toc_1) / 10), and returns n - n_toc_2. Without TOC it returns n. Requested n_slides Title slide TOC Outlines requested from the LLM TOC slides added in Step 3 Final slide count 8 yes no 8 0 8 10 yes yes 9 1 10 25 yes yes 22 3 25 0 (auto) any any model decides, max 50 see Step 3 outlines plus TOC

docs.t: 2.4 Build the prompt and record it
docs.x: get_outline_messages(...) builds the system and user messages (outlines.py:142-152). The text of those two messages, plus the extracted document text, is stored through MEM0_PRESENTATION_MEMORY_SERVICE.store_generation_context(...) (outlines.py:153-168) so the chat assistant can recall it later (Editing and chat assistant). The prompts themselves are dissected in Prompts and schemas.

generate_ppt_outline(...) (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:252) is an async generator. It: Picks the response model: get_presentation_outline_model_with_n_slides(n_slides) when a count is known, else PresentationOutlineModel (generate_presentation_outlines.py:267-271). Chooses a web search route when web_search is true: a hosted WebSearchTool for models with native search, or an external provider whose results are appended to additional_context after an LLM-generated query (generate_presentation_outlines.py:273-353). Details are in Images, icons, web search. Streams the structured response through stream_generate_events and yields every text delta (generate_presentation_outlines.py:372-403). If the provider only returns a final completion object, the serialized JSON is yielded once. On any exception, yields (not raises) the HTTPException produced by handle_llm_client_exceptions(e) (generate_presentation_outlines.py:404-405). The endpoint loop (outlines.py:170-205) forwards statuses as status events, turns a yielded HTTPException into an error event and stops, and forwards text deltas as chunk events while accumulating them in presentation_outlines_text. await asyncio.sleep(0) after each item (outlines.py:185) yields control to the event loop so the frame is flushed promptly.

docs.t: 2.6 Parse, normalize and enforce the count
docs.x: The accumulated text is parsed with dirtyjson.loads, which tolerates trailing commas and similar damage (outlines.py:207-216). A parse failure yields the error "Failed to generate presentation outlines. Please try again. <exception text>". The dict then passes through normalize_outline_payload(payload, MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES) (servers/fastapi/utils/outline_limits.py:37-68), which: unwraps a slides value that is a JSON string (some providers implement structured output with tool calls and return the array as a string), keeps at most 50 slides, trims each slide's content to MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS words (default 100). servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py (excerpt)

The handler writes presentation.outlines = presentation_outlines.model_dump() and a title from get_presentation_title_from_presentation_outline (outlines.py:248-254), stores the outlines in memory (outlines.py:256-259) and yields a complete event whose presentation key is the whole row (outlines.py:261-263). The stored outlines JSON looks like this: Gotcha The "title" is not generated separately. get_presentation_title_from_presentation_outline (outline_utils.py:19-41) takes the first 100 characters of the first outline, strips an optional ## Page N prefix, removes #, / and \, and replaces newlines with spaces. A first outline that starts with a long heading plus bullets produces a title that includes bullet text. The outline prompt compensates by requiring "First slide title must be the same as the presentation title."

Between streaming and preparing, the outline page can read and replace the outline: GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/{id} returns {"slides": []} when nothing is stored (outlines.py:44-56), and PUT /api/v1/ppt/outlines/{id} overwrites outlines, sets n_slides = len(outline.slides) and recomputes the title (outlines.py:59-81). The outline page PUTs the current outlines before it sends a message to the outline chat assistant and GETs them again after the assistant changes them (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlinePage.tsx:343-363). Manual edits in the outline editor live in Redux and reach the server through the /prepare body, so a PUT is not required for generation.

When the user picks a template and clicks generate, usePresentationGeneration posts the outline list and the template id (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/usePresentationGeneration.ts:107-111): The client trims outlines with limitOutlines (50 slides, 100 words each) before sending (presentation-generation.ts:226-234). The handler signature also accepts an optional title (presentation.py:1845), which the web UI does not send.

prepare_presentation rejects an empty list (400 "Outlines are required"), more than 50 outlines, and an unknown presentation id (presentation.py:1848-1858). The outlines are wrapped in PresentationOutlineModel(slides=outlines) (presentation.py:1860).

docs.t: 3.2 Load the layout from the template
docs.x: _resolve_prepare_layout(layout, sql_session) (presentation.py:1448-1470) is the bridge from a template row to the model the LLM sees: _extract_template_id strips whitespace and an optional custom- prefix (presentation.py:200-209). An empty id is a 400. sql_session.get(TemplateV2, template_id); a missing row is a 404 "Template layout not found". _copy_template_layout_payload(template) deep-copies template.layouts and stamps icon_type, icon_weight, name and template_id onto it (presentation.py:232-247). This dict is what will be saved in presentations.layout. _build_template_structure_layout calls _build_template_layout_model (presentation.py:410-470), which runs get_template_schema(layout_payload) from servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257 and turns each generated layout into a SlideLayoutModel(id, name, description, json_schema). The result is a PresentationLayoutModel with ordered=False. Template fonts come from template.assets["fonts"] via _extract_template_fonts_from_assets (presentation.py:337-340). How a template's components become that JSON schema is the subject of From template to schema to slide; the template format itself is in Template v2 format. PresentationLayoutModel and SlideLayoutModel live in servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:11-62 (re-exported by servers/fastapi/models/presentation_layout.py). Its to_string() (presentation_layout.py:49-62) renders the layout list that the structure prompt receives; with two illustrative layouts it produces:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) Because _build_template_layout_model always sets ordered=False (presentation.py:467), the LLM branch always runs for Template V2 layouts. generate_presentation_structure (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:157-211) returns PresentationStructureModel(slides=[...]), a list of layout indexes, one per outline. Its prompt and dynamic response model are covered in Prompts and schemas.

Structured output can still return too few indexes or out-of-range ones. _normalize_presentation_structure fixes both before anything is persisted: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) Extra indexes are dropped, missing ones are filled with a random layout, and negative or too-large ones are replaced with a random valid index (presentation.py:384-407). The test test_prepare_presentation_normalizes_incomplete_and_invalid_layout_indexes (servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_presentation_generation_flow.py:891) pins this behavior.

If include_table_of_contents is set (presentation.py:1891-1909): get_no_of_toc_required_for_n_outlines(n_outlines, title_slide, target_total_slides) (outline_utils.py:52-65) computes how many TOC slides are needed. When the row has a positive n_slides, it is used as the target total, so the TOC count matches what Step 2 reserved. select_toc_or_list_slide_layout_index(structure_layout) (servers/fastapi/utils/ppt_utils.py:59-82) searches each layout's id, name, description and schema title with case-insensitive word-boundary regexes, first for TOC patterns (table of contents, table-of-contents, agenda, contents, outline, index, toc) and then for list patterns (bullet list, bulleted list, bullet/bullets, numbered list, ordered list, unordered list, list). Patterns are tried in that priority order, and for each pattern the first matching layout wins (ppt_utils.py:34-56). It returns -1 if nothing matches. _insert_toc_layouts inserts that layout index n_toc_slides times at position 1 (after the title slide) or 0 (presentation.py:361-372). get_presentation_outline_model_with_toc (outline_utils.py:84-137) splits the non-title outlines into n_toc_slides contiguous, near-equal sections and inserts one TOC outline per section. Each line carries the final page number, computed as outlines_before_toc + total_toc_slides + global_outline_index + 1. For a title slide plus one TOC slide, the inserted outline reads: Titles come from _extract_outline_title: the first Markdown heading, else the first sentence, else the first non-empty line, else "Slide" (outline_utils.py:164-181). Gotcha If the template has no layout whose id, name, description or schema title matches a TOC or list pattern, toc_slide_layout_index is -1 and no TOC slide is inserted (presentation.py:367-368, presentation.py:1904). Step 2 already asked the LLM for fewer outlines to leave room for the TOC, so the final deck is shorter than the requested n_slides. Name or describe at least one layout with "agenda" or "list" if you rely on TOC. Gotcha In auto mode with TOC enabled, nothing re-checks the total after insertion. Step 2 stores n_slides = len(outlines) (up to 50), and Step 3 then adds TOC slides on top of that, so a 50-outline auto deck becomes 55 slides. MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES is checked against len(outlines) before the insertion (presentation.py:1850).

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) The outlines are stored again in memory (presentation.py:1923-1926) and the response is {"presentation_id": "<uuid>"}. The browser then navigates to /presentation?id=<id>&stream=true&type=standard (usePresentationGeneration.ts:121-123). Gotcha /prepare sets language = "", so every slide in the web UI path is generated with the slide-content prompt's auto-detect instruction ("auto-detect from the slide content and use the same language as the slide content"). The language you picked on the upload page only affects outline generation and OCR. The one-shot API (Step 6) keeps the requested language for slides. What /prepare does not do It does not write theme. The one-shot handler stores template_theme_for_presentation(...) in theme (presentation.py:2958); the web UI path leaves it null here. Theme handling is covered in Themes and fonts.

The presentation page opens an EventSource on /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationStreaming.ts:300-302). For a Standard deck (type=standard) it does not fetch the row first: preloadPresentationData is true only for editor=v2 or type=smart (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationPage.tsx:188-189). Instead, when the first Template V2 slide chunk arrives and the store has no template layout yet, the hook forces one GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} so the editor learns the layout (usePresentationStreaming.ts:223-263, usePresentationStreaming.ts:472-478). The flowchart below is the internal logic of stream_presentation (presentation.py:2281-2524).

docs.t: 4.1 Preconditions and layout loading (v1 and v2 branches)
docs.x: Smart rows branch off immediately to stream_smart_presentation (presentation.py:2288-2289, see Smart mode). Standard rows must have both structure and outlines (400 "Presentation not prepared for stream" or "Outlines can not be empty", presentation.py:2290-2299). Then three objects are rebuilt from JSON columns inside a try that maps any failure to 400 "Presentation has invalid generated data" (presentation.py:2301-2309): structure = presentation.get_structure() (a PresentationStructureModel), layout = _get_presentation_stream_layout(presentation), outline = presentation.get_presentation_outline(). The layout loader is where the two data formats diverge: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) presentations.layout shape Detected by Layout model built by Notes Template V2 payload: dict with a layouts list (written by /prepare and /generate) _is_template_layout_payload (presentation.py:483-487) _build_template_layout_model, schemas regenerated from components on every stream layout.name is the template id, so slides.layout_group becomes the template id Legacy payload: a serialized PresentationLayoutModel (name, ordered, slides[{id, name, description, json_schema}]) fallback presentation.get_layout() = PresentationLayoutModel(**self.layout) (models/sql/presentation.py:113-114) schemas are stored, not regenerated The PresentationVersion column (v1-standard or v2-standard) is not consulted here. The branch is decided by the JSON shape of layout. In this snapshot every new row is v2-standard with a Template V2 payload, so the first branch is the live one. The layout must contain at least one slide (400 otherwise, presentation.py:2311-2312). The structure is re-normalized against the current outline and layout counts and, if anything changed, the repaired structure is saved with a warning log before streaming starts (presentation.py:2313-2329). An ImageGenerationService is created for the images directory (presentation.py:2331).

docs.t: 4.2 The per-slide loop: sequential content generation
docs.x: inner() first computes image_urls_for_slides = get_images_for_slides_from_outline(outline.slides) (presentation.py:2335). That helper extracts http(s) URLs ending in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp from each outline's Markdown, de-duplicated in order (outline_utils.py:13-16, outline_utils.py:184-205). It then yields an opening chunk '{ "slides": [ ' and walks the structure: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) Each LLM call is awaited before the next begins, so in the web UI path slide text is generated strictly in order, one call at a time. Only asset fetching runs concurrently with the next slide's LLM call. concurrent_service is not used in this loop. What get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline does (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py:229-275): _prepare_response_schema(slide_layout.json_schema) removes __image_url__ and __icon_url__, returns None if no content properties remain, forces type: object, adds a required __speaker_note__ string (100 to 500 characters) and makes sure every array has items (generate_slide_content.py:203-226). If the schema is None (a decorative-only layout), it returns {} without calling the LLM. Otherwise it calls generate_structured_with_schema_retries(...) with the schema as both response_format and validation schema.

docs.t: 4.3 How slide JSON is validated and repaired
docs.x: generate_structured_with_schema_retries (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py:310-389) is the only validation layer between the model and the database: Inner loop: up to 3 attempts to obtain any parseable JSON object, sleeping 0.5 s then 1.0 s between attempts (llm_utils.py:332-351). JSON text is parsed with dirtyjson (llm_utils.py:414-435). If all fail: 400 "LLM did not return any content". Outer loop: up to 4 validation rounds (validate_schema_max_loop_count=4). Each round validates against the JSON schema with jsonschema; on errors it appends a user message listing up to 10 errors and the previous JSON (truncated to 6,000 characters) and asks for corrected JSON (llm_utils.py:276-307, llm_utils.py:362-387). After the last round it logs "Validation error after max fixes, returning last response" and returns the invalid content anyway (llm_utils.py:372-377). So in the worst case one slide costs 12 provider calls, and a slide can still be stored with schema violations. The template hydrator is defensive about that: _apply_template_content_to_ui and the per-type helpers ignore values of the wrong type and keep the template's original element (presentation.py:575-623, presentation.py:865-881). The prompt-level details are in Prompts and schemas.

docs.t: 4.4 Placeholders, UI hydration and image sizing
docs.x: Right after the SlideModel is built (presentation.py:2394-2399): process_slide_add_placeholder_assets(slide) walks slide.content for any dict containing __image_prompt__, image_prompt or prompt and sets its URL to /static/images/placeholder.jpg, and for __icon_query__, icon_query or query sets /static/icons/placeholder.svg (servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:22-23, process_slides.py:427-453). Template slides get image_url and icon_url; legacy slides get __image_url__ and __icon_url__ (process_slides.py:102-127). slide.ui = _apply_template_content_to_ui(slide.ui, slide.content) writes the generated text, lists, tables, charts and placeholder images into a deep copy of the template layout JSON (presentation.py:575-623). slide.ui starts as a copy of the matching template layout from _template_slide_ui (presentation.py:490-500). image_target_sizes_from_template(...) hydrates a throwaway copy of the layout with unique marker URLs to learn the width and height of each image box, keyed by JSON path, so the image generator can request a matching aspect ratio (process_slides.py:35-99). Any error returns {}, because sizing is optional.

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) process_slide_and_fetch_assets (process_slides.py:173-288) collects every image prompt and icon query in the slide content. For image slot k, if the outline contained a usable image URL at position k, that URL is used directly; otherwise it calls image_generation_service.generate_image(ImagePrompt(...)). Icons go to ICON_FINDER_SERVICE.search_icons(query, weight=...). All calls run in one asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) because allow_image_fallback=True. A failed image becomes /static/images/placeholder.jpg plus a warning {"status_code", "detail", "code"}; a failed icon search raises; an empty icon result falls back to the placeholder icon. Generated files come back as ImageAsset rows that are saved with the slides. Providers, icon search and the fallback logic are explained in Images, icons, web search. notify_slide_assets_ready (presentation.py:2341-2357) awaits the task, logs and records a warning {"type": "asset_generation_failed", "message": "Some slide assets could not be generated."} if it raised, and always pushes the slide index onto asset_events. After yielding the slide's chunk event (presentation.py:2421-2424), the loop drains every index already on asset_events with get_nowait(), re-hydrates that slide's ui and yields a slide_assets event with the updated slide and its warnings (presentation.py:2426-2446). Gotcha The browser only toasts warnings that have a string detail (usePresentationStreaming.ts:537-553). Image-provider failures carry detail; the asset_generation_failed warning produced when the whole asset task raises (for example an icon search error) has only type and message, so it reaches the client silently.

After the last slide the loop yields a closing chunk ' ] }', then blocks on asset_events.get() until every slide has produced its slide_assets event (presentation.py:2448-2470). It gathers all asset tasks with return_exceptions=True, logs and skips failures, and flattens the ImageAsset lists (presentation.py:2472-2484). Every slide's ui is hydrated one final time (presentation.py:2486-2487). Persistence is deliberately late: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) The final event is complete with PresentationWithSlides built from _presentation_response_data(presentation) plus the slides (presentation.py:2503-2511). _presentation_response_data drops layout and structure and adds type and can_regenerate (presentation.py:343-358).

Situation What happens Database effect Slide content call raises HTTPException (provider error, empty output) error event with the exception's detail, generator returns (presentation.py:2379-2381) nothing written; old slides untouched Any other exception inside inner() safe_sse_stream rolls back the session and emits error with "Failed to generate presentation slides. Please try again." (presentation.py:2516-2524, servers/fastapi/utils/sse.py:24-38) rollback; old slides untouched Client closes the EventSource when the ASGI server cancels the response generator, safe_sse_stream catches asyncio.CancelledError, logs it and returns (sse.py:21-23) nothing written Client reconnects (the hook retries up to 3 times) a new request starts generation from slide 1 only the last successful run's slides are kept Gotcha Standard streaming has no checkpoints. All slide rows are written in one transaction at the very end, so a dropped connection after slide 19 of 20 loses all 19 LLM calls, and the hook's retry (usePresentationStreaming.ts:198-221) pays for them again. Smart mode, by contrast, checkpoints each slide (see Smart mode). Gotcha stream_presentation takes no Request, so the slide-content calls get no disconnect_checker. Cancellation relies on the ASGI server cancelling the response generator. Asset tasks were started with asyncio.create_task and nothing in inner() cancels them, so image generation already in flight keeps running after a disconnect; its ImageAsset rows are never saved because the final commit is never reached.

Generation does not export in the web UI path. The editor exports on demand (see PPTX and PDF export). For API clients and retries, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export with body {"export_as": "pptx"} or "pdf" calls the same export_presentation(presentation_id, title, export_as, cookie_header=...) helper used by the one-shot endpoints and returns {"presentation_id", "path", "edit_path": "/presentation?id=<id>"} (presentation.py:1642-1678). build_export_cookie_header forwards the caller's cookies, or a desktop or internal session cookie, so the export browser can load the authenticated presentation page (presentation.py:1473-1496).

The one-shot endpoints run outline, structure, content, assets, save and export inside a single handler, generate_presentation_handler (presentation.py:2684-3166). They are the REST API documented for integrators in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

GeneratePresentationRequest (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:8-46): Field Type Default content str required (may be empty) slides_markdown list[str] or null null instructions str or null null tone Tone default verbosity Verbosity standard web_search bool false n_slides int or null null (auto) language str or null null (auto) template str "general" include_table_of_contents bool false include_title_slide bool true files list[str] or null null (paths from /files/upload) export_as "pptx" or "pdf" "pptx" trigger_webhook bool false Gotcha trigger_webhook is declared but never read. The handler always schedules WebhookService.send_webhook for PRESENTATION_GENERATION_COMPLETED or PRESENTATION_GENERATION_FAILED (presentation.py:3133-3138, presentation.py:3150-3155); delivery depends only on whether a subscription exists for that event (servers/fastapi/services/webhook_service.py:12-21).

check_if_api_request_is_valid (presentation.py:2620-2681) allocates the presentation UUID and rejects: no content, slides_markdown or files; n_slides <= 0 or > 50; more than 50 slides_markdown entries; TOC with n_slides < 3. It then resolves template: a TemplateV2 id (optionally custom- prefixed) is accepted and normalized to the row id; a bundled public name such as general is accepted if resolve_default_template_id finds templates/<name>/template.json (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:62-87); anything else is 400 "Template not found. Please use a valid template.".

Disconnect hook: when called from the sync route, request_http.is_disconnected becomes the disconnect_checker, and raise_if_client_disconnected() raises asyncio.CancelledError (presentation.py:2693-2705). slides_markdown shortcut: if present, n_slides is overwritten with its length (presentation.py:2710-2717). Without slides_markdown: update async status to "Generating presentation outlines"; load files with DocumentsLoader(...).load_documents() (no temp dir, parsed now) and join into additional_context; reduce the outline count for TOC only when n_slides is given; build and record the prompt; consume generate_ppt_outline(...) (no SSE, just concatenation); parse with dirtyjson, normalize, fail on too few outlines, trim extras (presentation.py:2719-2834). With slides_markdown: each string becomes one SlideOutlineModel(content=...) and no LLM outline call is made (presentation.py:2836-2853). Async status "Selecting layout for each slide"; _resolve_generation_layout(request.template, ...) returns the layout payload, layout model, template fonts and template theme (presentation.py:262-306). Unlike /prepare, it accepts bundled names and returns 503 if a bundled template has not been imported yet. Structure: generate_presentation_structure(..., using_slides_markdown=..., disconnect_checker=...) (presentation.py:2891-2903), then a lighter clamp than /prepare (presentation.py:2905-2912). TOC: only when include_table_of_contents and not slides_markdown (presentation.py:2914-2935). Build the PresentationModel in memory with outlines, layout, structure, fonts, theme, the requested language and a title from the first outline (presentation.py:2942-2959). It is not committed yet. Generate slide content concurrently in batches of 10 (below). Await all asset tasks with plain asyncio.gather (presentation.py:3073), log image warnings, run _hydrate_template_slide_ui on every slide (presentation.py:3084-3085). Save presentation, slides and assets in one commit (presentation.py:3088-3091). Export with export_presentation(...) and build PresentationPathAndEditPath (presentation.py:3098-3109). Async status completed with path and edit_path in data (presentation.py:3111-3130), then the success webhook.

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) Up to 10 slide-content LLM calls run at once; the next batch starts only when the whole batch has returned. After each batch, the async task's created_slides and remaining_slides are updated, and asset tasks for the batch are started immediately so they overlap with the next batch's LLM calls (presentation.py:3025-3059). Outline image URLs are honored only in slides_markdown mode (presentation.py:3035-3040).

Work Web UI stream (/presentation/stream) One-shot (/generate) Slide content LLM calls one at a time, in order asyncio.gather in batches of 10 Image and icon fetching one asyncio.create_task per slide, overlaps later LLM calls one task per slide, started after each batch Asset failure policy per-slide task failure is logged and skipped final asyncio.gather without return_exceptions, so a raised icon error fails the request CONCURRENT_SERVICE not used only to fire webhooks in the background (servers/fastapi/services/concurrent_service.py:10-28) Disconnect checks none passed to LLM calls before outline, inside LLM streams, before each batch Each LLM call runs its blocking provider iterator in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread inside stream_generate_events (llm_utils.py:503), so a batch of 10 occupies 10 threads of the default executor. See Streaming (SSE).

With slides_markdown, you supply the outline yourself: The outline LLM call, the TOC step and n_slides are all skipped or overridden. The structure call uses the slides-markdown prompt variant, which embeds every layout's full JSON schema and rules such as "If content contains table, then select either table layout or graph layout" (generate_presentation_structure.py:16-63). Image URLs found in each slide's Markdown are fed to process_slide_and_fetch_assets as outline_image_urls, so the first image slot of the second slide above uses https://example.com/team.png instead of generating an image.

POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async validates the same way, inserts an AsyncTaskModel (type: "presentation.generate", status: "pending", message: "Queued for generation") and schedules _run_generate_presentation_task with FastAPI BackgroundTasks (presentation.py:3240-3279). The background task re-establishes the owner context, opens its own session and calls the same handler with async_status set and no request_http, so it has no disconnect checker (presentation.py:3198-3237). GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/status/{id} returns the row, with data links made absolute for MCP callers (presentation.py:3282-3298). Messages progress through "Starting presentation generation", "Generating presentation outlines", "Selecting layout for each slide", "Generating slides", "Fetching assets for slides", "Exporting presentation" and "Presentation generation completed". In practice a poller never sees "Exporting presentation": the handler sets it and calls sql_session.add but does not commit (presentation.py:3093-3096), so it is first written together with "Presentation generation completed". On success data gains path and edit_path; on failure status becomes "error" and error holds {"status_code", "detail"} from APIErrorModel (presentation.py:3157-3163, servers/fastapi/models/api_error_model.py:5-13). The sync route returns PresentationPathAndEditPath (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_and_path.py:5-11): path is whatever EXPORT_TASK_SERVICE.export_from_url reports (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:43-73, see PPTX and PDF export). When the request carries the header X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, absolute_mcp_result_links turns host-relative path and edit_path values into absolute URLs (presentation.py:3185-3190, servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py:13-52); other callers get them unchanged. Gotcha The one-shot structure clamp is weaker than /prepare's. It slices the list to the outline count and replaces indexes >= total_slide_layouts, but it neither pads a short list nor replaces negative indexes (presentation.py:2905-2912). Validation retries usually prevent a short list, but generate_structured_with_schema_retries returns the last response even when it still fails validation. A short list then raises IndexError (reported as 500 "Presentation generation failed"), and a negative index silently selects a layout from the end of the list. If you touch this

docs.x: Concern Web UI (create, stream outlines, prepare, stream slides) One-shot /generate Template id must be a TemplateV2 row id (_resolve_prepare_layout) row id or bundled name (_resolve_generation_layout) Documents decomposed to .txt before /create, read at outline time original uploads parsed during the request Slide language cleared to "" by /prepare, auto-detected per slide requested language kept theme column not set set from the template Human review of outlines yes no Export separate call part of the request Persistence at the end of the slide stream at the end, before export

Reads: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_web_search_query.py, servers/fastapi/utils/get_dynamic_models.py, servers/fastapi/utils/schema_utils.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py, servers/fastapi/utils/outline_limits.py · Builds on: Standard generation pipeline · Time: ~40 min Every Standard-mode deck is produced by four kinds of LLM calls: web search query, outline, structure (layout selection) and slide content. This chapter reads each prompt line by line, explains why each rule exists, and shows exactly how Pydantic models and template layouts become the JSON schemas sent to the provider and then used to validate the answer. It closes with the numeric limits that bound the whole system and a worked example of changing a prompt without breaking anything.

docs.t: The four calls at a glance
docs.x: Call Function Messages built by Response schema JSONSchemaResponse strict flag Server-side validation Streams text to the browser Web search query generate_web_search_query (generate_web_search_query.py:39-74) inline SEARCH_QUERY_RESPONSE_SCHEMA (generate_web_search_query.py:25-36) False yes, up to 4 rounds no Outline generate_ppt_outline (generate_presentation_outlines.py:252-405) get_messages (generate_presentation_outlines.py:218-249) dynamic Pydantic model with exactly N slides, or PresentationOutlineModel False parse plus Pydantic after streaming, no schema retry loop yes, as chunk events Structure generate_presentation_structure (generate_presentation_structure.py:157-211) get_messages or get_messages_for_slides_markdown dynamic model with exactly N integers False yes, up to 4 rounds no Slide content get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline (generate_slide_content.py:229-275) get_messages (generate_slide_content.py:169-192) the layout's JSON schema, transformed True yes, up to 4 rounds no (the finished slide is streamed) All four obtain a client with get_client(config=get_llm_config(...)) and a model name with get_model(); provider selection is covered in Configuration and LLM providers. The strict flag is handed to the external llmai package (pinned to 0.3.15 in servers/fastapi/uv.lock); what each provider adapter does with it is not visible in this repository and is not covered here.

get_messages(...) returns [SystemMessage(get_system_prompt(...)), UserMessage(get_user_prompt(...))] (generate_presentation_outlines.py:218-249). The system prompt depends only on verbosity, include_title_slide and include_table_of_contents; everything request-specific goes into the user prompt.

docs.t: 1.2 The system prompt, rule by rule
docs.x: get_system_prompt (generate_presentation_outlines.py:67-167) concatenates fixed sentences with a few computed blocks. The table quotes the important rules in order and explains what each one is for. Rule (verbatim fragment) Purpose "Generation settings are authoritative." The settings block in the user prompt wins over conflicting text in Content, Instructions or Context (for example a prompt that says "make 20 slides" when n_slides is 8). "If Language is not auto-detect, generate every presentation title and slide outline in exactly that language" Stops source documents or instructions in another language from switching the output language. "Generate flow based on user content and use context just for reference." Documents and web results inform the deck but must not replace the user's topic. DIRECT_CONTENT_VOICE_RULES: "Never refer to 'this presentation', 'this slide'..." (double quotes in the source) Removes meta-commentary such as "This slide presents...". Also tells the model not to mention the supplied date unless relevant (generate_presentation_outlines.py:42-48). "Presentation title should be plain text, not markdown." The title is later derived from the first outline, so Markdown noise is unwanted. "Never generate more than {MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES} slide outlines" and "Each slide outline must be {MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS} words or fewer." Mirrors the server-side limits (50 slides, 100 words by default). Verbosity sentence, for example "Slide content should be around 40 words" Length target per outline (table below). "Apply slide-specific instructions only to the exact slide mentioned and only once." Prevents "add a chart on slide 5" from leaking onto every slide. "Give each slide one clear purpose and split overloaded topics across multiple slides." Encourages one idea per slide, which makes layout selection easier. "Include presenter name in first slide." or "Do not include presenter name in any slides." Controlled by include_title_slide. "Include a table of contents slide in the outline sequence." Only when include_table_of_contents is true. "Each slide content: Must have a ## title. Must be in Markdown format. Don't use bold and italic text. First slide title must be the same as the presentation title." Outline formatting contract (generate_presentation_outlines.py:95-102); the ## heading is what _extract_outline_title reads for TOC entries.

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py (excerpt) _resolve_prompt_language maps None, empty, auto and auto-detect (any case) to auto-detect (generate_presentation_outlines.py:170-178). _resolve_prompt_n_slides(None) renders auto-detect, maximum 50 (generate_presentation_outlines.py:181-184). For a request with 8 slides, English, professional tone and no documents, the rendered user message is: Note Include Title Slide: True uses Python's str(bool) while the TOC line is lowercased, and the TOC line only appears when TOC is on. When documents were attached, Context: carries the full extracted text joined with blank lines (Document ingestion). When external web search runs, its formatted results are appended to that same context inside generate_ppt_outline (generate_presentation_outlines.py:350-353). Gotcha The endpoints call get_messages once to record the prompt in memory (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:142-168), and generate_ppt_outline calls it again internally (generate_presentation_outlines.py:377-387). The second call is the one that reaches the model and it may include web search context that the recorded copy does not. If you add a new prompt input, thread it through both call sites. Gotcha With TOC enabled, the system prompt asks the model to include a TOC slide, and /prepare also inserts generated TOC outlines (Standard generation pipeline). Nothing removes a model-written TOC outline, so watch for duplicated agenda slides when you change either side.

docs.t: Step 2: Forcing slide counts with dynamic Pydantic models
docs.x: JSON Schema can pin an array length with minItems and maxItems, and Pydantic emits those from Field(min_length=..., max_length=...). Because the count is only known per request, Presenton defines the model classes inside a function: servers/fastapi/utils/get_dynamic_models.py (excerpt) get_presentation_structure_model_with_n_slides(n) does the same for slides: List[int] with description "List of slide layouts" (get_dynamic_models.py:32-40). For n = 3 the outline model's model_json_schema() has this shape (reconstructed from the model definitions, as Pydantic v2 emits it; not captured from a running server): Where each constraint is actually enforced: Constraint Sent to the provider Enforced on the server exactly N outlines minItems/maxItems in the outline schema after streaming: fewer than N is an error, more than N is trimmed (outlines.py:228-243) at most 50 outlines PresentationOutlineModel.slides max_length=50 (servers/fastapi/models/presentation_outline_model.py:24-28) and the prompt normalize_outline_payload slices to 50 before validation (outline_limits.py:59-67) 100 to 1,200 characters per outline minLength/maxLength in the dynamic schema only not enforced: the server re-parses with the base PresentationOutlineModel, which has no character bounds at most 100 words per outline description text and the prompt trimmed by normalize_outline_content in the field validator (presentation_outline_model.py:18-21) and by normalize_outline_payload exactly N layout indexes structure schema validation retry loop, then _normalize_presentation_structure pads or fixes Gotcha The 1,200-character max_length is hard-coded while the word limit comes from the MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS environment variable. If you raise MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS to 250, the prompt and the server allow 250 words but the schema still tells the provider 1,200 characters, roughly 200 English words. Raise both together.
servers/fastapi/utils/schema_utils.py holds every schema transformation. Here is each function, what it does to a schema, and where it is used in this pipeline.

Deep-copies the schema, runs ensure_strict_json_schema only when strict=True, and always runs ensure_array_schemas_have_items (schema_utils.py:265-276). The outline and structure calls use it with strict=False (generate_presentation_outlines.py:362-365, generate_presentation_structure.py:189-192), so in practice only the array fix is applied.

Walks every dict and list in a deep copy; any node whose type is "array" (or a list containing "array") and has no items gets "items": {"type": "string"} (schema_utils.py:237-262). The docstring gives the reason: the Codex Responses API requires items on arrays. Tested in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_llm_utils_and_schema.py:32.

Adapted from the OpenAI SDK (comment at schema_utils.py:91). When enabled it mutates the schema in place: Recurses into $defs and definitions. Adds additionalProperties: false to every type: object that lacks it. Makes every property required: required = list(properties.keys()). Recurses into properties, items, anyOf, allOf. For arrays without items, takes prefixItems[0] as items (Zod tuples) or defaults to {"type": "string"}. Collapses a single-entry allOf into its parent. Removes string format values outside the supported list (date-time, time, date, duration, email, hostname, ipv4, ipv6, uuid). Removes default: null. Inlines a $ref that has sibling keys, then re-runs itself on the result. None of the four calls in this chapter pass strict=True to prepare_schema_for_validation, so this function is currently inactive for generation. Keep that in mind before assuming provider-strict schemas: optional properties stay optional.

Deep-copies, finds every dict that has a properties key anywhere in the tree (via get_dict_paths_with_key, servers/fastapi/utils/dict_utils.py:6-22), deletes the named properties, and removes them from every required list (schema_utils.py:26-46). Slide content uses it to drop __image_url__ and __icon_url__.

Adds one property at the root only, creating properties if needed, and adds or removes the name in root required; an empty required list is removed entirely (schema_utils.py:49-88). Slide content uses it to add __speaker_note__.

Prepares the schema, picks the right jsonschema validator class with validator_for, checks the schema itself, and returns sorted messages formatted as "$.path[0].field: message" (schema_utils.py:279-309). These strings are what the model sees in the repair message (Step 8).

remove_titles_from_schema strips schema title keys while preserving properties literally named title (schema_utils.py:312-336); it is not called by the generation pipeline. generate_constraint_sentences is explicitly marked # ? Not used (schema_utils.py:339).

get_messages(presentation_layout, n_slides, data, instructions, source_content) (generate_presentation_structure.py:108-134) fills GET_MESSAGES_SYSTEM_PROMPT (generate_presentation_structure.py:66-105) and sends the layouts plus outlines as the user message: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py (excerpt) Key rules in the system prompt and why they exist: Rule (verbatim fragment) Purpose "Opening/closing → Title layouts", "Comparisons/contrasts → Side-by-side layouts", "Data/metrics → Chart/graph layouts" Content-driven mapping from slide purpose to layout family. "Don't use same layout for multiple slides unless necessary." and "Adjacent slide layouts should be different unless instructed/necessary otherwise." Visual variety. "Must only use table of contents layout if slide content contains table of contents." Keeps agenda layouts for the inserted TOC outlines. "Extract visual constraints from User Instructions and Original User Request; User Instructions win conflicts." The original prompt (presentation.content) is passed as # Original User Request: so visual intents such as "bar chart on slide 4" survive even though outlines must not contain them. "Slide numbers are one-based, and 'all' or 'every' includes the title slide." (double quotes in the source) Resolves "images on all slides". "A numeric table on a chart-requested slide is chart data, not a request for a table-only layout." Pairs with the outline rule that turns chart requests into Markdown tables. "Select layout index for each of the {n_slides} slides" Restates the count that the schema enforces. The layouts are described by PresentationLayoutModel.to_string() (servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py:49-62): index, name and description only, no schemas. The outlines come from PresentationOutlineModel.to_string(): servers/fastapi/models/presentation_outline_model.py (excerpt) {slide} formats the SlideOutlineModel object itself, so the model sees Pydantic's default string form (content='...', with newlines escaped) rather than the raw Markdown.

When the one-shot API receives slides_markdown, get_messages_for_slides_markdown (generate_presentation_structure.py:137-154) uses STRUCTURE_FROM_SLIDES_MARKDOWN_SYSTEM_PROMPT (generate_presentation_structure.py:16-63). It embeds presentation_layout.to_string(with_schema=True), so every layout's full JSON schema is in the system prompt, and adds hard selection rules: "If content contains table, then select either table layout or graph layout.", "Don't select layout with image unless content contains image or the user explicitly requests imagery.", and "Must select a layout that supports n-1 charts for n columns." The user message is just the outline text.

The schema comes from get_presentation_structure_model_with_n_slides(len(outlines)) and is validated with up to 4 rounds (generate_presentation_structure.py:167-208). The parsed dict is loaded into the base PresentationStructureModel, which has no length constraint, and any failure is converted by handle_llm_client_exceptions (generate_presentation_structure.py:209-211).

docs.t: Step 5: The slide content prompt and its response schema
docs.x: This is the call that turns one outline plus one layout schema into slide JSON. How a template's components become slide_layout.json_schema is explained in From template to schema to slide; here we start from that schema.

docs.t: 5.1 From layout schema to response schema
docs.x: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py (excerpt) ASSET_ONLY_FIELDS = ["__image_url__", "__icon_url__"] (generate_slide_content.py:86). If the remaining schema has no properties, get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline returns {} without creating a client (generate_slide_content.py:240-242); test_slide_content_generation_skips_asset_only_schema (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_generate_slide_content.py:55) covers this.

The integration test test_stream_presentation_uses_template_schema_for_content_generation (servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_presentation_generation_flow.py:1066) uses a template with one component hero containing one editable text element headline with min_length: 2 and max_length: 32. get_template_schema turns that layout into (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:585-639): _prepare_response_schema then adds the speaker note at the root: This dict is used three times: as JSONSchemaResponse(name="response", json_schema=..., strict=True), as the validation schema, and, serialized with json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False), inside the system prompt as "- Follow this response schema exactly: {...}" (generate_slide_content.py:103-110). A valid answer is: The whole dict, including __speaker_note__, is stored in slides.content, and __speaker_note__ is also copied into slides.speaker_note (Standard generation pipeline).

SLIDE_CONTENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (generate_slide_content.py:20-67) is a raw string with five placeholders filled by get_system_prompt (generate_slide_content.py:113-149). Rule (verbatim fragment) Purpose "Slide Language is authoritative when it is explicitly set." Same precedence idea as the outline prompt. "Speaker notes must be plain text (no markdown)." Notes go into PPTX speaker notes verbatim. "Never exceed max character limits" and "rephrase instead" (do not clip mid-sentence) The template's maxLength values are its text-capacity hints (From template to schema to slide), so overflow means text spilling out of the design. "Do not use emojis or $schema fields." Template schemas carry a $schema key; the model must not echo it as data. "Treat chart, layout, styling, positioning, and other visual instructions as production controls." Visual instructions are honored through the chosen layout, never written as slide text. "For chart fields, populate the requested labels, series, and values" Chart elements need data, not prose. Math rules: "Wrap every LaTeX expression in <latex> and </latex>" The renderer turns <latex> runs into math (see servers/fastapi/utils/latex_text.py). "Strictly use markdown to emphasize important points, by bolding or italicizing the part of text." Emphasis is converted into bold or italic text runs by _template_text_runs_from_markdown (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1157-1198). # User Instructions: block Present only when instructions is set. # Tone Instructions: "Make slide as {tone} as possible." Present whenever tone is truthy. # Verbosity Instructions: See the verbosity table in Step 1. # Output Fields: plus the schema JSON The full response schema in text form. Gotcha Tone and verbosity are interpolated raw. The default tone is the string default, so the prompt literally says "Make slide as default as possible.", and sales_pitch becomes "Make slide as sales_pitch as possible." If you want better behavior for these values, map them to descriptive phrases in get_system_prompt rather than changing the enum values, which are stored in the database.

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py (excerpt) {language} is the stored language, or, when empty or auto, the instruction "auto-detect from the slide content and use the same language as the slide content" (generate_slide_content.py:87-100). In the web UI path /prepare clears the language, so this instruction is what slides always see. {slide_number_section} is # Slide Number:\n<n> with a one-based number (generate_slide_content.py:152-155), which lets "on slide 5" instructions apply. {content} is the outline Markdown for this slide.

docs.t: Step 6: Image prompts and icon queries in schemas and content
docs.x: Images and icons are not generated by the slide-content LLM. The LLM writes a prompt or query, and the asset step resolves it to a URL (Images, icons, web search). Schema family Field the LLM fills URL field written later Removed from the LLM schema Template V2 (current) image_prompt for images, icon_query when the element has is_icon: true (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1211-1223, schema.py:1541-1542) image_url, icon_url nothing to remove: URL fields are never in the V2 schema Legacy layout schemas __image_prompt__, __icon_query__ __image_url__, __icon_url__ __image_url__, __icon_url__ via ASSET_ONLY_FIELDS In a V2 component schema an image element becomes an object with additionalProperties: false and one required string property; its description is "Prompt for the replacement image." or "Search query for the replacement icon." (_component_content_field_schema, schema.py:1211-1223, with the text from schema.py:1545-1548). The older element-level builder at schema.py:373-375 emits the same key without a description. The user prompt fixes the language of these strings to English ("# Icon Query And Image Prompt Language:\nEnglish"), because image models and the icon index work best in English even when the slide text is not. An image slot moves through three states (field names from servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:22-24 and process_slides.py:110-127; the slot name is illustrative): The first is the LLM output, the second is after process_slide_add_placeholder_assets, and the third is after process_slide_and_fetch_assets. Placeholder and app-data paths are passed through normalize_slide_asset_url, which makes them absolute when a FastAPI base URL is configured (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:51-60). The asset code searches for any of __image_prompt__, image_prompt, prompt and __icon_query__, icon_query, query at any depth, so both schema families work. Gotcha Because the asset scanner treats any dict containing a prompt or query key as an asset slot (process_slides.py:22-23), a template field literally named prompt or query inside an object will be treated as an image or icon request. Avoid those element names in templates.

docs.t: Step 7: The web search query prompt
docs.x: When web search is enabled and routed to an external provider, generate_web_search_query asks the model for one query (generate_web_search_query.py:8-23). The rules: "Keep the query focused and at most 12 words.", preserve names, places, dates and technical terms, add "latest", the year or "statistics" when useful, and "Do not answer the user's request." The user message is TODAY'S DATE: <date>, CONTENT: <prompt>, INSTRUCTIONS: <instructions>. The response schema is {"query": string, minLength 1, maxLength 200} with additionalProperties: false (generate_web_search_query.py:25-36). The result is whitespace-collapsed and cut to 200 characters; a non-string result returns None, and the caller falls back to build_web_search_query(content, instructions), which is the first 500 characters of the cleaned prompt plus instructions (servers/fastapi/utils/web_search.py:187-189). Tested in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_generate_web_search_query.py:18-49.

docs.t: Step 8: Structured generation with retries and repair
docs.x: Three of the four calls go through generate_structured_with_schema_retries (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py:310-389): servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py (excerpt) Facts worth knowing: Every request streams, even in background tasks, because the Anthropic SDK refuses long non-streaming requests (comment at llm_utils.py:75-83; tests in servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_llm_utils_disconnect.py:69-104). No max_tokens is set by get_generate_kwargs unless passed (llm_utils.py:110-137). Provider-specific extra_body (for example disabling DeepSeek thinking when a response format is used) comes from get_extra_body (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_config.py:489). Content is taken from the final completion object if present, otherwise from the concatenated streamed text, parsed with dirtyjson (llm_utils.py:100-107, llm_utils.py:414-435). When validation fails and rounds remain, this message is appended and the call repeats with the longer conversation: (Built by structured_validation_feedback_user_message, llm_utils.py:276-307, with at most 10 errors listed and the JSON truncated at 6,000 characters.) The outline call is different: it streams through stream_generate_events directly, and its output is validated only by Pydantic after the stream ends, with no repair round (generate_presentation_outlines.py:372-403). Gotcha After the fourth round the last, still-invalid response is returned with only a warning log (llm_utils.py:372-377). Downstream code must tolerate schema violations. If you need hard guarantees for a new call, check the result yourself or raise instead of returning.

Limit Value Defined at Enforced where MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES 50 servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:4 /create, /prepare, /update, /generate validation, outline model, normalize_outline_payload, prompts MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS env, default 100, must be a positive integer constants/presentation.py:5-23 prompts, outline validators, trim_text_to_word_limit (outline_limits.py:15-26) Outline characters (dynamic schema) 100 to 1,200 get_dynamic_models.py:13-20 provider hint only Speaker note 100 to 500 characters, required generate_slide_content.py:214-225 validation rounds Structured retries 3 parse attempts times 4 validation rounds llm_utils.py:319, llm_utils.py:332 every structured call Repair message 10 errors, 6,000 JSON characters llm_utils.py:280-281 repair rounds Web search query 12 words (prompt), 200 characters (schema and trim) generate_web_search_query.py:17, generate_web_search_query.py:31, generate_web_search_query.py:73 query generation Fallback search query 500 characters web_search.py:187-189 external search Web UI client limits 50 slides, 100 words (constants) servers/nextjs/utils/presentationLimits.ts:1-2 limitOutlines before rendering and before /prepare count_outline_words counts runs of non-whitespace (\S+), so Markdown markers such as ## and - count as words (outline_limits.py:8-12). Trimming cuts at the end of the Nth word and right-strips. Gotcha The Next.js client hard-codes MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS = 100 (servers/nextjs/utils/presentationLimits.ts:2) and trims outlines with it while streaming and before /prepare. Raising MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS on the server alone therefore has no effect in the web UI.

docs.t: Step 10: Worked example, safely changing a prompt
docs.x:
Suppose you want outlines to prefer metric units. The change is one sentence in the outline system prompt. Find the right builder. Outline rules live in get_system_prompt (generate_presentation_outlines.py:67-167). It is built from adjacent string literals, some of which are f-strings. Add a plain literal, for example "Use metric units unless the user specifies otherwise.
", next to the other style rules around generate_presentation_outlines.py:146-151. Keep the trailing 
, because adjacent literals are concatenated with no separator. Mind .format() templates. If you edit SLIDE_CONTENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, SLIDE_CONTENT_USER_PROMPT, GET_MESSAGES_SYSTEM_PROMPT or STRUCTURE_FROM_SLIDES_MARKDOWN_SYSTEM_PROMPT, remember they are passed to str.format. A literal { or } (for example a JSON example) must be written as {{ and }}, or every call raises at runtime. In f-strings the same applies. Check the phrases tests pin. servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_generate_presentation_outlines.py:74-107 asserts fragments such as "Do not include URLs", "Give each slide one clear purpose", "Generation settings are authoritative" and "user-visible content plan, not a production brief". test_generate_slide_content.py:14-31 pins "visual instructions as production" and "# Slide Number:
1"; test_generate_presentation_structure.py:26-55 pins "Slide numbers are
one-based" (including the line break) and the # Original User Request: header. Rewording any of those requires updating the test in the same change. Add a test for the new rule. Run the focused suites from servers/fastapi: CI runs the whole suite with uv run --locked python -m pytest --verbose --tb=short (.github/workflows/test-all.yml:74-75). Consider side effects. The outline system prompt is stored in memory through store_generation_context for later chat turns, so the new rule also becomes context for the assistant (Editing and chat assistant). Prompts are not versioned per presentation, so regenerating an old deck uses the new rule.
