presentation_type: "standard" or "smart" (default standard); message: str 1 to 8,000 chars; conversation_id: UUID or null; attachments: list[ChatAttachment], at most 8 ChatAttachment type: "document"; name 1 to 255 chars; file_path 1 to 4,000 chars; mime_type up to 255 or null ChatMessageResponse conversation_id: UUID; response: str; tool_calls: list[str] (tool names in call order) A smart-deck request from the editor looks like this (message abbreviated; Step 9 shows how the frontend builds it): The stream endpoint wraps PresentationChatService.stream_reply and maps its (event_type, value) pairs to SSE frames (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:136-165): Frame type Payload Emitted when status status: "Reading deck context", "Finalizing response" or "Saving chat" Start of turn, tool-limit path, before persisting chunk chunk: text delta Every content delta from the model trace trace: an object with kind model_note, tool_plan, tool_call or limit Reasoning summary, planned tools, each tool start and finish, tool-limit notice complete chat: {conversation_id, response, tool_calls} After the turn is saved error detail Only for an HTTPException raised while streaming A pair of tool_call traces for a smart save: The slide_index fields come from _tool_focus_from_arguments and _tool_focus_from_result (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:632-754), which read index,

PresentationChatService.__init__ (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:74-94) creates three collaborators: a ChatConversationStore (SQL history plus Mem0 chat memory), a PresentationContextStore (an alias of PresentationChatMemoryLayer from servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:103, servers/fastapi/services/chat/presentation_context_store.py:1-3) bound to the presentation and its type, and ChatTools(memory, mode=chat_mode). The chat_mode parameter defaults to "presentation" and no route passes anything else; ChatTools stores it but never reads it (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:91).

stream_reply (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:114) first calls self._tools.set_turn_context(user_message) (which resets the per-turn list of generated assets), yields "Reading deck context", then _prepare_turn_context (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:275-351): Reject an empty message (400), a missing presentation (404), and a presentation_type that differs from the stored generation_mode (400 "Presentation type does not match the stored generation mode."). Build attachment context (4.3). Use the given conversation_id or create uuid4(); load the thread's history (Step 7) and convert rows to UserMessage/AssistantMessage, stripping any stored "UI context" prefix. Build a memory query from the user message without its UI context prefix, plus attachment names, and run two searches: self._memory.retrieve_context(query) (deck scope) and retrieve_semantic_context(...) (this conversation's scope). If attachments were parsed, store their text in deck memory as [document_extracted_text]. Assemble [SystemMessage(build_system_prompt(...)), *history, UserMessage(model_user_message)]. build_system_prompt (servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py:227) picks SMART_CHAT_AI_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT for smart decks and CHAT_AI_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT otherwise, then appends "Deck memory (background only; may be partial or stale):" and "Chat memory (earlier messages in this conversation):" blocks when non-empty. The smart prompt is the shorter of the two: servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py (excerpt) It goes on to restate the smart HTML rules from chapter 13 (root section classes, no scrolling or clipping, decoration-only positioning, complete Chart.js canvas plus script, no CDN scripts), replaceOldSlideAtIndex=true for edits and false for inserts, and a cap of 50 slides (servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py:168-224). The standard prompt (servers/fastapi/services/chat/prompts.py:10-166) is a long protocol: 1-based slide numbers versus 0-based tool indexes, inspect with getSlideAtIndex before visible edits, prefer reusable template blocks over primitives (mandatory getAvailableBlocks before new tables and charts), vector and infographic rules, chart and table data-preservation rules, asset rules (generate first, reuse URLs exactly), outline tools limited to 50 slides and MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS words (default 100, MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS env,

Documents attached in the chat composer have already been uploaded; the request carries their temp paths. _should_parse_attachments (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:516-531) decides whether to read them: always if the user text is empty or matches DOCUMENT_CONTENT_INTENT_PATTERN (words like read, extract, summarize, chart, table, create, generate, "based on", "use the attached document"); never if it only matches DIRECT_FILE_PLACEMENT_PATTERN (place, put, insert, attach, display, show, move, resize, position, replace, add); otherwise yes. When the files are not parsed, the model only gets a "UI context: the user attached document file(s), but this request appears to place or reference the file..." note followed by Document N: name lines. When parsing, DocumentsLoader loads every file and each document is trimmed to min(3000, remaining) characters out of a 6,000-character total (MAX_CHAT_ATTACHMENT_FILE_CHARS, MAX_CHAT_ATTACHMENT_CONTEXT_CHARS, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:46-47). The resulting "UI context: the user attached parsed document(s)..." block is inserted just before the User message: line (_compose_user_message_for_model, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:534-552). The persisted user message is the stripped text plus "Attached files: a.pdf, b.docx" (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:555-567).

The loop runs at most MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 40 rounds (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:45, :134). Each round streams the model with tools=build_chat_llm_tools(self._tools.get_tool_definitions()); build_chat_llm_tools returns the function tools unchanged, and its docstring notes that web search is intentionally not offered to chat (servers/fastapi/services/chat/llm_tools.py:4-9). Content deltas are yielded immediately as chunk events; reasoning deltas are collected and, after the round, summarized into one model_note trace (whitespace-collapsed, capped at 600 characters, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:455-465). servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py (excerpt) Tool calls in one round run sequentially, in the order the model listed them. A round with no tool calls ends the loop: its streamed text (or the completion's text, or "I could not generate a response for that request.") is the final answer. If all 40 rounds call tools, the service emits a limit trace and the "Finalizing response" status, makes one more call without tools (_try_final_response_without_tools, servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:433-452), and if that fails falls back to the message of the last successful tool result or a generic "I completed several tool operations..." sentence (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:814-830). The non-streaming POST /chat/message runs the same loop through _run_llm_with_tools (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:376-431) with blocking client.generate calls in a worker thread and no traces.

ChatTools.execute_tool_call (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:454-526) is the single dispatcher. It returns a JSON-serializable envelope that is fed back to the model verbatim: servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py (excerpt) The pipeline is: Unknown name: {"ok": false, "error": "Unsupported tool: X", "recovery": {"retryable": false, ...}}. _parse_args (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1039) accepts tolerant JSON: it tries dirtyjson then json on the raw string, on the contents of a Markdown fence, and on the outermost {...} or [...] substring, then converts any string "null" to None. _repair_tool_args (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1190-1218) normalizes JSON-string fields (for example an object passed where content, element or component must be a JSON string), and for chart, table and image inserts fills in missing data from the user's latest message or from assets generated earlier in this turn. The chart repair parses label and number pairs such as "North 120, South 95" (at least 2 and at most 12 rows, servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1515-1553); the table repair understands "headers A, B data: x, y; z, w" and CSV-like lines. Call the handler. On an exception, repair once more with the error text (MAX_TOOL_REPAIR_RETRIES = 1, servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:68) and retry only if the repair changed the arguments. Success: {"ok": true, "tool": name, "result": {...}}, plus "repair": {"applied": true, "notes": [...]} when repairs were made. Failure: {"ok": false, "tool": name, "error": str(exc), "repair": {...}, "recovery": {"retryable", "message", "guidance": [...], "expected"?, "received_keys"?}}, where _build_tool_recovery (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:1733-1845) maps error text to guidance and example payloads (a correct chart element, a table, an image with a generated URL, the reusable-block workflow). Gotcha ok: true only means the handler did not raise. Most mutating handlers report business failures as data, for example {"saved": false, "message": "Smart slide HTML failed validation.", "validation_errors": [...]}. The trace for such a call still has status: "success", and the frontend refreshes as if a mutation happened. The prompts tell the model to check saved=true; code that consumes traces should check the result too.

_persist_turn (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:353-374) calls ChatConversationStore.append_turn with the user message stripped of its UI context, the final answer and the list of tool names, commits the request session, and returns ChatTurnResult(conversation_id, response_text, tool_calls). The stream route turns that into the complete frame.

ChatTools.get_tool_definitions (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:127) returns one of two lists, depending only on self._memory.presentation_type. All tools are declared with strict=False. Argument schemas live in servers/fastapi/services/chat/schemas.py; every model sets extra="forbid" and strict=True (servers/fastapi/services/chat/schemas.py:11-12), and the OpenAIStrictSchemaModel subclass fills omitted fields with None before validation (servers/fastapi/services/chat/schemas.py:15-28), which is why the prompt tells the model to "Include required nullable fields with null".

Tool Arguments What it does getSmartPresentationContext includeSlideHtml (default false), maxHtmlCharsPerSlide 0 to 50,000 (0 means full) Returns title, language, tone, verbosity, instructions, fonts, community_design_ids, outlines, structure, slide count, and per slide its ID, index, title, HTML length and a 1,200-character text preview (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:985-1038) readSourceDocuments query, maxChars 1,000 to 30,000 Re-parses the deck's file_paths within a character budget (default 12,000); when no file can be read, falls back to a deck-memory search (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:554-683) searchSlide query 1 to 1,000 chars, limit 1 to 10 Scores slides by full-phrase match (8 points) plus matched tokens over text extracted from HTML (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:187-247) getSlideAtIndex index 0 to 1,000, includeFullContent Returns previews, and with includeFullContent=true the complete html (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:249-290); retries index-1 if nothing is found (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:597-614) generateAssets assets: 1 to 12 of {kind: "image" or "icon", prompt} Generates images (committing an ImageAsset row) or finds icons, returns URLs (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:763-786, servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:703-722) saveSlide html up to 500,000 chars, index, replaceOldSlideAtIndex, optional speakerNote, editPrompt save_html_slide (below) deleteSlide index Deletes and reindexes; deleting the last slide inserts an "Untitled slide" placeholder section (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1161-1255) save_html_slide (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1040-1159) is where the chat assistant mutates a smart deck: servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py (excerpt) It refuses non-smart decks, runs exactly the generation-time validator from chapter 13 (so a chat edit with a scrolling container, an orphan chart canvas or overlapping positioned text is rejected with the validator's message, which the model then sees), derives the title from data-slide-title or the first heading, and either replaces the row in place (keeping its id) or inserts a new row at min(index, slide_count), shifting later slides and updating n_slides, with the 50-slide cap. The editPrompt argument is accepted by the schema but not used, and nothing is

Group Tools Backing method and notable behavior Outline addOutline, updateOutline, deleteOutline Edit presentation.outlines, recompute n_slides and title, then store_generated_outlines (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:4021-4041) Discovery getTemplateSummary, getAvailableLayouts, getContentSchemaFromLayoutId, getAvailableBlocks, getAvailableInfographics, searchSlide, getSlideAtIndex, readSourceDocuments Read-only. getAvailableBlocks searches reusable component blocks collected from presentation.layout and the referenced TemplateV2 row's merged components, components, layouts and raw layouts (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:2864-2911; default 20 results, max 50); getAvailableInfographics returns entries from INFOGRAPHIC_CATALOG Whole slide addNewSlide, addNewSlideLayout, saveSlide, updateSlide, deleteSlide save_slide validates content with Draft202012Validator against the layout schema (up to 10 errors); on replace it runs the asset reuse logic of Step 1.5 and assigns a new id, on insert it fetches all assets with process_slide_and_fetch_assets; both rebuild ui and store a [slide_edit] memory (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:777-983) Rendered UI addElement, addInfographic, updateElement, deleteElement, addComponent, createComponent, updateComponent, deleteComponent Mutate a deep copy of slide.ui and save it with _save_slide_ui, which strips component size and commits; the slide keeps its id; nothing is written to Mem0 (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1320-1328) Assets generateAssets Same as in smart mode Two of these use the utilities introduced at the end of chapter 13. addInfographic (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:855-910) validates data with normalize_infographic_data, defaults the position to (128, 170), the size to the catalog's default_size, the colors to a two-color meter palette or a six-color palette (white plus five blues), and the text color to 111111, optionally creating a blank slide first (target: "new_slide"). Text updates go through replace_text_runs, so a string such as "Area = <latex>\pi r^2</latex>" becomes a text run plus a LaTeX run that keeps the existing run's font (servers/fastapi/services/chat/slide_ui_helpers.py:2252). The rendered element model itself is documented in chapter 16. addElement, addComponent and createComponent also enforce the "reuse template blocks

docs.t: Step 6: How tools reach the database
docs.x: All chat tools share the request's AsyncSession through the memory layer, and each mutating method commits on its own (for example save_html_slide commits at servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1102 or :1150). There is no turn-level transaction: if round 3 fails after round 2 saved a slide, the round 2 change stays. The final _persist_turn commit only covers the two history rows. Reads such as getSlideAtIndex query by (presentation, index) on every call, which is why the standard tool description calls it "Live SQL" and "authoritative" (servers/fastapi/services/chat/tools.py:251) and the smart prompt calls the returned HTML authoritative.

Threads live in chat_history_messages (servers/fastapi/models/sql/chat_history_message.py:12): Column Type Notes id UUID PK owner_id UUID FK user.id, nullable, indexed Defaults to the current owner; excluded from serialization presentation_id UUID FK presentations.id (cascade), nullable, indexed template_v2_id string FK template_v2.id (cascade), nullable, indexed Supported by sql_chat_history, but no route in this snapshot passes a template ID conversation_id UUID, indexed The thread position int, indexed, >= 1 Order within the thread role string user or assistant content Text Stripped user text or final assistant text created_at timezone-aware datetime Assistant row is user time plus 1 microsecond tool_calls JSON list of strings Set on the assistant row only servers/fastapi/services/chat/sql_chat_history.py implements the operations. Every function requires exactly one of presentation_id or template_id (_resource_filter, :53-62). append_turn (:190-236) reads max(position) for the thread and inserts two rows at max+1 and max+2. list_conversations (:239-275) reads all rows for the deck newest first and keeps the first row per conversation, so last_message_preview is the latest message trimmed to 200 characters. delete_conversation and replace_messages filter deletes by owner_id as well. Owner scoping in general is covered in chapter 25.

Before SQL history existed, turns were only stored in Mem0. ChatConversationStore.load_history (servers/fastapi/services/chat/conversation_store.py:13-37) therefore reads SQL first and, when the thread is empty, loads the legacy Mem0 thread and writes it back with replace_messages. GET /chat/history does the same and commits when it migrated something (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/chat.py:60-74). append_turn writes to both stores (servers/fastapi/services/chat/conversation_store.py:39-61). Gotcha The SQL path loads the entire thread on every turn (load_messages has no limit), and only the final user and assistant texts are stored, not tool calls or tool results. Long threads grow the prompt without bound, and the model cannot see earlier tool outputs; it has to call discovery tools again. CHAT_MAX_STORED_TURNS (default 20) only limits the legacy Mem0 loader (servers/fastapi/services/chat/chat_memory_store.py:27-29, :343).

servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py holds a single process-wide mem0.Memory instance used by both memory services. Its docstring describes the namespacing: deck-level memories use the Mem0 user_id {namespace}:{presentation_id}, chat threads use {namespace}:{presentation_id}:conversation:{conversation_id} (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py:1-11). get_shared_mem0_client (:167-218) initializes it lazily and only once: Return None if MEM0_ENABLED is false (default true). If MEM0_REQUIRE_SPACY_MODEL is true (default), spacy.load(MEM0_SPACY_MODEL or "en_core_web_sm") must succeed, otherwise a warning is logged and Mem0 stays off. Build the configuration from the environment (_oss_config_from_env, :92-154), create the directories, point Mem0's telemetry directory at {mem0_dir}/telemetry/oss, and call Memory.from_config. Any exception is logged (with a specific hint when the fastembed model file is missing) and leaves the client None. _init_attempted is set before trying, so a failed initialization is not retried until the process restarts. servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py (excerpt) Environment variable Default Used for MEM0_ENABLED true Master switch (checked by the client and both services) APP_DATA_DIRECTORY /tmp/presenton Base for MEM0_DIR MEM0_DIR {APP_DATA_DIRECTORY}/mem0 (Compose sets /app_data/mem0) Root of all Mem0 files MEM0_QDRANT_PATH {MEM0_DIR}/qdrant Local on-disk Qdrant vector store MEM0_HISTORY_DB_PATH {MEM0_DIR}/history.db Mem0's SQLite history MEM0_COLLECTION_NAME presenton_memories Qdrant collection MEM0_EMBEDDER_PROVIDER fastembed Local embedding provider MEM0_EMBEDDER_MODEL BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 Embedding model MEM0_EMBEDDING_DIMS 384 Vector size, used by both store and embedder MEM0_LLM_MODEL OLLAMA_MODEL, else llama3.1:latest Mem0's LLM (provider openai, temperature 0.1, max tokens 2000) MEM0_LLM_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY, else ollama Mem0's LLM key MEM0_LLM_BASE_URL OLLAMA_URL, else http://host.docker.internal:11434 (suffixed with /v1) Mem0's LLM endpoint MEM0_SPACY_MODEL, MEM0_REQUIRE_SPACY_MODEL en_core_web_sm, true spaCy precondition MEM0_TOP_K 8 Results per search MEM0_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS 6000 Cap on the joined search result MEM0_PRESENTATION_NAMESPACE_PREFIX presentation Deck namespace MEM0_CHAT_NAMESPACE_PREFIX falls back to the presentation prefix Chat namespace CHAT_MAX_STORED_TURNS 20 Legacy chat history

Mem0PresentationMemoryService (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:18) writes each memory as a single user message whose first line is a tag. Messages longer than 20,000 characters are cut and suffixed with [TRUNCATED] (:47-50). Tag Written by Content [presentation_source_prompt], [presentation_generation_instructions], [outline_system_prompt], [outline_user_prompt], [document_extracted_text] store_generation_context, called from outline generation (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/outlines.py:153), the API generation path (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2764, :2846), and chat attachments (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:325, document text only) The generation inputs [generated_outlines] store_generated_outlines, from /prepare (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1923), outline endpoints, and chat outline tools Outline JSON [slide_edit] store_slide_edit, from /slide/edit, /slide/edit-html, and chat template save_slide (edit prompt [chat_tool_save_slide_replace] layout_id=... or [chat_tool_save_slide_new] ...) slide_index=, user_edit_prompt=, edited_slide_content= lines [chat_turn] ChatMemoryStore.store_chat_turn (servers/fastapi/services/chat/chat_memory_store.py:150) in the conversation scope turn_created_at=, user=, assistant= lines Smart generation itself (stream_smart_presentation) writes nothing to Mem0, and neither does the chat assistant's smart saveSlide. For a smart deck, deck memory therefore only contains /slide/edit-html edits and documents attached in chat.

retrieve_context(presentation_id, query) (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:186-242) calls client.search(query, filters={"user_id": scope}, top_k=MEM0_TOP_K), accepts either a {"results": [...]} dict or a list, takes each item's memory, text or data field, removes duplicates while keeping order, joins with blank lines and truncates to MEM0_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS. The chat store does the same in the conversation scope and also accepts memories or items keys (servers/fastapi/services/chat/chat_memory_store.py:103-116, :207-270). Both services retry add and search (and the chat store also get_all) with an alternative call signature on TypeError, to work across Mem0 versions. Note that _truncate appends \n\n[TRUNCATED] after the cut, so a capped context is slightly longer than MEM0_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS.

Memory is strictly best-effort. Each service method returns early when the client is None, catches BaseException, re-raises only exceptions that are neither Exception nor SystemExit (for example KeyboardInterrupt), turns a SystemExit from the Mem0 runtime into a per-process "disabled" flag on that service with a logged error, and logs everything else and continues with "" or [] (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:92-102, :207-218). All blocking Mem0 calls run in asyncio.to_thread and are serialized by run_shared_mem0_operation, a process-wide RLock, because local Qdrant keeps one SQLite connection that fails on concurrent commits (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py:32-42; covered by test_presentation_and_chat_operations_are_serialized, servers/fastapi/tests/test_mem0_presentation_memory_service.py:228). The scope-isolation test servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_mem0_session_scope_security.py checks that Mem0's session-scope encoding keeps a user_id like presentation:<uuid> intact and that crafted IDs cannot read another scope's history. Gotcha Because the lock is process-wide and searches run on every slide edit and chat turn, heavy concurrent use serializes on Mem0. The client is also created lazily on first use, so the first edit or chat turn after startup pays for initializing the embedder and the local Qdrant store. Setting MEM0_ENABLED=false removes memory entirely without any other behavior change, since every caller already tolerates an empty context.

Chat.tsx sends through a small adapter (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/chat/chat-adapter.ts:4-23) to PresentationChatApi.streamMessage (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:398). Before sending, buildBackendMessage (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:992-1126) prefixes the user's text with "UI context:" lines and ends with User message: .... For a smart deck with a selected element the lines are: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx (excerpt) The selection is the chatHtmlSelection written by SmartHtmlEditor in chapter 13; its HTML is capped at 3,500 characters (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:134) and wrapped in <selected_html> tags, preceded by Selected element tag: and Selected element text: lines. Other context lines cover the current slide, the outline variant, template v2 selections (component IDs and element paths), pasted images with optional extracted text, and links. The selection is cleared from Redux as soon as the message is sent (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1734). When a message starts with UI context:, the backend's _strip_ui_context_prefix (servers/fastapi/services/chat/service.py:492-499) removes everything up to the first \nUser message: before storing or searching, so history and memory hold only what the user typed. Gotcha ChatMessageRequest.message is limited to 8,000 characters, and that limit applies to the full composed string, including the UI context lines and up to 3,500 characters of selected HTML. A long prompt plus a large selection fails with 422 before the assistant runs.

streamChatMessage (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:104-319) uses fetch and a ReadableStream reader rather than EventSource (the request is a POST). It splits the buffer on blank lines, ignores frames whose event: is not response, and dispatches chunk to onChunk, status to onStatus, trace to onTrace (accepting both slide_index and slideIndex spellings), complete to the final response, and error by throwing (with a re-authentication prompt for ChatGPT session errors). If the stream ends without complete, it throws.

Chat.tsx wires those handlers (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1767-1876): chunks are appended to the assistant bubble; statuses and formatted traces become an activity list; a start trace for a mutating tool snapshots the affected slide for an edit preview; a success trace for a mutating tool triggers refreshPresentationIncrementally, which calls the page's onPresentationChanged (a re-fetch) and, while one refresh is in flight, queues at most one more (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1383-1408); and after complete, refreshPresentationIfNeeded re-fetches once more if any returned tool name is mutating (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1410-1422). Mutating tools are the 15 names in MUTATING_TOOLS (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/chat/chat-activity.ts:28-44). The edit preview lets the user switch between the original and modified slides; switching writes the chosen slide objects back through PATCH /presentation/slide_update (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/Chat.tsx:1307-1381). The active conversation ID is kept in sessionStorage under presenton:chat:{scope}:{presentationType}:conversationId:{resourceId} (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/chat/chat-utils.ts:141-170), so a reload in the same tab reopens the thread through GET /chat/history. Gotcha MUTATING_TOOLS does not include addInfographic, so a turn whose only mutation is a new infographic does not refresh the editor; the change appears after the next reload or the next mutating turn. Separately, restoring the "original" version after a template saveSlide or updateSlide sends the pre-edit slide object, whose id no longer exists because save_slide assigned a new UUID (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:871), and slide_update answers 404 "Slide not found" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2599-2601). Smart saveSlide keeps IDs, so restore works there. Gotcha The frontend appends presentation_type as a query parameter to the list, history and delete calls (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:330, :348, :369), but those routes do not declare it, so FastAPI ignores it. Threads are filtered by presentation only.

docs.p: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP
docs.x: Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/api/v2/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py, servers/fastapi/services/async_tasks.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/webhook/router.py, servers/fastapi/services/webhook_service.py, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py · Builds on: Standard generation pipeline, Auth and multi-user · Time: ~50 min Presenton is not only a web app: the same FastAPI process is a headless presentation API that other programs and AI agents can drive. This chapter walks through that product surface in execution order: how a program authenticates, the full GeneratePresentationRequest contract, what the synchronous /generate endpoint does and returns, how the async variant persists progress in an async_tasks row that you poll, what happens to those rows when the server restarts, how Smart generation is exposed under /api/v2, how webhooks are stored and delivered (and what they do not do), and how mcp_server.py turns a static OpenAPI document into a Model Context Protocol server with mode-gated tools and a key-for-session exchange.

docs.x: With account login enabled, SessionAuthMiddleware requires authentication for every /api/ path except five public auth routes (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:30). It resolves a principal in resolve_request_principal (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22): a presenton_session JWT cookie first, otherwise an Authorization: Bearer <token> header verified as an API key.

docs.p: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP
docs.x: servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py (excerpt) A key looks like sk-presenton-0123456789abcdef.<secret>: a 16-hex-character id (secrets.token_hex(8), also the api_keys.id primary key) and a secret from secrets.token_urlsafe(40). parse_api_key rejects anything without the prefix, a dot, a valid id, or a secret of at least 32 characters (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:50). Only a password hash of the secret is used for verification; an encrypted copy of the whole token (Fernet, keyed by a SHA-256 of the auth secret) lets an admin reveal it again.

docs.p: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP
docs.x: verify_api_key (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:107) loads the row by id, rejects it if revoked or expired, checks the secret against secret_hash (upgrading the hash if the helper asks), requires the owning user to be active, and stamps last_used_at. The middleware then: Sets request.state.auth_principal with method="api_key". Mints an internal session JWT for that user (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:123). The export step needs it: the headless browser that renders the deck must load the editor page as that user, and build_export_cookie_header turns it into a presenton_session= cookie (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1486). Sets the owner context variables, so every row created during the request is stamped with the key owner's id and every ORM SELECT is filtered to it. Keys are issued, listed, revealed and revoked under /api/v1/admin/api-keys from an admin browser session (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:44). An API key can never call those admin routes, nor the handful of admin-only paths listed at servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:100. The full model, including hashing and tenancy, is in Auth and multi-user. Note When DISABLE_AUTH is enabled (Electron's single-user mode), the middleware returns before any of this and requests run without an owner (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:59). The README states that external REST and MCP access are not available in the Electron app.

docs.x: With slides_markdown, each string becomes a SlideOutlineModel(content=...) directly (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2838). Each item is still passed through the outline word limit (MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS, default 100) by the model's validator, and the LLM still chooses layouts and fills the template schema, so text can be rephrased. http(s) image URLs ending in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp inside an item are used for that slide's image slots instead of generating images. files are resolved by DocumentsLoader, which only accepts paths inside the server's temp upload area (servers/fastapi/services/documents_loader.py:171). Upload first: The returned array (path shape shown schematically) goes into files unchanged. Document parsing is covered in Document ingestion.

docs.x: generate_presentation_sync (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3170) validates, then awaits generate_presentation_handler (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2684) with async_status=None. The handler is the same code the async path runs. Its stages, which Standard generation pipeline explains in depth: Outline. Unless slides_markdown is set: load files into additional_context, compute the outline count (adjusted for a TOC), store generation context in Mem0, stream generate_ppt_outline into a string, parse it with dirtyjson, and normalize it. Fewer outlines than requested is a 400 (Failed to generate presentation outlines with requested number of slides. Please try again.); extra outlines are silently truncated (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2830). Layout. _resolve_generation_layout loads the TemplateV2 row and returns the layout payload, a PresentationLayoutModel, fonts and theme. A bundled template whose row was never imported yields 503 Bundled template '<name>' is not available. Restart the service to import bundled templates. (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:279). Structure. Ordered layouts map one to one; otherwise an LLM picks a layout index per outline. Out-of-range indices are replaced with random valid ones. Table of contents layouts are inserted when requested. Slides are generated in batches of 10 with asyncio.gather, and each slide's asset task starts immediately so images overlap the next batch's LLM calls (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2985). Persist. After all asset tasks finish, the presentation, slides and generated ImageAsset rows are committed in one transaction (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3088). Export via export_presentation(presentation_id, title, export_as, cookie_header=...) (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:43), described in PPTX and PDF export. Respond and fire the completion webhook.

docs.x: Any non-HTTPException inside the handler is printed and replaced by HTTPException(500, "Presentation generation failed"); then the failure webhook fires; then, for a sync call, the exception propagates as the HTTP response (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3142). The body is FastAPI's standard {"detail": "..."}. Gotcha A sync request that the client abandons is cancelled cooperatively: raise_if_client_disconnected checks request.is_disconnected() before each batch and raises asyncio.CancelledError (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2697). CancelledError is a BaseException, not an Exception, so it skips the handler's except Exception block: no failure webhook is sent and no error is recorded. Use the async endpoint for anything long-running.

The handler moves the row through these states: message status Set at Visible to pollers Queued for generation pending request handler yes Starting presentation generation pending background task start yes Generating presentation outlines pending before the outline LLM call (skipped with slides_markdown) yes Selecting layout for each slide pending after outlines yes Generating slides pending before the first batch; remaining_slides reset to the final count yes (data only) pending after each batch of 10, created_slides grows yes Fetching assets for slides pending after all batches are scheduled yes Exporting presentation pending before export no Presentation generation completed completed after export; data gains path and edit_path yes Presentation generation failed error on any exception yes Gotcha The "Exporting presentation" update is sql_session.add(async_status) without a commit() (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3093), and the next write overwrites the message before committing. Pollers therefore see "Fetching assets for slides" for the whole export, which can take a while for PDF or large decks. Do not treat a long stall on that message as a hang. docs.t: Step 7: What happens to in-flight tasks on restart
docs.p: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP
docs.x: Background tasks are plain coroutines inside the FastAPI process. If the process dies (a crash that start.js restarts, a container restart, a deploy), the coroutine is gone but its row still says pending. The lifespan hook fixes that before the server accepts requests (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:59): servers/fastapi/services/async_tasks.py (excerpt) The query runs at startup with no owner context, so it covers every user's tasks. There is no resume and no re-queue: the client must submit a new job. Uploaded source files do not survive a restart either. TEMP_FILE_SERVICE is a module-level singleton whose constructor calls cleanup_base_dir(), which deletes everything under TEMP_DIRECTORY (default /tmp/presenton) when the process starts (servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py:13 and servers/fastapi/services/temp_file_service.py:187). A resubmitted job that reuses files paths from before the restart therefore fails with 404 File not found when DocumentsLoader resolves them; upload the files again first. Gotcha No webhook is sent for tasks failed this way; fail_interrupted_async_tasks only updates rows. A webhook-only integration never hears about a job lost to a restart, so it should also poll, or at least reconcile with GET /api/v1/async-tasks?status=error. And because every pending row is failed at startup, running two FastAPI processes against one database would let one process's restart fail the other's live jobs.

docs.x: servers/fastapi/services/webhook_service.py (excerpt) send_webhook (servers/fastapi/services/webhook_service.py:12) selects all subscriptions for the event and posts to them concurrently with asyncio.gather. Reading the code, delivery is: Authenticated by bearer secret only. The subscriber receives Authorization: Bearer <secret>. There is no HMAC signature, timestamp, or event-id header. Single attempt. No retries, no backoff, no dead-letter record. The response status is ignored, so a 500 from the subscriber counts the same as a 200. No explicit timeout. The ClientSession uses aiohttp's defaults. Owner-scoped. asyncio.create_task copies the current context variables, so the owner id set by the middleware (sync path) or by _run_generate_presentation_task (async path) is still set inside send_webhook, and the session's owner filter limits the SELECT to that user's subscriptions. With auth disabled there is no owner and every subscription matches. Gotcha trigger_webhook in the request does nothing: a repository-wide search finds it only in the model definition. Webhooks fire for every Standard generation through generate_presentation_handler, sync or async, whenever the owner has a matching subscription. Conversely, the failure payload carries no presentation_id or task id, so a subscriber cannot tell which job failed when several run at once. Gotcha url is an unvalidated string, and the server posts to it from inside your network. Any user who can authenticate can register an internal address. If you expose the API to untrusted users, add URL validation in subscribe_to_webhook (servers/fastapi/api/v1/webhook/router.py:26).

docs.x: mcp_server.py is a separate Python process started by start.js as python mcp_server.py --port 8001 with stdio: "ignore" (start.js:608). Its main() (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:417) exits immediately when PRESENTON_ELECTRON is truthy, otherwise serves FastMCP's HTTP transport on 127.0.0.1:<port>. nginx exposes it at /mcp and /mcp/ (nginx.conf:77 and nginx.conf:94) with: client_max_body_size 145M, enough for the 100 MiB base64 upload limit (base64 inflates by a third), proxy_read_timeout 30m, Host localhost:8001 rewritten, because FastMCP's host check only allows localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:41), while the public host travels in X-Forwarded-Host, no auth_request: the MCP server authenticates bearer keys itself. The README describes it as an MCP 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP endpoint at /mcp. Gotcha Unlike FastAPI and Next.js, the MCP child process is not registered with watchManagedProcess in start.js (only an error listener is attached at start.js:618), and its output is discarded. If it crashes, nothing restarts it and nothing is logged. A failing MCP client while the web app works is the usual symptom.

docs.t: 10.5 The token verifier and the key-for-session exchange
docs.p: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP
docs.x: When auth is enabled, create_mcp_auth_provider returns a PresentonTokenVerifier; with DISABLE_AUTH it returns None and the MCP endpoint is open (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:324). servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py (excerpt) The returned AccessToken carries claims u (username), role (admin or user), user_id, api_key_id and internal_session_token, a one-hour JWT (MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60, chosen so a 10 to 20 minute generation including export does not outlive its session, per the comment at servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:35). Then, on every outbound call to FastAPI, the httpx request hook attach_request_auth_header (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:365) rewrites the request: Always set X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, and forward the client's X-Forwarded-Host (or Host) and X-Forwarded-Proto. If the outgoing request already has Authorization or Cookie, stop. If the verified token has an internal_session_token, send it as Cookie: presenton_session=<jwt>. The long-lived API key is never forwarded to FastAPI. If the token has a user_id but no session could be minted, raise RuntimeError rather than fall back to the key. Fallbacks for auth-disabled development: forward Bearer <token> or the incoming Authorization header. FastAPI then authenticates the cookie like a browser session, which is also why the export step works without further plumbing: build_export_cookie_header copies the incoming cookie header verbatim.

docs.x: servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json is a committed, minified copy of the FastAPI OpenAPI document (about 144 KB, OpenAPI 3.1.0, 93 paths). It is produced by: servers/fastapi/scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py The script does not add its parent directory to sys.path (unlike warm_fastembed_cache.py), so run it from servers/fastapi as a module, python -m scripts.generate_openapi_spec, or with PYTHONPATH=.; importing api.main executes the app's module-level setup, so the environment must be able to import the app. Several routes set explicit operation_ids (generate_smart_presentation_async, mcp_files_upload, mcp_template_upload, template_list) precisely so the MCP_TOOL_NAMES keys stay stable; the others rely on FastAPI's generated ids such as generate_presentation_async_api_v1_ppt_presentation_generate_async_post. Unit tests read the committed file to assert template-related operation ids and schemas (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_mcp_openapi_templates.py:28). Gotcha The MCP server never asks the live app for its schema. If you add a field to GeneratePresentationRequest or rename a route and forget to regenerate openai_spec.json, MCP clients keep seeing the old tool schema, and a renamed operation id silently drops out of MCP_TOOL_NAMES (keeping its long generated name) or out of the route maps entirely. Regenerate the file and restart the MCP process after any API change.

Reads: templates/general/template.json, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py, servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py, servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py, layouts.json · Builds on: Data model · Time: ~35 min

Every slide Presenton generates is a copy of a "Template v2" layout with some values swapped out. This chapter specifies that format field by field, from the Pydantic models that validate it and from the 16 template bundles that ship in the repository. You will learn the top-level template.json keys, how layouts, components and elements nest inside a 1280 x 720 canvas, every element type and property, the decorative/name/limit flags that turn an element into a content field, and how the same data is stored in the template_v2 table. The chapter ends with the inventory of built-in templates and an explanation of the stray layouts.json file at the repository root.

A Template v2 template exists in three places during its life, and the shape changes slightly between them. Keep this map in mind; the rest of the chapter refers back to it. Shape Where layouts merged_components Fonts, icons, thumbnail Bundle templates/<name>/template.json bare list bare list top-level fonts, icon_type, thumbnail Row template_v2 table {"layouts": [...]} {"components": [...]} inside the assets JSON column Deck presentations.layout {"layouts": [...], "icon_type", "icon_weight", "name", "template_id"} not copied presentations.fonts Slide slides.ui one layout object not copied not copied The wrapping happens in _coerce_slide_layouts and _coerce_merged_components (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:202 and :210), which accept either a bare list or an already wrapped object. The deck copy is built by _copy_template_layout_payload (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:232). Chapter 17 walks through those transitions; this chapter is about the data itself.

Each bundle directory contains one template.json and a static/ folder of assets. Here is the head of the General bundle and its last two keys, verbatim (the 17,000 lines of merged_components and layouts in between are elided): templates/general/template.json (excerpt) The keys, what validates them, and where they end up: Key Type Required Validation at import Stored as id string no stripped; falls back to the directory name; must not contain / or \ (default_templates.py:177) template_v2.id (primary key) name string no stripped; falls back to the id (default_templates.py:189) template_v2.name description string no stripped; empty becomes null template_v2.description thumbnail string no static/... rewritten (Step 10) assets.thumbnail icon_type string no normalized to one of bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin; default bold (servers/fastapi/utils/icon_weights.py:5) assets.icon_type and assets.icon_weight merged_components list no MergedComponents Pydantic model template_v2.merged_components layouts list yes SlideLayouts Pydantic model, at least one layout template_v2.layouts fonts object no must be an object, otherwise {} assets.fonts theme object no none at import, stored if it is an object template_v2.theme components object no stored only if it is an object (no bundle uses it) template_v2.components _load_default_template (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:113) performs exactly these steps: servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py (excerpt) Gotcha: the docstring says UUIDs, the data says names resolve_default_template_id (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:62) explains that bundled templates "use UUIDs as database IDs" while clients send the public directory name. In this snapshot every one of the 16 bundles sets "id" equal to its directory name ("general", "momentum", and so on), so the translation is the identity. The code path still matters: if you ship a bundle whose id is a UUID, clients can keep sending the directory name and generation resolves it. It is only validated later, as PresentationThemeData, when GET /api/v1/ppt/template/{template_id} builds its response (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:2149). A layout is one slide design. A component is a reusable region of that slide. Both are plain Pydantic models in servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py (excerpt) Model Field Rule Source SlideLayout id string, unique across the template layouts.py:98, layouts.py:114 SlideLayout description string; the structure-selection LLM reads it (chapter 17) layouts.py:100 SlideLayout components list; ids unique within the layout layouts.py:101, layouts.py:103 Component id string; becomes the top-level key of the slide's content JSON layouts.py:55 Component description string layouts.py:56 Component position {x, y} on the 1280 x 720 canvas layouts.py:57 Component elements at least one element layouts.py:58 SlideLayouts layouts at least one layout layouts.py:112 There is no size on a component. Do not include component size." (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:1331). The renderer computes a component's extent from its children.
