docs.t: Step 4: The coordinate system and how positions nest
docs.x: Layouts use a fixed 1280 x 720 pixel canvas (docs/template-v2.md:159; TEMPLATE_V2_HTML_WIDTH/HEIGHT at servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:153). Positions are always relative to the nearest positioned ancestor: The rules come from two places that must agree: the compiler that writes layouts and the renderer that reads them. Component origin. When the certification compiler builds a component, it sets position to the top-left corner of the union bounds of the component's source elements, then subtracts that offset from each element (_localize_top_level_element, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py:3050, and the position assignment at :2998). Components render as groups. renderItem treats any record with an elements array and no known element type as a component and renders it as a group whose children are its elements (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:308). Groups position children absolutely. renderGroup renders every child in "absolute" mode, which emits left/top from the child's position (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:839 and frameStyleFromBox at :3209). Containers choose per child. renderContainer renders its single child absolutely when the child has a position, otherwise in flow mode inside a flexbox that honors alignment and padding (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:485). Flex and grid flow their children. Children render in "flow" mode (position: relative, no left/top) and are laid out by the shared flow engine (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:534, :777). The one exception is a child flagged __presenton_manual_position, which the flow engine treats as manually placed (htmlFlowLayoutDeps, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:583). Vectors have no position. readBox derives a vector's box from the minimum and maximum of its points (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3221, polygonBox at :3413), so the points themselves are coordinates in the parent's space. The compiler shifts vector points rather than a position when it localizes them (certified_generation.py:3061). In Step 7 you will see the consequence: in a component placed at (672, 199.47), a divider whose points run from (0, 144) to (80, 148) is drawn at canvas coordinates (672, 343.47) to (752, 347.47).

Every element is a member of one discriminated union, keyed by type: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) The table below lists all eleven types, which schema fields each carries, and how often each appears across the 383 layouts of the 16 bundles (counted by walking every component, including nested children). type Model decorative name Limit fields Count in bundles text Text (elements.py:203) required required max_length, min_length 3,623 image Image (elements.py:240) required required none (is_icon required) 2,251 group Group (elements.py:611) absent required none 2,038 flex Flex (elements.py:567) absent required max_children, min_children 1,132 vector Vector (elements.py:342) absent optional none 733 container Container (elements.py:224) absent absent none 255 chart Chart (elements.py:361) required required none 113 infographic Infographic (elements.py:549) required required none 51 grid Grid (elements.py:589) absent required max_children, min_children 45 text-list TextList (elements.py:265) required required max_items, min_items, max_item_length, min_item_length 35 table Table (elements.py:302) required required max_columns, min_columns, max_rows, min_rows 7

Every type except vector has optional position ({x, y}, floats) and size ({width, height}, floats). Almost every type has rotation (degrees), flip_h and flip_v. The renderer turns them into one CSS transform, rotate(...) scaleX(-1) scaleY(-1) with transform-origin:center (transformStyle, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3478).

Model Fields Source Font size, family, color, bold, italic, underline, line_height, letter_spacing, ellipsis, opacity (all optional) elements.py:126 Alignment horizontal in left, center, right, justify; vertical in top, middle, bottom elements.py:121 Fill color (required), opacity elements.py:139 Stroke color, width (required); opacity, dash (list of floats), line_cap (butt/round/square), line_join (bevel/miter/round), start_marker, end_marker elements.py:150 StrokeMarker type in arrow, diamond, open, oval, stealth, triangle; length and width in sm, med, lg elements.py:144 Shadow color (required), blur, opacity, offset_x, offset_y elements.py:168 BorderRadius tl, tr, bl, br (all required) elements.py:161 Padding top, right, bottom, left (all required) elements.py:114 line_height is read two ways downstream: values above 2 are treated as pixels, values up to 2 as a multiple of the font size (_text_capacity_geometry, certified_generation.py:2499, and the same rule in _table_cell_typography, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:152).

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) A text element has an element-level font and a list of runs, each with its own optional font. The renderer merges them per run ({...font, ...run.font}, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:399), so a run only needs to carry what differs. In the bundles, runs usually repeat the full font. A run can instead be a LaTeX run ({"type": "latex", "latex": "...", "display_mode": false}, up to 4,000 characters), which the HTML renderer typesets with KaTeX (chapter 17). fill, stroke and shadow on a text element style the box, not the glyphs; a shadow becomes a CSS text-shadow (textShadowStyle, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3460). max_length and min_length are character counts. They become maxLength/minLength in the content schema the LLM must satisfy (chapter 17). Certification computes them from geometry: characters per line times line count, multiplied by a 0.85 safety factor, never below the current text length (_estimated_text_capacity, certified_generation.py:2375, TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR at :62).

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) Field Meaning data URL of the image. Replaceable images hold a placeholder: /static/images/replaceable_template_image.png for photos, /static/icons/placeholder.svg for icons (certified_generation.py:63). Decorative images keep their real asset URL. fit contain, cover or fill. The HTML renderer defaults to contain when it is missing (imageFit, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3980). focus_x, focus_y Percentages (0 to 100) for CSS object-position (imageFocusValue, :4008). crop_scale Zoom factor clamped to 1 to 6, applied as a CSS scale() around the focus point (imageCropScale, :3989). border_radius Per-corner radius. clip_path A CSS clip-path. Only path, polygon, circle, ellipse and inset functions pass the sanitizer (normalizeCssClipPath, :4026). color Icon tint. When color is set and is_icon is true, the renderer draws the icon as a CSS mask filled with that color (renderImage, :357). opacity Element opacity. prompt The prompt or icon query that produced the current data, written back during hydration (chapter 17). is_icon Distinguishes a searchable icon from a photo or illustration. It changes the generated content field from image_prompt to icon_query. icon_type Icon style: bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin.

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) items is a list of items, each item a list of runs. marker is bullet, number or none. gap is the vertical space between items in pixels and marker_gap the horizontal space between the marker and the text. The limits bound both the number of items and the characters per item.

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) columns is the header row; rows are the body rows. A cell's background is its color (a Fill), and borders holds an optional Stroke per side (TableCellBorders, elements.py:287). The renderer treats row 0 as the header and bolds it unless the cell sets bold explicitly (tableCellStyle, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3559). The certification compiler insists that every body row has exactly as many cells as columns (certified_generation.py:3539).

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) Vectors replace the older rectangle/line types (you will see those in layouts.json, Step 12). The fields: shape is polygon (default) or ellipse. An ellipse is drawn inside the bounding box of its points, so two opposite corners are enough (renderEllipseVector, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:1019). points needs at least two entries. With two points and closed unset it is an open line; with three or more it is closed unless closed is false (polygonClosed, :3403). corner_radii lists one radius per vertex; the renderer rounds each corner with a quadratic curve, capping the radius at half of each adjacent edge (roundedPolygonPoints, :3307). curve: {"type": "smooth"} resamples the outline as a Hermite spline; tension defaults to 0.4 in the renderer and segments to 16, clamped to 1 to 96 (curveSettings, :3336). start_marker/end_marker (none, arrow, stealth, triangle, circle, square, diamond) only render on open paths. Markers can also sit on the stroke, where the PPTX names oval and open map to circle and arrow (vectorMarker, :946). fill applies to closed shapes only. An open path without a stroke color is drawn in black (renderPolygon, :863). Vectors have no decorative flag and no content schema: they are always fixed artwork.

Chart (elements.py:361) carries the chart type, the data, and its styling: Group Fields Type chart_type: bar, horizontal_bar, line, area, pie, donut, stacked_bar, horizontal_stacked_bar, scatter, radar, polar_area (ChartType, elements.py:76) Data categories (list of strings), series (list of {name, values}), source Text title, x_axis_title, y_axis_title Colors colors (palette in renderer order), title_color, legend_color, text_color, axis_color, grid_color Toggles x_axis, y_axis, x_axis_grid, y_axis_grid, legend, legend_position (left/right/top/bottom), data_labels (base/mid/top/outside) Three validators run on every chart. Pie and donut charts keep only their first series (elements.py:395). A legacy boolean data_labels: true becomes "top" and false becomes null (:405). An explicit size smaller than 80 x 60 pixels is rejected (:418).

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt) InfographicType (elements.py:427) enumerates 27 kinds. Two are metrics with a strict shape (extra="forbid"): progress_bar and gauge, each {type, min_value, max_value, value} with max_value > min_value (elements.py:464, :479). The other 25 (gantt, timeline, roadmap, milestone_timeline, staircase, supply_chain, stair_step_blocks, maturity_model, pillar_framework, transformation_hub, diagonal_circles, risk_matrix, chevron_process, radial_cycle, conversion_funnel, vertical_funnel, pyramid, segmented_wheel, customer_journey, before_after, impact_effort_matrix, comparison_matrix, org_chart, decision_tree, mind_map) are "structural": the model allows extra keys and normalizes them through normalize_infographic_data in servers/fastapi/utils/infographic_catalog.py (elements.py:523). For metrics, colors[0] is the track and colors[1] the filled value (infographicBaseColor/infographicHighlightColor, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3037). In the bundles the 51 infographics are 26 gauges, 19 progress bars, two timelines, two vertical funnels, one maturity model and one staircase.

Container (elements.py:224) is a styled box around exactly one optional child: fill, stroke, border_radius, shadow, padding and alignment. It has no name and no decorative, so it is pure layout; any content lives in its child.

docs.t: 5.11 flex, grid and group: flexible and repeated regions
docs.x: These three types are how a template expresses "this region holds a variable number of items". Type Layout fields Schema fields Behavior flex direction (row/column, required), wrap, align_items, justify_content (flex-start, flex-end, center, stretch), gap, column_gap, row_gap, children name, max_children, min_children One-dimensional flow. grid columns (required), rows, gap, column_gap, row_gap, align_items, justify_items, children name, max_children, min_children Two-dimensional flow. group children name Free placement; children keep absolute positions. When all children of a flex or grid expose the same editable fields, the content schema turns the region into an array whose length is bounded by min_children and max_children (chapter 17). A group whose children repeat becomes an array bounded by half to all of its items. The certification compiler sets min_children to max(1, (n + 1) // 2) for a repeated region of n items and to n for a fixed one, with max_children = n (certified_generation.py:3301).

Three kinds of fields decide whether an element is content or decoration. decorative is the switch. Only elements with decorative: false whose type is one of text, image, text-list, table, chart or infographic become fields in the content schema (CONTENT_TYPES and _is_editable_element, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:15 and :53). Everything else is copied untouched into every slide. In the bundles, 3,584 of 3,623 text elements and 607 of 2,251 images are editable; all charts, tables, text lists and infographics are editable. name is the field's key in the content JSON. Names are lowercase snake case; the semantic certification pass enforces ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and at most 80 characters (SemanticElementAnnotation.name, layouts.py:128). For flex, grid and group, the name becomes the key of the nested object or array. Limit pairs (min_length/max_length, min_items/max_items, min_item_length/max_item_length, min_columns/max_columns, min_rows/max_rows, min_children/max_children) bound the generated content. Certification refuses negative limits and a minimum above its maximum (_certify_element_tree, certified_generation.py:3531). Gotcha: the min-equals-half rule is defined but not enforced elements.py opens with _validate_min_max, which raises unless a minimum equals half of its maximum, rounded up (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:13). Nothing calls it. The "half rounded up" convention is applied by the generators instead (for example (len(columns) + 1) // 2 for tables at certified_generation.py:1513), and the bundles do not follow it everywhere: the General title has min_length: 8, max_length: 25. Do not rely on the relation when you read or hand-edit templates.

Here is the entire title_description_image layout from the General bundle (templates/general/template.json:9148). Whitespace has been compacted so short objects fit on one line; every key and value is unchanged. templates/general/template.json, layout title_description_image (compacted) Reading it top to bottom: What Meaning slide_background A full-canvas white rectangle drawn as a closed vector. No editable elements, so it contributes nothing to the content schema. Components render in array order, so this one sits at the bottom. left_visual_card at (88, 184) A rounded white card (vector with corner_radii and a soft shadow) and, on top of it, a 512 x 320 image at the same local origin. The image is editable (decorative: false), is a photo (is_icon: false) and still points at the replaceable placeholder. Its schema field is left_visual_card.main_visual_image.image_prompt. right_text_stack at (672, 199.47) A 60 px bold heading limited to 8 to 25 characters, a purple 80 x 4 accent bar at local y 144, and an 18 px paragraph limited to 105 to 274 characters. The sample strings ("Product Overview" and the dashboard sentence) are placeholders the generator replaces. Fonts Poppins appears in both the element font and each run's font; the template's fonts map tells the browser where Poppins lives (chapter 19). Chapter 17 feeds this exact layout through the schema builder and the hydrator.

merged_components is a catalog of interchangeable component variants collected from all layouts: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py (excerpt) Each entry groups full Component objects (with position and elements) that can stand in for one another. In General, the first group, background_canvas, holds the white full-slide rectangles from several layouts as separate variants. The catalog is produced by an LLM clustering pass plus a structural de-duplication step during custom-template creation (chapter 18). The generation pipeline never reads merged_components. It is consumed by three side features: prompted layout generation passes up to eight matching groups to the model as reusable components (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:726), the chat assistant turns them into insertable block candidates (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:2905), and the template editor offers them as insertable blocks (chapter 18). Gotcha: variants are copies, not references A variant is a full copy of a component, not a pointer into layouts. Editing a layout does not update its variant, and scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs exists precisely to push edited slide UIs back into both layouts and the matching variants by deep equality (chapter 18). If you hand-edit a bundle, edit both places.

docs.t: Step 9: The fonts and theme blocks
docs.x: fonts maps a display family name to a URL: {"Montserrat Semi-Bold": "static/Montserrat SemiBold.ttf", ...}. A URL is either a bundle-relative static/... font file or a Google Fonts CSS URL. The bundles mix both: Civic ships six local font files, General only a Google Fonts URL for Poppins. Template fonts are stored as assets.fonts and later copied into presentations.fonts. theme has the shape of PresentationThemeData (servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py:32): a colors object with exactly 16 roles (primary, background, card, stroke, background_text, primary_text, graph_0 to graph_9) and fonts.textFont: {name, url}. The theme is a semantic summary of the template's palette; layouts do not reference it, every element carries literal colors. Gotcha: Google Fonts URLs in bundles are never fetched A test asserts that runtime frontend code never loads fonts.googleapis.com (servers/nextjs/local-font-loading-validation.test.mjs:26). The browser-side font loader ignores any URL that is not a font file and maps the family name to the vendored copy in servers/nextjs/public/vendor/fonts instead. A Google Fonts URL in a bundle is therefore only a hint; if the family is missing from the vendored catalog, the text falls back to another font. Chapter 19 covers the font pipeline.

import_default_templates_on_startup (walked through in chapter 17) turns each bundle into a TemplateV2 row. The columns, from servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16: Column Type Built-in bundle value Custom template value id string PK, default uuid4() bundle id UUID owner_id UUID FK to user.id, nullable, cascade delete null creating user name, description string from bundle from request or PPTX file name raw_layouts JSON null PPTX-to-JSON output, {"layouts": [...]} components JSON null (unused) null merged_components JSON {"components": [...]} from clustering layouts JSON {"layouts": [...]} certified layouts theme JSON bundle theme generated theme assets JSON see below see chapter 18 is_default bool true false created_at, updated_at timestamptz set on insert / update same Two rewrites happen before validation: servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py (excerpt) Every string anywhere in the JSON that starts with static/ (image data, thumbnail, font URLs, even theme.fonts.textFont.url) is rewritten to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/..., and the bundle's static/ folder is copied to $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/templates/<id>/static (default_templates.py:295). Strings that start with /static/ (with a leading slash), such as the image placeholder, are left alone because they are FastAPI's own static files. _build_assets (default_templates.py:220) then assembles: The images list holds every distinct image data value found in layouts and merged_components (_collect_image_urls, default_templates.py:267); the two values shown are the first two real entries, and the full list for General has 18.

Counts were taken from the bundles in this snapshot. "Icon type" is the stored icon_type, with absent values shown as the import default bold. "Merged groups" counts entries in merged_components. "Static files" counts files under static/. Directory and id Name Layouts Merged groups Icon type Theme text font Static files civic Civic 29 38 regular Montserrat 87 dynamic Dynamic 32 40 bold (absent) Montserrat 23 editorial Editorial 24 9 thin DM Sans Bold 116 executive Executive 32 47 bold (absent) Montserrat Bold 20 general General 12 15 bold (absent) Poppins 17 horizon Horizon 28 29 regular Poppins 84 landmark Landmark 27 17 regular Poppins 123 modern Modern 10 19 bold Montserrat 1 momentum Momentum 28 27 bold (absent) Lato 33 mosaic Mosaic 34 67 regular Montserrat 108 nova Nova 28 26 regular Poppins 102 pulse Pulse 28 20 regular Inter 1 114 signal Signal 24 20 regular Inter 1 98 standard Standard 11 19 bold Playfair Display 3 swift Swift 9 20 bold Inter 3 verdant Verdant 27 31 regular DM Sans 70 Total 383 444 The template picker shows Momentum, Dynamic and Executive first; the rest keep the API order, newest first (FEATURED_BUILT_IN_TEMPLATE_ORDER, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/hooks/useTemplateSummaries.ts:12). Gotcha: bundles are authoritative and read-only Built-in rows are overwritten from disk on every start, their static folder is deleted and recopied, and rows for bundles that no longer exist are deleted along with their assets (default_templates.py:142, :154, :305). The API refuses to edit or delete them with 403 Built-in templates are read-only (_require_private_template, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:2170). To change a built-in template, edit its bundle and restart.

docs.t: Step 12: layouts.json at the repository root
docs.x: The repository root contains a 252 KB layouts.json. Its shape is a doubly wrapped layout list, {"layouts": {"layouts": [...]}}, holding 14 layouts with ids such as business_proposal_cover_layout, content_index_slide and slide_14_component_layout. It predates the current element union: Feature in layouts.json Current format rectangle (46 elements) and line (3) types replaced by vector size on components not part of Component chart fields data, color, label_color, show_values replaced by categories, series, colors, text_color, data_labels image URLs such as http://127.0.0.1:8000/app_data/pptx-to-json/<session>/images/... bundle-relative static/... paths A search of the whole repository (excluding node_modules and this tutorial) finds no file that reads or references layouts.json: no Python module, no Next.js code, no script, no test, no Dockerfile. It was added in the commit "feat: template v2 rendering issues fix and adds ui in slide model to save the layout edits" and looks like a development artifact from an earlier PPTX conversion. It would not validate against SlideLayouts today, because rectangle and line are not members of the SlideElement union. Treat it as a historical sample, not as a reference.

docs.t: From template to schema to slide
docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: Reads: servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py, servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/utils/ppt_utils.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx · Builds on: Template v2 format · Time: ~45 min

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: This chapter follows one layout through its whole life: imported from a bundle at startup, stored as a row, turned into a JSON Schema the LLM has to fill, chosen for a slide, filled with generated content, hydrated back into a renderable layout tree, and finally drawn as HTML in the browser. You will see the schema builder's rules for every element type (including repeated regions and the length limits), the exact hydration algorithm that writes content back into elements, and every branch of the HTML renderer. A worked example runs a real General layout through the real schema builder and hydrator.

docs.t: Step 1: Importing the built-in templates at startup
docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: The FastAPI lifespan calls import_default_templates_on_startup() after migrations, admin bootstrap and the cleanup of interrupted tasks (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:64). The function is short enough to read in full: servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py (excerpt) Step by step: Find the bundles. The root is Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "templates" (default_templates.py:58), which resolves to the repository-level templates/ directory. Every subdirectory with a template.json is a bundle, processed in alphabetical order. Load and validate. _load_default_template reads the JSON, rewrites static/... strings to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/..., validates layouts through SlideLayouts and merged_components through MergedComponents (dropping unknown keys), and assembles assets (chapter 16, Step 10). The row is built with raw_layouts=None and is_default=True (default_templates.py:128). Copy static assets. _copy_default_template_static_assets deletes $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/templates/<id>/static and copies the bundle's static/ folder in its place. It raises RuntimeError("APP_DATA_DIRECTORY must be set to import default templates") if the variable is missing (default_templates.py:295). Upsert. An existing row has every content column overwritten (_update_template_from_default, default_templates.py:142); otherwise the new row is inserted. Each template is committed on its own. Remove stale defaults. Any is_default row whose id was not seen in this run is deleted, and its templates/<id> asset directory removed (default_templates.py:154, :310). Built-in rows have owner_id = NULL, because no user context exists during startup. They are still visible to everyone: the session-level loader criteria for TemplateV2 admit rows that belong to the current owner or rows with owner_id IS NULL AND is_default IS TRUE (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:87). User-created templates are stamped with the creator's id on flush (services/database.py:100). Chapter 25 covers the ownership model. Gotcha: one broken bundle stops the server The loop has no try/except. A template.json that fails SlideLayouts validation, a static/../ path, or an id containing a slash raises out of the lifespan, and FastAPI does not start. The unit tests test_bundled_general_template_json_matches_template_v2_shapes and test_new_bundled_templates_load_with_layouts_and_assets

docs.t: Step 2: The row that comes out
docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: After the import, a template is a template_v2 row (servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16). The columns that matter for generation are: Column Used for id lookup key; also written into every slide's layout_group layouts {"layouts": [...]}; the source of both the schemas and the slide UIs assets.fonts copied to presentations.fonts assets.icon_type the icon weight used when searching icons for this deck theme wrapped and copied to presentations.theme on the API path (chapter 19) raw_layouts, merged_components not used by generation Clients name templates either by id or, for built-ins, by directory name. resolve_default_template_id maps a directory name to the id stored in its template.json, after rejecting ., .. and any name containing / or \ (default_templates.py:62).

docs.t: Step 3: Resolving a template for a deck
docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: Two endpoints resolve a template into a layout payload. The UI path, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare, uses _resolve_prepare_layout (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1448), which strips an optional custom- prefix and looks the id up directly, returning 404 Template layout not found on a miss. The API path, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate, uses _resolve_generation_layout (presentation.py:262), which also accepts bundled directory names and answers 503 with "Restart the service to import bundled templates." when a bundle exists on disk but its row is missing. Both end in _copy_template_layout_payload: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) This payload is stored in presentations.layout. From here on the deck is independent of the template row's layouts: later edits to the template do not change existing decks. _template_icon_type checks assets, then the payload, then layouts, and keeps the first value that is not the default bold (presentation.py:250).

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: The LLM never sees layout JSON. It sees one JSON Schema per layout, carried by two small models: servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py (excerpt) _build_template_layout_model (presentation.py:410) produces them: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) ordered is always False for templates (presentation.py:467), so an LLM always chooses the layout for each slide. A layout with no editable elements still gets a model, with a stub schema containing only title and description; the content call for such a slide is skipped (Step 6). The same builder runs again when a prepared deck is streamed (_get_presentation_stream_layout, presentation.py:1435), so schemas are always regenerated from the stored payload rather than cached.

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: get_template_schema (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257) returns {"source_file", "layout_count", "layouts": [{"slide", "layout_id", "schema"}]}. Each layout schema is assembled by _template_layout_schema (schema.py:585), one property per component that has at least one editable field: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py (excerpt)

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: Each component's schema comes from get_component_schema (schema.py:192). The key under which it is placed is the component id. When the same id occurs more than once in a layout, the keys become id_0, id_1, and so on (_template_component_key, schema.py:671); the hydrator computes the same keys with _template_component_content_keys (presentation.py:538) so the two stay in sync. Within a component, a second field with the same name becomes name_2, then name_3 (_component_add_schema_property, schema.py:877).

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: _component_schema_nodes_for_element (schema.py:762) walks the element tree: An element whose type is in CONTENT_TYPES (text, image, text-list, table, chart, infographic), whose decorative is exactly False, and which has a non-empty name, becomes a leaf field. A container passes through to its child. If the container itself has no name, the child's fields are lifted to the parent level. A flex, grid or group with a name becomes either an array (if its children repeat, Step 5.4) or a nested object. Without a name, its children's fields are lifted. Everything else (vector, decorative elements, unnamed leaves) contributes nothing.

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: _component_content_field_schema (schema.py:1200) maps each leaf type: Element Field schema Constraint source text {"type": "string", "minLength", "maxLength"} min_length, max_length image, is_icon: false {"type": "object", "properties": {"image_prompt": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["image_prompt"]} none image, is_icon: true same with icon_query none text-list {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "minLength", "maxLength"}, "minItems", "maxItems"} min_items, max_items, min_item_length, max_item_length table {"columns": [string...], "rows": [[string...]...]} object min/max_columns, min/max_rows, plus computed text limits chart {"chart_type", "title"?, "categories", "series"} object fixed caps (below) infographic {"data": {...}} object, per infographic type per type (below) Every leaf also gets a human title (main_visual_image becomes Main Visual Image), x-element-type and x-element-path, and image fields get a description ("Prompt for the replacement image."). Those annotations are then removed for the layout schema: _strip_component_schema_metadata deletes every $schema, title, description, x-element-type and x-element-path keyword while preserving property names (COMPONENT_SCHEMA_METADATA_KEYS, schema.py:40, and schema.py:647). Table text limits. Table cells have no stored character limits, so _table_text_limits (schema.py:57) estimates them from geometry: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py (excerpt) With TABLE_CELL_HORIZONTAL_PADDING = 12, TABLE_CELL_VERTICAL_PADDING = 6, a glyph width of 0.58 x font size (0.62 when bold) plus letter spacing, a line height of 1.2 x size unless the font says otherwise, and a 14 px default font (schema.py:47 to :50, :128). The maximum is floor(chars_per_line x lines x 0.85), but never less than the longest existing cell; the minimum is 1 if every existing cell has text, otherwise 0 (schema.py:106). Chart fields. _chart_content_schema (schema.py:1490) always requires chart_type (enum of 12 values: area, bar, bubble, donut, horizontal_bar, horizontal_stacked_bar, line, pie, polar_area, radar, scatter, stacked_bar), categories (at most 24 strings) and series (at most 12 objects {name, values} with at most 24 numbers). title is included only if the layout's chart already has a non-empty title. Infographic fields. _infographic_content_schema (schema.py:1448) produces {"data": {"type": {"const": "<type>"}, ...}}.

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: When the children of a named flex, grid or group expose identical editable fields, the region becomes a JSON array (_component_repeated_children_schema_result, schema.py:898). The algorithm: Compute the field nodes of every child. If any child has no editable fields, the region is not repeated. With fewer than two children, repeat only if max_children is larger than the child count (_can_expand_repeated_children, schema.py:561). This is how a grid with one sample child can become an array of up to eight. Try three name-normalization strategies in order: numeric strips an index token such as _1 from names (card_1_heading and card_2_heading both become card_heading), none compares names as they are, and prefix strips the first underscore-separated token. The first strategy under which every child's item schema is identical wins. If none matches but every child is a single wrapper with matching root names, flatten the wrappers to their leaf fields and try again. The comment at schema.py:935 explains why: a leading divider can add an extra wrapper around every item after the first. Bound the array. For flex and grid, minItems/maxItems are the element's min_children/max_children. For a group, they are item_count // 2 and item_count (_component_repeated_item_limits, schema.py:1038). A component whose top-level elements are all groups that repeat is collapsed into a single array field, named after the first group with its index token removed (_component_repeated_top_level_group_node, schema.py:822). The Civic layout side_badges_with_comparison_rows_6038, for example, has two category_badge groups and produces: Gotcha: n // 2 for groups, (n + 1) // 2 elsewhere Groups use floor division for their minimum (item_count // 2), so three repeated groups allow a single item. Certification sets min_children for flex and grid to max(1, (n + 1) // 2). The two rules differ by one for odd counts; do not assume they are interchangeable when you hand-edit limits.

docs.t: 9.2 Matching an element to its value
docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: _apply_template_content_to_element (presentation.py:626) looks up the element's name in the current content object. _template_content_name_candidates (presentation.py:743) tries three keys in order: the name itself, the name with a _<digits> token removed (metric_2_value becomes metric_value), and that result with its first underscore-separated prefix removed (metric_value becomes value). For the second and later occurrences of the same name in one scope, it first tries name_2, name_3 and so on, mirroring the schema builder's de-duplication (_template_repeated_content_keys_for_name, presentation.py:851). A value is applied only if the element has decorative: False, a name, a found value, and a type in GENERATED_VALUE_ELEMENT_TYPES (text, math, image, text-list, table, chart, infographic; presentation.py:503). Otherwise the element is copied as is, and containers, flex, grid and group elements recurse into their children with the nested content object. When an array item is applied to a repeated child (direct_value=True) and the item is not wrapped in the child's name, the item itself is the value. The comment at presentation.py:674 gives the example: three repeated image children are emitted as [{"image_prompt": ..., "image_url": ...}, ...], not as [{"gallery_photo": {...}}, ...].

docs.x: For a flex, grid or group whose value is a list, _apply_template_content_to_children builds one child per item (presentation.py:758). The template child used for item i comes from repeated_child_source_index: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py (excerpt) More items than template children: extra items reuse the last child. _repeated_child_for_index deep-copies it, removes __presenton_manual_position, and renumbers index tokens in every nested name to the new position (_normalize_repeated_names, presentation.py:813, which rewrites _\d+ to _<index+1>). Fewer items, flex or grid: the first n children are used and the flow engine re-spaces them. Fewer items, group or top-level groups: center_when_reduced is true, so the middle n children are used. Their absolute positions are kept, which centers the remaining items within the original spread. Running the real hydrator on the Momentum layout center_title_agenda_grid_wave_7815, whose grid (min_children: 1, max_children: 8, columns: 4) holds a single sample child, with three agenda items produces three copies of that child: Gotcha: expansion copies geometry verbatim A copied child keeps the source child's position and size. Inside flex and grid that is harmless because the flow engine places children. Inside a free-form group, a copy beyond the template count lands exactly on top of the last child. The schema prevents this for groups by capping maxItems at the number of template groups, but if you raise max_children on a hand-edited group, expect overlapping items.

docs.p: From template to schema to slide
docs.x: TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx:218) always renders the slide at its native 1280 x 720 and scales it with a CSS transform. A ResizeObserver tracks the container width, and the natural scale is: TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx (excerpt) so previews never upscale beyond 100% and leave a 2% margin. With fitBounds, the component instead zooms to a sub-rectangle of the slide, with default padding of 8% horizontally and 10% vertically (:376). The slide is hidden (opacity: 0) until a scale is known, which avoids a flash at the wrong size. The markup is injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML and pointer-events: none.

docs.x: Despite their names, the "V1" components are part of the current Template v2 stack. V1ContentRender (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/V1ContentRender.tsx:159) is the slide body used by the presentation page. It renders TemplateV2KonvaSlide, the Konva editor surface, for every slide, using the slide's ui or, for blank slides, BLANK_TEMPLATE_V2_LAYOUT. It wraps the surface in an error boundary and, in edit mode, can overlay TemplateV2PromptOverlay, a prompt box that previews the layout through TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview at a scale of 0.085 and dispatches a PRESENTON_BLANK_SLIDE_PROMPT_EVENT window event when submitted. The API call and the state update are commented out (V1SelectEdit.tsx:569), and no file imports the component. It is dead code from the HTML-template era. v1 decks are rejected outright. When a presentation's version is v1-standard, usePresentationData shows "Unsupported presentation" and redirects to the dashboard (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:33). New decks are created with version=V2_STANDARD (presentation.py:2944). Gotcha: two renderers must agree The Konva editor and the HTML preview are separate implementations of the same format. They share the flow engine (flowLayout.ts) and the text-run normalization, but everything else (vector rounding, table cells, infographic drawings) is written twice. Tests such as template-v2-json-to-html-metadata.test.mjs ("allocates unsized flex children like the Konva renderer") and template-v2-renderer-fields.test.mjs pin the two together. When you add an element property, implement it in both renderers and in both exporters (PPTX and PDF export).

This chapter follows a user's .pptx file from the upload dropzone to a persisted, certified TemplateV2 row. You will see the font check and font replacement pass, how slide preview images are rendered, the four vision passes that turn raw PPTX elements into editable layouts (and every fallback when a pass fails), how reusable components are clustered and a semantic theme is derived, and every route in the template API. The chapter ends with the template studio and editor in Next.js and the two Node scripts that turn a stored template into a bundled templates/<id>/template.json.

docs.t: Step 1: The two creation workflows and the API surface
docs.x: Everything lives under TEMPLATE_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/template", tags=["Templates"]) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:96), mounted inside API_V1_PPT_ROUTER (prefix /api/v1/ppt, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22, include at :39). The font routes are a separate router, FONTS_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/fonts") (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py:18), included at servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:25. There are two ways to turn preview images plus a PPTX into a template: One-shot asynchronous creation. POST /template/async stores an async_task row and runs _run_create_template_task as a FastAPI background task. It certifies every slide in parallel, clusters components, derives a theme and inserts one TemplateV2 row at the end. The template studio's Generate Template button uses this route, and so does the MCP tool flow. Incremental creation. POST /template/init stores a row with raw_layouts and no layouts. The client then calls POST /template/layouts/create per slide, saves each result with PATCH /template/{id}/layouts, and finally calls POST /template/generate-blocks to cluster components and derive a theme. This is wired into the useTemplateCreation hook and is also what the template editor uses to "reconstruct" a single slide. docs.t: Step 3: Check the fonts in the PPTX
docs.x: checkFonts in useTemplateCreation.ts:135 posts the file as pptx_file to POST /api/v1/ppt/fonts/check. The route is registered without a decorator, as a call on the router: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py (excerpt) check_fonts_in_pptx_handler (servers/fastapi/templates/fonts_and_slides_preview.py:1160) does the following, in order: Rejects anything not ending in .pptx with 400 "Invalid file type. Expected PPTX file". Rejects uploads of 100 MB or more with 413 (MAX_FONT_CHECK_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024, :150; the check is size >= MAX, :1040). Writes the bytes to a temporary presentation.pptx and validates the ZIP package (_validate_pptx_package, :1045): testzip() must pass, and [Content_Types].xml, ppt/presentation.xml and at least one ppt/slides/slide*.xml must exist, otherwise 400 "The uploaded PowerPoint file is corrupted or unsupported.". Extracts every font family and the variants actually used (extract_used_font_variants_from_pptx, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py:366). Variants are one of regular, bold, italic, bold_italic, derived by _font_style_variant (pptx_font_utils.py:330) from the b and i attributes on run properties plus the family name itself. Theme references such as +mj-lt are resolved to the theme's major/minor fonts (_resolve_theme_typeface, :193). Calls get_available_and_unavailable_fonts_for_pptx (pptx_font_utils.py:813). For every family/variant it first looks for a matching embedded font (ppt/fonts/*.fntdata), then the packaged catalog through get_static_font_url (:177). Anything left is unavailable. For unavailable fonts, looks in the global font_uploads table (get_font_uploads_for_names_by_variant, servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py:406). A previously uploaded file whose variant matches moves the entry into available_fonts with its /app_data/fonts/... URL. A response looks like this (one entry per family and variant; name is the display name built by _font_info_entry, fonts_and_slides_preview.py:874): Gotcha Embedded fonts are reported as available with a fake URL. docs.x: If any font is missing, the studio shows a picker per missing font. The user can upload a font file or pick a fallback from the local catalog LOCAL_FONT_OPTIONS (CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1199); a default fallback is pre-selected by preferredFallbackFont (:208), which tries the font's family_name and original_name against the catalog and otherwise takes the first catalog entry. When every font is covered, fontUploadAndPreview (useTemplateCreation.ts:259) posts multipart form data to POST /api/v1/ppt/template/fonts-upload-and-slides-preview: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/hooks/useTemplateCreation.ts (excerpt) Gotcha The google_font_* form fields no longer carry Google Fonts. The values the studio sends are local catalog fonts (fontUrl: selectedFont.sourceUrl, a /vendor/fonts/... path, CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1267). The field names are kept for API compatibility. The route forwards to upload_fonts_and_preview_handler (fonts_and_slides_preview.py:1304, via the thin wrapper in servers/fastapi/templates/preview.py). Its steps: Validate the pairs. font_files and original_font_names must both be present and equal in length (400 otherwise). _selected_google_font_maps (:76) applies the same rule to the replacement names and URLs and returns selected_fonts {replacement_name: url} plus replacements {original_name: replacement_name}. The cap is MAX_TEMPLATE_PREVIEW_SLIDES = 50 (:149; _resolve_template_preview_slide_cap, :1069). Save uploaded font files with the 10 MB limit (read_upload_with_size_limit,

docs.t: How previews are rendered (and who converts PPTX to JSON)
docs.x: Python does not parse slide geometry. Both the conversion and the rendering are tasks for the Node export runtime, a runner.mjs resolved from EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT or a sibling presentation-export directory (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:129 to :151) and spawned as a child process with LITEPARSE_NODE_BINARY (default node, :124). The runtime is synced into the image at build time (both Dockerfile and Dockerfile.dev run node scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --force); its internals are covered in PPTX and PDF export. render_pptx_slides_to_images makes two runtime calls: servers/fastapi/templates/fonts_and_slides_preview.py (excerpt) convert_pptx_to_json (export_task_service.py:687) sends {"type": "pptx-to-json", "pptx_path": ...} and returns PptxToJsonDocument {layouts: list[dict]} (:101). render_jsons_to_images (:580) sends {"type": "json-to-images", "jsons": [...], "width", "height", "fonts"} and expects exactly one PNG path per slide; a count mismatch is a 500 (fonts_and_slides_preview.py:836). The preview width is always 1280 and the height follows the PPTX aspect ratio (_preview_dimensions_from_document, :165): the code comment explains that the export runtime normalizes PPTX-to-JSON coordinates to a 1280px-wide canvas, so a 1707x960 deck is captured at 1280x720. The previews are therefore a rendering of the parsed JSON, not of PowerPoint itself. That is intentional: the vision passes later compare the JSON against these pixels, so both views agree on fonts and geometry. Each preview is copied to <session_dir>/slide_<n>.png (create_slide_previews, :1741). The response: The exact host prefix depends on absolute_fastapi_asset_url; the modified PPTX filename comes from _build_modified_pptx_filename (:1033). Note _build_slide_preview_html (:692) builds a full HTML document with Tailwind, Chart.js and the datalabels plugin. It is still covered by unit tests (servers/fastapi/tests/test_pptx_font_utils.py:719) but no production code path calls it anymore; previews come from the JSON renderer only.

MCP clients cannot send multipart bodies, so POST /template/mcp-upload (template.py:1220) accepts base64. Each file is decoded with base64.b64decode(..., validate=True) (_decode_mcp_upload, :211); the PPTX may be up to 100 MiB, each font up to 10 MiB, and the combined decoded size is capped at MCP_TEMPLATE_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024 (:102), with a pre-check on the encoded length in McpTemplateUploadRequest.validate_combined_upload_size (:181). The decoded bytes are wrapped in UploadFile objects and passed to the same upload_fonts_and_slides_preview_handler. MCP tooling in general is covered in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

From the preview step, the Generate Template button opens a name/description modal and then calls handleCreateTemplate (CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1446): servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/CustomTemplatePage.tsx (excerpt) TemplateService.createTemplate (app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/template.ts:205) posts that body to /api/v1/ppt/template/async. The request model is: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py (excerpt) LayoutGenerationOptions (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py:34) is extra="forbid", strict=True with three booleans, all default true: text_growth, visual_replacement, flexible_grouping. The semantic pass always runs. create_template (template.py:1574) then: Resolves pptx_url to a file with resolve_app_path_to_filesystem. A URL that is not a file inside Presenton's own app-data (for example a host application's attachment id) is rejected with 400 before any task is stored (:1581). Pre-allocates template_id = str(uuid.uuid4()). The template row does not exist yet; the id is reserved in the task data so retries reuse it. Inserts an AsyncTaskModel with type="template.create", status=PENDING, message="Queued for template creation", and payload equal to the request (with generation_options included only if the caller sent it, _explicit_template_generation_options, :558). Sets task.data with _template_task_progress_data (:396). Schedules _run_create_template_task(task.id, get_current_owner_id()) on BackgroundTasks and returns the task. The progress object stored in task.data and returned by the async-task API has this exact shape: thumbnail is the first non-empty slide image URL (_template_request_thumbnail, :444); name falls back to the PPTX filename without extension via _derive_template_name (:455), and finally to "Untitled template". Gotcha The background task runs in the same process as the API, through Starlette's BackgroundTasks. There is no queue or worker: if the process restarts mid-creation, the task stays pending forever and the template row is never written. Recovery is the retry route, which only accepts tasks in ERROR state (Step 9). The async-task table itself is described in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.t: Step 6: Prepare the template source in the background
docs.x: _run_create_template_task (template.py:1482) restores the owner context (set_current_owner_id(owner_id), set_current_owner_is_admin(False); see Auth and multi-user), opens its own session from async_session_maker, re-validates task.payload as a CreateTemplateRequest, sets message="Creating template" and then "Generating slide layouts", and calls _create_template_with_task_progress (:1403). That function begins with _prepare_template_source (:925), shared with init: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py (excerpt) The PPTX is converted a second time (the preview step's JSON is not reused). The result validates into RawSlideLayouts, a list of RawSlideLayout {id, description, elements} (layouts.py:44); the element models are the Template v2 element union described in Template v2 format. Extra slides beyond the preview count are dropped silently, because the preview step may have trimmed the deck to 50 slides; extra preview images are an error. The function returns (pptx_path, raw_layouts, raw_layouts_json, fonts) where fonts is the request's font map cleaned by _coerce_font_map (:863, keeps only non-empty string keys and values). A first progress commit with zero completed layouts follows (_commit_template_task_progress, :664).

docs.t: Step 7: Certify every slide (four vision passes)
docs.x: _generate_slide_layouts_with_task_progress (template.py:709) is the async driver. It requires one image per raw slide, creates a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(MAX_PARALLEL_SLIDE_LAYOUTS, slide_count)) with MAX_PARALLEL_SLIDE_LAYOUTS = 10 (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:47), and submits one generate_slide_layout per slide with max_tokens=SLIDE_LAYOUT_GENERATION_MAX_TOKENS. Each submission runs inside copy_context().run so context variables such as the current owner survive the thread hop. As each future completes (asyncio.as_completed), the slide index is added to completed_layout_indices and progress is committed immediately, which is how the UI can show per-slide ticks. If any slide raises, the remaining tasks are cancelled and the error propagates. templates.v2.generation.generate_slide_layout (generation.py:612) is a thin public wrapper over certified_generation.generate_slide_layout (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py:3651). That is the core of the chapter. Every pass uses the same machinery, _generate_structured_with_provider_fallback (certified_generation.py:4305): a system prompt, a user message containing the slide image (as raw bytes when the URL resolves to a local file, _openai_image_part, :4194) and a JSON payload, a JSON Schema response format with strict=False, Pydantic validation of the parsed JSON, and an extra_validator that checks semantic rules against the source. On any exception it appends the bad response and a repair prompt and tries again: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt) With DEFAULT_VALIDATION_RETRIES = 5 (:59) that is five attempts in total per pass, not five retries after a first try. _template_structured_providers (:4204) returns a single provider built from the configured client and model (get_client(config=get_llm_config()), get_model()), resolved through the public generation module so tests and integrations can monkeypatch it. Gemini models get a special visual-data schema and an extra table-encoding instruction (_response_schema_for_model, :4257; _messages_for_structured_provider, :4271).

Only when options.visual_replacement is true. _visual_data_generation_payload (:1076) sends the source layout id/description, every top-level element with its source_index (with decorative stripped), and visual_region_candidates: every container, group or non-icon image element at least 24x12 px, found recursively through child and children (_visual_data_region_candidates_in_element, :1105). Each candidate carries a path such as elements.3.children.1, its bounds, and a content preview. The model returns a VisualDataReplacementPlan (layouts.py:497): a list of replacements discriminated by kind (chart, infographic, table, text-list; layouts.py:173, :390, :432, :449). Each names a primary path, the extra top-level consumed_paths it absorbs, typed data, and (except for text lists) new bounds. The intent, per DETECT_VISUAL_DATA_REGIONS_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:180), is to turn a chart that the PPTX stored as a picture or as a pile of shapes into a real editable chart element. _apply_visual_data_replacement_plan (:1291) swaps the elements in. If the pass fails for any reason the exception is logged and the source regions are kept.

docs.t: Pass 2: semantic manifest (the only mandatory pass)
docs.x: _semantic_generation_payload (:1555) sends: Candidates are all text, image, text-list, table, chart and supported infographic elements at any depth (_SEMANTIC_ELEMENT_TYPES, :1054). The system prompt GENERATE_SLIDE_LAYOUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:111) is long and opinionated. Its key rules: partition the elements into the smallest useful reusable components; keep a repeated collection (cards, steps, metrics) together in one component; mark replaceable content decorative=false and scaffolding (backgrounds, logos, frames, connectors, rings) decorative=true; name fields in generic snake_case from structure, never from sample content; set is_icon, an icon color and an icon_type (bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin) on every image annotation. The reply is a SemanticSlideManifest (layouts.py:575): id (snake_case, at most 80 chars), description (10 to 300 chars), components with element_indices, and one annotation per candidate path. _validate_semantic_manifest (:1640) enforces, among other things: every source index is assigned to exactly one component, in ascending order within each component; repeated_items must be null in this pass; annotation paths equal the candidate paths exactly (it reports missing= and extra= lists in the error so the repair prompt can fix them); only image annotations may carry is_icon; icon annotations must carry color and icon_type; charts, infographics, tables and text lists can never be decorative. If this pass fails after five attempts, the slide does not fail. generate_slide_layout logs "semantic pass failed; using fidelity-preserving fallback" and returns _fallback_slide_layout (:3874). _fallback_semantic_manifest (:3593) puts every element into one component called slide_content, makes all text, charts, tables, lists and infographics editable, keeps images' existing decorative flag, and derives safe identifiers from the element names.

Only when options.flexible_grouping is true. The payload is the manifest plus indexed elements (_flexible_generation_payload, :1729). The model returns a FlexibleSlidePlan (layouts.py:696, whose regions are FlexibleRegionPlan objects, layouts.py:663): at most one region per component, each a tree of flow nodes with mode row, column, grid or group and at least two items, each item either a list of source indices (a leaf) or a nested flow_id. _validate_flexible_plan (:2512) checks geometry: repeated items must be structurally equivalent (_region_items_are_structurally_equivalent, :2649), must not overlap, and regular repeats must have regular spacing (_validate_regular_repeat_geometry, :2814). Failure leaves FlexibleSlidePlan(regions=[]). When compiled (_compile_flow_node, :3088), a flow becomes a flex, grid or group element. A repeatable flow gets elastic limits, which is what lets generation produce three cards from a four-card source: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt) So a repeated region with 4 source items accepts 2 to 4 items, and one with 5 accepts 3 to 5. How the schema builder exposes these limits to the content LLM is covered in From template to schema to slide.

Only when options.text_growth is true. The payload adds editable_text_boxes (the non-decorative text elements with their paths, _text_capacity_generation_payload, :1746). The model returns TextCapacityAdjustment items (layouts.py:716) per path: left_characters and right_characters (0 to 200), top_lines and bottom_lines (0 to 12), and a horizontal and vertical alignment. It never returns pixels; the compiler converts characters and lines into geometry and refuses growth that would collide with other content. Independently of the LLM, every editable text box gets geometry-derived length limits (_normalize_existing_text_box_limits, :2391). The estimate is deliberately crude: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt) Capacity units are floor(width / char_width) * line_count, where a character is 0.58 x font_size wide (0.62 when bold) plus letter spacing (_estimated_text_character_width, :2449), the font size defaults to 18 and the line height to 1.2 x font_size (_text_capacity_geometry, :2483), and the line count is capped at 12. The safety factor is TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR = 0.85 (:62). max_length is only ever raised, never lowered, and never set below the length of the sample text.

The four plans are fed to _compile_semantic_layout (:2895) with a fallback ladder: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt) Duplicate combinations are skipped by a JSON signature. The compiler deep-copies the source elements, writes each annotation's name, decorative, is_icon, color and icon_type onto the element at its path, marks unsupported infographics decorative, applies text limits and growth, and then builds components. Two details matter when you modify it: Component positions are the bounding box of their elements on the 1280x720 canvas, and element positions are rewritten to be local to that box (_localize_top_level_element, :3050). Components are sorted by their lowest source index, not by the model's order. The code comment explains why: the model may return components in reading order, which could lift a full-slide background above the title and hide it. _certify_compiled_layout (:3491) then rejects the result if any component is empty, any number is non-finite, any size is not positive, any min_* exceeds its max_* (_SCHEMA_LIMIT_PAIRS, :1066), a table row length differs from its column count, a chart series length differs from its categories, a flex/grid child count falls outside min_children..max_children, a grid's columns x rows cannot hold its children, or a component has editable elements but get_component_schema returns no schema. If all four attempts fail, the fidelity-preserving fallback is compiled instead.

docs.t: Placeholders for editable images and icons
docs.x: The last step on every path is _replace_content_image_urls (:3886), which walks every element with _replace_content_image_url_in_element (:3902): servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt) Editable photos become /static/images/replaceable_template_image.png with fit: cover; editable icons become /static/icons/placeholder.svg. Decorative images keep their original /app_data/... URL. With visual_replacement=false, editable images are instead frozen as decorative. Gotcha generate_slide_layout never raises for LLM quality problems: semantic failure and compile failure both fall back to a one-component "preserve everything" layout. A template full of slide_content components with generic field names is the visible symptom of a weak or non-vision model. Check the logs for semantic pass failed before debugging the renderer. After all slides finish, _ensure_unique_async_slide_layout_ids (template.py:686) suffixes duplicate ids with _<n>, and _with_randomized_layout_ids (:833) appends a random _1000 to _9999 suffix to every layout id, so a certified title_with_image_cards becomes, for example, title_with_image_cards_4821.

docs.t: Step 8: Cluster components and derive the theme, then persist
docs.x: Two jobs run concurrently with asyncio.gather (template.py:1447), each in its own single-thread executor (_run_template_generation_thread, :809).

merge_similar_components (certified_generation.py:550) flattens every component of every layout into one indexed list and sends compact summaries (_component_clustering_summary, :600: id, description, position, content bounds, the flattened element type hierarchy, and the editable JSON schema) to the LLM with CLUSTER_SIMILAR_COMPONENTS_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:445). The reply is a SimilarComponentsList of index groups; _validate_similarity_groups (:623) rejects out-of-range or repeated indices. _build_merged_components (:642) turns each group into a MergedComponent {id, description, variants} (layouts.py:81), and every component not in a group becomes its own singleton. A deterministic pass then runs: _deduplicate_merged_components (:670) computes a structural signature for every variant (_component_duplicate_signature, :740) and unions groups that share a signature. The signature ignores names and min/max limits (_IGNORED_DUPLICATE_SCHEMA_KEYS, :79), ignores replaceable content values (text runs, list items, image data, chart data; _CONTENT_VALUE_KEYS_BY_ELEMENT_TYPE, :94), and snaps positions and sizes to a grid relative to the component size (_DUPLICATE_POSITION_GRID_UNITS = 5, :78). If clustering raises a ValidationError or ValueError, _merge_generated_components (template.py:626) stores an empty MergedComponents(components=[]) and creation continues. Merged components feed the editor's insert palette and the prompted-layout generator (Step 10).

generate_template_theme (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py:246) profiles every color and font in the certified layouts (build_theme_profile, :145), asks the LLM to assign roles by profile id (select_theme_roles_with_llm, :261, 2 retries, 2,000 max tokens), falls back to select_theme_roles_deterministically (:305) on any error, and materializes a PresentationThemeData (materialize_theme, :357). If even that raises, _generate_generated_theme (template.py:649) stores theme=None. The profile, the role rules and the contrast repair are explained in Themes and fonts.

_build_created_template (template.py:1320) assembles the TemplateV2 row with the pre-allocated id: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py (excerpt) icon_type is the most common icon_type across all certified icon images (_most_common_icon_type_in_layouts, :520), falling back to the request's icon_type. assets.images lists every distinct image.data URL found in the raw layouts. raw_layouts is kept so a single slide can be re-certified later without re-uploading the PPTX. The column layout of template_v2 is described in Template v2 format. On success the task becomes COMPLETED with message="Template creation completed". On any exception it becomes ERROR with message="Template creation failed" and error set to an APIErrorModel dump; non-HTTP exceptions are reduced to a generic 500 "Template creation failed" so internal messages do not leak.

The template library polls. useTemplateSummaries({ includeProcessingTemplateTasks: true }) (app/(presentation-generator)/hooks/useTemplateSummaries.ts) loads default and custom templates with two GET /template/all?page_size=100&default=... calls, plus GET /api/v1/async-tasks?type=template.create&order_by=created_at&order=desc&limit=50&offset=0&created_at=<one hour ago> (services/api/template.ts:219). It keeps tasks whose status is pending or error and re-polls every 30 seconds (setInterval(..., 30000)), refreshing the template list whenever a pending task was seen. The panel ((dashboard)/templates/components/TemplatePanel.tsx:69) offers a retry button whose handler calls the hook's retryTemplateTask, which in turn calls TemplateService.retryTemplateCreateTask (useTemplateSummaries.ts:194). retry_create_template (template.py:1626) only accepts a task that exists (404), has type template.create (400), is in ERROR (409), still has a dict payload (409), and whose reserved template_v2_id does not already exist as a row (409 "Template has already been created"). It resets the same task to PENDING, increments attempt, and schedules the same background function. The whole PPTX is processed again from scratch. Gotcha GET /template/all filters out any template whose layouts is empty (if layout_count == 0: continue, template.py:1164), and paginates in Python after loading every row. A row created by init stays invisible in the library until at least one layout is patched in. The frontend applies the same rule again in filterTemplatesWithLayouts.

These routes exist for the per-slide flow, for the editor, and for API users who want control. POST /template/init (template.py:1277) runs _prepare_template_source and immediately inserts a row with layouts=None and assets {pptx_url, icon_type, icon_weight, fonts, slide_image_urls, images, layout_indexes: []}. It returns the id as a JSON string. POST /template/layouts/create (:1789) accepts index or indices (never both; at most MAX_PARALLEL_SLIDE_LAYOUTS = 10, unique, non-negative; CreateTemplateLayoutsRequest._validate_indices, :241). It loads raw_layouts, checks each index is in range and has a stored slide image, merges saved and override generation options (_template_generation_options, :564), and runs _generate_indexed_slide_layouts (:1071) in a thread. It returns {layouts: [{index, layout}]} but does not save anything. PATCH /template/{id}/layouts (:1929) saves. It serializes concurrent patches to the same template with a per-template asyncio.Lock (_get_template_layout_patch_lock, :916) so out-of-order saves from parallel slide generations cannot overwrite each other. _merge_template_layout_items (:1031) keys existing layouts by their original slide index (stored in assets.layout_indexes), inserts or replaces the patched ones, sorts by index, and re-validates SlideLayouts. Duplicate layout ids are rejected by the SlideLayouts validator (test test_patch_template_slide_layout_rejects_duplicate_layout_ids, test_template_api.py:1633). POST /template/generate-blocks (:1874) runs the Step 8 clustering and theme jobs on the saved layouts and stores merged_components and, if non-null, theme. POST /template/layouts/generate (:1700) creates a brand-new layout from a text prompt. generate_prompted_slide_layout (generation.py:631) ranks existing layouts and merged components by how many prompt words (longer than two characters) appear in their ids and descriptions, sends at most 4 reference layouts and 8 reusable components (PROMPTED_LAYOUT_MAX_REFERENCE_LAYOUTS, PROMPTED_LAYOUT_MAX_REUSABLE_COMPONENTS, :114), trims the context to 160,000 characters, and asks for one SlideLayout under GENERATE_PROMPTED_TEMPLATE_LAYOUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:88). The extra validator requires a snake_case id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,79}$ that is not already used, at least one component, and at least one decorative=false element. Images marked editable get the standard placeholders. The

After creation, the library links to /template-preview?templateV2Id=<id> (TemplatePanel.tsx:59). TemplatePreviewClient.tsx loads the template with GET /template/{id} (TemplateService.getTemplateDetails, services/api/template.ts:142, which strips an optional template-v2- prefix from the id) and the theme with GET /template/{id}/theme (TemplatePreviewClient.tsx:236). Editing is allowed only when !template.is_default (canEditTemplate, :275). What can be edited, and how it is saved: Action Where Backend call Move, resize, restyle elements on the Konva canvas handlePreviewLayoutChange (:405) none until Save Edit layout id and description handleLayoutMetadataChange (:451) none until Save Edit a schema field's sample value, its min/max constraint, or toggle decorative handleSchemaFieldChange (:493), handleSchemaConstraintChange (:512), handleSchemaDecorationChange (:529) none until Save Preview content density (fill text and repeated arrays to min or max) applyContentDensity none (preview only) Duplicate a layout duplicateActiveLayout (id suffixed -copy) none until Save Generate a new slide from a prompt TemplatePreviewClient.tsx:648 POST /template/layouts/generate Re-certify the active slide from the original PPTX reconstructActiveLayout (:783) POST /template/layouts/create Save saveTemplate (:1046) PATCH /template/{id} with the full template, edited layouts and layout_count Delete :1139 DELETE /template/{id} Before saving, the editor dispatches COMMIT_TEMPLATE_V2_INLINE_TEXT_EVENT and waits one tick so an open inline text editor flushes its pending change (:1064). buildTemplateSavePayload (template-preview/components/editor/templatePreviewUtils.ts:1179) clones the loaded template record and replaces layouts, name, id and layout_count. Every TemplateService write invalidates the 5-minute theme cache for that template (invalidateTemplateTheme). The Konva canvas and inline text editing are the same components the slide editor uses; see Slide editor. Gotcha The studio also contains a second, per-slide creation path in useTemplateCreation.ts (generateTemplateV2, :446): init, then one layouts/create call per slide (TEMPLATE_V2_LAYOUT_BATCH_SIZE = 1, awaited sequentially), a PATCH .../layouts after each, then generate-blocks. In this snapshot CustomTemplatePage destructures only retrySlide from that part of the hook, so the button path is the async route. If you wire

docs.t: Step 12: Turning a stored template into a bundled template
docs.x: Two Node scripts turn a stored template into the bundle format that the 16 built-in templates under templates/<id>/template.json use. Both are pure file transformations; neither talks to the API.

node scripts/convert-template.mjs <input.json> [--output <path>] [--app-data <dir>] converts a template JSON (for example a GET /template/{id} response saved to disk) into the bundle format: buildTargetShape (scripts/convert-template.mjs:81) keeps exactly id, name, description, thumbnail, merged_components, layouts, fonts (TOP_LEVEL_KEYS, :17). layouts and merged_components may be arrays or wrapped objects ({layouts: [...]}, {components: [...]}) and are unwrapped. id falls back to the output directory name; thumbnail falls back to the first assets.slide_image_urls entry; fonts comes from assets.fonts or fonts. replaceEditableImages (:116) rewrites every non-decorative image's data to the icon or image placeholder, exactly like Step 7. planAssets (:206) finds every string that points into app-data (/app_data/... URLs, app_data/... paths, or absolute paths under the app-data root) or into a sibling static/ folder, verifies each file exists, and plans a copy into <output dir>/static/. The thumbnail is renamed thumbnail.<ext>; name collisions get a 12-character SHA-256 suffix. Every planned path is checked with assertInside so a crafted path cannot escape the root. rewriteStrings (:257) replaces those strings with static/<name>, the files are copied, stale files in static/ are deleted (cleanStaticDirectory, :268), and the JSON is written with two-space indentation. At startup, default_templates.py rewrites static/... back to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/... and copies the folder into app-data; see From template to schema to slide.

node scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs <presentation.json> [--output] [--app-data] [--id] [--name] [--description] [--thumbnail] starts from a presentation detail response instead. This lets a designer tweak slides in the normal editor and fold those edits back into the template. buildTemplateFromPresentation (scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs:133): Reads the presentation's layout (the copied template payload), its merged_components, and its slides. Collects each slide's edited ui tree keyed by its layout id; two slides with conflicting edits of the same layout are an error. For each edited layout, finds every original component in the original merged catalog by deep equality (findVariant, :80; exactly one match required), replaces that variant with the edited component, marks removed components, and appends components that were added in the editor as new singleton groups. Verifies every final component is present in the final catalog, then hands the result to convertTemplateData for asset packaging. The scripts are covered by scripts/convert-template.test.mjs and scripts/convert-presentation-template.test.mjs. Gotcha TOP_LEVEL_KEYS in convert-template.mjs does not include theme, yet every bundled template.json in this snapshot has a theme block. Running the converter on a template drops its theme; you have to add it back by hand (or extend buildTargetShape) before committing a bundle, otherwise get_template_theme will derive a deterministic theme at first request.

Reads: servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py, servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/applyPresentationThemeDom.ts, servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/local-fonts.ts, nginx.conf · Builds on: Custom templates from PPTX · Time: ~35 min

A Presenton "theme" is a small JSON object with sixteen color roles and one text font, and a "font map" is a dictionary from family name to font file URL. This chapter specifies both, shows how a theme is derived from a template's layouts, where themes and fonts are stored on templates and presentations and which one wins, how the browser loads fonts and applies the theme, and where fonts live on disk and on the wire. It also explains the one surprising fact that governs everything else: template slides carry literal colors and font families, so the theme mostly affects newly inserted content, not existing slides.

The backend contract is four Pydantic models in servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py: servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py (excerpt) Role Meaning (from THEME_ROLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py:131) CSS variable set by the frontend background a large, frequently repeated surface color --background-color primary the dominant branded or accent color, not a neutral background --primary-color card a secondary surface --card-color stroke a subtle structural or border color --stroke background_text text color that contrasts with background --background-text primary_text text color that contrasts with primary --primary-text graph_0 to graph_9 distinct chart and accent colors, in order --graph-0 to --graph-9 fonts.textFont {name, url} the dominant readable font font-family, --heading-font-family, --body-font-family Note the camelCase textFont inside an otherwise snake_case model; the frontend reads exactly that key. Every built-in template.json carries a theme block in this shape. For example, templates/momentum/template.json has primary: "#213EBB", background: "#F6F7FC", primary_text: "#FFFFFF", background_text: "#000000" and textFont: {"name": "Lato", "url": "static/Lato Regular.ttf"}. The TypeScript mirror is TemplateTheme in servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts: a flat record of the same sixteen keys (TEMPLATE_THEME_COLOR_KEYS, lib/template-theme.ts:1) plus an optional fonts.textFont. The frontend flattens colors into the top level.
