docs.t: How a presentation gets its fonts and theme
docs.x: When a presentation is created from a template, the backend copies the template's font map, never a mutable reference: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt) _coerce_presentation_font_map (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:322) keeps only non-empty string names and URLs and returns None for an empty map. The UI flow sets presentation.fonts = template_fonts in prepare_presentation (presentation.py:1919); blank presentations get them at creation (:1810); the API generate_presentation_handler sets both fonts=template_fonts and theme=template_theme (:2957 to :2958). The API path's theme is not the raw template theme but a wrapper built by template_theme_for_presentation (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py:405): servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py (excerpt) During streaming, the backend also emits the font map as an SSE event {"type": "fonts", "fonts": {...}} (presentation.py:1953, :2037), which usePresentationStreaming.ts:407 merges into the Redux presentation. See Streaming (SSE). Gotcha There is no API that changes a presentation's theme. PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update (presentation.py:2527) accepts only id, n_slides, title and slides; a theme key in the body is ignored. servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_presentation_template_theme_updates.py pins this: updates with {"theme": None} or a new theme leave the stored theme unchanged. The chat assistant reads the theme (get_template_theme in servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1265, documented as "without offering theme customization") but cannot write it.

docs.t: Step 3: Deriving a theme from layouts
docs.x: When a custom template is created (see Custom templates from PPTX), or when GET /template/{id}/theme finds no valid stored theme, the backend derives one in three stages.

build_theme_profile(layouts, available_fonts) (theme.py:145) walks every element of every layout with _collect_element_profile (:431) and records per-color statistics in _ColorStats (:91): Source in the element JSON Counted as fill fill (with normalized area = width x height / (1280 x 720), clamped to 1) stroke stroke color (icon tint) fill font.color, and font.color inside runs, items, columns, rows text table cell color fills inside columns and rows fill colors[] infographic for infographic elements, else chart title_color, legend_color, text_color text axis_color, grid_color stroke Every text color is also paired with the nearest enclosing fill (the "effective background"); text with no enclosing fill is paired with the slide's largest fill. Fonts are counted by family (case-insensitive) with an average size (_record_font, :590). Colors are then clustered: sorted by an importance score, and any color within RGB Euclidean distance 8 of an existing cluster is merged into it (NEAR_COLOR_DISTANCE = 8.0, :30; _cluster_colors, :638). The importance score is: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py (excerpt) The profile keeps at most 14 colors (ids c0..c13), 8 foreground/background pairs with their WCAG contrast ratio, and 5 fonts (ids f0..f4) (MAX_PROFILE_COLORS, MAX_PROFILE_PAIRS, MAX_PROFILE_FONTS, :27 to :29). Fonts that appear in the template's font map but not in the layouts are added with a usage count of zero, and each profile font carries its URL from the map when one exists (_build_profile_fonts, :604). If the layouts contain no colors at all, the profile is seeded with #FFFFFF, #111111, #2563EB and #E5E7EB.

generate_template_theme (:246) first asks the LLM. select_theme_roles_with_llm (:261) sends the profile with font URLs removed, compact JSON, and requires a ThemeRoleSelection (:77) whose values are profile ids only. Its validator rejects unknown ids; it uses 2 validation retries and 2,000 max tokens. On any exception it falls back to select_theme_roles_deterministically (:305): background: max by (fill_area, slide_count, fill_count, -saturation). primary: among the rest, max by (chart_count + infographic_count, saturation, fill_count, slide_count). card: max by (fill_area, fill_count, -saturation). stroke: max by (stroke_count, fill_count). graph_colors: the rest sorted by chart usage, then saturation, first 10. background_text and primary_text: _best_text_candidate (:664), the most-used text color with contrast at least 4.5 against the surface. text_font: the most-used profile font. _derive_template_theme in the template endpoint (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:882) skips the LLM entirely and always uses the deterministic selector.

materialize_theme (:357) turns ids back into hex colors and repairs them: Text colors with contrast below 4.5 are replaced by the best observed text color that passes, or else by black or white, whichever contrasts more (_repair_text_color, :680). A card within RGB distance 10 of background becomes a background variant shifted by 0.06 lightness; a stroke within 12 becomes a 0.14 variant (_surface_variant, :723). Graph colors are de-duplicated, primary is appended, and the list is padded to exactly 10 by rotating the primary hue in steps of 0.137 with lightness clamped to 0.25..0.78 (_complete_graph_colors, :698). With no font, the text font defaults to {"name": "Inter", "url": ""}. servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_template_theme.py covers clustering of near colors (:117), contrast repair and graph completion (:136), that the LLM receives only the compact profile (:163), and the fallback path (:197).

GET /api/v1/ppt/template/{template_id}/theme (template.py:2093) returns {"template_id": ..., "theme": PresentationThemeData | null}. If the stored theme is missing or fails validation, it derives one deterministically and writes it back to the row before responding (:2112 to :2117). A GET with a side effect is unusual; it means old templates acquire a theme the first time anyone opens them. On the frontend, TemplateService.getTemplateTheme (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/template.ts:153) caches results per template id for TEMPLATE_THEME_CACHE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 (:10), de-duplicates concurrent requests, caches a 404 as "no theme" (old decks can outlive their template), and does not cache other failures so they can be retried. Every write through TemplateService invalidates the cache entry. These behaviors are tested in servers/nextjs/tests/template-theme-infographics.test.mjs (:119, :176, :197).

docs.t: Step 5: Normalizing any theme payload in the browser
docs.x: The frontend receives themes in at least four shapes: the API response {template_id, theme: {colors, fonts}}, a bare {colors, fonts}, the presentation wrapper {name, data: {colors, fonts}, source, template_id}, and legacy flat {primary, background, ...}. normalizeTemplateTheme (lib/template-theme.ts) accepts all of them: servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts (excerpt) Each key must match ^#?[0-9a-f]{6}$ (six-digit hex only, no rgb(), no alpha) and is lower-cased; missing or invalid keys fall back to DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_THEME (primary: "#4a6ebd", background: "#ffffff", and so on). A text font is kept only when both name and url are non-empty. The Redux reducer setPresentationData runs every incoming theme through this function (servers/nextjs/store/slices/presentationGeneration.ts:135). There is also a pure-frontend fallback, resolveTemplateTheme (lib/template-theme.ts), used by the template editor (TemplatePreviewClient.tsx:159). If the template has no explicit theme it scans the layouts' JSON keys for hex values, classifies them by key path (font, text_color, title_color, legend_color as text; stroke, axis_color, grid_color as stroke; chart, infographic, colors as graph; everything else as fill), and picks roles with simple weights and a 4.5 contrast rule. It is a cousin of the Python deterministic selector, not a copy, so the two can disagree.

docs.t: Step 6: Which theme wins when a deck opens
docs.x: usePresentationData.fetchUserSlides (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:27) decides: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts (excerpt) resolveTemplateIdFromPresentation (lib/template-theme.ts) looks at template_id, then design_v2_id, then the first slide's layout_group, then presentation.layout, ignoring the placeholder values no, blank and template-v2. So the precedence is: the template's current theme, then the presentation's stored theme, then the built-in default. The presentation's font map is loaded separately and in full (useFontLoader(normalizedData.fonts), :67), and the theme's text font is loaded on top (:71). Finally the theme is applied to #presentation-slides-wrapper (:74). Gotcha Because the live template theme wins, editing a template's theme (with PATCH /template/{id}) restyles the theme-driven parts of every presentation made from it the next time they load (after the 5-minute client cache expires). The stored presentations.theme is only a fallback for decks whose template was deleted. If you need per-deck theme snapshots, the precedence in usePresentationData.ts:52 is the line to change. Gotcha The PDF/export renderer page does not follow the same precedence. PdfMakerPage.tsx loads presentation.fonts (:184) and applies only the stored presentation.theme (:186 to :191), wrapped in a try/catch so theme errors cannot block export. Decks created through the UI have theme = null (only the API generate path stores one), so their export page applies no theme variables at all. Whether that changes pixels depends on Step 7. The export pipeline itself is in PPTX and PDF export.

docs.t: Step 7: What applying a theme actually does
docs.x: applyPresentationThemeToElement(element, theme) (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/applyPresentationThemeDom.ts:38) normalizes the theme and sets sixteen CSS custom properties as inline styles on the given element. If there is a text font, it loads it and sets three more properties: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/applyPresentationThemeDom.ts (excerpt) It is called for the editor wrapper (usePresentationData.ts:74, and again in a useLayoutEffect in PresentationPage.tsx:506 because leaving present mode remounts the tree and loses inline styles), for present mode (PresentationMode.tsx:270), and for export (PdfMakerPage.tsx:188). clearPresentationThemeFromElement (:24) removes the same properties; the outline page clears them with its own copy of the list (outline/hooks/usePresentationGeneration.ts:66). Now the important part. The Template v2 HTML renderer writes literal styles. fontStyle in servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3491 emits color: from the element's font.color (default #111827) and font-family: from font.family when present, and the slide root sets font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:298). The renderer contains no var(--...) references at all. The Konva editor surface likewise reads colors and families from the element JSON. Consequences: An existing template slide looks the same whatever theme is applied: its colors come from its own elements. The inherited font-family on the wrapper reaches only HTML that does not set its own family. Template text elements imported from PPTX almost always carry font.family, and the slide root resets to Arial anyway. The CSS variables exist for other UI that might read them, but a search of app/, components/ and lib/ finds no var(...) reference to any of the sixteen color variables or to --heading-font-family and --body-font-family. Where the theme does matter is new content. The editor's insert palette passes resolvePresentationTheme(presentationData) (PresentationActions.tsx:2121) into createTextInsertElements and the other creators, which run applyTemplateThemeToElement (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/insert/insert-elements.ts, around :3212): Inserted element Theme roles applied text, text-list font.color = background_text, font.family = textFont.name on the element and every run table header cells:

Presenton ships its fonts. There are two catalogs that must stay in sync: Backend: servers/fastapi/templates/assets/fonts.json, a JSON array of 95 {"font_name", "font_url"} entries, for example {"font_name": "Anton", "font_url": "/vendor/fonts/display/anton/Anton-Regular.ttf"}. It is read through importlib.resources (get_static_font_catalog, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py:162), so it must be packaged into the wheel; the production Dockerfile:22 asserts at build time that the catalog is non-empty, and servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_font_catalog_packaging.py checks it loads outside the source tree. Frontend: LOCAL_FONT_OPTIONS in servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/local-fonts.ts:70, 95 entries built with font(family, category, dir, file, italicFile?) for variable fonts and staticFont(family, category, dir, files[]) for families with one file per weight. Weights are inferred from file names (fontWeightFromFileName, :58). One extra application font, Syne, is added outside the catalog (APPLICATION_FONT_OPTIONS, :174), and inter variable is aliased to Inter. The files themselves live in servers/nextjs/public/vendor/fonts/<category>/<dir>/ with categories display, handwritten, monospace, sans_serif, script, serif, slab_serif. servers/nextjs/local-font-loading-validation.test.mjs asserts exactly 95 catalog entries and 320 font files, and that runtime code under app/, components/ and lib/ never references fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com or next/font/google. next.config.mjs:18 adds one response header rule: /vendor/fonts/:path* gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, because "Sandboxed community previews load public fonts from an opaque origin". servers/nextjs/tests/font-cors.test.mjs asserts this is the only wildcard CORS rule and that it never sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials. Gotcha Built-in templates still contain Google Fonts URLs. templates/general/template.json maps "Poppins" to https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:... in both fonts and theme.fonts.textFont.url. Nothing downloads it: the frontend parser only accepts URLs ending in a font file extension (isFontAssetUrl, local-fonts.ts:391), so the stylesheet URL is discarded and the family name Poppins is matched against the local catalog instead. A custom family that is not in the catalog and only has a CSS URL will silently fall back to the browser default.

docs.t: Step 9: Loading fonts in the browser
docs.x: The public entry point is a plain function with a hook-like name: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/hooks/useFontLoad.tsx hooks/useFontLoader.tsx only re-exports it. Despite the use prefix it uses no React state and is safe to call from event handlers and non-component code, which is exactly how applyPresentationThemeToElement calls it. localFontOptionsFromUnknown (local-fonts.ts:249) is a tolerant parser that walks any value (a font map, a list of {family, url} objects, CSS text, nested structures) and produces LocalFontOption records: A family -> url pair is accepted only when the URL is a data:font/ URI or ends in .eot, .otf, .ttf, .woff or .woff2 (isFontAssetUrl, :391). If the family is in the local catalog and the URL starts with /vendor/fonts/, the full catalog option (with all its faces) is used. Otherwise a single-face option is created. Weight is read from an explicit weight field, else 100 900 for variable files whose name contains [wght], else inferred from the filename; style is italic when the family or URL contains "italic". Aliases strip trailing weight words, so Lato Bold also registers as Lato (fontFamilyAliases, :431). Bare family names, and font-family: declarations inside CSS strings, are resolved against the catalog. ensureFontOptionLoaded (:558) injects one <style data-local-font-family="..."> per family into document.head with @font-face rules from renderLocalFontFaceCss (:482), using font-display: swap and a format() hint derived from the extension. A template-provided font is allowed to replace a catalog font's style tag, but not the other way round (data-font-source is template or vendor). It then waits for 400 16px "<family>" and 700 16px "<family>" through document.fonts.load, with a 3-second timeout after which it resolves anyway (waitForFontDescriptorsLoaded, :522). Concurrent waits for the same descriptor set share one promise. The Konva editor needs fonts loaded before it measures text, so useFontLoadState (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/surface/fontLoading.ts:25) collects font descriptors from every element, run, list item and table cell of a slide, triggers ensureLocalFontsForDescriptors (skipping system families such as Arial, Helvetica, Georgia and the generic families, SYSTEM_FONT_FAMILY_KEYS, local-fonts.ts:181) and ensureTemplateFontsForDescriptors, and bumps a revision counter when they are ready so

FONTS_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py:18) is mounted at /api/v1/ppt/fonts: Method and path Purpose Response POST /fonts/upload multipart font_file; validates, stores, indexes {success, font_name, font_url, font_path, message} GET /fonts/list all uploads with metadata {success, fonts: [{id, filename, font_name, original_name, font_url, font_path, font_type, file_size, family_name, subfamily_name, full_name, postscript_name, normalized_family_name, weight_class, width_class, format}], message} GET /fonts/uploaded compact list {fonts: [{id, name, url}]} POST /fonts/check PPTX font availability (see Custom templates from PPTX) FontCheckResponse DELETE /fonts/delete/{filename} delete by stored filename or by row UUID {success, message} In the files read for this chapter, the Next.js app calls only /fonts/check; the other routes are available to API and MCP clients (they appear in servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json). persist_upload_file (servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py:346) implements the upload: safe_font_filename keeps only the basename and replaces slashes (:126). The extension must be one of .eot, .fntdata, .otf, .ttc, .ttf, .woff, .woff2 (ALLOWED_FONT_EXTENSIONS, :24), else 400. The target name is <stem>_<8 hex chars><ext>, to avoid collisions, inside <APP_DATA_DIRECTORY>/fonts/ (default /tmp/presenton/fonts, get_fonts_directory, :68). The body is read in 64 KiB chunks and rejected with 413 as soon as it passes MAX_FONT_UPLOAD_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024 (:35, read_upload_with_size_limit, :148); only then is it written to the target path. fontTools parses the name table (get_font_details); a parse error is a 400 and the written file is deleted (remove_font_file_quietly). A font_uploads row is flushed, refreshed and only then committed, so a refresh failure cannot leave a committed row without a file (_persist_built_font_upload, :304). _font_display_name (fonts.py:41) prefers family_name, then full_name, then the normalized family, then the filename stem. _font_original_name (:50) strips the 8-character suffix back off for display. Variants for matching are computed by get_font_upload_variant (font_uploads.py:75): weight class 700 is bold, 400 is regular, and any other weight class is unsupported and ignored by matching; without a weight class, tokens like bold or gras in the metadata decide, and medium or black (with no bold token)

Font URLs are built by _font_path_to_url (font_uploads.py:173) as /app_data/<path relative to app data> through absolute_fastapi_asset_url. In Docker, nginx serves app-data directly with alias, and most locations are gated by auth_request /_auth_check, a subrequest to /api/v1/auth/verify (nginx.conf:133). Two are not: nginx.conf (excerpt) FastAPI's own SessionAuthMiddleware mirrors this with _PUBLIC_APP_DATA_PREFIXES = ("/app_data/fonts/", "/app_data/templates/") (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:38), and servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_session_auth_middleware.py:14 (named test_only_shared_app_data_asset_prefixes_do_not_require_auth) asserts that /app_data/fonts/embedded/font.ttf and /app_data/templates/default/thumbnail.png are public while images, uploads and conversion outputs under /app_data/pptx-to-html/... are not. The code does not state the reason in a comment. What it does show is that these are the two shared asset trees: fonts are not owner-scoped (above), and /app_data/templates/<id>/static/ holds bundled template assets such as static/Lato Regular.ttf from templates/momentum, which default_templates.py rewrites to /app_data/templates/momentum/static/Lato Regular.ttf and which every user's presentation references. Fonts are also fetched by @font-face and by headless renderers, where attaching session credentials is less straightforward than for page requests. Treat both directories as public: never write user-private files there.

docs.t: Step 11: Fonts in Docker and at export
docs.x: The production image installs only Noto fonts system-wide and then deletes everything else: Dockerfile (excerpt) The apt package list includes fonts-liberation alongside the Noto packages (Dockerfile:98), but the cleanup removes Liberation too. Chromium inside the container therefore resolves Arial, Helvetica and sans-serif through fontconfig to a Noto face. Any text whose family is not supplied as a web font (through the presentation font map, the theme text font, or the inlined @font-face CSS) renders in Noto in screenshots, previews and PDF exports, while the same deck in a desktop browser renders in the real Arial. The Template v2 renderer's root font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif is exactly such a case. Dockerfile.dev:43 does the same. How the export runtime receives and embeds fonts (the font map passed to json-to-images and to the PPTX writer, and PPTX font embedding) is covered in PPTX and PDF export. Template creation previews pass fonts the same way, as shown in Custom templates from PPTX. Gotcha A missing font never fails loudly. Backend catalog misses fall through to "unavailable" only at /fonts/check time; the frontend parser silently drops unusable URLs; waitForFontDescriptorsLoaded resolves after 3 seconds even if nothing loaded; and Docker falls back to Noto. When a slide "looks wrong" in export but right in the editor, compare the presentation's fonts map against what the export page actually injected before suspecting layout code.

Reads: servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts, servers/nextjs/app/layout.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx, servers/nextjs/store/store.ts, servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/ · Builds on: Runtime topology · Time: ~40 min This chapter takes the Next.js server apart layer by layer: how it is built, how URLs map to route files, which layouts run on the server and which components run in the browser, how the proxy.ts request hook gates and rewrites traffic to FastAPI, how the browser decides which origin to call, what lives in the Redux store, and which function calls which backend endpoint. By the end you should be able to open any file under servers/nextjs and know where it sits in the request path. All paths below are relative to the repository root; inside prose, servers/nextjs/ is abbreviated where the context is obvious.

Everything starts in servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs. The file is short, but each option has a deployment consequence. servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs (excerpt) Option Value Where Why it matters reactStrictMode false servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:9 Effects are not double-invoked in development, so the many useEffect-driven EventSource streams open once. distDir .next-build servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:10 Build output does not go to the default .next folder. Any Dockerfile, Electron packager or script that copies the build must look for .next-build. output standalone servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:11 Next.js emits a self-contained server.js plus a pruned node_modules, which is what the Docker image and the Electron bundle run (see Docker build and deployment). turbopack.root directory of the config file servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:12-14 Pins Turbopack's workspace root to servers/nextjs instead of letting it walk up to the monorepo root. headers() Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on /vendor/fonts/:path* servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:15-23 Community previews render in a sandboxed (opaque-origin) frame and still need the bundled fonts. allowedDevOrigins 127.0.0.1, localhost servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:24-31 Only spread in when NODE_ENV !== "production". images.unoptimized true when PRESENTON_ELECTRON_BUILD or PRESENTON_ELECTRON is "true" servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:37 The packaged desktop app lives in a read-only directory, and the image optimizer writes into <distDir>/cache. images.remotePatterns nine HTTPS hosts servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:38-75 Only these hosts can be used with next/image: an R2 bucket, two pptgen-public S3 hosts, img.icons8.com, present-for-me.s3.amazonaws.com, a Supabase project host, images.unsplash.com, picsum.photos and unsplash.com. The dependency versions that shape the rest of this chapter come from servers/nextjs/package.json: next 16.4.1, react 19.2.6, @reduxjs/toolkit ^2.2.8, react-redux ^9.1.2, konva ^10.3.0 with react-konva ^19.2.4, Tiptap 3.30.5, @dnd-kit/core ^6.3.1, mixpanel-browser ^2.67.0, and tailwindcss ^3.4.1 for the build-time stylesheet. The scripts block is minimal: dev, build, start, lint (eslint .) and test (node --test). Gotcha Two Tailwind versions coexist. The application chrome is compiled at build time with Tailwind 3 (servers/nextjs/tailwind.config.ts), but Smart-mode slides are LLM-generated HTML

The App Router directory servers/nextjs/app uses three route groups. A route group is a folder whose name is wrapped in parentheses: it organizes files and can carry its own layout.tsx, but it does not appear in the URL. Every page, its file, and whether the page file is a server or a client component: URL Page file (under servers/nextjs/app/) Page kind Guards and notes / page.tsx async server Auth disabled or signed in: renders ConfigurationInitializer around Home (onboarding). Otherwise renders AuthGate (servers/nextjs/app/page.tsx:7-25). /dashboard (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx server, renders client DashboardPage Has loading.tsx. /settings (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx async server Calls getServerAuthStatus() and renders SettingPage for admins, UserAccountSettings for everyone else (.../settings/page.tsx:11-17). /admin (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/admin/page.tsx async server requireAdminSession() (.../admin/page.tsx:8-11). /community (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/community/page.tsx server, dynamic = "force-dynamic" notFound() when PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED is a disabled value (.../community/page.tsx:7-19). /templates (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/templates/page.tsx server Redirects to /dashboard when PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE normalizes to smart. /upload (presentation-generator)/upload/page.tsx server Reads PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE and PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED on the server and passes them as props to the client UploadPage (.../upload/page.tsx:46-66). /documents-preview (presentation-generator)/documents-preview/page.tsx server wrapper Renders the client DocumentPreviewPage. /outline (presentation-generator)/outline/page.tsx server (exports metadata) Renders the client OutlinePage. /presentation (presentation-generator)/presentation/page.tsx client ('use client') Reads ?id; shows "No presentation id found" without it. /custom-template (presentation-generator)/custom-template/page.tsx server, force-dynamic Redirects to /dashboard in smart-only mode. docs.t: Step 3: The root layout and the client provider shell
docs.x: servers/nextjs/app/layout.tsx is a server component. It exports static metadata (title, Open Graph and Twitter cards pointing at https://presenton.ai) and renders the document shell: servers/nextjs/app/layout.tsx (excerpt) Four client components hang off it.

servers/nextjs/app/providers.tsx:7-12 is the only place the Redux store is attached to React: it wraps children in react-redux's Provider store={store} and mounts ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler as a sibling. Because the store is a module-level singleton (servers/nextjs/store/store.ts:7-14), some non-component code (for example syncStoreAfterCodexSignOut() in servers/nextjs/utils/storeHelpers.ts:376-392) imports store directly and dispatches without React.

This component renders nothing. It listens on window for the custom event presenton:chatgpt-auth-required (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:5, listener at servers/nextjs/app/ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler.tsx:50). Any code that detects an expired ChatGPT (Codex OAuth) session calls requestChatGptReauth(), which tracks Codex Reauth Required and dispatches the event (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:86-106). The handler then: Guards against re-entry with handlingRef and releases the guard after 2 seconds (.../ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler.tsx:22-23, :45-47). Shows an 8 second error toast with id chatgpt-auth-required (:25-30). Calls logoutChatGptAuth(), which posts to /api/v1/ppt/codex/auth/logout and then clears the Codex fields in Redux (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:108-127). Navigates to /settings?chatgpt=reauth, using replace if already on /settings (:38-43). Detection is centralized in ApiResponseHandler.handleResponse() (Step 9) and in the two SSE hooks, which call isChatGptAuthRequiredMessage() on error events. A response counts as "ChatGPT auth required" if it carries the header x-presenton-auth-action: codex-reauth, or if it is a 401/403 whose message contains CHATGPT_AUTH_REQUIRED:, chatgpt authentication, chatgpt session or codex oauth (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:54-84).

servers/nextjs/app/MixpanelInitializer.tsx:7-20 calls initMixpanel() once and tracks a Page View event with { url: pathname } on every pathname change. Whether anything is actually sent depends on /api/telemetry-status; the full mechanism is in Settings, onboarding, auth UI.

servers/nextjs/components/runtime/TailwindBrowserRuntime.tsx:25-58 injects a <style type="text/tailwindcss"> block and the browser Tailwind script with strategy="afterInteractive". On /pdf-maker it renders nothing; on / it defers loading until some component dispatches presenton:tailwind-runtime-request, which useTailwindRuntimeReady() does on mount (:60-76). Once the script loads it fires presenton:tailwind-runtime-ready exactly once per page lifetime (:17-23). Toaster is the Sonner wrapper in servers/nextjs/components/ui/sonner.tsx; the rest of the app calls it through notify.error/success/info/warning/loading(title, description, options) plus notify.dismiss(id) (servers/nextjs/components/ui/sonner.tsx:44-56).

docs.t: Step 4: Server-side session gating in layouts
docs.x: Page protection happens in server components, not in proxy.ts. The proxy comment states this explicitly (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:5-9). The helpers are in servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts. getServerAuthStatus() (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:37-88) reads the incoming cookie header with headers() and calls FastAPI GET {base}/api/v1/auth/status with cache: "no-store", where base is FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL, else NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, else http://127.0.0.1:8000 (:17-30). It returns: servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts (excerpt) available is false when the backend could not be reached or answered non-2xx. When DISABLE_AUTH is truthy (1, true, yes, on, checked by isAuthDisabled() in servers/nextjs/utils/auth.ts:1-20), it short-circuits to an authenticated admin named electron. Two guards are built on it: Guard Used by Not available Not configured Not authenticated Wrong role requireAppSession() (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:94-108) (presentation-generator)/layout.tsx:7 redirect / redirect / redirect /?reason=unauthorized not checked requireAdminSession() (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:110-121) /admin page redirect /?reason=unauthorized not distinguished redirect /?reason=unauthorized redirect /dashboard The root page (servers/nextjs/app/page.tsx:7-26) is the only entry that is not behind requireAppSession(): it renders AuthGate for setup and sign-in, which turns the ?reason=unauthorized query into a toast. Because the guard lives in the (presentation-generator) layout, an unknown URL still produces the normal 404 page instead of a login redirect; the layout only executes for routes that exist under it. Gotcha The server guard only proves that a session cookie is valid. The browser-side role used by the UI comes from a second call to the same endpoint inside ConfigurationInitializer (Step 5). Until that resolves, state.userConfig.role is null, and components such as Home (servers/nextjs/components/Home.tsx:19-27) and SettingPage treat null as "not admin".

servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx wraps both the root page and every (presentation-generator) route. It is a client component that holds the page behind a full-screen "Loading Presenton..." screen until it has established three facts: the backend is reachable, who the user is, and whether a usable text provider is configured. The key code paths: Reachability. assertBackendReachable() (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:155-179) fetches getApiUrl("/api/v1/auth/status") with credentials: "include" and throws BackendConnectionError unless the response is 2xx, has a JSON content type, and parses to a non-array object. The JSON check exists because a same-origin Next.js 404 or 500 is HTML and must not be mistaken for a healthy backend. Role. role becomes "admin" or "user" only if authenticated is true (servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:226-249). Admin config. Admins load /api/user-config, which proxies FastAPI's GET /api/v1/admin/provider-settings with real secrets (Step 10). Validity is computed client-side with hasValidLLMConfig() plus, for LLM === "presenton", a linked Presenton Cloud account (:251-299). An Ollama selection additionally calls isOllamaModelAvailable() and bounces to / if the model is not pulled (:305-328). User config. Regular users load /api/runtime-config, whose secrets are redacted to __configured__, so validity comes from the server-computed configured flag rather than client validation (:344-379). Routing. A valid config on / pushes /upload; an invalid admin config on any route other than / or /settings pushes / (where Home shows onboarding). Navigation completion is detected by polling window.location.pathname every 500 ms in setLoadingToFalseAfterNavigatingTo() (:191-203). Splash timing. The loading screen stays up for at least PRESENTON_SPLASH_MIN_DURATION_MS (3000 ms, servers/nextjs/components/ui/presenton-splash-loader.tsx:11) even if everything resolves faster (servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:178-189, :382-384). A second effect re-validates on every navigation once role is known (:75-176), skipping /, /settings* and /pdf-maker*. It re-fetches /api/user-config (admin) or /api/runtime-config (user) with cache: "no-store" and re-dispatches setLLMConfig. If the config is no longer valid it shows a "Provider setup required" warning toast and, for admins only, calls router.replace('/') (:113-125). For

Next.js 16 runs servers/nextjs/proxy.ts (the file convention formerly called middleware) before routing. Its matcher covers every path except _next/static and favicon.ico (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:174-176). The function makes decisions in a fixed order:

getFastApiBaseUrl() resolves FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL, then NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, then http://127.0.0.1:8000, stripping trailing slashes (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:10-23). rewriteToFastApi() keeps the original path and query string (:43-49). The comment at :107-109 explains why the rewrite is done at request time: in Docker, nginx already routes /api/v1, /api/v2, /app_data and /static to FastAPI, but Electron has no nginx and picks random loopback ports at start-up, so the destination cannot be baked into Next.js's build-time route manifest.

Class Test Lines FastAPI API /api/v1, /api/v1/*, /api/v2, /api/v2/* servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:25-32 FastAPI assets /app_data, /app_data/*, /static, /static/* servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:34-41 Auth-exempt API /api/v1/auth/*, /api/telemetry-status, /api/update-svg, /api/export-presentation-data/* servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:87-95 Everything else under /api/ is a Next.js API route (Step 10) and needs a valid session.

The export pipeline opens /pdf-maker?id=...&exportSession=<token> in a headless browser that has no cookies. The proxy converts the query parameter into a cookie and redirects to the clean URL: servers/nextjs/proxy.ts (excerpt) SESSION_COOKIE_NAME is presenton_session and SESSION_TTL_SECONDS is 30 days (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:62-63). The token is not validated here; it becomes the session cookie and FastAPI validates it on the next API call. The rest of the export flow is in PPTX and PDF export.

Admin-issued API keys have the prefix sk-presenton-. A request whose Authorization header starts with bearer sk-presenton- (compared lowercase) is passed straight through to FastAPI for /api/v1 and /api/v2 paths, without a cookie check, because FastAPI owns key validation. The same header on any Next.js API route gets a 403 with {"detail": "API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API"} (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:146-156). This keeps API keys away from local configuration routes like /api/user-config.

For everything else the proxy calls FastAPI GET /api/v1/auth/status forwarding the cookie header (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:65-85). An error or non-2xx is treated as {configured: true, authenticated: false}, which yields 401. A deployment with no account yet yields 428 {"detail": "Login setup is required", "setup_required": true}. Both carry Cache-Control: no-store (:158-171).

When PRESENTON_ELECTRON === "true", desktopRequestDenied() runs first for every matched request, including pages (servers/nextjs/lib/desktop-auth.ts:14-44). It requires PRESENTON_DESKTOP_TOKEN to be at least 32 characters and PRESENTON_DESKTOP_ORIGINS to be non-empty (else 503), the Host header to match one of those origins and any Origin header to be one of them (else 403), and the token to arrive either in the x-presenton-desktop-token header or the presenton_desktop_session cookie, compared with timingSafeEqual (else 401). Details belong to Electron desktop app. Gotcha The proxy calls FastAPI's /api/v1/auth/status for every authenticated Next.js API request and every proxied /api/v1 or /api/v2 call. That is one extra in-cluster HTTP round trip per API request. If you add a high-frequency endpoint, account for it, or add it to isApiAuthExempt() only if it is genuinely public.

docs.t: Step 7: How the browser picks the backend origin
docs.x: Browser code never hardcodes the FastAPI host. It calls getApiUrl(path) from servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts. servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts (excerpt) The decision table: Runtime Result for /api/v1/... Source Browser, web or Docker, no fastapiUrl query relative path, same origin (nginx or proxy.ts forwards it) servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:88-100 Browser, Electron (window.electron exists) window.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API (or location.origin) + path servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:106-120 Browser, trusted ?fastapiUrl= query that origin + path servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:56-78 Server, no configured URL relative path servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:136-138 Non-API path such as /api/user-config always relative servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:132-134 The ?fastapiUrl= override exists for export pages, but it is deliberately narrow: the value is accepted only if its origin equals the configured NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API origin or the page's own origin (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:63-74). A link can therefore select a backend the application already trusts, but never introduce a new destination for cookies or API keys. tests/backend-connectivity.test.mjs:46-68 checks this against look-alike hosts such as https://backend.example.evil.test and https://backend.example@collector.example.

The backend stores image, upload and font paths in several shapes (absolute file paths, file: URLs, absolute URLs on its own origin, relative paths). resolveBackendAssetUrl() (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:292-343) maps all of them to a URL the current runtime can load, using toBackendServedPath() (:232-269): Input contains Output path Lines /_next/static/ or /vendor/fonts/ unchanged (served by Next.js) servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:236-241 /app_data/ slice from /app_data/ :243-246 /static/ slice from /static/ :248-251 last /images/ /app_data/images/... :253-256 last /uploads/ /app_data/uploads/... :258-261 last /fonts/ /app_data/fonts/... :263-266 data: and blob: URLs pass through; absolute URLs on any origin that is not one of this deployment's backends (configured, query, runtime, or page origin) are left alone so Presenton Cloud assets keep their full URL (:315-323). normalizeBackendAssetUrls() walks a whole JSON tree and rewrites every string that looks like an asset path (:395-416); the presentation loaders run every API response through it. Gotcha Server-side getFastAPIUrl() falls back to http://127.0.0.1:5001 (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:119), while proxy.ts, serverAuth.ts and lib/fastapi-internal.ts fall back to http://127.0.0.1:8000. In Docker both are normally overridden by environment variables, but in a bare local run the two defaults disagree.

The store combines four slices (servers/nextjs/store/store.ts:7-14): servers/nextjs/store/store.ts (excerpt) No middleware, persistence or RTK Query is configured; all network I/O happens in components and hooks, which dispatch plain actions.

State (servers/nextjs/store/slices/presentationGeneration.ts:53-79): Field Type Initial Meaning presentation_id string or null null Active deck id; the outline page falls back to it when ?id is missing. isLoading boolean false Set false by setError; also read by autosave as a pause condition. isStreaming boolean or null null True while the presentation SSE stream is open; disables editing and autosave. outlines {content: string}[] [] Outline cards on the outline page, always passed through limitOutlines(). error string or null null Cleared by setPresentationId. presentationData PresentationData or null null The whole deck: metadata, slides, theme, layout, fonts. generationMetrics GenerationMetrics or null null Live token counts from Smart-mode streams. isSlidesRendered boolean false Has a reducer; no dispatcher in this snapshot. isLayoutLoading boolean false Read by autosave; no dispatcher in this snapshot. enableHtmlSelector boolean false Smart-mode "select an element for the AI" toggle. chatHtmlSelection ChatHtmlSelection or null null The element picked in a Smart slide, with its HTML and slide index. PresentationData (:9-28) has id, language, layout, n_slides, title, slides, theme, and optional template_id, design_v2_id, version, generation_mode, can_regenerate, type, community_design_ids, components, fonts, structure. GenerationMetrics (:40-51) has model, input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, total_tokens, tokens_per_second, duration_seconds, estimated, thinking_tokens_estimated, supports_thinking. Reducers: Action Payload Effect Dispatched from setStreaming boolean sets isStreaming usePresentationStreaming setLoading boolean sets isLoading not dispatched (local setLoading state functions share the name) setLayoutLoading boolean sets isLayoutLoading not dispatched setPresentationId string sets id, clears error, clears chat selection when the id changes upload, outline and documents-preview pages setSlidesRendered boolean sets flag not dispatched setError string sets error, isLoading = false not dispatched (same-name local states) clearPresentationData none nulls presentationData, generationMetrics, chatHtmlSelection outline generate, stream start, regenerate setGenerationMetrics metrics or null replaces metrics usePresentationStreaming clearOutlines / setOutlines none / outlines setOutlines runs limitOutlines() (max 50 items, 100 words each)

State {config: PresentationConfig or null, files: any} with one reducer, setPptGenUploadState, that overwrites both fields from the payload (servers/nextjs/store/slices/presentationGenUpload.ts:4-27). PresentationConfig (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/type.ts:122-132) has slides (string or null), language, prompt, tone, verbosity, instructions, includeTableOfContents, includeTitleSlide, webSearch. The upload page stores the form here so the outline page can show and regenerate from the same settings; files holds the decompose responses ([{name, file_path}] arrays).

State {role: "admin" or "user" or null, llm_config: LLMConfig} with initial llm_config = {LLM: "", IMAGE_PROVIDER: "gpt-image-1.5"} and role = null; reducers setLLMConfig (replace) and setUserRole (servers/nextjs/store/slices/userConfig.ts:4-28).

A deck-level history of slides arrays (servers/nextjs/store/slices/undoRedoSlice.ts:4-26): Field Initial Meaning past [] Older snapshots, at most maxHistorySize. present null The current snapshot. future [] Snapshots available to redo. maxHistorySize 30 past.shift() drops the oldest beyond 30. isUndoRedoInProgress false Guard while an undo/redo is being applied. pendingHistorySkips 0 The next N addToHistory calls are ignored. Actions: addToHistory({slides, actionType}), undo, redo, finishUndoRedo, clearHistory. finishUndoRedo is exported but nothing dispatches it in this snapshot; clearHistory is dispatched by usePresentationData on a fresh load and by the header's regenerate action. The skip counter is what stops the undo from recording itself: undo sets pendingHistorySkips = 1, and the autosave effect's next addToHistory (fired because presentationData changed) consumes it (:32-39, :88-105). Snapshots are compared by reference, which is valid because Immer replaces changed arrays (:46-58). How this interacts with the per-slide editor history is covered in Slide editor.
Browser calls to FastAPI live in servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/. Every function uses getApiUrl() and funnels the response through ApiResponseHandler.

getHeader() returns Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json and three Access-Control-Allow-* headers; getHeaderForFormData() returns only the three CORS headers so the browser can set the multipart boundary (.../services/api/header.ts:1-17). The CORS headers are response headers and have no effect when sent on a request; they are harmless. ApiResponseHandler.handleResponse(response, defaultMessage) (.../services/api/api-error-handler.ts:35-89): 204 returns true; any other 2xx returns parsed JSON, or {} if parsing fails. Errors parse {detail, message, error} with extractApiErrorMessage() (servers/nextjs/utils/apiErrorMessages.ts), trigger requestChatGptReauth() when the response matches the ChatGPT rules, and throw ApiResponseError with status, optional code, and retryable. retryable comes from the body's retryable flag if present, else defaults to true for 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 (servers/nextjs/utils/apiErrorMessages.ts:21-39). If the error body is not JSON, a fixed message per status code is used (api-error-handler.ts:142-169). handleResponseWithResult() (:92-139) is the non-throwing variant that returns {success, message}; delete calls use it.

The routes under servers/nextjs/app/api/ run inside the Next.js server. They exist for work that needs the Next.js filesystem view, server-only secrets, or a same-origin endpoint. Route Method Auth inside the handler Purpose /api/user-config GET authenticated; admins get FastAPI's real settings, others get the redacted config servers/nextjs/app/api/user-config/route.ts:39-67 /api/user-config POST requireAdminApi(); Content-Type must be application/json (415 otherwise); body must be a JSON object (400) forwards as PUT /api/v1/admin/provider-settings (:69-104) /api/runtime-config GET authenticated readRuntimeProviderConfig(): {configured, config} with secrets redacted (servers/nextjs/app/api/runtime-config/route.ts:7-20) /api/telemetry-status GET none (exempt in proxy) {telemetryEnabled} from DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING in env or the user config file /api/has-required-key GET none in handler (proxy requires a session) {hasKey}: whether OPENAI_API_KEY exists in the config file or env. Nothing in the Next.js source calls it. /api/read-file POST authenticated returns the text of a decomposed .txt document inside allowed directories (servers/nextjs/lib/readable-local-file.ts) /api/upload-image POST authenticated writes one image (max 20 MB) to APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/uploads[/users/{id}]/<random>.png and returns its absolute filePath /api/export-presentation POST authenticated runs the bundled exporter for {format: "pdf" or "pptx", id, title}, moves the result into the user's export folder, returns {success, path: "/api/export-presentation/file?name=..."} /api/export-presentation/file GET authenticated, owner-scoped name streams the file from APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/exports with a download Content-Disposition /api/export-presentation-data/[id] GET x-export-cookie header required (exempt in proxy) proxies GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} with that cookie for the headless renderer /api/update-svg GET none (exempt in proxy) recolors an SVG from /static/icons/ only; max 5 MB; returns image/svg+xml /api/github-stars GET none in handler {stars} for presenton/presenton, revalidated hourly (revalidate = 3600); 502 on failure; used by the upload page's GenerateHeader Three of these deserve a closer look. /api/user-config is the only path by which browser code writes provider settings. The POST forwards the raw body text to FastAPI along with the caller's cookie and, in Electron,

servers/nextjs/types/llm_config.ts:1-153 defines LLMConfig, a flat optional-field interface whose keys match the backend's environment-variable names. Groups: Group Keys Selection LLM Hosted text providers OPENAI_*, DEEPSEEK_*, GOOGLE_*, VERTEX_*, AZURE_OPENAI_*, BEDROCK_*, OPENROUTER_* (including OPENROUTER_PROVIDER_ORDER as string[]), FIREWORKS_*, TOGETHER_*, CEREBRAS_*, ANTHROPIC_* Gateways and local LITELLM_*, LMSTUDIO_*, OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL, CUSTOM_LLM_URL, CUSTOM_LLM_API_KEY, CUSTOM_MODEL Images DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION, IMAGE_PROVIDER, PEXELS_API_KEY, PIXABAY_API_KEY, COMFYUI_URL, COMFYUI_WORKFLOW, OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_*, OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_*, GPT_IMAGE_2_QUALITY, GPT_IMAGE_1_5_QUALITY Generation controls DISABLE_THINKING, EXTENDED_REASONING, LLM_GENERATION_PROFILE, LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, LLM_REASONING_MODE, LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, LLM_REASONING_BUDGET_TOKENS Web search WEB_GROUNDING, WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER, WEB_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS, SEARXNG_BASE_URL, TAVILY_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY, SERPER_API_KEY Codex OAuth CODEX_MODEL, CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN, CODEX_TOKEN_EXPIRES, CODEX_ACCOUNT_ID, CODEX_USERNAME, CODEX_EMAIL, CODEX_IS_PRO UI only USE_CUSTOM_URL, DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING (string) servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/types/slide.ts:25-42 defines the client Slide: id, index, type, design_index, images, properties, icons, graph_id, optional presentation, speaker_note, layout, layout_group, html_content, ui, and content (a loose SlideContent with title, body, optional description, graph, diagram, infographics, image_prompts, icon_queries). In practice, standard slides carry their rendering in ui and Smart slides in html_content; the backend schema is in Data model. servers/nextjs/types/presentation.ts:1-20 (GenerateRequestBody, SlideData, PresentationResponse with thumbnail and file) is a legacy shape; current pages type responses with PresentationResponse from services/api/dashboard.ts:9-33 instead. servers/nextjs/types/global.d.ts:16-32 declares window.electron (exportPresentation, readFile) and window.env (NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, APP_VERSION, DISABLE_AUTH), which Electron injects at runtime.

Reads: servers/nextjs/app/page.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx, servers/nextjs/components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlinePage.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationStreaming.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/components/PresentationHeader.tsx · Builds on: Next.js architecture · Time: ~40 min This chapter follows one user from the first page load to a downloaded PPTX, and records every HTTP request, every Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream and every Redux update along the way. You will see exactly which component fires which request, what the JSON body looks like, which slice action stores the response, and how the URL carries state between pages. The standard path (upload, then outline, then presentation) is covered first, then the Smart-mode variant that skips the outline page. All paths are relative to servers/nextjs/ unless they start with servers/. Endpoints written as /api/v1/... are FastAPI endpoints; the browser reaches them through getApiUrl() and the proxy.ts rewrite described in Next.js architecture. Endpoints written as /api/<name> without a version are Next.js route handlers under app/api/.

The root route is a Server Component. It runs on the Next.js server before any JavaScript reaches the browser. servers/nextjs/app/page.tsx (excerpt) isAuthDisabled() (utils/auth.ts:18) reads DISABLE_AUTH from window.env in the browser or process.env on the server and accepts 1, true, yes, on (utils/auth.ts:1). Electron sets it, so the desktop app never shows a login form. Otherwise getServerAuthStatus() (utils/serverAuth.ts:37) forwards the incoming cookie to FastAPI GET /api/v1/auth/status and normalizes the reply to {configured, authenticated, username, user_id, available, role}. A network failure becomes available: false, authenticated: false (utils/serverAuth.ts:78). Every other page in the app lives under app/(presentation-generator)/layout.tsx, which calls requireAppSession() (utils/serverAuth.ts:94). That helper redirects to / when FastAPI is unreachable or auth is not configured, and to /?reason=unauthorized when the user is not signed in. The Auth and multi-user chapter covers the cookie and the FastAPI side.

docs.t: Step 2: Setup or login in AuthGate
docs.x: When the server decides the visitor is not signed in, it renders AuthGate (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:30), a client component with two modes chosen by status.configured: Mode Shown when Title Endpoint Password minimum Setup configured === false (no admin exists) "Create your admin login" POST /api/v1/auth/setup 8 characters, plus a matching confirm field Sign in configured === true "Sign in to continue" POST /api/v1/auth/login 6 characters On mount the component fetches GET /api/v1/auth/status again from the browser with credentials: "include" (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:106). It also keeps a splash screen up for at least PRESENTON_SPLASH_MIN_DURATION_MS so the page does not flash. Client-side validation runs before any request (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:170): the username is trimmed and must be at least 3 characters (the input also strips whitespace on every keystroke and has maxLength={128}), and the password must meet the mode's minimum. The request body is the same for both modes: After a successful setup the gate does not sign the user in. It flips to sign-in mode and shows "Account created. Sign in with your new username and password to continue." (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:280). After a successful login the response carries authenticated: true, and an effect calls window.location.replace("/") (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:80), a full reload so the server re-renders / with the new cookie. If the URL contains ?reason=unauthorized (set by requireAppSession()), the gate shows an "Unauthorized" toast (only when auth is configured and the visitor is not signed in) and strips the query string with history.replaceState (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:87). Gotcha A 401 whose detail equals UNAUTHORIZED_DETAIL is rewritten to "The username or password is incorrect. Please try again." (components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:255). Any other 401 detail is shown verbatim, so FastAPI error strings reach the user unchanged.

docs.t: Step 3: ConfigurationInitializer decides where you land
docs.x: A signed-in request to / renders <ConfigurationInitializer><Home /></ConfigurationInitializer>. The initializer is also mounted by the (presentation-generator) layout, so it wraps every app page. Its job is to fill the userConfig slice and enforce "no provider, no app". fetchUserConfigState() (app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:205) runs once on mount: assertBackendReachable(); on failure, a "Cannot reach backend" toast and stop. GET /api/v1/auth/status to learn the role. dispatch(setUserRole("admin" | "user")) (app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:249). Admin branch: GET /api/user-config (the Next.js route that proxies FastAPI GET /api/v1/admin/provider-settings with real secrets), then normalizeLLMConfig() and dispatch(setLLMConfig(config)). If LLM === "presenton", GET /api/v1/auth/presenton/status to check the cloud link. Valid config: if the current route is /, router.push("/upload"). Invalid config: if the route is not / and not /settings, router.push("/") so the admin lands on onboarding. Regular-user branch: GET /api/runtime-config, which returns {configured, config} with secrets replaced by "__configured__". If configured is false the user sees "Instance not configured. Ask the administrator..." and stays put. A second effect (app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:75) re-validates the provider on every route change except /, /settings and /pdf-maker. For admins an invalid config forces router.replace('/'). Home (components/Home.tsx:11) is the onboarding wizard. A non-admin who somehow lands on / is pushed to /upload (components/Home.tsx:20). Onboarding itself is described in Settings, onboarding, auth UI. Gotcha ConfigurationInitializer keeps the splash screen up until window.location.pathname actually equals the push target, polling every 500 ms (app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:191). If a push is swallowed (for example an earlier navigation wins), the polling interval is never cleared and the splash stays. When you change the redirect logic, keep the target path passed to setLoadingToFalseAfterNavigatingTo() identical to the path you push.

/dashboard renders DashboardPage (app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/dashboard/components/DashboardPage.tsx:392) inside the (dashboard) layout, which adds DashboardSidebar. The layout reads two environment variables on the server: PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE (the "Standard" templates link is hidden when the mode is smart) and PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED (the Community link is hidden when it is 0, false, no or off; empty means enabled, utils/community.ts:1).

On mount fetchPresentations() fires two requests in parallel (DashboardPage.tsx:426): Call Request Purpose DashboardApi.getPresentations("v2-standard") GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all?version=v2-standard Current decks, with slides (first slide drives the thumbnail) DashboardApi.getPresentations("v1-standard", { includeSlides: false }) GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all?version=v1-standard&include_slides=false Legacy decks, listed in LegacyPresentationsTable only A 404 is treated as "no presentations" and returns [] (services/api/dashboard.ts:58). Both lists are sorted newest first by Date.parse(created_at), with unparsable dates sorted as 0 (DashboardPage.tsx:200). The grid/list toggle is local state (deckViewMode), not persisted.

PresentationCard (.../dashboard/components/PresentationCard.tsx:31) handles three actions: Action Request Result Click card none router.push("/presentation?id=ID&type=standard") or type=smart when presentation.type or generation_mode is smart (PresentationCard.tsx:74) Delete DELETE /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} card removed from local state via onDeleted Duplicate POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/duplicate returned deck is prepended via onDuplicated A v1-standard card is rendered with aria-disabled and clicking it shows "Unsupported presentation" instead of navigating (PresentationCard.tsx:60).

The "Blank Presentation" action card opens BlankPresentationDialog (.../dashboard/components/BlankPresentationDialog.tsx). It has two steps (DialogStep = "choice" | "templates"). Choosing a template loads the template list through useTemplateSummaries() (see Step 7). Either path calls createBlankPresentation(templateId?) (DashboardPage.tsx:452), which is guarded by a useRef flag so a double click cannot create two decks: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/presentation-generation.ts (excerpt) Without a template the body is omitted entirely. tests/blank-presentation.test.mjs:32 pins this: it asserts the URL ends in /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create/blank, the method is POST, the Content-Type header is application/json, and the body is undefined or {"template_id": ...}. The response must contain a string id or the client throws "Blank presentation response did not include an id". On success the user goes straight to /presentation?id=ID&type=standard, skipping upload and outline.

/upload (app/(presentation-generator)/upload/page.tsx:46) is a Server Component that reads PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE and PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED and passes them as props to the client component UploadPage (.../upload/components/UploadPage.tsx:151).

UploadPage keeps everything in React state until Generate is pressed. Nothing is written to Redux while you type. Field (PresentationConfig) Default Control slides null ("Auto slides") SlideCountSelect in ConfigurationSelects.tsx:79 language LanguageType.Auto = "Auto (English)" LanguageSelect (searchable list of every LanguageType value) prompt "" PromptInput textarea tone "default" Advanced settings verbosity "standard" Advanced settings instructions "" Advanced settings includeTableOfContents false Advanced settings includeTitleSlide false Advanced settings webSearch false, then overwritten by llmConfig.WEB_GROUNDING (UploadPage.tsx:227) no UI control on this page ToneType values are default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch; VerbosityType values are concise, standard, text-heavy (upload/type.ts:134). The URL can preload state (UploadPage.tsx:179): ?prompt=... fills the prompt, ?mode=smart|standard picks the mode if the deployment allows it, and ?communityId=N (positive safe integer, community enabled, smart mode available) fetches GET /api/v1/ppt/community/presentations/{N} and preselects that design as a reference. The Community page uses these parameters (see Settings, onboarding, auth UI).

PromptInput (.../upload/components/PromptInput.tsx:23) is a plain Textarea; Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter submits (PromptInput.tsx:33). Selected community references render as removable chips above it. SupportingDoc (.../upload/components/SupportingDoc.tsx:27) renders the paperclip and the round submit arrow. Files are filtered by extension only: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/SupportingDoc.tsx (excerpt) Drag and drop goes through the same addFiles(). Extra files beyond 8 are dropped with a "Maximum file limit reached" warning (SupportingDoc.tsx:46). The files stay as browser File objects in local state; nothing is uploaded until Generate.

The slide-count popover offers presets 5, 8, 9, ... 20 plus a free numeric field (ConfigurationSelects.tsx:59). Every change goes through clampSlideCountValue() (utils/presentationLimits.ts:39): non-digits are stripped, leading zeros removed, and the value is capped at MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES = 50. On submit parseLimitedSlideCount() turns null or "" into null, which the backend reads as "decide automatically".

AdvanceSettings (.../upload/components/AdvanceSettings.tsx:23) edits a draft copy. Changes reach config only on Save (AdvanceSettings.tsx:57); Escape or the close button discards them. While open, it sets document.body.style.overflow = "hidden".

The "Presentation Mode" link opens GenerationModeDialog (.../upload/components/GenerationModeDialog.tsx:15): two cards with autoplaying videos (/Standard.mp4, /Smart.mp4). Hovering a card pauses the other video. The segmented control next to it does the same thing without the dialog. Availability comes from isGenerationModeAvailable() (utils/presentationGenerationMode.ts:23): PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE Initial mode Smart button Standard button unset, invalid, or both standard enabled enabled standard standard disabled enabled smart smart enabled disabled

Only in Smart mode with community enabled, CommunityReferencePicker (.../upload/components/CommunityReferencePicker.tsx:19) loads GET /api/v1/ppt/community/presentations?page=1&page_size=8&order_by=priority&order=desc and shows the first four, filtered client side by title, author or prompt. Cmd+K or Ctrl+K focuses its search box when no dialog is open. Previewing a card calls GET /api/v1/ppt/community/presentations/{id} for full slides. "Use design" stores the selection as communityReference; "Use prompt" copies the design's prompt into the textarea.

handleGeneratePresentation() (UploadPage.tsx:410) runs in this order: validateConfiguration() (UploadPage.tsx:377): language must be set; with files attached the language may not be Auto ("Please choose a language before processing uploaded documents."); there must be a prompt, a file, or (Smart plus community) a selected reference. In Standard mode only, ensureStockImageProviderReady() (UploadPage.tsx:342): unless DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION is set, when the image provider is pexels or pixabay, a probe GET /api/v1/ppt/images/search?query=business&limit=1&provider=pexels&strict_api_key=true is sent, with the key in an X-Provider-Api-Key header unless it is the redacted placeholder "__configured__" (services/api/images.ts:120). A failure aborts with "Image provider unavailable". With files: handleDocumentProcessing(). Without files: handleDirectPresentationGeneration(). The document path makes three calls in sequence: # Call Body 1 POST /api/v1/ppt/files/upload multipart/form-data, one files part per file 2 POST /api/v1/ppt/files/decompose {"file_paths": <upload response>, "language": "English"} 3 POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create see below, with file_paths taken from the decompose response getDocumentPaths() (UploadPage.tsx:131) flattens the decompose response and keeps every file_path string. How the backend extracts text is in Document ingestion. The create body built by PresentationGenerationApi.createPresentation() (services/api/presentation-generation.ts:82) looks like this for a prompt-only Standard run: community_design_ids: [id] is added only in Smart mode with a selected reference. n_slides is clamped again inside the API helper to 1..50 (presentation-generation.ts:112). The helper returns the FastAPI response spread with type: generation_mode. Then the same three Redux writes on both paths. The prompt-only path (UploadPage.tsx:568) stores files: []; the document path (UploadPage.tsx:505) stores files: responses, the raw decompose results: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/upload/components/UploadPage.tsx (excerpt) pptGenUpload keeps the config and the decompose results so the outline page can regenerate later. clearOutlines() empties presentationGeneration.outlines, which matters because the outline stream only starts when that array is empty. Finally getGenerationDestination() (UploadPage.tsx:309) picks the next URL: Mode Destination

app/(presentation-generator)/documents-preview/ still exists. DocumentPreviewPage (.../documents-preview/components/DocumentPreviewPage.tsx:50) reads pptGenUpload.files, loads each extracted text through window.electron.readFile or POST /api/read-file with {"filePath": "..."}, and has its own handleCreatePresentation() that posts to /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create and then calls router.replace("/outline"). No code path navigates there any more. A search of app, components, utils, lib and store finds /documents-preview only in the dashboard Header component's active-route list (.../dashboard/components/Header.tsx:13). UploadPage decomposes documents itself and goes straight to the outline. Gotcha If you revive this page, note that it navigates to /outline without ?id=. OutlinePage would then fall back to presentationGeneration.presentation_id from Redux, which survives only within the same tab session. It also omits generation_mode, so it always creates a Standard deck.

docs.t: Step 7: The outline page, template stage
docs.x: /outline renders OutlinePage (.../outline/components/OutlinePage.tsx:113). The presentation id comes from the URL first and Redux second: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlinePage.tsx (excerpt) An effect copies the URL id into Redux with setPresentationId (OutlinePage.tsx:161). Without any id the page shows EmptyStateView. The page opens in the template stage (isTemplateStage = true). TemplateSelection (.../outline/components/TemplateSelection.tsx:38) calls useTemplateSummaries(), which issues two parallel requests (hooks/useTemplateSummaries.ts:107): When the text provider is presenton, both gain &presenton_cloud_only=true and the result is deduplicated by default|custom plus lowercased name. Templates whose layout_count is 0 are dropped. Built-in templates are reordered so momentum, dynamic, executive come first (useTemplateSummaries.ts:12). With no custom templates, a single "Templates" grid is shown; otherwise "Custom" and "Built-In" sections. The "Create custom template" card is hidden for Presenton Cloud users. ?template= in the URL preselects a template whose id matches or whose name, lowercased with non-alphanumerics replaced by -, matches (TemplateSelection.tsx:35). The user still has to click it to proceed. Clicking a card runs handleTemplateSelect() (OutlinePage.tsx:209): it stores selectedTemplateId, sets isTemplateStage = false and scrolls to the top. That flip is what starts the outline stream. Gotcha The outline does not stream while the user browses templates. useOutlineStreaming(presentation_id, !isTemplateStage && hasSelectedTemplate) (OutlinePage.tsx:139) is disabled until a template is picked, so the LLM call for the outline is deferred to that moment.

useOutlineStreaming() (.../outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:18) opens a native EventSource: It returns early when disabled, when there is no id, or when outlines already has entries (useOutlineStreaming.ts:52). That last check is why the upload page dispatches clearOutlines(). All messages arrive as the named SSE event response with a JSON data field, handled by type: data.type Handling Redux status setStatusMessage(data.status) none chunk append data.chunk to a string buffer, run jsonrepair() on the whole buffer, JSON.parse; if the result has slides, apply limitOutlines() setOutlines(nextSlides) on every parsable chunk complete read data.presentation.outlines.slides, apply limitOutlines() setOutlines(final); close the stream closing reset state, status "Outline ready" close the stream error if the detail mentions ChatGPT auth, request re-auth; otherwise retry none jsonrepair turns a truncated JSON prefix such as {"slides":[{"content":"# Intro into valid JSON, so each chunk renders as a growing outline. The hook also tracks which slide index changed last (activeSlideIndex) and the highest index seen; OutlineItem uses these to render the active item through marked.parse() with a 60 ms throttle (.../outline/components/OutlineItem.tsx:120) and to auto-scroll it into view. Retries: up to MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 3, waiting 1000 ms * retryCount (1 s, 2 s, 3 s) between attempts (useOutlineStreaming.ts:14). Each retry resets the buffer, so the server replays from the start. When retries run out, a server error event produces the toast "Outline streaming failed" and a dropped connection (onerror) produces "Connection failed". limitOutlines() (utils/presentationLimits.ts:24) caps the list at 50 entries and each content at 100 words (MAX_OUTLINE_CONTENT_WORDS), cutting at the end of the 100th word. The setOutlines reducer applies it again (store/slices/presentationGeneration.ts:128). The SSE event format on the server side is in Streaming (SSE).

While streaming, items are rendered with keys streaming-outline-{index} and dragging is disabled. After the stream ends, OutlineContent (.../outline/components/OutlineContent.tsx:40) wraps them in a dnd-kit SortableContext. Stable ids come from useStableOutlineIds() so React keys survive reorders. The pointer sensor needs 6 px of movement before a drag starts (OutlineContent.tsx:54), and the keyboard sensor uses sortableKeyboardCoordinates. Interaction Handler Redux Drag and drop useOutlineManagement().handleDragEnd(old, new) uses arrayMove (.../outline/hooks/useOutlineManagement.ts:11) setOutlines(reordered) Click an item, edit markdown, blur OutlineItem.handleMarkdownBlur() calls onUpdate only if the draft changed (OutlineItem.tsx:90); OutlinePage.handleUpdateOutline() trims to 100 words setOutlines(updated) Tab key in the editor inserts a literal tab character none Add slide appends {content: "Outline title"}, refused at 50 (useOutlineManagement.ts:30) setOutlines([...outlines, new]) None of these edits is saved to the server immediately. They live in Redux until Continue, or until the outline assistant is used.

OutlinePromptBar edits a draft copy of the saved upload config (slides, language, advanced settings). "Regenerate" runs handleRegenerateOutline() (OutlinePage.tsx:223), which creates a brand new presentation with POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create (no generation_mode, so standard), stores the draft with setPptGenUploadState, clears outlines, and replaces the URL with the new id: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlinePage.tsx (excerpt) The new id re-runs the streaming effect, which opens a fresh EventSource. The old presentation row is left behind.

When a template is selected, the right rail renders <Chat variant="outline"> (OutlinePage.tsx:470). Before each message, handleBeforeOutlineChatSend() pushes the current Redux outlines to the server with PUT /api/v1/ppt/outlines/{id} and body {"slides": [{"content": "..."}]} (services/api/presentation-generation.ts:270). After the assistant changes the outline, handleOutlineChanged() reloads it with GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/{id} and dispatches setOutlines. The chat protocol itself is covered in Editing and chat assistant.

GenerateButton (.../outline/components/GenerateButton.tsx:13) is disabled while the stream is loading or running and before a template is chosen. Its label walks through "Select a Template", "Loading...", "Continue", and the loading message. Clicking it calls usePresentationGeneration().handleSubmit() (.../outline/hooks/usePresentationGeneration.ts:87): Read the newest outlines straight from the store with store.getState() (not from a stale closure). Validate: at least one outline, a template id, at most 50 outlines. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare: On success: dispatch(clearPresentationData()), clearTheme() removes the inline CSS variables --primary-color, --background-color, --card-color, --stroke, --primary-text, --background-text and --graph-0 to --graph-9 from #presentation-page (usePresentationGeneration.ts:66), then router.replace("/presentation?id=ID&stream=true&type=standard"). The overlay shows "Generating presentation data..." with a 30 s progress bar during the prepare call. What prepare stores (the chosen layouts per slide) is explained in From template to schema to slide.

/presentation is a client page (app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/page.tsx:7). Without ?id it shows "No presentation id found". Otherwise it renders PresentationPage (.../presentation/components/PresentationPage.tsx:144). mode, slide and stream are read by usePresentationNavigation() (.../presentation/hooks/usePresentationNavigation.ts:16-20); type and editor are read by PresentationPage itself (PresentationPage.tsx:188-198): Parameter Meaning stream=true open the generation stream instead of fetching the saved deck (any non-empty value counts) type=smart Smart deck; also enables preloading the prepared presentation mode=present&slide=N presentation mode at slide N editor=v2 also enables preloading (PresentationPage.tsx:188) The hooks are wired in this order: useAutoSave({debounceMs: 2000, enabled}) (PresentationPage.tsx:275), usePresentationData() (provides fetchUserSlides), usePresentationNavigation(), then usePresentationStreaming() (PresentationPage.tsx:306). Without stream, usePresentationStreaming simply calls fetchUserSlides() (usePresentationStreaming.ts:133). That function (.../presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:27) does: GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} with cache: "no-store" and credentials: "include". A v1-standard deck triggers "Unsupported presentation" and router.replace("/dashboard"). normalizeBackendAssetUrls(data) rewrites asset URLs for the current runtime. Resolve the template id and fetch its theme with TemplateService.getTemplateTheme(); fall back to the response theme, then DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_THEME. dispatch(setPresentationData(themedData)) and, by default, dispatch(clearHistory()) to reset undo. Load fonts with useFontLoader() and apply the theme CSS variables to #presentation-slides-wrapper.

With stream=true, startStream() (usePresentationStreaming.ts:690) dispatches setStreaming(true), clearPresentationData() and setGenerationMetrics(null), optionally preloads the prepared deck with GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} (so the template layout and theme are known before the first slide), and then opens: Event handling (usePresentationStreaming.ts:315): data.type Handling Redux generation_metrics merge counters, keeping maxima across events setGenerationMetrics(next) fonts store the font map setPresentationData({...prev, fonts}) slide_html Smart mode: build or take data.slide, html_content = data.html setPresentationData with one slide merged in chunk (a) if the chunk alone parses as one slide object with string layout, number index and object content, merge that slide; (b) also append to a buffer, jsonrepair it, and if it has slides, merge them all setPresentationData slide_assets a slide whose image and icon URLs are now resolved; warnings[].detail shown once each as "Some images could not be generated" (12 s toast) setPresentationData complete full presentation in data.presentation, or (Smart) only presentation_id, in which case fetchUserSlides({clearHistory: false}) setPresentationData, setStreaming(false) closing same as complete with data.presentation setPresentationData, setStreaming(false) error retryable === false fails immediately; otherwise retry; the message appends "N of M slides were saved and will be reused." when completed_slides > 0 setStreaming(false) on final failure After completion the hook removes stream from the URL with history.replaceState (usePresentationStreaming.ts:610), so a page refresh loads the saved deck instead of streaming again. Retries use the same 3 attempts and linear 1 s backoff as the outline hook.

Chunk events replay slides with placeholder assets even after a slide_assets event delivered the real URL. streamAssetMerge.ts prevents flicker back to the placeholder: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/streamAssetMerge.ts (excerpt) A string counts as a placeholder when it contains any of /static/images/placeholder, /static/images/replaceable_template_image, /static/icons/placeholder, placeholder.jpg, placeholder.svg or replaceable_template_image.png (streamAssetMerge.ts:1).
