docs.t: UC1: QBR deck from the Sales dashboard for EMEA, last quarter
docs.x: The analyst opens the Sales Overview dashboard, sets Region to EMEA and Period to last quarter, and types in the chat panel (master) or the Studio page (6.1): QBR deck from the Sales dashboard for EMEA, last quarter. Board template. Lead with revenue versus prior year, then product mix, then top countries. Context Capture reads the dashboard's native_filters_key from the URL, converts it into a durable permalink, and submits a request like this: CreateDocumentRequest for UC1 The response is 202 with document_id, job_id and task_uuid. Sections stream into the preview as section.ready events. The resulting PPTX has a KPI group whose revenue value is the same number the dashboard's Big Number chart shows for the same user and filters, a stacked column chart whose "Edit Data" opens the monthly rows by product line, and a native table of the top countries. The narrative reads, for example, Revenue moved {{f:f_rev_yoy}} year over year across the region, with the token rendered as a separate text run.

docs.t: UC3: Incident brief when an alert fires
docs.x: An Alert in Superset evaluates "orders in the last hour below threshold" every five minutes. Its Webhook recipient targets https://<superset>/extensions/databound/docgen/v1/hooks/<token>. When the alert triggers, the Trigger Service validates the token, ignores the payload's text fields, and runs the alert_brief template as the trigger's run-as user. Within seconds a Slack post appears: What fired: Hourly orders below threshold (threshold from the alert's validator_config_json, last value from the report execution log). What changed: orders fell {{f:f_orders_chg.abs}} versus the previous hour, led by {{f:f_worst_region.label}}. Where to look: links to the live dashboard and chart. No screenshot is taken by Superset either: the alert is chart-scoped with report_format = TEXT on 6.1, or NONE on master, so the reports pipeline never starts a browser (see Superset landscape (6.1)).

The executive asks once, in the Studio: "Every Monday at 7 in Paris, email me a one-screen KPI summary of last week from the Executive KPIs dashboard." The analyst saves the document and creates a trigger: TriggerSpec for UC4 Every Monday the beat task databound_docs.trigger_tick schedules run_trigger. The refresh re-resolves every binding as user 42, rolls Last week forward, keeps the prose and updates its tokens unless a drift rule fires (a sign flip, a change in the top three, or a cited value moving more than 10%), and sends the email. If nothing changed, refresh.unchanged is recorded and no new version is created.

The analyst generates a page from the Sales dashboard with no region filter and shares it in live mode with the Regional Managers role. When the manager for EMEA opens GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/pages/<document_id>, the page calls render-model?live=1, and the server re-resolves every binding as that manager. RLS restricts the rows to EMEA, tokens resolve to EMEA values, and claim lint re-checks each narrative against the manager's facts. If the narrative no longer holds for that viewer's data, it is replaced by deterministic sentences with a "Summary written for different data" notice and a "Regenerate for me" button.

docs.t: UC7: Brief from a SQL Lab result
docs.x: In SQL Lab, after a query succeeds, the analyst clicks "Generate brief from results" in the results toolbar (sqllab.results). The panel captures the query's remoteId from sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess. The backend reloads the Query row, checks that it belongs to the user, and accepts it as a sql binding only when the operator enabled DATABOUND_DOCS["ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS"] (default False) and raise_for_access(sql=..., force_dataset_match=True) passes. Otherwise the panel offers "save as dataset first", after which the brief is built from a governed dataset binding. The prompt might be: Two-paragraph brief of this result for the ops channel: what stands out, what to check next.

docs.t: UC8: Board deck from an external agent
docs.x: An external agent connected to superset mcp run calls the MCP prompt dbd_deck_from_dashboard(dashboard, template, audience) to get the ordered steps, then extensions.databound.docgen.dbd_list_templates, then extensions.databound.docgen.dbd_generate_document with a CreateDocumentRequest, and polls dbd_get_job. On master the call runs as the user the agent's JWT or API key resolves to. On 6.1, MCP calls run as MCP_DEV_USERNAME unless middleware sets g.user, so DBD's mutate and data tools refuse to run for the dev user unless DATABOUND_DOCS["MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER"] (a Data-Bound Documents setting, not a Superset one) is set for development.

On an existing deck the analyst types: Make slide 2 a line chart and add a slide on deal size by country. The Planner runs in edit mode and returns JSON Patch operations restricted to /sections, /facts, /title, plus binding additions that go through the Binding Registry. The server validates the patch against the current version, re-runs only the affected bindings and narratives, and writes a new version. If the planner cannot decide (two datasets both have a deal_size column), it emits job.needs_input with options and ends the task; the answer schedules continue_generation.

A regulated deployment has no LLM endpoint. The operator sets the template planner strategy, and tpl_kpi_brief declares fixed bindings and deterministic sentences such as {binding_title}: {{f:x}} ({{f:delta}} versus the prior period). The same Binding Resolver, Fact Engine, renderers and triggers run. Only the prose is less fluent. Gotcha: prompts are not data access A prompt such as "include salaries by employee" cannot widen what a user sees. The Planner can choose only from candidates and datasets the user can already access, and every binding is re-checked by ChartDataCommand.validate(), which calls raise_for_access before running anything (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108). A request for data outside the user's access becomes an entry in the outline's gaps, not a query.
Requirements are grouped by the stage they constrain. "Must" items are MVP scope unless the Phase column says otherwise; phases are defined in Roadmap.

Id Requirement Phase FR-01 Accept a prompt, a template reference (id, version), a data context and typed parameters through one request schema, CreateDocumentRequest, from UI, REST and MCP MVP FR-02 Capture a dashboard's live filter state at request time and persist it as a dashboard permalink, so later refreshes reproduce the same selection MVP FR-03 Support context from a dashboard, explicit chart ids, explicit dataset ids and a SQL Lab query; support semantic views where SEMANTIC_LAYERS is enabled MVP ([M] for semantic views, v2) FR-04 Offer a "what will the AI see" preview of the exact Data Digest before generation (POST /context/digest) MVP FR-05 Deduplicate identical submissions (double clicks) into one job through a deterministic GTF task_key MVP

Id Requirement Phase FR-06 Plan sections with a schema-constrained outline whose binding choices are enums generated per request from the digest MVP FR-07 Choose layouts deterministically by slot compatibility (shape, x kind, series and category counts), with an LLM tie-break only when two layouts score within 3 points MVP FR-08 Provide three planner strategies with one plan contract: pipeline (default), template (no LLM) and agent (opt-in, master only) MVP (agent v2) FR-09 Let admins import branded PPTX and DOCX masters whose shapes or content controls are named slot:<type>:<name>, and version templates immutably MVP for JSON templates, v1 for master import FR-10 Ask a clarifying question (job.needs_input) instead of guessing, without blocking a worker v1

"Dynamic" is ambiguous. In this design it has a precise meaning: every data-bearing element is a re-executable reference to a governed Superset query, not a copy of numbers. The reference is a DataBinding; the numbers are a BindingResult produced by running it at a specific time as a specific identity.

A binding records what to run, not what came back: its source (chart, dataset, semantic [M] or sql); its filters: dashboard native filters to apply, explicit filters, time_range, time_grain, $param.* references; its shape (scalar, series, xy, xyz, table, pivot) and format; its mode (live or snapshot) and, for chart sources, follow (live reloads the chart's current saved query context on every run; pinned uses a stored snapshot of it and flags definition_changed when the live chart drifts). Rows exist in an artifact only as rendered output: chart caches and embedded workbooks in PPTX, table cells, token runs, embedded JSON in a static page. They are stored in dbd_binding_result.rows only for snapshot mode or when an audit policy requires it.

Mode What happens when the artifact is used Whose data LLM involved Live page Every open re-resolves live bindings as the viewer; tokens re-resolve; narratives follow the viewer rule the viewer only on "Regenerate for me" Refresh in place Re-resolve, then replace_data, table rewrite and guarded token rewrite inside the existing PPTX or DOCX; a new version the run-as user (or the requester) only if the narrative policy fires Regenerate Full pipeline with the same prompt, template and context; structure may change the requester yes Snapshot Frozen rows, never re-queried; exported and shared as generated stored no

A refresh is defined by five rules: Same query, new time. Parameters roll forward: a binding with time_range: "$param.time_range" and a parameter value of Last quarter resolves to the quarter that is "last" at refresh time. Absolute ranges (2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01) stay absolute. Same filters. Dashboard filters come from the stored permalink (filter_mode: "captured"), or from the dashboard's current defaults when the document opts into filter_mode: "defaults". Same identity rules. Refreshes run as the requesting user, or as the trigger's run_as_fk, which is re-validated (active, still has can_refresh, still has access to every bound datasource) before every run. There is no fallback to another user. In place, never re-laid-out. A refresh rewrites chart caches, embedded workbooks, table cells and token runs, and nothing else. An XML diff between two refreshes of a PPTX touches only those parts. A token run edited by a human since generation is skipped and reported as token_edited_skipped. Prose follows policy. With the default regenerate_on_drift, a narrative is rewritten only when a drift rule fires for one of its facts (sign_flip, rank_change_top3, abs_change_pct>10); otherwise only its tokens update. user_edited narratives are never rewritten. Gotcha: filter state keys expire, permalinks do not The native_filters_key in a dashboard URL points to filter state held in FILTER_STATE_CACHE_CONFIG, a cache with a TTL. The default is a SupersetMetastoreCache with a 90-day timeout that is refreshed on every read (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1551-1555), but operators often move it to Redis with a shorter timeout, and any cache entry can be evicted. A document that stored only that key could silently lose its filters. Context Capture therefore converts it into a dashboard permalink at capture time. Permalinks are key-value rows written without an expiry (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/permalink/create.py:110-115), and the permalink key is what refreshes use months later.

It does not mean real-time streaming. Data changes are detected by schedules, alert conditions, freshness sentinels and definition-change listeners. Superset has no change data capture or dataset-refresh event to subscribe to. It does not mean a PPTX that queries Superset by itself when opened in PowerPoint. Office files are refreshed by Data-Bound Documents (on a trigger, in the Studio, or by uploading a previously exported copy to POST /documents/<id>/refresh-upload); the live, open-time behavior belongs to page documents. It does not mean the LLM re-reads the data on every refresh. Most refreshes involve no LLM call at all.

No pixel of a Superset UI page is ever captured, and no bound element is ever stored as a raster image. Superset's own report pipeline does exactly what this forbids: PNG reports are browser captures and PDF reports are a stack of those captures (apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41). Superset landscape (6.1) explains why that pipeline exists and why the design cannot reuse it for rendering. Allowed Forbidden A native PPTX or DOCX chart built from resolved rows, with an embedded workbook A PNG or JPEG of a Superset chart or dashboard, from any source A native table with formatted text cells build_pdf_from_screenshots or any PDF made of images of charts Vector SVG computed from rows in Python (Vega-Lite through vl-convert-python), or later ECharts server-side SVG Loading a Superset page in a headless browser, for any purpose, including "to make the frontend save a query context" Chromium printing DBD's own static HTML to PDF with network access disabled (text stays text, SVG stays vector) Importing superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots, superset.utils.screenshot_utils or superset.utils.pdf A PNG rasterized from DBD's own SVG, only for email clients that block SVG MCP get_chart_preview with format: "png" Static template assets (logos, backgrounds) as image elements An image element whose source is a capture

"Native" has a testable meaning in PPTX: the chart is a c:chartSpace part with cached category and value points and an embedded .xlsx workbook, so PowerPoint's "Edit Data" opens the real rows. python-pptx produces exactly this: ChartPart.new writes the chart XML and then chart_workbook.update_from_xlsx_blob(chart_data.xlsx_blob), and Chart.replace_data later rewrites both the cached values and the workbook while keeping formatting. Values are stored as numbers with an Excel number format derived from Superset's d3 format, so a reader can restyle, re-sort or copy them.

The requirement is enforced by machines, not by convention: an import-linter contract in superset-databound-docs forbids the screenshot and PDF-from-screenshot modules listed above; a renderer contract test unzips every generated PPTX and DOCX and fails if any shape named dbd:*, or any dbd:binding content control, targets an image part (the only exception is a native: "svg" element whose SVG was generated from rows); unsupported viz types fall back to vector SVG from rows, a native table, or a link to the live chart. Gotcha: Alerts used as triggers must not take screenshots either A dashboard-scoped Report or Alert always produces PNG or PDF attachments, so pointing one at the DBD webhook would still start a browser on every run. Use a chart-scoped alert with report_format = TEXT on 6.1, or NONE on master, and keep the dashboard id in the DBD trigger record.

Non-goal Why What happens instead Putting an LLM, or any Presenton code, into apache/superset core Superset should not depend on an LLM; importing Presenton code into an ASF repository would be a code donation Data-Bound Documents lives in its own Apache-2.0 repository as a wheel plus extension; only small generic hooks are proposed upstream (Roadmap) Letting the LLM author SQL or adhoc expressions Large attack surface and no governance The LLM chooses chart candidates and proposes dataset queries over saved metrics and columns only; sql bindings are opt-in and come from saved queries, the user's own SQL Lab queries or template admins Pixel-identical reproduction of Superset's ECharts look in Office files Office charts are a different engine Office charts approximate colors, formats and types; the live page uses ECharts for parity Rendering WebGL maps (deck.gl, Mapbox) natively No faithful vector rendering exists An aggregated native table, a narrative and an "Open live map" link Replacing Superset dashboards or Alerts and Reports They remain the authoring and alerting tools DBD reads dashboards and uses alerts as triggers; Superset dashboard output arrives only in v2 A new authentication path, service account or credential broker Any of these is an exfiltration risk All data access is in-process under override_user; schedules use an explicit run-as user Real-time streaming dashboards in documents No upstream change event exists Event triggers and live pages Generation for embedded (guest) users in MVP Guest identity on 6.1 is unverified, and extensions do not load in embedded dashboards Guest live pages are v2 and master only Using @presenton/export-core License unknown, distributed outside npm, browser DOM measurement python-pptx, a DrawingML writer and vector HTML printing (PPTX and PDF export shows what is replaced) Free-form "smart mode" HTML generated by the LLM Cannot guarantee data provenance Template-driven pages whose data elements are bindings Multi-tenancy beyond Superset's Tenancy follows the Superset deployment Owner-scoped documents, explicit shares, template visibility scopes Gotcha: 6.1 has no button on dashboards On stock 6.1 an extension can contribute UI only in SQL Lab; the global chat slot that appears on dashboards and Explore exists only on master. Reads: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py, superset/tasks/decorators.py, superset/tasks/manager.py, superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py, superset/charts/data/api.py, superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py, superset/security/manager.py, superset/commands/report/execute.py, superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/ · Builds on: Vision and requirements · Time: ~50 min This chapter is the inventory of what Apache Superset already provides that Data-Bound Documents builds on, with exact module paths, signatures, routes and payloads. You will walk through the extensions framework (backend and frontend), the Global Task Framework, the built-in MCP service, the chart data API and query context, dashboards and their filter state, datasets and metrics, SQL Lab, security, theming, the embedded SDK, and Alerts and Reports. For each piece you will see whether it exists in the 6.1.0 release or only on master, and what the design does on 6.1 when it is missing. The chapter ends with a single availability table you can use as a checklist.

docs.x: All citations refer to apache/superset master at cabd8d4ecc6101f04184bd93b5fa77152d139c4d (2026-11-02) unless marked otherwise. 6.1.0 facts come from the 6.1.0 tag, its versioned documentation and UPDATING.md, whose ## 6.1.0 section starts at apache/superset: UPDATING.md:2689; everything above it, under ## Next, is master only. Artifact Version Released Notes Apache Superset 6.1.0 tag dated 2026-05-13 latest stable; a 7.0 branch exists apache-superset-core (PyPI) 0.1.0 2026-05-11 backend extension API; master's copy is the unreleased 0.2.0 line apache-superset-extensions-cli (PyPI) 0.1.0 2026-05-11 superset-extensions command @apache-superset/core (npm) 0.1.0 2026-05-11 frontend extension API @superset-ui/embedded-sdk (npm) 0.4.0 in master's superset-embedded-sdk/package.json not checked release paired with 6.1 not checked; method set at the 6.1.0 tag in Step 10 Tags used below: [6.1] present in 6.1.0 and on master; [M] master only (expected in 7.0, unverified); [M*] present in 6.1.0 but changed on master. Both superset-core and the CLI declare Development Status :: 3 - Alpha, and ENABLE_EXTENSIONS is a development-lifecycle flag defaulting to False (apache/superset: superset/config.py:788). Plan for churn.

An extension is a .supx zip (or, in development, a local dist/ folder) discovered at process startup. The host initializes in a fixed order inside init_app_in_ctx: views first, then init_all_dependencies_and_extensions() (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:640-655), which always replaces the superset_core stubs with host implementations and, only when ENABLE_EXTENSIONS is on, calls init_extensions() (:657). That function imports each extension's backend entrypoint inside extension_context(manifest) with eager_import(backend.entrypoint) (:686). Facts that shape the design: Every process imports the extension. Celery workers build the app with create_app() (apache/superset: superset/tasks/celery_app.py:29-33) and so does the MCP server (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/flask_singleton.py:75-90). With ENABLE_EXTENSIONS on in each process's config, a GTF task or MCP tool defined in the extension is executable in a worker or in superset mcp run. Discovery is startup only. GET /api/v1/extensions/ re-reads the folder on every request (apache/superset: superset/extensions/api.py:104-115), so a new bundle's frontend appears, but its backend is not imported until restart. There is no install, enable or upload API. Backend code is never written to disk. An InMemoryFinder on sys.meta_path compiles bundle sources with a supx://<id>/backend/src/... filename (apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:51-158). Failures are isolated. A broken extension is logged and the app still starts (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:657-701). Configuration keys: Key Default Location Availability FEATURE_FLAGS["ENABLE_EXTENSIONS"] False apache/superset: superset/config.py:788 [6.1] LOCAL_EXTENSIONS: list[str] [] apache/superset: superset/config.py:3681 [6.1] EXTENSIONS_PATH: str or None None apache/superset: superset/config.py:3682 [6.1] EXTENSION_DENYLIST, EXTENSION_VERSION_POLICY [], {} apache/superset: superset/config.py:3687, 3693 [M] EXTENSIONS_EPHEMERAL_STORAGE, EXTENSIONS_PERSISTENT_STORAGE 7 days and 100 KB; 100 MB quota and 1 MB values apache/superset: superset/config.py:1580-1609 [M]

The superset-extensions CLI (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py) has six commands: init scaffolds a project, validate checks extension.json against ExtensionConfig and npm at least 10.8.2, update bumps metadata, build (:554) runs npm run build and copies backend files matched by [tool.apache_superset_extensions.build] include (copy_backend_files, :225), bundle (:587) zips dist/ into {name}-{version}.supx by default (:612), so with name docgen the default file is docgen-1.0.0.supx; the canonical databound-docgen-<version>.supx is produced with superset-extensions bundle --output databound-docgen-1.0.0.supx, and dev (:634) watches and rebuilds into dist/ for use with LOCAL_EXTENSIONS. build_manifest (:149) derives two identifiers you cannot choose freely: the backend entrypoint <publisher_snake>.<name_snake>.entrypoint, so for publisher databound and name docgen it is databound.docgen.entrypoint; the Module Federation name <camel(publisher)>_<camel(name)>, here databound_docgen. The extension id is computed as f"{publisher}.{name}" (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/types.py:38-84), here databound.docgen. The accepted bundle layout is manifest.json, frontend/dist/<file> and backend/src/<module path>.py; anything else raises "Unexpected file in bundle". 6.1.0 accepted only flat files under frontend/dist; master allows nested paths [M*]. extension/extension.json (Data-Bound Documents) Gotcha: a .supx cannot install dependencies Only files matched by include are copied, and the host imports only from the in-memory bundle. [project] dependencies in the backend pyproject.toml are installed by nothing. python-pptx, python-docx, an HTTP client and every other library must be preinstalled in the web, worker and MCP images. This is why Data-Bound Documents is a "thin .supx, fat wheel" design: the superset-databound-docs wheel holds the engine and the bundle holds only the Superset wiring. Gotcha: dependencies and permissions are not enforced A grep of master finds no consumer of the manifest's dependencies or permissions lists. Authorization must come from FAB permissions on the extension's API classes and MCP tools.

Every public function or class in superset_core is a stub that raises NotImplementedError until the host overwrites the module attribute in initialize_core_api_dependencies() (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:318-333) and initialize_core_mcp_dependencies() (apache/superset: superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py:375). Two consequences: Import superset_core decorators inside the extension's modules, which are imported after injection. A library imported earlier (for example from superset_config.py) would bind the stubs. Models and DAOs are replaced by the host's: superset_core.common.models.Chart becomes superset.models.slice.Slice, Dataset becomes SqlaTable, Dashboard becomes superset.models.dashboard.Dashboard (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:82-125). Host DAOs apply access base filters evaluated against the current Flask user (apache/superset: superset/daos/chart.py:47, superset/daos/dashboard.py:505, superset/daos/dataset.py:80).

Decorator Module What registration does Availability @api(id, name, description=None, resource_name=None) on a RestApi subclass superset_core.rest_api.decorators In extension context the route base becomes /extensions/{publisher}/{name} plus /{resource_name}, the id becomes extensions.{publisher}.{name}.{id}, and the class is registered immediately with appbuilder.add_api and appbuilder._add_permission (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:179-227) [6.1] @tool(func_or_name=None, *, name=None, description=None, tags=None, protect=True, class_permission_name=None, method_permission_name=None, annotations=None), usable bare or called superset_core.mcp.decorators (:51-61) Name prefixed extensions.{publisher}.{name}.{tool}; wrapped in mcp_auth_hook when protect=True; added to the FastMCP singleton (apache/superset: superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py:145-271) [6.1] @prompt(func_or_name=None, *, name=None, title=None, description=None, tags: set[str] or None=None, protect=True) superset_core.mcp.decorators (:130-138) Same prefixing and auth [6.1] @task(name=None, scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=None, subscription_policy=None) superset_core.tasks.decorators (:32-37) Task type prefixed extensions.{publisher}.{name}.; registered in TaskRegistry (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:147-175) [6.1]; subscription_policy [M] @semantic_layer(id, name, description=None) superset_core.semantic_layers Registers a semantic layer provider [M], behind SEMANTIC_LAYERS With @api(id="dbd_api", name="Data-Bound Documents API", resource_name="v1") inside databound.docgen, every route lives under /extensions/databound/docgen/v1. That is the REST base path used throughout Part VII. Note it is not under /api/v1. backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py (minimal skeleton) Gotcha: extension APIs inherit csrf_exempt = True RestApi subclasses FAB's BaseApi directly (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/rest_api/api.py:21-29), not Superset's BaseSupersetApiMixin, which sets csrf_exempt = False (apache/superset: superset/views/base_api.py:340-341). FAB's BaseApi declares csrf_exempt = True (seen in FAB 5.0.2; not re-checked for 5.2 and later). Master's UPDATING.md documents the same inheritance for extension storage routes (apache/superset: UPDATING.md:109-123). Set csrf_exempt = False on any API with cookie-authenticated state changes. Gotcha: @tool

superset_core.extensions.context.get_context() returns .extension (the manifest) and .storage.ephemeral / .storage.persistent (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/context.py:52-119). Persistent storage is a table extension_storage with 1 MB values and a 100 MB quota per extension. Gotcha: backend context appears to exist only during import The host sets the extension ContextVar in one place, around eager_import(entrypoint) (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:686). Storage accessors resolve the extension id from that variable on every call (apache/superset: superset/extensions/storage/utils.py:84-97) and raise when it is unset. Inside a REST handler, an MCP tool or a GTF task body, get_context() therefore appears to fail (inferred from source, not exercised). Data-Bound Documents captures EXTENSION_ID = "databound.docgen" as a constant at import and keeps its own dbd_ tables instead of extension storage.

The npm package is mostly type stubs; the host assigns real implementations to window.superset in ExtensionsStartup (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/extensions/ExtensionsStartup.tsx:56-67). The only view locations the host defines are SQL Lab's: apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/SqlLab/contributions.ts:40-50 Location Rendered by Kind Props Availability sqllab.leftSidebar SqlLab/components/TableExploreTree/index.tsx:441-442 menu none [6.1] sqllab.rightSidebar SqlLab/components/AppLayout/index.tsx:101, 141 view none [6.1] sqllab.panels SqlLab/components/SouthPane/index.tsx:110, 225, 244 view and menu none [6.1] sqllab.editor SqlLab/components/SqlEditorTopBar/index.tsx:45-46 menu none [6.1] sqllab.statusBar SqlLab/components/StatusBar/index.tsx:41, 47 view none [6.1] sqllab.results SqlLab/components/ResultSet/index.tsx:493-494 menu none [6.1] sqllab.queryHistory SqlLab/components/QueryHistory/index.tsx:125 menu none [6.1] chat (singleton) ChatFloatingHost, ChatPanelHost in App.tsx:248-264 trigger and panel none [M] Views render with no props at all: resolveView(id) wraps the component in an ErrorBoundary and passes nothing (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/core/views/index.ts:87-97), and toolbar menus call commands.executeCommand(command.id) with no arguments (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/components/PanelToolbar/index.tsx:59, 85). GTF is Superset's engine for long-running work, behind GLOBAL_TASK_FRAMEWORK (default False, apache/superset: superset/config.py:909). Data-Bound Documents runs every generation, refresh, render and trigger run as a GTF task.

apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/decorators.py:32-37 TaskWrapper.__call__(*args, **kwargs) runs synchronously; TaskWrapper.schedule(*args, options: TaskOptions | None = None, **kwargs) enqueues and returns a PENDING task. The function's return value is discarded; output goes to the task payload. get_context() returns a TaskContext inside a running task, with update_task(progress=None, payload=None) ([6.1]; the keyword immediate= is [M]), on_abort(handler), on_cleanup(handler) and, on master, get_dependency_payloads(). TaskScope: PRIVATE (default, per user), SHARED (dedup across users, requires a task_key), SYSTEM (admin only). TaskStatus: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILURE, ABORTING, ABORTED, TIMED_OUT (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:30-51). TaskOptions(task_key, task_name, timeout) on 6.1; master adds depends_on for DAGs (types.py:138-193) [M*]. progress accepts a float 0 to 1, an integer count, or a (current, total) tuple. On master, payload merges into the existing payload; the 6.1.0 docs said each call replaced it, so write the full payload each time to be portable.

TaskManager.submit_task(...) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:518-611) creates or joins a task row under a distributed lock, keyed by type, scope and task_key. Only for a new row, it enqueues the single generic Celery task: execute_task.delay(task_uuid=str(task.uuid), task_type=task_type, args=args, kwargs=kwargs) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:582). The Celery task tasks.execute (apache/superset: superset/tasks/scheduler.py:396-512) loads the row, builds a TaskContext, starts the timeout timer, looks up the executor in TaskRegistry (:584) and runs it inside use_context(ctx) (:595). Two design choices follow directly. First, task_key = sha256(user_id, template@version, canonical(context), prompt, parameters) makes a double click join the same job. Second, because every GTF task travels as tasks.execute with the GTF type in the task_type keyword, a Celery router function can send Data-Bound Documents work to its own databound_docs queue without any Superset change (behavior on 6.1 is a prototype gate in Roadmap). Gotcha: GTF does not switch users TaskContext.__init__ (apache/superset: superset/tasks/context.py:60-125) does not set g.user. Superset's own GTF task passes user_id and guest_token as arguments and wraps its body in with override_user(_resolve_user(user_id, guest_token), force=False): (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175, 273-297). A generation task that skips this runs DAO filters, permission checks and RLS without the requester. Gotcha: positional @task arguments break The stub's first positional parameter is name, but the host implementation's first positional parameter is func (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:57-79). Always use keywords: @task(name="generate_document", scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=900). The host also rejects task functions with parameters named ctx or options (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:165-173). backend/src/databound/docgen/tasks.py (skeleton)

TaskRestApi (resource_name = "task", class_permission_name = "Task") is registered only when the flag is on at startup (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:342-345; class at apache/superset: superset/tasks/api.py:60-95): Route Method Availability /api/v1/task/ (rison q), /_info, /related/<col> GET [6.1] /api/v1/task/<task_uuid> GET [6.1] /api/v1/task/<task_uuid>/status GET [6.1] /api/v1/task/status_changes?cursor=&task_type= GET [M] /api/v1/task/<task_uuid>/cancel POST [6.1] The Task List UI under Manage shows and cancels DBD jobs for free. Abort is cooperative: registering on_abort makes the task abortable and starts polling every TASK_ABORT_POLLING_DEFAULT_INTERVAL = 10 seconds, or uses Redis pub/sub when DISTRIBUTED_COORDINATION_CONFIG is set. Master adds heartbeats (GTF_TASK_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 15) and orphan reaping. GTF has no scheduler GTF runs work now, or after prerequisites on master. It has no cron, no run_at and no retry policy (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:143-150 lists them as future work). Recurring work needs a Celery beat entry in the operator's CELERY_CONFIG.beat_schedule, which no superset_core API can add. Data-Bound Documents ships one beat task, databound_docs.trigger_tick, documented as a required configuration line.

superset mcp run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5008 (apache/superset: superset/cli/mcp.py:28-41) starts a FastMCP server inside a Flask app context. It is an optional extra: fastmcp>=3.1.0,<4.0 in 6.1.0, fastmcp>=4.1.0,<5.0 on master (apache/superset: pyproject.toml:202-203). Master ships 79 tools; 6.1.0 shipped 24.

docs.t: 3.2 Identity: the main 6.1 versus master difference
docs.x: Master. get_user_from_request() (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:889-950) resolves, in order: a JWT bearer mapped to a username by MCP_USER_RESOLVER (default prefers preferred_username, then username, email, sub; apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:937-967); a FAB API key (sst_ prefix); MCP_DEV_USERNAME; then g.user from external middleware. A JWT that resolves to no user fails closed. 6.1.0. Only g.user (set by external middleware) and then MCP_DEV_USERNAME are consulted. MCP_AUTH_ENABLED and MCP_JWT_* authenticate the transport, but every call still runs as the dev user unless middleware sets g.user. RBAC: with MCP_RBAC_ENABLED = True (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:150), check_tool_permission verifies can_<method> on <class_permission_name> before a tool runs (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:397-440). An extension tool declared with class_permission_name="DataBoundDocs" gets the same check; the method defaults to write when the tags contain mutate, else read. Gotcha: never call MCP tool functions in-process from a worker Without a request context, _setup_user_context pops g.user (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:1107-1121), and MCP_DEV_USERNAME outranks g.user in resolution. A worker that imports and calls a tool function directly can end up running as the dev user. Data-Bound Documents calls MCP only over the transport with a short-lived per-user JWT (master, agent planner only), and its own data path never touches MCP. Gotcha: MCP responses are capped Master caps responses at 50,000 bytes (MCP_RESPONSE_SIZE_CONFIG, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:499-512); 6.1.0 used a 25,000-token estimate. That is enough for planning and far too small to carry a deck's data. Final numbers always come from the Binding Resolver. On 6.1, the design therefore uses only the pipeline and template planners, and DBD's own MCP tools refuse to mutate or read data when the resolved user is the configured dev user unless DATABOUND_DOCS["MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER"] (a Data-Bound Documents setting, not a Superset one) is set for development.

Please save the chart again." when the chart has none (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:180). On master, ?filters_dashboard_id=<int> merges the dashboard's saved default native filters in scope for that chart (:191-219) and adds a dashboard_filters object to the response listing each filter's id, name, status (applied, not_applied, not_applied_uses_default_to_first_item_prequery) and column.

ChartDataQueryContextSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1677-1770) has, on 6.1.0, exactly datasource, queries, custom_cache_timeout, force, result_type, result_format and form_data. Master adds force_nonce, async_mode and tab_id. A dataset-source binding in Data-Bound Documents compiles to a payload like this: QueryContext for 'revenue by month, last quarter, EMEA' (6.1 compatible) QueryObject fields the design relies on (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1388-1675): columns (with the BASE_AXIS adhoc column for temporal x), metrics (saved metric names or SIMPLE adhoc metrics), filters (ChartDataFilterSchema; operators include ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, LIKE, ILIKE, IN, NOT IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, TEMPORAL_RANGE), extras, orderby, row_limit, series_limit, time_offsets and post_processing. Registered post-processing operations (apache/superset: superset/utils/pandas_postprocessing/__init__.py:49-67) include aggregate, boxplot, compare, contribution, cum, diff, histogram, pivot, rank, rename, resample, rolling, select, sort and flatten. Keeping a chart's own post_processing list means shares, pivots and cumulative sums are computed server-side exactly as the dashboard computes them. result_type values (apache/superset: superset/common/chart_data.py:20-48) are columns, full, query, results, samples, timegrains, post_processed and drill_detail. query returns compiled SQL without running it, which is useful for an optional SQL appendix; post_processed applies the table and pivot shaping the frontend would apply. result_format is csv, json, xlsx, and on master arrow.

Each entry of result (or of ChartDataCommand(...).run()["queries"] in-process) carries colnames, coltypes (GenericDataType: NUMERIC=0, STRING=1, TEMPORAL=2, BOOLEAN=3, MULTI_VALUE=4 [M]), data (records; temporal values as epoch milliseconds), rowcount, applied_filters, rejected_filters, cache_key, cached_dttm, queried_dttm, is_cached, query, status, error, detected_currency, from_dttm and to_dttm (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1807-1940). Every one of these feeds a Provenance field in the Document Spec: "data as of", "filter not applied to this chart", "Top 10 of 47", currency resolution.

docs.t: 4.4 Caching, limits and the async hazard
docs.x: Cache. Results are cached in the data cache, NullCache by default (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1532). force: true bypasses it. The cache key includes RLS through get_rls_cache_key (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304), so two users with different RLS never share rows. Limits. ROW_LIMIT = 50000 (apache/superset: superset/config.py:186) is the default when row_limit is 0 or null, and SQL_MAX_ROW = 100000 (:1853) is the hard cap. A slide wants 1 to 500 aggregated rows, so every binding sets an explicit row_limit. Async on 6.1.0. With GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES on, every cacheable JSON request to the chart data endpoint returns 202, and the follow-up requires the async JWT cookie; a bearer-token client gets 401. On master, async is opt-in per request through async_mode. Gotcha: do not call the chart data HTTP endpoint from a worker On 6.1 with GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES, a server-to-server call can get 202 and then 401. Alerts and Reports work around this by logging an executor in with cookies and calling the endpoint over HTTP. Data-Bound Documents instead calls the same command in-process, which has no transport, no cookie and no credential.

The command the endpoint wraps is ChartDataCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:36). Its validate() calls self._query_context.raise_for_access() before validating queries (:107-108), so a caller-supplied filter is never rendered for a resource the user cannot read. Master's dashboard Excel export is the reference implementation of "every chart on a dashboard, with live filters, as the user": it stamps form_data, applies the filter context, sets g.form_data = json_body so Jinja macros such as filter_values work (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:225), loads the schema and runs the command (:191-232) [M]. databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (excerpt) ChartDataCommand, ChartDataQueryContextSchema and override_user are internal Superset APIs: superset_core exposes no chart-data API. All of them live in one module, the Superset Adapter, with contract tests per Superset version. A public run_chart_query in superset_core is the first item of the upstream SIP in Roadmap.

A chart (Slice) stores params (the Explore form data) and query_context (a full QueryContext). The query context is produced client-side by each viz plugin's buildQuery and saved when the chart is saved in Explore, so old, imported or API-created charts can have none. Explore backfills it when a user with write access opens the chart (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/explore/components/ExploreChartPanel/index.tsx:235-254). Master adds a server-side rebuild, build_query_context_from_form_data(form_data, datasource, viz_type=None) (apache/superset: superset/common/form_data_query_context.py:1801), with explicit adapters for tables, every ECharts timeseries type, pie, big number, pivot, histogram, box plot, waterfall, gantt, treemap, sunburst, bubble and maps, and a generic top-N fallback [M]. It is absent from the 6.1.0 tree. Situation Master 6.1 fallback Chart has a saved query context use it (follow: live reloads it each run) same Chart has none rebuild from params with a provenance warning rebuilt_from_form_data binding status error with the remediation "Chart has no saved query context: open and save it in Explore", mirroring apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:180 Gotcha: the stored query context is a snapshot of params If someone edits params through the API without re-saving in Explore, query_context can drift from params. The dashboard renders from query_context, so the design prefers it and treats params only as a fallback.

Dashboard endpoints [6.1] include GET /api/v1/dashboard/<id_or_slug> (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/api.py:738), /datasets (:831), /tabs (:919), /charts (:981) and /<id_or_slug>/embedded (:3235-3362). The /datasets response returns, per dataset, columns, metrics, verbose_map, column_formats, main_dttm_col and currency_code_column: everything a renderer needs for labels and formats in one call. position_json is a flat dict of components, each {type, id, children, parents, meta}, with types ROOT, GRID, HEADER, ROW, COLUMN, CHART, MARKDOWN, TABS, TAB, DIVIDER and DYNAMIC. Grid width is 12 columns. CHART.meta holds chartId, width, height and sliceNameOverride; MARKDOWN.meta.code holds author narrative. The Data Digest walks this tree depth-first in layout order (master has get_charts_in_layout_order at apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/layout.py:69-84, which DBD ports for 6.1), turning tabs into section hints and Markdown into context, treated as untrusted data. json_metadata (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/schemas.py:200-235) contains native_filter_configuration, chart_configuration (cross-filter scoping), color_scheme, label_colors, shared_label_colors, map_label_colors, color_scheme_domain and cross_filters_enabled. One native filter entry looks like this (shape from superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/query/types/Dashboard.ts:70-93): native_filter_configuration entry (illustrative values)

Native filters publish a data mask {extraFormData, filterState, ownState}. Server-side constants define how extraFormData merges into a query (apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-234): append keys adhoc_filters, filters, interactive_groupby, interactive_highlight, interactive_drilldown, custom_form_data; override keys granularity_sqla (mapped to granularity), time_column, time_grain, time_range, time_grain_sqla; extra override keys relative_start and relative_end. Function Works on Location Availability merge_extra_form_data(form_data) form data, before buildQuery apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1184-1260 [6.1] get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id, chart_id, *, active_data_mask=None) -> DashboardFilterContext loads filters, checks dashboard access, computes scope, resolves values from the live mask or the saved defaults apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272 (dataclass at :60) [M] apply_dashboard_filter_context(query_context, extra_form_data) an already-built query context apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:365 [M] On 6.1 Data-Bound Documents uses its own port, databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61. It reads native_filter_configuration, uses chartsInScope when present and otherwise scope.rootPath and scope.excluded, takes each value from the permalink's data mask or from defaultDataMask, appends filters with isExtra: true, and overrides the time keys. It deliberately does not implement cascading parents, requiredFirst or defaultToFirstItem pre-queries; a binding affected by one records a rejected filter with reason unsupported_on_6.1 instead of guessing.

The permalink key is stored in DashboardContext.permalink_key, so a refresh reproduces the selection long after the filter-state cache entry expires. chartStates is also present in the 6.1.0 tag's DashboardPermalinkState (checked against the tag source; 6.1.0 types urlParams as list[tuple[str, str]]). docs.t: Step 6: Datasets, metrics and semantic layers
docs.x: GET /api/v1/dataset/<id_or_uuid> [6.1] returns main_dttm_col, currency_code_column, template_params, and per column column_name, verbose_name, type, type_generic, is_dttm, groupby, filterable, advanced_data_type, description; per metric metric_name, verbose_name, expression, d3format, currency ({symbol, symbolPosition}), description and warning_text (apache/superset: superset/datasets/api.py:331-420). These fields drive three parts of the design: The Binding Registry accepts a planner proposal only if every metric is a saved metric of the dataset (or a SIMPLE aggregate over a numeric column) and every dimension is a column with groupby = True; temporal dimensions must have is_dttm. Formatting follows Superset's precedence: the metric's d3format and currency, then the chart's y_axis_format, number_format or currency_format, then SMART_NUMBER. AUTO currency resolves from the result's detected_currency. Data exposure policies use advanced_data_type and column names to default PII columns to "never shown to the LLM". GET /api/v1/dataset/<id_or_uuid>/related_objects (apache/superset: superset/datasets/api.py:1351) lists the charts and dashboards using a dataset, which helps fan out "this dataset changed" events. On master, the headless POST /api/v1/datasource/<type>/<id>/query (DatasourceQuerySchema, apache/superset: superset/datasource/schemas.py:165-260) accepts metrics, dimensions, filters, time_range, time_column, time_grain, limit and order and validates names against saved definitions; it is the cleanest "semantic" contract and is what the dataset binding source mirrors in a 6.1-compatible QueryObject. Semantic layers (@semantic_layer, SemanticView.get_table(...), apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/semantic_layers/view.py:131-214) are master only and behind SEMANTIC_LAYERS (apache/superset: superset/config.py:776); they back the semantic source kind in v2.

Path What it checks Availability Role in the design POST /api/v1/sqllab/execute/ (apache/superset: superset/sqllab/api.py:546) DML gating, raise_for_access(..., force_dataset_match=True) on master [6.1] not used: CSRF applies, results are not cached by chart semantics, raw SQL is a large attack surface Database.execute(sql, QueryOptions) and execute_async (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/common/models.py:87-171) Jinja, SQL_QUERY_MUTATOR, disallowed functions and tables, DML only if allow_dml, RLS by AST rewrite, SQL_MAX_ROW, caching [6.1] opt-in sql bindings only get_sqlglot_dialect(database) (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/queries/query.py:38-48) dialect lookup [6.1] SELECT-only parse of opt-in SQL QueryOptions fields are catalog, schema, limit, timeout_seconds, template_params, cache: CacheOptions(timeout, force_refresh) and dry_run; QueryResult carries status, statements (each with data as a DataFrame, row_count, truncated), query_id and is_cached (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/queries/types.py:49-130). Gotcha: Database.execute does not check datasource access A grep of superset/sql/execution/ finds no raise_for_access or can_access call. The executor applies RLS but does not itself check that the user may query the referenced tables (inferred from source). Data-Bound Documents therefore parses opt-in SQL with sqlglot, rejects anything that is not a single SELECT, and calls security_manager.raise_for_access(database=..., sql=..., catalog=..., schema=..., force_dataset_match=True) before Database.execute, mirroring MCP execute_sql.

FAB permissions. @api registers the API class and its permission view immediately (appbuilder._add_permission), so class_permission_name = "DataBoundDocs" with method_permission_name produces can_read, can_generate, can_write, can_refresh, can_schedule, can_manage_templates, can_share_snapshot and can_admin on the DataBoundDocs view, assignable to roles in the normal Security UI. Object access. raise_for_access(dashboard=None, chart=None, database=None, datasource=None, query=None, query_context=None, table=None, sql=None, catalog=None, schema=None, template_params=None, force_dataset_match=False, ...) (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:5199) raises SupersetSecurityException on denial; can_access_datasource (:2673) is the boolean form. Chart data is gated by dataset-level access, so a user can render a chart in a document exactly when they could see it in Superset. Access-filtered DAOs. Host DAOs apply ChartFilter, DashboardAccessFilter and DatasourceFilter for the current user, so listing candidates for the digest never reveals objects the user cannot see.

get_rls_filters(table) (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6110) returns the RowLevelSecurityFilter rows for the current user's subjects (master: users, roles and groups; 6.1.0: roles only). REGULAR filters apply to matching subjects; BASE filters apply to everyone except them; filters sharing a group_key are ORed and different groups are ANDed. SqlaTable.get_sqla_row_level_filters(...) (apache/superset: superset/connectors/sqla/models.py:1171) injects them as SQL predicates while the query is built, and clauses are Jinja-rendered as the executing user. Guest RLS rules from a guest token are added for guests. The design consequence is simple and strict: any path that ends in ChartDataCommand with the right g.user gets RLS automatically, and the framework never opens its own connection to an analytics database. Its only job is to make g.user correct, which it does with override_user(user, force=False) (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1633).

Dashboards have no server-side composition. Native filters are applied in the browser, so dashboards can be delivered only as PNG or PDF; tabular formats are guarded by self._report_schedule.chart and ... (execute.py:1675-1677). docs.t: Step 1: The interpretation this architecture serves
docs.x: The request was for "a common framework" that gives Apache Superset the workflow Presenton gives PowerPoint: write a prompt, pick a template, get a finished artifact. The same flow should produce documents, text and pages, run on the fly and on events, use dynamic data, and never use screenshots. This design adopts the following reading of that request, and every component below exists to satisfy one part of it. Build one common, output-agnostic generation framework that turns three inputs into four kinds of output: Inputs: a prompt, a chosen template, and a Superset data context. The data context is any of: a dashboard with its live native-filter state, saved charts, datasets with their saved metrics, a semantic view [M], or a SQL Lab query. Outputs: (a) PowerPoint decks (PPTX); (b) documents (DOCX, PDF, Markdown); (c) text (narratives, executive summaries, emails, Slack posts, alert briefs); (d) web pages (interactive HTML reports and, in v2, generated Superset dashboards). Triggers: on demand (a button or chat message in Superset, a REST call, an MCP tool call) or by events (cron schedules, Superset Alerts firing a webhook, data freshness changes, chart or dashboard definition changes, external webhooks). Three data rules are non-negotiable: Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query executed with the requesting user's permissions and row-level security (RLS). Scheduled runs use an explicitly recorded run-as user. Data elements are rendered natively: editable PPTX and DOCX charts with an embedded workbook, real tables, real text runs, vector SVG on the web. No Superset UI page is ever captured as pixels. Every artifact is re-runnable. A refresh re-executes the queries and replaces the data in place. The design keeps Presenton's stage shape (outline, layout structure, schema-constrained content, hydration, export; see Standard generation pipeline) but changes one thing at its core. Presenton asks the LLM for chart categories and series[].values (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534) and copies them into the slide (presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1367-1432). In Data-Bound Documents the LLM never produces a number. It picks bindings from menus Superset has validated and writes prose that cites facts by token. Numbers enter an artifact only through deterministic code.

Each principle rules out a whole family of alternative designs. When you modify the system, check your change against this list first. Superset is the data plane. All data access goes through ChartDataCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:36), or through Database.execute for the narrow SQL case, inside a Superset process with g.user set to the right user. The framework never opens its own connection to an analytics database and never calls Superset's chart-data HTTP endpoint from a worker. The agent proposes, the engine disposes. The LLM outputs structure, binding choices from validated menus, and prose with tokens. Every number, label and chart series is produced by deterministic code. A binding exists only if the Binding Registry accepted it. The LLM can name only ids the registry issued, as JSON Schema enums, so it cannot invent a query. One spec, many renderers. The same DocumentSpec renders to a deck, a document, a page and a text brief. Thin .supx, fat wheel. A .supx bundle carries only the extension's own .py files and cannot install dependencies (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:225-275). The framework therefore ships as a preinstalled wheel plus a small extension that holds only the Superset wiring. One version-sniffing Superset Adapter. Every import of non-public Superset code lives in one module, databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py, which detects capabilities at import time. Fail closed, render honestly. A forbidden or failed binding becomes a visible placeholder and removes the narrative that depends on it. Nothing ever falls back to a picture of a chart. Gotcha: why not call /api/v1/chart/data from the worker It looks simpler to have a worker call Superset's REST chart-data endpoint with a token. On 6.1 with GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES on, that endpoint answers JSON requests with 202 and then requires the async JWT cookie, returning 401 without it. A bearer-token worker cannot read the data. Alerts and Reports work around this by logging the executor in with machine-auth cookies, which is exactly the "executor's data, not the recipient's" model this design avoids. In-process ChartDataCommand under override_user has neither problem.

The framework has sixteen named components. The table gives each one's single responsibility, where it runs and where its code lives. The sub-steps after the table group them by the job they do. Component Responsibility Runs in Package or module Document Spec (DocumentSpec) Output-agnostic, data-bound description of one immutable document version everywhere databound_docs.spec Context Capture Turns "what the user is looking at" into ids plus a durable dashboard permalink browser, web extension frontend plus the POST /documents handler Data Digest Deterministic, token-budgeted summary of the context that the LLM is allowed to see worker databound_docs.planner.digest Planner (pipeline, agent, template) Decides sections, layouts and which bindings fill which slots worker (GTF task) databound_docs.planner Superset Adapter The only module that imports Superset internals; version-sniffed at import web, worker, MCP databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py Binding Registry The only way a binding enters a document: validates names, access, shape and limits, assigns b_* ids worker, web, MCP databound_docs.binder.registry Binding Resolver Runs every DataBinding in-process through ChartDataCommand as the right user and records provenance worker, web (live pages), MCP databound_docs.binder plus the Superset Adapter Fact Engine Derives facts (totals, changes, ranks, labels) from resolved rows with pure functions everywhere databound_docs.facts Narrative Writer One schema-constrained LLM call per section; writes text with fact tokens only worker databound_docs.planner.writer Narrative Verifier Deterministic checks on tokens, numerals, entities, direction and length, plus a repair loop worker, web databound_docs.planner.verify Renderers PPTX Renderer, DOCX Renderer, HTML Renderer, PDF Printer, Text Renderer: resolved spec to native files worker (PDF optionally in a sidecar) databound_docs.render DrawingML Chart Writer Writes raw c:chartSpace XML for charts python-pptx cannot create (combo, emulations) worker databound_docs.render.drawingml Template Registry Versioned templates with data slots, PPTX and DOCX masters, importer web, worker databound_docs.templates plus table dbd_template Trigger Service Schedules, alert webhooks, freshness sentinels, definition-change listeners, external webhooks beat, worker, web databound_docs.triggers plus the extension Document Studio Chat

docs.t: 3.1 Data plane: Context Capture, Superset Adapter, Binding Registry, Binding Resolver
docs.x: These four components are the reason the framework can promise "live data with the user's permissions". Context Capture runs synchronously in POST /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/documents. It checks can_generate on DataBoundDocs, loads each dashboard through the access-filtered DAO, and calls security_manager.raise_for_access(dashboard=...). If the request carries a short-lived native_filters_key, it reads the data mask with GetFilterStateCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/filter_state/get.py:30) and converts it into a durable permalink with CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand(dashboard_id, state) (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/permalink/create.py:45). The result is a DataContext that can be replayed months later. Superset Adapter (databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py) is the only module that imports Superset internals: ChartDataCommand, ChartDataQueryContextSchema, override_user (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1633), the filter-context helpers, the form_data rebuild, the permalink and filter-state commands, and the guest-token helpers. It sniffs capabilities at import time and exposes a stable internal interface (as_user, run_query_context, apply_dashboard_filters, chart_query_context). Building the Superset extension walks through the file. Binding Registry is called by every planner strategy, by chat edits and by MCP. It loads the chart or dataset through access-filtered DAOs, re-checks can_access_datasource, verifies that every metric is a saved metric (or a simple aggregate over a real numeric column) and every dimension a groupby=True column, caps row_limit, and only then issues an id b_<slug>. Binding Resolver compiles each binding into a query context JSON, applies the filter merge (dashboard filters, binding filters, parameters, time overrides), sets g.form_data, loads it through ChartDataQueryContextSchema, calls ChartDataCommand(qc).validate() (which runs raise_for_access first, apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108) and .run(). It then shapes rows and fills a Provenance record. Data-bound slide model specifies every field. The resolver follows the same recipe as master's dashboard Excel export, which replays each chart's saved query context as the requesting user with live dashboard filters: apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:200-231 (excerpt)

docs.t: 3.2 Language plane: Data Digest, Planner, Narrative Writer, Narrative Verifier
docs.x: These components are the only ones that talk to an LLM, and each one is fenced so that the LLM cannot affect numbers. Data Digest builds everything the LLM may see: dashboard inventory in layout order, chart and dataset metadata, and profiles (not rows) of each candidate binding, formatted and labeled with candidate fact ids. It is bounded by DATA_POLICY.max_digest_tokens (default 12,000) and an exposure level (metadata_only, aggregates by default, samples). The digest preview endpoint POST /context/digest returns exactly this JSON so a user can see "what the AI will see". Planner has three strategies that all produce the same Plan object whose bindings are always registry ids: Strategy Availability How it plans pipeline (default) [6.1], [M] Fixed stages with strict JSON schemas: outline, deterministic layout fit (with an optional LLM tie-break), section writing. Binding proposals are enums in the outline schema agent (opt-in) [M] only Tool-calling loop over a read-only MCP allowlist, ending in submit_plan. Needs per-user MCP identity, which 6.1 lacks template (no LLM) [6.1], [M] The template declares fixed bindings and deterministic sentences. For air-gapped or regulated deployments and scheduled briefs Narrative Writer makes one call per section. It receives the section intent, the text fields with character budgets, and a FACTS table restricted to that section. It never receives rows. Its response schema has a regex that forbids digits, %, $ and braces except inside valid tokens. Narrative Verifier is deterministic: token validity, no literal numbers or number words, no literal category names (the entity scan), direction words that agree with the sign of the cited change fact, superlatives only next to rank facts, and length. Violations go back to the writer at most twice, then the field is replaced by a deterministic sentence and marked fallback. All LLM calls go through call_structured() on an LLMProvider protocol (openai_compatible, anthropic, bedrock, vertex). Roles (planner, writer, verifier) map to profiles in DATABOUND_DOCS["LLM"], and allowed_hosts restricts egress. Generation flow gives every prompt and schema.

docs.t: 3.3 Output plane: Renderers and the DrawingML Chart Writer
docs.x: Every renderer reads a resolved DocumentSpec version and its BindingResult rows. None of them re-queries unless asked to refresh, and none of them loads a Superset UI page. Renderer Library What it produces PPTX Renderer python-pptx 1.0.2 (MIT) Native charts with an embedded XlsxWriter workbook, native tables, KPI groups, token runs, speaker notes, the /customXml/dbd-manifest.json part. Refresh through Chart.replace_data DrawingML Chart Writer lxml over python-pptx's OPC layer Combo charts (c:barChart plus c:lineChart on a secondary axis) and emulations (waterfall, funnel, bullet) DOCX Renderer python-docx 1.2.0 (MIT) Styled paragraphs, native tables, DrawingML chart parts (prototype gate G5) or vector SVG from rows HTML Renderer Jinja templates, ECharts (live pages), vl-convert-python (static SVG) Live pages that resolve as the viewer, static HTML with embedded JSON snapshots PDF Printer Playwright Chromium page.pdf() on a local file (or a printer sidecar, or WeasyPrint) Vector PDF printed from DBD's own static HTML, network disabled Text Renderer plain Python Markdown, plain text, email HTML, Slack mrkdwn, alert briefs Native rendering, no screenshots covers each renderer in detail, including the d3-to-Excel number format mapping and the viz_type matrix.

docs.t: 3.4 Lifecycle plane: Template Registry, Trigger Service, Document Studio, DBD Extension
docs.x: Template Registry stores immutable template versions in dbd_template: JSON layouts derived from Presenton Template v2 with data slots, plus optional PPTX and DOCX masters in object storage. Masters are imported deterministically from shape names such as slot:chart:trend (no vision model). Built-ins ship in the wheel: tpl_exec_review, tpl_dashboard_walkthrough, tpl_analytical_report, tpl_interactive_report, tpl_kpi_brief, tpl_weekly_email, alert_brief. Trigger Service covers the five trigger types cron, alert_webhook, freshness, definition_change and external_webhook. GTF has no cron, so a plain Celery beat task databound_docs.trigger_tick runs every minute and schedules run_trigger GTF tasks with a deduplicating task_key. Scheduling and live refresh has the details. Document Studio is the UI. On master it lives in the global chat slot (chat.registerChat, apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/chat/index.ts:76-80), which is visible on dashboards and Explore. On 6.1 it is a SQL Lab panel at sqllab.panels plus a standalone Studio page served by the extension. DBD Extension (databound.docgen) is the wiring: the @api REST class DataBoundDocsApi, the GTF @task functions, the guarded @tool and @prompt registrations, and the frontend contributions. Gotcha: there is no dashboard or Explore contribution area The new extension framework renders contributed views only in SQL Lab, plus the global chat slot on master. The legacy keys dashboard.nav.right, dashboard.slice.header.menu and explore.chart.header live in a module-local registry inside the host bundle that a .supx cannot reach. Data-Bound Documents covers the gap with the chat slot [M], the Studio page and SQL Lab panel [6.1], and an optional databound-docs-ui-overrides npm package for deployments that build their own Superset frontend. Upstream slots are proposed in the Roadmap.

Note what is missing from the diagram: there is no separate generation server, no second web origin, and no arrow from any renderer back to a Superset page. The only path to the analytics databases goes through the Superset Adapter.

docs.t: Step 4: Packaging, thin bundle and fat wheel
docs.x: A .supx is a zip of manifest.json, frontend/dist/<file> and backend/src/<module>.py. Superset imports the backend files from memory through InMemoryFinder; nothing installs [project] dependencies. python-pptx, python-docx, an HTTP client and the renderers therefore cannot ride in the bundle. The framework ships as two artifacts built from one repository: the superset-databound-docs wheel, preinstalled in the web, worker and MCP images, and the databound-docgen-<version>.supx bundle, dropped into EXTENSIONS_PATH. The repository has three top-level folders: core/ (the wheel, package databound_docs with spec, planner, binder, facts, format, render, templates, triggers, compat, llm, storage and db), extension/ (built with the superset-extensions CLI, backend modules entrypoint.py, api.py, tasks.py, tools.py, triggers.py and superset_adapter.py under databound/docgen/), and the optional ui-overrides/ npm package. Building the Superset extension walks through every file. The identifiers follow from publisher: "databound" and name: "docgen": Identifier Value Derived by Extension id databound.docgen publisher.name (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/types.py:38-84) Backend entrypoint databound.docgen.entrypoint the CLI build_manifest Module Federation name databound_docgen the CLI REST base path /extensions/databound/docgen/v1 @api(resource_name="v1") in extension context (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:189-207) GTF task types extensions.databound.docgen.<task> host task decorator prefixing (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:147-160) MCP tool names extensions.databound.docgen.<tool> host tool registration (apache/superset: superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py:123-142) Bundle file databound-docgen-<version>.supx superset-extensions bundle The core package databound_docs must not import Superset at module top level. That rule keeps the Fact Engine, the Narrative Verifier, the renderers and the spec testable without a Superset install, and it keeps the stub-binding problem away: superset_core decorators must be imported after the host has injected its implementations, which happens before the extension entrypoint is imported. Gotcha: two frontend bundles from one source 6.1 maps @apache-superset/core to window.superset through webpack externals, while master injects it through the Module Federation

There is no new service. "Runtime" means the databound_docs library executing inside Superset's own processes, which all build the app with create_app() and therefore all import the extension when ENABLE_EXTENSIONS is on in their config. Process DBD code loaded Role Superset web (gunicorn) .supx backend plus wheel REST API, Context Capture, synchronous text briefs, live page data, webhook receiver Celery worker, queue databound_docs same GTF tasks: digest, LLM calls, resolution, rendering Celery beat config only fires databound_docs.trigger_tick every minute MCP server (superset mcp run), optional .supx backend plus wheel dbd_* tools for external agents; on master also the tool plane for the agent planner PDF Printer Chromium (Playwright) in the worker image, or a printer sidecar prints DBD's own static HTML to vector PDF

All configuration lives in superset_config.py. Feature flags must be on in every process, because Superset registers APIs and imports extensions from the flag value at startup. superset_config.py (Data-Bound Documents section) DATABOUND_DOCS is read at call time from current_app.config, never at import time, so a library imported by superset_config.py itself does not freeze stale values.

docs.t: 5.2 Isolating long jobs on their own queue
docs.x: GTF enqueues every task through one generic Celery task, tasks.execute (apache/superset: superset/tasks/scheduler.py:396), passing the GTF type as a keyword: apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:582 (call shape) Celery accepts router functions in task_routes, so DBD can route on that keyword without any change to Superset: databound_docs/celery_routing.py Operators run at least one worker with -Q databound_docs and keep the default queue for reports, thumbnails and other GTF work. A 90-second LLM job then cannot starve a thumbnail. Whether the router sees task_type identically on 6.1 is covered by prototype gate G8; the fallback is a concurrency semaphore in the metadata database.

Install superset-databound-docs, python-pptx==1.0.2, python-docx==1.2.0, httpx, vl-convert-python, jsonschema and, optionally, playwright into the web, worker and MCP images. Copy the .supx into EXTENSIONS_PATH. Run superset dbd db-upgrade (DBD's own Alembic environment, version table dbd_alembic_version). Restart every process. Extension discovery happens only at startup. Run superset dbd doctor. It checks flags per process, installed packages, the beat entry and router, storage write access, the bundle variant, DATA_CACHE_CONFIG (warning on NullCache), and that MCP_DEV_USERNAME is unset when the agent strategy is used.
Five request paths cover every trigger. All of them converge on the same Binding Resolver call under a well-defined identity.

docs.t: 6.1 On-demand deck from a filtered dashboard
docs.x: This is the headline flow. The web request does only the synchronous part (access checks, filter capture, row inserts) and returns 202 in well under a second; everything else runs in one GTF task. Three details make this path robust: Deduplication. task_key = sha256(user_id, template_id@version, canonical(context), prompt, parameters), so a double click joins the same GTF task instead of starting a second one. Identity. GTF does not switch the executing user. The task receives user_id as an argument and wraps its body in override_user(user, force=False), the pattern of Superset's own execute_chart_query (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175). Events. Fine-grained events (outline.ready, binding.resolved, section.ready, artifact.ready) go to dbd_job_event and are served by long poll (GET /jobs/<id>/events?after=<seq>&wait=25). Coarse progress is mirrored into GTF with get_context().update_task(progress=(i, n), payload=...), so the built-in Task List shows it too. Gotcha: GTF runs your task as nobody in particular TaskContext.__init__ (apache/superset: superset/tasks/context.py:60) records the task UUID, abort and cleanup handlers and the timeout timer, and neither it nor the tasks.execute executor sets g.user. Superset's own async chart-data task says so in its docstring: "The GTF executor does not impersonate on its own" (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175). If a task body forgets override_user, DAO base filters, raise_for_access and RLS evaluate without the requester. Depending on configuration that either fails every query or, worse, runs with a broader identity. The as_user helper in the Superset Adapter is the only sanctioned way in, and it refuses an inactive or missing user.

kind: "text" with options.sync: true (and the MCP tool dbd_brief) runs steps 2 to 10 inline in the web request within a 20-second budget. If the budget runs out, the call falls back to the asynchronous path and returns 202. This is the "text on the fly" answer: a one-paragraph KPI brief from a dashboard needs one digest, one writer call and a handful of cached queries.

docs.t: 6.3 Live page opened by a viewer
docs.x: A page document is never a static file by default. The HTML shell loads a standalone bundle that calls GET /documents/<id>/render-model?live=1, and the server re-resolves every live binding as the viewer, under the viewer's own session. If the viewer's RLS fingerprint differs from the one the narrative was written under, tokens still re-resolve to the viewer's values, claim lint re-runs against the viewer's facts, and a failing narrative is replaced by deterministic sentences with a "Summary written for different data" notice. Because LLM prose holds no literal numbers or category names, the stored text itself leaks nothing. Security, RLS, auth explains the rule.

Events do not get a human identity, so every trigger row carries run_as_fk, and DBD re-validates that user before each run. The alert route uses Superset's own Alerts and Reports scheduler purely as a data-condition detector. The alert should use report_format = TEXT on a chart-scoped alert (6.1) or NONE (master), so Superset takes no screenshot for nothing. The webhook payload is unsigned and carries no identity or data, so DBD treats it as a signal only.

An external agent (or Superset's own chat surface) can drive the same framework through dbd_* tools registered with superset_core.mcp.decorators.tool and class_permission_name="DataBoundDocs". MCP responses carry ids, statuses, display strings and at most 10 preview rows, which respects master's 50 KB response cap (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:499-512; 6.1.0 instead caps responses at an estimated 25,000 tokens). The full data for an artifact is always fetched by the worker's own Binding Resolver, never moved through MCP. Gotcha: MCP on 6.1 is a single shared identity On 6.1, get_user_from_request() checks only g.user (set by external middleware) and then MCP_DEV_USERNAME (6.1.0 tag, superset/mcp_service/auth.py:176-230). There is no JWT-claims-to-user mapping, so every call runs as the dev user unless your deployment adds middleware. DBD's mutate and data tools refuse to run when the resolved user is the configured dev user, unless MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER is true. Per-user MCP (MCP_USER_RESOLVER, API keys) is [M], which is also why the agent planner is master only.
