Kind of state Store Why there Templates, documents, immutable versions, binding results (provenance), artifacts index, jobs, events, triggers, shares, data policy, audit dbd_* tables in the Superset metadata database (or DATABOUND_DOCS["DATABASE_URI"]) Extension persistent storage [M] is capped at 1 MB per value and appears usable only at import time, so DBD owns its tables with a separate Alembic version table dbd_alembic_version PPTX, DOCX, PDF, HTML binaries object storage at dbd/<document_id>/<version>/<artifact_id>.<ext> Binaries do not belong in the metadata DB. On master, an adapter over EXPORT_STORAGE is available Chart data Superset's DATA_CACHE_CONFIG, keyed by Superset's own cache_key, which includes RLS (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313) Profiling and resolution then share cache hits with the dashboard, per user Data Digest Superset CACHE_CONFIG, 10 minutes Repeat generations from the same context are cheap Per-user UI preferences extension persistent storage [M] the one use that fits its limits

dbd_job.status mirrors the GTF statuses (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILURE, ABORTED, TIMED_OUT) and adds needs_input and partially_succeeded. dbd_job.task_uuid is the authoritative link to the GTF row. A single failed binding never fails a job: its element shows "data unavailable" and the job completes with warnings. Clarification never blocks a worker: the task persists its state, ends with payload {"status": "needs_input"}, and the user's answer schedules continue_generation.

Task (type extensions.databound.docgen.*) Scope Timeout Arguments generate_document PRIVATE 900 s job_id, user_id continue_generation PRIVATE 900 s job_id, user_id regenerate_sections PRIVATE 600 s job_id, user_id, section_ids refresh_document PRIVATE 600 s document_id, user_id, narrative, mode, force render_artifact PRIVATE 300 s document_id, version, fmt, user_id run_trigger SYSTEM 900 s trigger_id, scheduled_for, event resolve_binding [M] PRIVATE 120 s job_id, binding_id, user_id (DAG fan-out with depends_on) Gotcha: @task positional arguments and reserved names The superset_core stub's first positional parameter is name, but the host implementation's first positional parameter is func. @task("generate_document") passes a string as the function. Always use keywords: @task(name="generate_document", scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=900). The host also rejects task functions with parameters named ctx or options (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:165-173).

Reads: superset/charts/schemas.py, superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py, superset/utils/core.py, superset/dashboards/permalink/types.py, superset/security/manager.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py · Builds on: Target architecture · Time: ~45 min This chapter specifies the Document Spec, the data model every Data-Bound Documents component reads and writes, and its heart, the DataBinding. You will see every Pydantic model and field, how each binding source compiles into a real Superset query context, how dashboard filters, binding filters and parameters merge, how rows are shaped and formatted, what "live" and "snapshot" mean, and what provenance is recorded per resolution. Then the chapter shows how Presenton's Template v2 is extended with data slots, and how the schema builder exposes bindings to the LLM as enums instead of asking it for numbers. It ends with a complete three-slide deck, first as stored and then after resolution. The models below live in databound_docs.spec (the wheel). They are normative: the JSON Schema published at GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/schema/document-spec is DocumentSpec.model_json_schema(), and the Studio's TypeScript types are generated from it at frontend build time.

docs.t: Step 1: From "the LLM fills the chart" to "the LLM picks a binding"
docs.x: In Presenton a chart element is a box plus data. The Chart model carries categories: Optional[list[str]] and series: Optional[list[ChartSeries]], where ChartSeries is only a name and a list of floats: presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:176-178 The schema builder asks the LLM to produce those lists (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534), and the hydrator copies them into the element: presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1395-1398 There is no number format, no x values, no provenance and no way to refresh. From template to schema to slide walks through that path. Data-Bound Documents splits the same responsibility into seven concepts, so that numbers have exactly one way in: Concept What it is Who creates it Document One generated thing of kind deck, document, page or text; every change creates an immutable version the API, the Planner, edits, refreshes DataBinding A governed, re-runnable query plus instructions for shaping its rows only the Binding Registry Fact A deterministic scalar, label or list derived from one binding's resolved rows the Fact Engine Token The only way prose refers to data, for example {{f:f_rev}} the Narrative Writer, templates, users Element What a section shows: chart, table, kpi, text, narrative, image, link the Planner and templates Data slot A template-side placeholder that declares which element types and data shapes it accepts template authors and the importer Provenance As whom, when and how each binding was resolved, with which filters, cache state and RLS context the Binding Resolver The LLM touches only three of these, and only by choosing ids: it picks candidate or binding ids for slots, asks for facts by operation, and writes text containing tokens. A chart's series values, a table's cells and a KPI's number come from the Binding Resolver and the Fact Engine.

All models inherit from a base with extra="forbid", so an unknown field is a validation error instead of silently dropped data (Presenton's own ChartSeries drops unknown keys, see presenton: servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_pptx_json_element_metadata.py:79-103). databound_docs/spec/models.py (envelope) Field Type Meaning spec_version "dbd/1.0" The binder accepts the current and the previous major version id str ULID with prefix doc_ version int Immutable version number; each accepted edit, refresh or parameter change adds one kind deck, document, page, text Selects the default renderer and the template family title str User text from the request form; tokens allowed ({{p:region}}) language str Output language; databound_docs/spec/models.py (parameters) A parameter is a named, typed value that bindings reference with $param.<name> in filters[].val, time_range, time_grain and parameters. Parameters do three jobs: Reuse. One "Period" parameter drives every binding's time range. Roll-forward. A scheduled refresh can set time_range to "Last week" without touching any binding. Native filter override. With native_filter_id set, the parameter's value replaces that native filter's captured value for every binding the filter is in scope for. A live page renders such parameters as controls, and changing one re-resolves bindings without calling the LLM. time_range values use Superset's own grammar ("Last quarter", "2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01", "No filter"), so Superset resolves them and reports the result as from_dttm/to_dttm.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (context) Field Source at capture time Used for dashboard.permalink_key CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand(dashboard_id, state={"dataMask": ..., "activeTabs": ...}), or reused from a /superset/dashboard/p/<key>/ URL Reading state.dataMask at every resolution; the DashboardPermalinkState type has dataMask, activeTabs, anchor, urlParams, chartStates (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/permalink/types.py:21-30; chartStates is UNVERIFIED on 6.1) dashboard.native_filters_key the dashboard URL Audit only; it expires dashboard.data_mask_hash sha256 of the canonical data mask Detecting that two documents share a filter selection dashboard.filter_mode the request captured uses the permalink; defaults follows the dashboard's current defaultDataMask; none ignores native filters chart_ids, dataset_ids the request or the Studio picker Candidates and proposal targets in the Data Digest sqllab.query_id remoteId from sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess Reloaded and ownership-checked on the server; usable only as a sql binding when ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS is on locale, timezone the user's settings Formatting and the {{m:<binding_id>.as_of}} token Gotcha: filter state keys expire, permalinks do not A native_filters_key points at dashboard filter state stored in a cache with a TTL. A refresh three months later would find nothing. Context Capture therefore converts it into a permalink immediately and stores permalink_key; native_filters_key is kept only for audit. Switch a document to filter_mode: "defaults" when it should follow future edits to the dashboard's default filters instead of a frozen selection.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (DataBinding) Field Meaning Maps to in the Superset query context id b_ plus up to 48 lowercase characters, issued by the Binding Registry not sent; used in shape names (dbd:chart:<element_id>:<binding_id>), HTML data-dbd-binding, the manifest title Human label shown in the binding inspector and alt text not sent source Discriminated union on kind: chart, dataset, semantic [M], sql (Step 5) datasource plus the base queries dashboard_filters Whether and which native filters apply (Step 6) queries[].filters entries with isExtra: true, time overrides filters Extra filter clauses for this binding appended to queries[].filters time_range Time window override, literal or $param.* rewrites the TEMPORAL_RANGE filter time_grain Grain override (ISO 8601 duration such as P1M) extras.time_grain_sqla and the BASE_AXIS column's timeGrain parameters Jinja template_params for virtual datasets and SQL form_data values that Jinja macros read through g.form_data post_processing Server-side pandas steps; None keeps the source's own list queries[].post_processing row_limit 1 to 5,000, default 100; further capped by the registry queries[].row_limit (minimum of the saved value and this one for chart sources) shape How rows become a chart, table or scalar (Step 7) not sent; applied after the query format Per-column formats (Step 8) not sent mode live re-queries on every resolution; snapshot stores rows and never re-queries controls whether dbd_binding_result.rows is written and read cache_ttl Seconds custom_cache_timeout created_by Who introduced the binding: context (an existing chart), template, planner (a proposal), user audit and UI badges Gotcha: row_limit counts long-form rows, before pivoting For a timeseries chart grouped by a dimension, Superset applies row_limit to the SQL result (one row per month and product line), and the pivot post-processing runs on that limited frame. A limit of 50 on twelve months by seven product lines (84 rows) silently drops data before the pivot. Chart-shaped bindings need row_limit >= periods x series; the Binding Resolver reports truncated: true when rowcount equals the limit, and the slot assignment check refuses such a binding for a hero chart.

docs.t: Step 5: Binding sources and how each resolves to a Superset query
docs.x: Every source kind ends in the same three calls inside the Superset Adapter, under override_user: databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (run_query_context) ChartDataCommand.validate() is a one-liner that checks access before anything else runs: apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108 What differs between source kinds is how the json_body is built. Source When it is used Execution path Availability chart Default for anything the user already built Reload or pin the saved query context, stamp ids, merge filters, ChartDataCommand [6.1] with a saved query context; [M] adds a form_data rebuild dataset New visuals the planner proposes ("top countries by revenue") A QueryObject built from validated saved metrics and columns, ChartDataCommand [6.1] semantic Deployments with semantic layers SemanticView.get_table(...) [M] behind SEMANTIC_LAYERS sql Power users with a saved query, or template-admin SQL SELECT-only check, raise_for_access(..., force_dataset_match=True), Database.execute [6.1], disabled by default The LLM may choose chart bindings and propose dataset bindings through enums. It may never write SQL or adhoc SQL expressions.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (ChartSource) Resolution, step by step: Load the chart through the access-filtered chart DAO (base filter ChartFilter), so a chart the user cannot see is a 404, not a leak. Get the query context. follow: "live" loads Slice.query_context, the JSON that the viz plugin's buildQuery produced when the chart was last saved in Explore. Numbers are then identical to the dashboard. follow: "pinned" uses query_context_snapshot. When the live context's hash differs from query_context_hash, the resolver records definition_changed and the Studio offers "update to the new chart definition". If query_context is null: on [M] the adapter calls build_query_context_from_form_data(form_data, {"id": ..., "type": ...}, viz_type) (apache/superset: superset/common/form_data_query_context.py:1801-1805) and adds the provenance warning rebuilt_from_form_data. On [6.1] the binding resolves with status error and the remediation "Chart has no saved query context: open and save it in Explore", the same condition Superset's own endpoint reports (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:170-182). Stamp ids. Set form_data.dashboardId and form_data.slice_id, as the Excel export does for guest authorization (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:205-214). Merge filters in the order of Step 6. Force the result shape. result_type = "full", result_format = "json", and pop force unless this is a forced refresh. Execute with run_query_context, then read result["queries"][query_index]. Here is what a saved query context for an echarts_timeseries_bar chart typically looks like, and what the resolver changes. The saved part is illustrative: it is the shape the ECharts timeseries buildQuery saves, and exact keys vary by plugin version. Chart 102: saved query_context (illustrative excerpt) Chart 102: json_body sent to ChartDataCommand for binding b_rev_by_month (changed keys only) The pivot and flatten steps stay, so the result arrives wide, one column per product line, exactly as the dashboard renders it.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (DatasetSource) There is deliberately no SqlMetric. A planner proposal can name only saved metrics (governed definitions, with their d3format and currency) or a SimpleMetric over an existing numeric column. The Binding Registry rejects anything else before an id is issued. The compiler is 6.1-compatible and lives in the wheel. A temporal dimension becomes an adhoc BASE_AXIS column, the same pattern the ECharts plugins use: databound_docs/binder/dataset_query.py (excerpt) $param.* references are substituted before compilation (Step 6), so the compiler only ever sees literal values. When the shape has series_by, the compiler adds pivot and flatten steps that mirror the ECharts timeseries buildQuery, so a proposed "revenue by month by product line" arrives in the same wide form as a saved chart. The fields map one to one onto ChartDataQueryObjectSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1388-1675): columns, metrics, filters (ChartDataFilterSchema, with op restricted to FilterOperator values), orderby, row_limit, series_limit, time_offsets, post_processing and extras.time_grain_sqla. Gotcha: time_offsets columns are renamed, and need a time column Superset names comparison columns <metric>__<offset>, for example revenue__1 year ago. Facts and shapes must reference that exact name. The example deck below uses time_offsets on a query with a time_column but no temporal dimension (columns: []). On master, processing_time_offsets handles that case explicitly: with no join keys it falls back to a temporary join key and returns one joined row (apache/superset: superset/models/helpers.py:3604-3613, :3794). Whether the 6.1.0 code path does the same is UNVERIFIED and covered by the binding contract tests. If that test fails on 6.1, the fallback is to add order_date as a BASE_AXIS dimension at the period's grain (P3M), so the comparison has a temporal column to join on, and to read row 0.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (SemanticSource) On master with SEMANTIC_LAYERS on, the resolver calls the semantic view's get_table(...) through the host registry. The superset_core.semantic_layers package is absent from the 6.1.0 tag, so on 6.1 the registry refuses this kind with unsupported_on_6.1.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (SqlSource) SQL bindings exist only when ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS is true, and only from a saved query the user can access, a SQL Lab query the user owns, or SQL a template admin (can_manage_templates) wrote. The resolver renders Jinja with the document parameters, parses with get_sqlglot_dialect(database) and rejects anything but a single SELECT, calls security_manager.raise_for_access(database=..., sql=..., catalog=..., schema=..., force_dataset_match=True) (because Database.execute performs no datasource access check of its own), and then runs Database.execute(sql, QueryOptions(limit=..., timeout_seconds=60, cache=CacheOptions(...))). RLS applies; chart semantics (saved metrics, formats) do not. Security, RLS, auth covers the checks.

docs.t: 5.5 Previewing a binding from the Studio
docs.x: The binding inspector and the MCP tool dbd_propose_binding both validate a draft through the same registry call. The REST side is an ordinary superset_core API method: backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py (bindings preview, excerpt) And the Studio calls it with plain fetch, because SupersetClient is not shared with extension remotes: extension/frontend/src/studio/bindings.ts

databound_docs/spec/models.py (filters) FilterClause is a strict subset of Superset's ChartDataFilterSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1156): the same col, op and val, with op limited to scalar FilterOperator values (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:329). NOT LIKE, NOT ILIKE, IS TRUE and IS FALSE are left out of v1, and the array operators (CONTAINS_ANY, CONTAINS_ALL, IS_EMPTY, LENGTH_*), which accompany the master-only MULTI_VALUE column type, are not offered.

Filters are applied in this order, and later steps win: The source's own filters. For chart sources, the adhoc filters inside the saved query context. Dashboard native filters, when dashboard_filters.apply is true. [M]: fc = get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id=..., chart_id=..., active_data_mask=data_mask), then apply_dashboard_filter_context(json_body, fc.extra_form_data) when it is not empty (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272, 365). fc.to_dict()["filters"] goes into Provenance.dashboard_filters. [6.1]: databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61 reads json_metadata.native_filter_configuration. For chart sources it uses chartsInScope when present, else scope.rootPath and scope.excluded; for dataset sources it uses targets[].datasetId. It takes each value from the permalink dataMask or from defaultDataMask, appends filters with isExtra: true, and overrides time_range, time_grain_sqla, granularity_sqla and relative_start/relative_end, mirroring the EXTRA_FORM_DATA_* constants (apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-234). The binding's filters. Parameter values. $param.* references are substituted, and Parameter.native_filter_id overrides that native filter's value. time_range and time_grain overrides, which rewrite the TEMPORAL_RANGE filter with the same semantics as merge_extra_form_data (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1184-1260). Both branches return an object with the same contract as master's dataclass, so call sites never branch: apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:59-75 Gotcha: the 6.1 port refuses to guess The 6.1 port does not implement cascading parents, requiredFirst or defaultToFirstItem pre-queries. When an in-scope filter uses one of these, the binding resolves with that filter at its captured explicit value, or skips it with a rejected_filters entry {"reason": "unsupported_on_6.1"} that the provenance footer shows. It never invents a value. The binding contract tests assert that the 6.1 port and the master helper produce identical query contexts for filter_select, filter_range, filter_time and filter_timegrain. Gotcha: dataset proposals honor dashboard filters only when targeted A planner proposal over dataset 7 gets the dashboard's native filters only if dataset 7 is a target of those filters (targets[].datasetId). A proposal over a dataset no filter targets runs

databound_docs/spec/models.py (post-processing) These are Superset's own pandas operations (apache/superset: superset/utils/pandas_postprocessing/__init__.py:49-67), executed server-side inside ChartDataCommand. Shares, cumulative sums and rolling averages are therefore computed by Superset, so the deck and the dashboard agree. prophet, boxplot, histogram and the geo operations are not offered to proposals; chart sources keep whatever their saved query context contains. Gotcha: contribution is computed over the returned rows Post-processing runs on the result frame after row_limit is applied in SQL. In a single-query context, a contribution step on a top-10 query computes each row's share of the top 10, not of the whole region. Superset can do better: when the same query context also carries a totals query (metrics, no columns, no post_processing), ensure_totals_available runs it without a row limit and injects contribution_totals into every contribution step, so shares are of the true total (apache/superset: superset/common/query_context_processor.py:99-136, :709-740; ensure_totals_available is also present in the 6.1.0 tag). The Binding Resolver therefore appends such a metrics-only totals query to any dataset binding with a contribution step (a refinement not shown in the build_dataset_query_context excerpt above) and reads the binding's rows from queries[0]. The example deck would be safe either way, because its region has eight countries and rowcount stays below the limit; without a totals query and with truncated: true, a share fact must be labeled "share of the listed countries".

docs.t: 7.2 Shape: from rows to a renderable structure
docs.x: databound_docs/spec/models.py (Shape) kind Required result Feeds Check that fails loudly scalar one row, numeric value columns KPI groups, facts exactly one row with a numeric value series one x column plus numeric series columns category charts (column, bar, line, area, pie) one x column and at least one numeric series xy numeric x and y per series scatter numeric x and y xyz x, y, size bubble three numeric columns table any columns native tables, ranked lists listed columns exist pivot post-processed pivot tables with merged headers header levels present The resolver's shaping pass, in order: Convert temporal values (Superset serializes them as epoch milliseconds) to timezone-aware datetime in the document timezone. Date categories produce a date axis in python-pptx. Apply top_n: keep the N largest series (or categories) by total and fold the rest into one column named others_label. Compute the reserved virtual columns __row_total (row sum across series) and __row_index (0-based position after sorting). Facts can reference them, for example argmax over __row_total, or a where of {"__row_index_lt": 3}. Enforce the target slot's series, categories and rows ranges (Step 13).

databound_docs/spec/models.py (formats) Resolution follows Superset's own precedence: DataBinding.format.columns[col] (then "*" for value columns). The dataset metric's d3format and currency. The chart form_data keys y_axis_format, number_format and currency_format. SMART_NUMBER. A currency with symbol AUTO resolves from the result's detected_currency. The resolved format is then consumed in two different ways, and the distinction matters: Consumer Uses Why Fact displays, table cells, KPI values, token text d3 through the vendored format_number_with_config(d3_format, currency, value) (apache/superset: superset/utils/number_format.py:166, [M]; vendored for 6.1) The same strings a user sees in the browser Chart caches, axes, data labels, the embedded workbook excel, derived deterministically from d3 (for example ,.0f gives #,##0, .1% gives 0.0%) The workbook keeps raw numbers, so "Edit Data" in PowerPoint shows real values label comes from the column's verbose_name or the metric's verbose_name unless the binding overrides it. The full d3-to-Excel table is in Native rendering, no screenshots.

docs.t: Step 9: Live, snapshot, live-follow and pinned
docs.x: Two independent switches control how "dynamic" a binding is. mode decides whether data is re-queried; follow (chart sources only) decides whether the query definition is re-read. follow: "live" (chart definition re-read) follow: "pinned" (definition frozen) mode: "live" (data re-queried) Default. Edits to the chart in Explore and new data both flow into the next refresh New data flows in, but the query is the one captured at generation time; definition changes raise a flag mode: "snapshot" (rows stored) Rows frozen in dbd_binding_result.rows; a definition change is reported but not applied Fully frozen: what was sent is what is shown, forever Live pages re-resolve live bindings as the viewer on every open. Refresh in place re-resolves as the run-as user and rewrites the existing PPTX or DOCX. Snapshot shares require can_share_snapshot, because they carry the author's data. Scheduling and live refresh covers the refresh algorithm.

Every resolution produces a BindingResult, stored in dbd_binding_result and passed to the Fact Engine and the renderers. databound_docs/spec/models.py (results) Most provenance fields are copied straight from Superset's chart-data response (ChartDataResponseResult, apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1807-1940); the rest are computed by DBD: Field Origin cache_key, is_cached, queried_dttm, applied_filters, rejected_filters, from_dttm, to_dttm, detected_currency the query result returned by ChartDataCommand.run() coltypes GenericDataType ints: NUMERIC=0, STRING=1, TEMPORAL=2, BOOLEAN=3, MULTI_VALUE=4 [M] (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:251-260) dashboard_filters fc.to_dict()["filters"] on master, or the 6.1 port's equivalent query_hash sha256 of the canonical query JSON without force (sorted keys, no nonces) data_hash sha256 of canonical rows; equal hashes let a refresh emit refresh.unchanged and skip a new version rls_fingerprint hash of the RLS clauses applied to the executing user, from the same inputs as get_rls_cache_key (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313) executed_as_* the as_user context: the requester, the trigger's run-as user, or a parsed guest token (v2) truncated rowcount == row_limit Status mapping: SupersetSecurityException becomes forbidden (the element renders "You do not have access to this data" and every narrative citing its facts is removed); other errors become error and the element uses its fallback; zero rows is empty; a hit limit is truncated. Rows are persisted only for mode: "snapshot" or when an audit policy requires it; refreshes add rows and never overwrite them. Each artifact references (document_id, version, binding_result_ids), so "what data was in the file we sent on Monday" is always answerable. Provenance is also stamped into every output: a visible footer ("Data as of 2 Nov 2026 09:14 UTC. Filters: Region = EMEA."), PPTX shape names and alt text, the /customXml/dbd-manifest.json part, HTML data-dbd-binding, data-dbd-query-hash and data-dbd-as-of attributes.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (facts) A fact is a definition plus a computed value. The stored spec holds the definition (id, binding_id, op, args, format, description); value, label, display and sign are filled by the Fact Engine at every resolution with pure functions over the shaped rows, so a refresh recomputes them without the LLM. Op Args Value value, label_at column, row or where a cell value or label sum, mean, min, max, count column, optional where aggregate over rows first, last column first or last point in x order abs_change, pct_change column, baseline_column or vs (prev, first, a time_offsets column) delta, with sign set share column, label value divided by the column total rank_of column, label 1-based rank argmax, argmin column, label_column label plus its value top_k column, k list of label and value pairs count_where where number of matching rows period_label none resolved from_dttm to to_dttm as text as_of none queried_dttm

Token Resolves to Example rendering {{f:<fact_id>}} the fact's display $2.91M {{f:<fact_id>.label}} the fact's label France {{f:<fact_id>.abs}} the absolute value of a change fact, formatted 8.4% (for "fell by" phrasing) {{p:<param>}} a parameter's display value EMEA {{m:<binding_id>.as_of}} the binding's queried_dttm in the document timezone 2 Nov 2026 09:14 Each token renders as its own run: an a:r in PPTX, a w:r in DOCX, a <span data-dbd-fact="f_rev"> in HTML. That is what makes in-place refresh possible: the manifest records every token run, and a refresh rewrites a run only if its text still equals what DBD last wrote. Category names are tokens too (.label), because a label visible to the author may be invisible to another viewer under RLS; the Narrative Verifier's entity scan rejects literal category names in LLM prose.

A Section has id, layout_id, title (tokens allowed), intent, elements and speaker_notes (tokens allowed). Every element inherits id and slot from a small base class _El; the slot is the data slot name the element fills. The element union, discriminated on type: type Data fields Notes chart binding_id, native (column, bar, line, area, pie, doughnut, scatter, bubble, radar, combo, waterfall, funnel, histogram, step, sparkline, heat_table, svg), grouping (clustered, stacked, percent), title, legend, data_labels, secondary_series (combo only), colors, fallback (table, omit, link) native must be in the slot's native list; fallback applies when the binding fails or the viz is tier 3 table binding_id, columns, max_rows, overflow (truncate, continue, appendix), totals_row, heat_column cells are formatted strings; numeric cells right-aligned kpi value_fact, label, comparison_fact, comparison_label, sparkline_binding the delta color follows the comparison fact's sign text text, role (title, subtitle, heading, body, caption, footer), pinned_note template or user text; may hold tokens and literal digits; pinned_note marks a value a user typed by hand ("edited, not live") narrative purpose, fact_ids, max_chars (default 600), form (paragraph, bullets, headline), text, status (pending, verified, fallback, flagged, user_edited), verify_report, audience_rls_fingerprint LLM prose with tokens only; verified before it ships; user_edited text is never regenerated automatically image asset_ref, alt template assets only, never a capture link label, target (dashboard, chart, explore, page, url), ref links come from templates or bindings, never from LLM output

docs.t: Step 13: Extending Presenton Template v2 with data slots
docs.x: Templates keep Presenton's Template v2 element model for geometry and styling: the discriminated union SlideElement of Text, Container, Image, TextList, Table, Vector, Chart, Infographic, Flex, Grid and Group (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:624-640), every element positioned on the fixed 1280 x 720 canvas. On a 16:9 slide that is 9,525 EMU per template unit. Template v2 format documents the base format. Data-Bound Documents makes two additions.

A data_slot object is added to chart, table and text elements: databound_docs/templates/slots.py Field Meaning Checked against name Slot id within the layout; becomes element.slot unique per layout accepts Element types this slot can show the candidate's kind shapes Allowed Shape.kind values the profiled shape x_kind Allowed x axis kinds the x column's GenericDataType series, categories Inclusive count ranges profiled counts; categorical overflow is allowed when top_n can fold into "Other" rows Inclusive row range for tables rowcount and max_rows max_chars Narrative budget the rendered length with tokens replaced by their displays native Allowed native chart types the viz mapping for the candidate's viz_type aspect Box proportion used in layout scoring optional Whether the slot may stay empty layouts with an unfillable mandatory slot are discarded

Presenton has no KPI element (its Infographic kinds such as gauge and progress_bar hold LLM-supplied values). DBD adds one to the SlideElement union: databound_docs/templates/elements_ext.py The PPTX Renderer draws it as a group named dbd:kpi:<element_id> holding value, label and delta text boxes, plus an optional native LINE sparkline. The ported Presenton ChartSeries also gains typed x values, sizes and dates in DBD's copy, and bubble becomes a real ChartType, fixing the mismatch between the schema's CHART_TYPE_VALUES (which lists "bubble", presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:23-36) and the ChartType enum (which does not, elements.py:76-87).

Template tpl_exec_review v3, layout chart_takeaway (abridged) The chart element keeps its Presenton styling fields (chart_type, legend, legend_position), but categories and series are absent: they will never be filled by the LLM. A non-decorative text element without a data_slot (the title here) keeps Presenton's behavior, a string with minLength/maxLength, with one addition: the token-only pattern of Step 14.

docs.t: 13.4 Three ways a slot gets into a template
docs.x: Authoring in JSON, for built-ins and the Studio template editor. Shape-name convention in a PPTX or DOCX master. A designer names placeholders slot:chart:trend, slot:kpi:kpi_1, slot:narrative:takeaway and slot:table:detail in PowerPoint, or tags Word content controls with the same strings. The importer reads shape names, boxes and fonts with python-pptx, and for a designer chart it reads graphic_frame.has_chart, the chart type and the series and category counts to infer shapes, x_kind, series and categories. Narrative max_chars comes from Presenton's geometry-capacity idea (TABLE_TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR = 0.85, presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:49). The importer returns a validation report, for example "slot trend holds a pie chart but declares temporal x". No vision model is involved. Presenton certified import, an optional v2 plugin. It needs a vision model and @presenton/export-core, whose license is unknown, so it is not in the default build. See Custom templates from PPTX for how Presenton does it. Gotcha: a designer chart in a slot is a promise about shape In template-fill mode the PPTX Renderer calls chart.replace_data(...) on the designer's chart, which keeps all formatting. That only works if the binding's shape matches the chart: a pie slot cannot take three series, and a clustered column chart designed for six categories will look wrong with twenty. The importer turns the designer's chart into series and categories ranges precisely so that slot assignment refuses mismatched bindings up front instead of producing a broken slide.

docs.t: Step 14: How the schema builder exposes bindings to the LLM
docs.x: Presenton's builder walks a layout's elements and emits one JSON Schema property per non-decorative element (_is_editable_element, presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:53), with additionalProperties: False, every property required, and x-element-type/x-element-path annotations for hydration (_component_content_field_schema, presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1200-1281). A text element becomes {"type": "string", "minLength": ..., "maxLength": ...}; a chart becomes the categories/series object shown in Step 1. DBD keeps the walk, the budgets, the strictness and the annotations, and changes what each element type emits. The builder takes a layout and the menus the Binding Registry compiled for the section (which candidate, proposal or binding ids are compatible with each slot), and produces two projections, one per LLM call that needs it: the assignment projection, used by the layout tie-break and slot assignment call (Generation flow, step 4): data slots become enums of ids; the writer projection, used by the Narrative Writer (step 7): text and narrative fields become strings with budgets and a token-only pattern. databound_docs/templates/schema_builder.py (skeleton) walk_editable and strict_object are ports of Presenton's element walk and _object_schema (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:455; additionalProperties: false, all properties required, $defs hoisted). For layout chart_takeaway with the menus {"chart": ["cand_c102", "p_rev_by_country"]}, the two projections are: Assignment projection for chart_takeaway Writer projection for chart_takeaway (pattern abbreviated) The writer call wraps this projection with speaker_notes (no regex, because some providers reject very long patterns, but verified like every other field) and fact_requests, whose binding_id is an enum of the section's bindings and whose args_json is a string (strict structured-output modes reject open objects). Generation flow shows the full response schema. What the builder never emits for a data template: categories, series, values, table columns or rows, KPI numbers, URLs, or SQL. The menus are compiled per request from the Binding Registry, so the enum contains only ids the requester can access and that fit the slot. docs.t: Step 15: Full example, a three-slide deck before and after resolution
docs.x: The example is an executive review of a "Sales Overview" dashboard (id 12) filtered to EMEA for Q3 2026, generated by user 42 with template tpl_exec_review v3. Data values in 15.2 are illustrative.

This is exactly what dbd_document_version.spec holds. Notice what is absent: no rows, no fact values, no formatted numbers. Every number is a reference. DocumentSpec doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K, version 1 (as stored) Points to notice: The document title was typed by the user in the request form, so it is user text and may contain literal digits ("Q3 2026"). Every LLM-written field (section titles, narratives, speaker notes) uses tokens only. The second narrative says "the leading group of countries" instead of "the top three", because "three" is a number word and the Verifier rejects it in LLM prose. A {{f:<id>.count}} token for top-k sizes is a v1 grammar extension. b_rev_by_month and b_orders_kpi are created_by: "context": they reuse charts 102 and 101 as saved, so the deck's numbers equal the dashboard's. b_rev_kpi and b_top_countries are planner proposals over dataset 7, accepted by the Binding Registry because revenue is a saved metric and country a groupby=True column. __row_total and __row_index_lt are the Fact Engine's reserved virtual columns; revenue__1 year ago is Superset's naming for time_offsets results; the contribution step makes Superset compute shares server-side.

Resolution runs as user 42 inside override_user. Each binding becomes one BindingResult. Temporal values are shown after shaping (converted from Superset's epoch milliseconds); provenance is shown in full for one binding and abbreviated for the rest. BindingResult rows for version 1 (illustrative values) A few things the resolver did here: b_rev_by_month arrived from Superset with seven product-line columns (pivoted by the chart's own post-processing). top_n: 6 kept the six largest and folded "Trains" into "Other"; __row_total was added. The rowcount of 3 is post-pivot; the long-form SQL result had 21 rows, well under the limit of 500. b_rev_kpi reports truncated: true because a scalar binding's rowcount equals its row_limit of 1. For scalar shapes this is expected and is not shown as a footnote; the flag matters for tables and series. b_top_countries returned 8 rows under a limit of 10, so the contribution shares are of the whole region (see the Gotcha in Step 7). b_orders_kpi and b_rev_by_month were cache hits, because they are the dashboard's own queries and the dashboard had just run them for user 42. The cache key includes RLS, so those hits are per user.
The Fact Engine fills the computed fields. Formats come from the fact's own format, else the binding's column format. Facts after resolution

GET /documents/<id>/render-model returns what renderers and the live page consume: sections with tokens replaced, rows shaped for each element, and provenance for footers. Each resolved token keeps its fact id, so the PPTX Renderer can write it as its own run and record it in the manifest. Render model for version 1 (abridged) Series colors follow the theme rules of Native rendering, no screenshots: label_colors pins "Classic Cars" and "Motorcycles" to their dashboard colors, and the other series take palette colors. The chart keeps raw numbers in values and the Excel format separately, so the PPTX workbook holds real data; the table holds formatted strings, because table cells are text.

Next quarter, a cron trigger rolls time_range forward to "Last quarter" and calls refresh_document as the run-as user. The spec's bindings, facts and sections do not change. The resolver produces new BindingResult rows with new data_hash values; the Fact Engine recomputes every fact; the narrative policy regenerate_on_drift rewrites a narrative only if a drift rule fires (for example f_rev_yoy flips sign, or f_top_country changes); and the PPTX Renderer calls replace_data on the dbd:chart:e6:b_rev_by_month frame, rewrites the cells of dbd:table:e9:b_top_countries, and rewrites each token run whose text is still the one it last wrote. The result is version 2 with provenance.reason = "refresh" and parent_version = 1. If every data_hash is unchanged and skip_if_unchanged is true, no version is created and the job emits refresh.unchanged.

Reads: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py, superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py, superset/tasks/async_queries.py, superset/utils/core.py, superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py · Builds on: Data-bound slide model · Time: ~50 min This chapter walks one Data-Bound Documents job from the button click to the downloaded file, one step at a time. You will see the exact web request that captures the user's context, the Data Digest that is the only thing the language model is allowed to read, every LLM call with its system prompt and its response schema, how a binding is chosen, validated and executed as the requesting user, how prose is written with fact tokens and then checked, which events stream to the browser, and how the same ten steps produce a deck, a document, a text brief or a live web page. Interpretation this chapter implements One common, output-agnostic generation framework, Superset Data-Bound Documents, turns a prompt, a chosen template and a Superset data context (a dashboard with its live filter state, saved charts, datasets with their saved metrics, a semantic view [M], or a SQL Lab query) into (a) PowerPoint decks, (b) documents (DOCX, PDF, Markdown), (c) text (narratives, summaries, emails, alert briefs) and (d) web pages (interactive HTML reports, and in v2 generated Superset dashboards). It runs on demand (UI, REST, MCP) or on events (schedules, alerts, data freshness, definition changes, webhooks). Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query executed with the requesting user's permissions and row-level security (RLS), is rendered natively, never as a screenshot, and can be re-run to refresh with new data. Availability tags used below: [6.1] means present in the 6.1.0 release (May 2026) and on master; [M] means master only (expected in 7.0, unverified); [M*] means present in 6.1.0 but changed on master. Superset citations refer to master at cabd8d4 unless marked.

Presenton's Standard pipeline has five stages: outline, layout structure, schema-constrained content per slide, hydration, and export (Standard generation pipeline). Data-Bound Documents keeps that shape and changes one thing: the language model never produces a number. Presenton's content schema asks the model for chart categories and series[].values and copies them into the slide (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534). Here the model only chooses bindings from validated menus and writes prose that cites facts by token. Numbers enter an artifact through exactly two deterministic components, the Binding Resolver and the Fact Engine. Step Component Runs in LLM Typical duration Presenton analogue 1 Context Capture web request no under 300 ms POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create 2 Data Digest GTF task no 1 to 10 s, mostly cache hits none (Presenton reads uploaded files) 3 Planner, outline GTF task yes (A) 5 to 15 s, streamed generate_ppt_outline 4 Planner, layout fit GTF task only on ties (B) under 1 s, plus 5 s for a tie-break generate_presentation_structure 5 Binding Registry GTF task no under 1 s none 6 Binding Resolver, Fact Engine GTF task no 1 to 20 s none (the LLM invents data) 7 Narrative Writer GTF task yes (C, D) 3 to 8 s per section, up to 4 in parallel get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline 8 Narrative Verifier GTF task repair only (E), optional judge (F) under 2 s none 9 Assembly and preview GTF task no under 1 s hydration, stream_presentation 10 Renderers render_artifact task no 1 to 10 s per format @presenton/export-core Step 1 runs in the Superset web process. Steps 2 to 9 run inside one Global Task Framework (GTF) task, generate_document, on the dedicated Celery queue databound_docs, under override_user(requester, force=False). That is the same pattern Superset uses for its own async chart queries: _resolve_user explains that "the GTF executor does not impersonate on its own, so each task establishes the request user itself" (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175). Step 10 is one render_artifact task per format. The task wiring is covered in Building the Superset extension; this chapter is about what each step computes.

docs.t: Step 1: Capture the context (synchronous web request)
docs.x: The user is on a filtered dashboard (master: the chat panel databound.docgen.chat), in SQL Lab (6.1 and master: the panel databound.docgen.panel), or on the standalone Studio page (GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/studio, the 6.1 entry for dashboards). Whichever surface it is, it sends the same body to POST /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/documents. CreateDocumentRequest (from the chat panel on dashboard sales-overview) The handler performs eight sub-steps, in this order: Validate and authorize. Parse the body into CreateDocumentRequest (Pydantic, extra="forbid") and require can_generate on DataBoundDocs through @protect() and @permission_name("generate"). Load each dashboard as the user. Resolve id_or_slug through the access-filtered dashboard DAO from superset_core.common.daos (host-replaced at startup, apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:37-125), then call security_manager.raise_for_access(dashboard=dashboard). A 403 here ends the request; nothing is queued. Freeze the filter state. With native_filters_key: read the data mask with GetFilterStateCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/filter_state/get.py:30) and write a durable permalink with CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand(dashboard_id, state={"dataMask": ..., "activeTabs": ...}) (superset/commands/dashboard/permalink/create.py:45). Both are [6.1]. With permalink_key (the user opened /superset/dashboard/p/<key>/): reuse it as is. With neither: filter_mode: "defaults", which follows the dashboard's saved defaults on every refresh. SQL Lab context. Record database_id, catalog, schema, and either saved_query_id or query_id (the remoteId from sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess, apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/sqlLab/index.ts:214). The backend reloads the Query row and checks it belongs to the user. It becomes a sql binding only when ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS is true (see Security, RLS, auth). Persist. Insert dbd_document (version 0, status generating) and dbd_job. Deduplicate. task_key = sha256(user_id, template_id@version, canonical(context), prompt, parameters). GTF deduplicates on task_key, so a double click joins the running job. Schedule. generate_document.schedule(job_id=..., user_id=g.user.id, options=TaskOptions(task_key=..., task_name="DBD: <title>")). Return 202 {"document_id", "job_id", "task_uuid", "events_url"} and append the job.accepted and

The Data Digest is a deterministic, token-budgeted JSON summary of the context. It is everything the LLM may see. It is built only from objects the requester can access, and it is capped by DATABOUND_DOCS["DATA_POLICY"]["max_digest_tokens"] (default 12,000).

Dashboards. Walk position_json depth-first in layout order. On master this is get_charts_in_layout_order (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/layout.py:69-84) [M]; on 6.1 the wheel ships a port, databound_docs.compat.layout_order. Collect TAB titles as section hints, CHART components (chart id and width out of 12), and MARKDOWN.code blocks truncated to 1,000 characters and treated as data. Charts. slice_name, description, viz_type, metric verbose names, dimensions, time column and grain, and whether a saved query_context exists. Datasets used by those charts plus the request's dataset_ids: saved metrics (metric_name, verbose_name, description, d3format), groupable columns, temporal columns, main_dttm_col, and each column's exposure policy.

Every chart becomes a candidate cand_c<chart_id> with a default Shape from the viz mapping in Native rendering, no screenshots and a coverage tier. big_number_total and pop_kpi become KPI candidates. Each candidate is then profiled: the Binding Resolver runs it with row_limit = min(source limit, 200) and the captured filters. The query is the dashboard's own query, so with a configured DATA_CACHE_CONFIG it is usually a cache hit. The cache key includes the user's RLS clauses (get_rls_cache_key, apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313), so cache reuse is per RLS context, never across users with different row filters. Gotcha: Superset caches nothing by default DATA_CACHE_CONFIG defaults to {"CACHE_TYPE": "NullCache"} (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1532). Without a real cache, profiling re-runs every dashboard query against the warehouse, and step 6 runs them again. superset dbd doctor warns when the data cache is NullCache.

A candidate in the digest carries a profile, never its rows: row count, truncation flag, column names and GenericDataType (NUMERIC=0, STRING=1, TEMPORAL=2, BOOLEAN=3, plus MULTI_VALUE=4 for array-typed columns on master, apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:251-260; whether 6.1.0 has MULTI_VALUE is not verified, so the profiler treats unknown codes as STRING); for numeric columns: total, min, max, first, last, last versus first change, null count; for a temporal x: the covered range and grain; for categorical columns: the top 5 labels with value and share, plus the count of other labels. Displayed values are formatted with the column's format and carry candidate fact ids such as fc_c102_total and fc_c102_argmax_label that the outline may cite. Data Digest excerpt (exposure: aggregates)

Rule What it does Where it is configured Exposure metadata_only names and descriptions only, no values at all global, per dataset, per column (dbd_data_policy) Exposure aggregates (default) the profiles in 2.3 same Exposure samples adds up to 10 rows per candidate; opt-in per dataset, can be forbidden by an admin same Column exposure none the column name is visible, its values are not; PII columns (by advanced_data_type, by name patterns such as email, phone, ssn, or explicitly) default to none dbd_data_policy.pii, exposure Most restrictive wins global, dataset and column levels combine by taking the minimum resolver logic Label masking (optional) categorical labels become stable aliases (COUNTRY_1) in prompts and are restored at render time DATA_POLICY.label_masking Sanitization data values appear only inside a delimited DATA block, as JSON strings, cut to 80 characters, with control characters and Markdown link syntax stripped always on Transparency POST /context/digest returns exactly this JSON ("what will the AI see"); dbd_audit stores its hash and token count always on A column with exposure none can still be rendered in a table, because rendering happens after the LLM, unless the admin sets allow_in_documents: false. databound_docs/planner/digest.py (budgeting, sketch) The digest.ready event carries {candidates, datasets, exposure, tokens}. Candidates dropped for budget reasons are still eligible for template-declared bindings; the planner just cannot see them.

docs.t: Step 3: LLM call A, the outline with binding choices
docs.x: The default pipeline planner replaces Presenton's free Markdown outline (Prompts and schemas) with a strict schema whose enums are generated per request from the digest. The model can name a candidate only if it is in the enum, and it can propose a new query only over a dataset, metrics and dimensions that are in the enum. System prompt: outline (prompt_set dbd-prompts-1.0) User prompt: outline Response schema: outline (enums generated from the digest above) The schema generator is small and is the key safety mechanism: databound_docs/planner/outline.py (schema generation, sketch) Metric and dimension enums are the union across datasets, so a proposal can still pair a metric with the wrong dataset. That mismatch is caught deterministically in step 5, not by the model.

Every LLM call in the flow goes through call_structured() in databound_docs.llm, which adapts Presenton's generate_structured_with_schema_retries (presenton: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py:310): Providers with strict structured output get the schema natively: response_format: {"type": "json_schema", ...} on OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, vLLM, Ollama, LiteLLM), a forced tool input schema on Anthropic. Otherwise the response is validated locally with jsonschema and retried up to two times with the validator's errors quoted back to the model. Each call records model, latency, token counts and prompt hash in dbd_audit. on_delta streams raw fragments; for the outline they become outline.delta events, and the validated result becomes outline.ready. databound_docs/llm/structured.py (sketch) Gotcha: strict modes reject long regex and open objects Some providers reject very long pattern values, and strict modes reject additionalProperties: true. call_structured() strips patterns when regex_in_schema is false and re-checks them locally, and every schema in this flow avoids open objects (that is why fact requests in step 7 use an args_json string). In chat mode the user may edit the outline before the job continues (the job.needs_input mechanism in "Chat refinement and clarification" below).

docs.t: Step 4: Layout fit and slot assignment
docs.x: Layout choice is deterministic first and LLM-assisted only on ties. Templates declare data slots on their layouts (Data-bound slide model): what element types a slot accepts, which shapes, which x kinds, and how many series, categories or rows fit.

For every outline section and every layout of the template, build a bipartite graph: left nodes: the layout's slots; right nodes: the section's candidates, proposals and its narrative; an edge when the slot accepts the element type and the profiled shape satisfies shapes, x_kind, series, categories and rows. Categorical overflow is allowed when a top_n cut can fold the rest into "Other". A maximum matching (Hopcroft-Karp; the graphs are tiny) decides whether all mandatory slots can be filled. databound_docs/planner/layout.py (edge predicate and score, sketch) Rules: Score is 10 per filled mandatory slot plus 3 per filled optional slot, minus overflow, aspect and repetition penalties. A layout with an unfillable mandatory slot is discarded. If none remains, the section uses the template's generic_chart or generic_text layout and layout.selected carries fallback: true. Ordered templates (Presenton's structure_layout.ordered, presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1873-1874) skip layout selection and run slot assignment only.

If the top two layouts score within 3 points, one call runs with a schema generated from the surviving options only: System prompt: layout tie-break and slot assignment Response schema: slot assignment (generated, one section shown) The answer is checked against the matcher's edges after the call (an extra_checks hook in call_structured()), because the schema cannot express "slot chart must take cand_c102 only when layout is chart_takeaway". The result is a section plan: layout_id, the slot assignments, and each chart's native value chosen from the viz mapping and constrained by the slot's native list. Each section emits layout.selected {section_index, layout_id, slots, fallback}.

docs.t: Step 5: Validate through the Binding Registry
docs.x: A binding enters a document only through BindingRegistry.register(job_id, draft). The pipeline planner, the agent planner (through the MCP tool dbd_propose_binding), chat edits and the template strategy all call this one function. Check Rule Failure Access load the chart or dataset through access-filtered DAOs and re-check security_manager.can_access_datasource(...) binding.rejected {reason: "forbidden"} Names every metric is a saved metric of the dataset, or a SimpleMetric over an existing numeric column; every dimension has groupby=True; temporal dimensions are is_dttm; SQL adhoc expressions are rejected for planner proposals unknown_metric, unknown_column, not_groupable Pairing the proposal's metrics and dimensions belong to the proposal's dataset_id cross_dataset Policy columns with allow_in_documents: false cannot be bound policy_denied Limits row_limit from top_n, capped at 50 for charts, 200 for tables, MAX_ROWS_PER_BINDING overall; total bindings at most MAX_BINDINGS_PER_DOC limit_exceeded Filters dashboard native filters apply to a dataset binding when the dataset is a target (targets[].datasetId) of the dashboard's filters, so proposals honor the dashboard selection recorded, not a failure Registration assign b_*, store the draft in job state, emit binding.proposed {binding_id, source_kind, shape, tier} databound_docs/binder/registry.py (sketch) A rejection emits binding.rejected {ref, reason} and the section degrades to its remaining slots; it never fails the job. Because the LLM can only name enum values, the worst a confused or manipulated model can do is pick an irrelevant binding, which the user sees in the preview and which still passes raise_for_access at execution.

The Binding Resolver turns each DataBinding into a chart-data query context JSON and executes it in-process through the Superset Adapter. It never calls Superset's HTTP chart-data endpoint from a worker: on 6.1 with GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES on, that endpoint returns 202 and then 401 without the async cookie. Chart sources: follow: live reloads Slice.query_context. If it is null: on [M], call build_query_context_from_form_data(form_data, {"id": ds_id, "type": ds_type}, viz_type) (apache/superset: superset/common/form_data_query_context.py:1801) and record a provenance warning rebuilt_from_form_data; on [6.1], fail the binding with the same remediation Superset gives, "Chart has no query context saved. Please save the chart again." (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:170-182). follow: pinned uses query_context_snapshot; if the live context hash differs from query_context_hash, a definition_changed flag is recorded. Stamp form_data.dashboardId and form_data.slice_id, exactly as the master dashboard Excel export does (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:205-214). Apply the filter merge (6.2). Set result_type = "full", result_format = "json", and pop force unless this is a forced refresh. Dataset sources become one QueryObject: columns holds the dimensions, with an adhoc BASE_AXIS column for a temporal x; metrics, filters, orderby, row_limit, series_limit, time_offsets and post_processing follow. A series shape with series_by adds pivot and flatten steps, mirroring the ECharts timeseries buildQuery. Query context built for binding b_top_countries (dataset source) Semantic sources [M] go through the semantic view's get_table. SQL sources go through Database.execute after a SELECT-only sqlglot parse and raise_for_access(database=..., sql=..., force_dataset_match=True); see Security, RLS, auth.

Later steps win: The source's own filters (for charts, the adhoc filters inside the saved query context). Dashboard native filters when dashboard_filters.apply is true. [M]: fc = get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id=..., chart_id=..., active_data_mask=data_mask) (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272), then apply_dashboard_filter_context(json_body, fc.extra_form_data) (:365) when not empty. fc.to_dict()["filters"] goes into Provenance.dashboard_filters. [6.1]: the wheel's port databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61 reads json_metadata.native_filter_configuration, computes scope (chartsInScope, else scope.rootPath and scope.excluded; for datasets, targets[].datasetId), takes each value from the permalink dataMask or defaultDataMask, and appends filters with isExtra: true and overrides time_range, time_grain_sqla, granularity_sqla, relative_start and relative_end, mirroring EXTRA_FORM_DATA_* (apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-234). The binding's own filters. Parameter values: $param.* references are substituted, and Parameter.native_filter_id overrides that native filter's value. time_range and time_grain overrides, which rewrite the TEMPORAL_RANGE filter with the semantics of merge_extra_form_data (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1184-1260). Gotcha: the 6.1 filter port is deliberately incomplete The 6.1 port does not implement cascading parents, requiredFirst or defaultToFirstItem pre-queries. When an in-scope filter uses one of these, the binding resolves with that filter at its captured explicit value, or skips it with a rejected_filters entry {reason: "unsupported_on_6.1"} that appears in the provenance footer. It never guesses a value.

The worker is already inside as_user(user_id=...), a thin wrapper over superset.utils.core.override_user(user, force=False) (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1633). Execution follows the Excel export line by line (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:226-235): databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (run_query_context) ChartDataCommand.validate() is a single line, self._query_context.raise_for_access() (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108), so object access is checked before any SQL is rendered. RLS is injected later by get_sqla_row_level_filters, defined on BaseDatasource and inherited by SqlaTable, for whatever g.user is (apache/superset: superset/connectors/sqla/models.py:1171). Data-Bound Documents' only job is to make g.user correct. Each entry of result["queries"] has colnames, coltypes, data (records, temporal values as epoch milliseconds), rowcount, applied_filters, rejected_filters, cache_key, is_cached, queried_dttm, from_dttm, to_dttm and detected_currency (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1807-1940). The resolver reads queries[source.query_index] (mixed_timeseries has two).

Shaping. Convert epoch-ms temporal values to timezone-aware datetime; apply top_n with an "Other" row; compute the virtual columns __row_total and __row_index; enforce slot count limits. Shape checks fail loudly: scalar needs exactly one row with a numeric value, series needs one x column and at least one numeric series, xyz needs three numeric columns. Provenance. Copy cache_key, is_cached, queried_dttm, applied_filters, rejected_filters, from_dttm, to_dttm and detected_currency; add dashboard_filters; compute query_hash (sha256 of the canonical query JSON without force), data_hash (sha256 of canonical rows) and rls_fingerprint (from the same inputs as get_rls_cache_key). Errors. SupersetSecurityException becomes status forbidden: the element renders "You do not have access to this data" and every narrative citing its facts is removed. Other exceptions become status error and the element uses its fallback (table, omit or link). A job fails only when no binding resolves. databound_docs/binder/resolver.py (resolve one binding, sketch)

[6.1]: bindings resolve sequentially inside the task. ChartDataCommand needs the Flask app context and g, and per-thread app contexts are not worth the risk in the MVP. [M]: a document with more than DAG_THRESHOLD (default 12) bindings fans out one resolve_binding task per binding plus a continuation scheduled with TaskOptions(depends_on=[...]), which reads results through get_context().get_dependency_payloads() (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:259). Payloads carry result storage keys, never rows.

Facts are deterministic values derived from one binding's shaped rows by pure functions: Op Args Value value, label_at column, row or where a cell value or label sum, mean, min, max, count column, optional where aggregate over rows first, last column first or last point in x order abs_change, pct_change column, baseline_column or vs (prev, first, a time_offsets column) delta, with sign share column, label value divided by the column total rank_of column, label 1-based rank argmax, argmin column, label_column label plus its value top_k column, k list of label and value pairs count_where where number of matching rows period_label none resolved from_dttm to to_dttm as text as_of none queried_dttm databound_docs/facts/ops.py (two ops, sketch) Each section with narratives gets default facts per bound element (series: last, pct_change versus previous, argmax; tables: count, argmax of the first metric; scalars: value). Displays are formatted through format_number_with_config(d3_format, currency, value) (apache/superset: superset/utils/number_format.py:166) [M]; on 6.1 the wheel vendors the same module (databound_docs.format.d3, Apache-2.0). Facts referencing missing columns are dropped before the writer sees them, and candidate facts the outline saw (fc_*) are recomputed from the full results, so the authoritative value is always the resolved one.

docs.t: Step 7: LLM call C, the Narrative Writer
docs.x: The writer replaces Presenton's SLIDE_CONTENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT and keeps its per-layout strict schema approach (presenton: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py:229, 248-252). There is one call per section, up to four in parallel. The writer receives the section intent, the fields to fill with character budgets, and a FACTS table restricted to that section. It never receives rows. System prompt: Narrative Writer User prompt: Narrative Writer (section 2 of the example deck) Response schema: Narrative Writer (generated for layout chart_takeaway) A valid answer looks like this: Writer output (section 2) The field budgets come from the template geometry, using Presenton's capacity idea (TABLE_TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR = 0.85, presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:50); see From template to schema to slide for how Presenton derives them. Optional call D, fact requests. args_json is a string, not an open object, because strict structured-output modes reject free-form objects. The Fact Engine parses it against a per-op Pydantic args model and drops invalid requests with a warning. Valid requests are computed, and one short follow-up call receives only the new facts plus the draft and may revise the text. The loop is capped at one round. Each new fact emits fact.derived {fact_id, display} to the owner only. Gotcha: the regex is a first line, not the guarantee The pattern stops digits, %, $ and stray braces at decode time on providers that honor it, but number words ("three"), month names and category names pass any regex. Speaker notes carry no pattern at all, because some providers reject very long patterns. The Narrative Verifier in step 8 checks every field regardless of what the schema enforced.

The Verifier is deterministic and runs on every LLM-written field: section titles, KPI labels written by the planner, narratives, speaker notes and email subjects. Template-authored and user-authored text is exempt and recorded as such. # Check Rule Violation code 1 Token validity every {{...}} parses and resolves; a fact must be listed for that element and belong to a binding with status ok unknown_fact 2 Literal numbers after removing tokens: no digits, number words in the output language (lists for en, de, fr, es, pt, ja first), currency symbols, %, ordinal suffixes, or calendar patterns (Q[1-4], FY, H1, four-digit years) literal_number 3 Literal entities the categorical values in the job's results form an entity set; any occurrence outside a .label token is a violation (with label masking on, the aliases are included) literal_entity 4 Claim lint per sentence: direction words agree with the sign of the nearest change-fact token; superlatives sit next to an argmax, argmin, rank_of or top_k token; comparatives between two tokens hold numerically claim_mismatch 5 Length rendered length (tokens replaced by displays) fits max_chars too_long Check 3 matters for security as much as accuracy: a category name visible to the author may be invisible to another viewer under RLS, and it also goes stale after a refresh. databound_docs/planner/verify.py (checks 2 and 4, sketch)

docs.t: 8.1 LLM call E, repair, and the deterministic fallback
docs.x: A field with violations goes back to the writer with the violations quoted, at most twice: Repair prompt (user message appended to the writer conversation) The repair call uses a one-field schema derived from the writer schema (the same pattern and maxLength for that slot). If the field still fails, it is replaced by a deterministic sentence from a per-op template, for example "{binding_title}: {{f:x}} ({{f:delta}} versus the prior period).". The narrative gets status: "fallback" and the Studio labels it "auto-written". A section always ships verified text.

An optional LLM judge (off by default) receives each sentence with its resolved fact displays and answers {"claims": [{"sentence", "fact_ids", "supported": bool, "issue"}]}. It can flag text (narrative.flagged), never edit it. It also covers languages for which no claim-lint lexicon exists yet. The report is stored in NarrativeElement.verify_report, and narrative.verified {section_index, element_id, fallback} or narrative.flagged {section_index, element_id, violations} is emitted. The acceptance target is zero untokenized numerals and entities in shipped LLM text.

docs.t: Every LLM call in one table
docs.x: Call Step Role (profile) Input Response schema Retries Count per job A, outline 3 planner request, kind, template summary, parameters, Data Digest outline with candidate and proposal enums 2 schema retries 1 (plus 1 per chat refinement) B, tie-break 4 planner surviving layouts, slots, allowed ids slot assignment with oneOf per section 2 0 or 1 C, section text 7 writer intent, fields with budgets, FACTS table per-layout fields with token regex, fact_requests 2 1 per section with narratives D, fact follow-up 7 writer new facts, draft same as C 1 0 or 1 per section E, repair 8 writer violations, previous field one-field schema at most 2 rounds 0 to 2 per failing field F, judge 8 verifier sentences, resolved fact displays {claims: [...]} 1 0 or 1 per section (opt-in) Every call is server-side, from a worker (or, for synchronous text, from the web request), with keys from environment variables or a secrets manager, and egress restricted by DATABOUND_DOCS["LLM"]["allowed_hosts"]. The template strategy makes zero calls: the template declares fixed bindings and deterministic sentences, which is how air-gapped deployments and many scheduled briefs run.

docs.t: Streaming events to the browser (alongside steps 1 to 10)
docs.x:
Coarse progress is mirrored into GTF with get_context().update_task(progress=(i, n), payload={"stage": ..., "document_id": ...}) (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:209-216), so the built-in Task List and GET /api/v1/task/<uuid>/status [6.1] show it. The immediate= keyword exists on master; it is unverified on 6.1, so the code does not rely on it. Fine-grained events are rows in dbd_job_event (job_id, seq, type, data, created_on) with this envelope: Event envelope Event Data Emitted by job.accepted {document_id, task_uuid} API context.captured {dashboard_id, permalink_key, filters_summary} API digest.ready {candidates, datasets, exposure, tokens} task outline.delta {text} (raw JSON fragment) task outline.ready {title_hint, sections: [{index, intent, title_hint, visual_intent}], gaps} task layout.selected {section_index, layout_id, slots, fallback} task binding.proposed {binding_id, source_kind, shape, tier} Binding Registry binding.rejected {ref, reason} Binding Registry binding.resolved {binding_id, status, rowcount, truncated, is_cached, queried_dttm} task binding.failed {binding_id, status, code, message, remediation} task fact.derived {fact_id, display} (owner only) task section.ready {section_index, section} (resolved displays) task narrative.verified {section_index, element_id, fallback} task narrative.flagged {section_index, element_id, violations} task document.ready {document_id, version, preview_url} task artifact.progress {format, pct} render task artifact.ready {artifact_id, format, size, download_url} render task job.needs_input {question, options} task (chat mode) job.completed, job.failed, job.cancelled {status, error?, error_type?, retryable?, stage?} task refresh.unchanged {document_id, version} refresh task The error_type and retryable fields on terminal events mirror Presenton's SSEErrorResponse (presenton: servers/fastapi/models/sse_response.py:32-45, which also carries detail, source, status_code, completed_slides and total_slides); error and stage are Data-Bound Documents additions. See Streaming (SSE). Two transports serve the same rows: Long poll (default): GET /jobs/<id>/events?after=<seq>&wait=25 returns at once when events exist, otherwise polls every 500 ms for up to wait seconds. It works with every gunicorn worker class. SSE (opt-in): GET /jobs/<id>/stream writes event: <type>
data: <json>

The task writes DocumentSpec version 1 to dbd_document_version, renders a preview HTML with the HTML Renderer (one 16:9 page per section for decks), and emits document.ready. Document Studio shows it in a sandboxed iframe with an inspector per element: Binding inspector. Source (with a link to the chart or Explore), captured and explicit filters, time range, last resolution time, cache state, row count against the limit, applied and rejected filters. Actions: change the chart native within compatible values, change top_n, swap the binding for another registered candidate, switch follow (live or pinned) or mode (live or snapshot), open in Explore. Data cells are read-only. "Pin a value" creates a visibly marked TextElement with pinned_note, which provenance reports as "edited, not live". Text editing is free. Typing a digit shows a hint to insert a fact through a picker. An edited narrative gets status: "user_edited"; it is never regenerated automatically, but its tokens still refresh. Section operations: reorder, delete, "regenerate this section" (steps 4 to 8 for one section through POST /documents/<id>/regenerate, task regenerate_sections), and "add a section from a prompt". Every edit is an RFC 6902 JSON Patch against a base version: PATCH /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/documents/doc_01JC8Z6Q4M5K The server validates the patched spec against DocumentSpec, re-runs the Verifier on any changed LLM field (user text is exempt but tokens must still resolve), creates version 2 and returns {version: 2}, or 409 when base_version is stale. Presenton's editor makes the same kind of change by rewriting slide JSON directly (Editing and chat assistant); here patches are the unit, so every version stays auditable.

POST /documents/<id>/export {"formats": ["pptx", "pdf"], "refresh": false} schedules one render_artifact task per format; md and text render inline and return 200 {artifacts}. Renderers read the version's spec and its stored binding results and never re-query unless refresh: true. Artifacts land in object storage under dbd/<document_id>/<version>/<artifact_id>.<ext>, and GET /artifacts/<id>/download streams the file after checking ownership or a share grant (and, for snapshot shares, re-checking that the recipient can access every bound datasource). How each format is produced natively is the subject of Native rendering, no screenshots.

The ten steps are output-agnostic because they produce a DocumentSpec, and the Renderers are the only part that knows about files. What changes per kind is small: Aspect deck document text page Built-in template tpl_exec_review, tpl_dashboard_walkthrough (ordered) tpl_analytical_report tpl_kpi_brief, tpl_weekly_email, alert_brief tpl_interactive_report Sections slides, typically 5 to 12 chapters and subsections, 3 to 20 1 to 3 blocks scrollable sections with parameter controls Outline call A yes yes, min_sections higher often skipped: the template fixes the blocks yes Layout fit (step 4) full matcher over slide layouts matcher over block layouts (chart_with_text, table_full) fixed layout matcher over web blocks, wider slots Narrative forms headline, short paragraph, speaker_notes long paragraph, bullets headline, bullets, email subject paragraph, headline Typical max_chars 160 to 420 600 to 1,500 280 (Slack) to 1,200 (email) 400 to 900 Runs async async sync within 20 s, else async async generation, then resolved per viewer on open Default export PPTX, optional PDF DOCX, PDF, Markdown text, Markdown, email HTML, Slack live HTML, static HTML Whose data at view time the generator's (a file) same same the viewer's (render-model?live=1 resolves as g.user) Two details deserve emphasis: Text briefs are the "on the fly" path. A kpi_brief with two bindings and one narrative needs one profiling pass, often no outline call, one writer call and the Verifier, which fits the 20-second synchronous budget on warm caches. The same path serves the MCP tool dbd_brief and alert briefs. Pages generate exactly like a deck, but their artifact is the spec itself. When a viewer opens GET /pages/<document_id>, the bindings re-resolve under the viewer's session, tokens re-resolve to the viewer's values, and a narrative written under a different audience_rls_fingerprint is re-linted against the viewer's facts and replaced by deterministic sentences if it fails (Security, RLS, auth).

docs.t: Event-triggered runs use the same flow
docs.x: A trigger is just another way to reach step 2 or the refresh algorithm. The Celery beat task databound_docs.trigger_tick (every minute) finds due cron triggers with cron_schedule_window (apache/superset: superset/tasks/cron_util.py:74) and schedules run_trigger with task_key = "<trigger_id>:<scheduled_for>", so a duplicate tick is harmless.
