Alert webhooks, freshness sentinels, definition-change listeners and signed external webhooks schedule the same task. run_trigger re-validates the recorded run_as user (active, still has can_refresh or can_generate, still has access to every bound datasource), then either refreshes in place (no LLM unless the narrative policy fires) or runs the full generation flow as that user. It never falls back to another identity. GenerationInfo.trigger records which path started the run. Details are in Scheduling and live refresh.

Clarification. When the planner cannot decide (two dashboards match "sales"), it emits job.needs_input {question, options}, persists its state under dbd_job.agent_state_key, and ends the GTF task with payload {"status": "needs_input"}. The answer arrives at POST /documents/<id>/messages {"answer": ...}, which schedules continue_generation. No worker ever blocks on a human. Refinement. "Make slide 2 a line chart and add a slide on deal size by country" runs the planner in edit mode with the current spec. Its schema allows only JSON Patch operations on /sections, /facts and /title, plus binding additions that go through the Binding Registry. The server validates the patch and re-runs only the affected bindings and narratives.

On master, a deployment can set PLANNER_STRATEGY = "agent". Steps 3 to 5 are then replaced by a tool-calling loop (default budget 24 tool calls, 6 minutes, 60,000 input tokens) over a read-only allowlist: the built-in MCP tools get_dashboard_info, get_chart_info, get_chart_data and get_dataset_info (present in 6.1, changed on master for the first and third) and the master-only get_dashboard_layout, get_dashboard_data and query_dataset, plus dbd_get_template_slots, dbd_propose_binding, dbd_derive_fact and dbd_validate_plan. It ends with a local submit_plan tool whose schema equals the pipeline plan schema. The worker mints a 10-minute JWT for the requester that MCP_USER_RESOLVER maps to the Superset user (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:937-967). Gotcha: never call MCP tools in-process from a worker Without a request context, _setup_user_context pops g.user (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:1107-1121), and MCP_DEV_USERNAME outranks g.user in user resolution (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:889-950). On 6.1 every MCP call runs as the dev user unless middleware sets g.user, so a 6.1 deployment that sets agent is downgraded to pipeline at startup with a warning. Whatever the strategy, final numbers come from the worker's own Binding Resolver run (step 6), never from MCP previews, which are capped at 50 KB on master and used for planning only.

Reads: superset/commands/report/execute.py, superset/utils/pdf.py, superset/utils/number_format.py, superset/mcp_service/chart/preview_utils.py, superset/config.py · Builds on: Generation flow · Time: ~55 min This chapter turns a resolved Document Spec into files without ever loading a Superset page in a browser. You will build the PPTX Renderer step by step with python-pptx (native charts with embedded workbooks, tables, KPI tiles and token text runs), add combo and emulated charts through the DrawingML Chart Writer, store binding metadata inside the file so refresh can call Chart.replace_data in place, and then see how the same rows become DOCX, live and static HTML, vector PDF, Markdown, email and Slack. The chapter ends with the full viz_type mapping, theme and color rules, the automated no-screenshot guarantee, and golden-file tests for every renderer. Interpretation this chapter implements Superset Data-Bound Documents is one output-agnostic framework that turns a prompt, a chosen template and a Superset data context into decks, documents, text and web pages, on demand or on events. Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query run with the requesting user's permissions and RLS. This chapter covers the last promise: each of those values is rendered natively from data (editable PPTX and DOCX charts with an embedded workbook, real tables, real text, vector SVG on the web), never as a screenshot, and every artifact is re-runnable, so a refresh replaces data in place. Availability tags: [6.1] in 6.1.0 and master, [M] master only, [M*] changed on master.

docs.t: Why Superset's own reports cannot be reused
docs.x: Superset's Alerts and Reports already produce PNG, PDF, CSV and text. Only the data formats are data. BaseReportState._get_notification_content() (apache/superset: superset/commands/report/execute.py:1649) sends PNG requests to _get_screenshots(), which loads Explore or dashboard URLs in a headless browser (execute.py:1096), and PDF requests to _get_pdf(), which stacks those PNGs: apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41 The reason is structural: chart rendering exists only in the browser. Each visualization plugin's buildQuery and transformProps are TypeScript, and the Python backend returns DataFrames with no renderer. Superset landscape (6.1) covers this in depth. Data-Bound Documents therefore reuses only Superset's data path (ChartDataCommand, as the user) and brings its own renderers, which work from rows. Presenton's export is no help either: it drives @presenton/export-core, a browser-based DOM measurer with an unknown license that is distributed outside npm (PPTX and PDF export), so it is not used. Property Superset report screenshot Data-Bound Documents Input pixels of a browser page after async loading BindingResult.rows from ChartDataCommand Requires a full UI session in headless Chromium (Firefox by default on 6.1), auth cookies, readiness heuristics Python only for PPTX and DOCX; a local file print for PDF Text rasterized, not searchable real text (a:t, w:t, SVG text) Numbers baked into an image numbers in the chart cache plus an embedded workbook, editable through Edit Data Refresh re-capture the page Chart.replace_data on new rows Failure modes blank or partial captures, spinners, tiling query errors, reported per binding

Every renderer reads a resolved DocumentSpec version plus its BindingResults and the template. None of them queries Superset (unless the caller asked for a refresh, which re-resolves first), and none of them loads a Superset UI page. databound_docs/render/base.py The render_artifact task loads the inputs, computes the render cache key sha256(spec_sha256, data_hashes, template_version, renderer_version, format), reuses an existing artifact on a hit, and otherwise calls RENDERERS[fmt].render(inp) and writes dbd///.. Every element type maps to a handler, which is Presenton's hydrator dispatch pattern (presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:865-881) applied to bound elements: Element PPTX DOCX HTML Text chart native chart, emulation, or row-derived SVG chart part (gate G5) or row-derived SVG ECharts (live) or Vega-Lite SVG (static) deterministic sentence plus link table native table Word table GitHub table or preformatted text kpi named group of text boxes, optional sparkline chart styled paragraph KPI card KPI line text, narrative runs, one run per token runs, one run per token spans with data-dbd-fact resolved text image template asset only template asset only of a template asset omitted link hyperlink run hyperlink anchor URL

docs.t: Step 2: Number formats for text and for Excel
docs.x: Two formatting paths exist, and mixing them up is the most common renderer bug. Text (fact displays, table cells, KPI values, narrative tokens) goes through format_number_with_config(d3_format, currency, value) (apache/superset: superset/utils/number_format.py:166) [M]. Its docstring describes it as the report-side counterpart of the frontend CurrencyFormatter, so text matches what users see in the browser. The module is absent from 6.1.0, so the wheel vendors it as databound_docs.format.d3 (Apache-2.0) and the adapter prefers the host copy when present. Charts (axes, data labels and the embedded workbook) keep raw numbers and receive an Excel format code, so the workbook stays numeric and editable. d3 or Superset format Excel format ,d, ,.0f #,##0 ,.Nf #,##0. followed by N zeros .N% 0. followed by N zeros, then % +,.Nf, +.N% three sections, for example +#,##0.0;-#,##0.0;0.0 $,.2f, or a currency {symbol, symbolPosition} "$"#,##0.00, symbol from a currency table, suffix position supported .3s, SMART_NUMBER, $,.2s [>=1000000]#,##0.0,,"M";[>=1000]#,##0.0,"K";#,##0; when the max absolute value is at least 1e9, the series is pre-scaled to billions and the axis title gets "(billions)" %Y-%m-%d, %b %Y, smart_date yyyy-mm-dd, mmm yyyy, or by grain: P1D gives d mmm, P1M gives mmm yyyy, P1Y gives yyyy anything unmappable General on the axis; data labels are written as text through the d3 port databound_docs/format/excel.py (sketch) Gotcha: Excel number formats allow only two conditions A SMART_NUMBER axis cannot express thousands, millions and billions in one Excel format. The renderer pre-scales series whose peak is at least 1e9 and adds "(billions)" to the axis title, and the workbook header records the scale so a human editing the data is not misled.

docs.t: Step 3: Compose a PPTX deck from a template
docs.x: A deck template is one of two things, and both are handled by the same renderer (python-pptx 1.0.2, MIT; it adds only itself to a Superset image, because XlsxWriter and Pillow are already Superset dependencies). A JSON layout set (built-ins and Studio-authored templates). Elements use Presenton's Template v2 model (Template v2 format) in a 1280 x 720 coordinate space. On a 16:9 slide of 12,192,000 x 6,858,000 EMU, one template unit is 9,525 EMU. Flex and Grid containers are resolved to absolute boxes by a Python layout pass, and text height is measured with Pillow FreeType and the template's bundled fonts. The renderer draws on a blank layout of the template's theme file. A PPTX master whose layouts contain shapes named slot:<type>:<name> (for example slot:chart:trend, slot:kpi:kpi_1, slot:narrative:takeaway). The renderer clones the layout and fills each slot in place. A designer chart in a chart slot keeps its formatting through replace_data ("template-fill mode"); an empty frame is replaced by add_chart at the same geometry. databound_docs/render/pptx/compose.py (sketch) Gotcha: python-pptx does not lay out text TextFrame.auto_size values are applied by PowerPoint at render time, and fit_text() needs the font file in the worker. The renderer relies on the character budgets that the Narrative Writer already respected (Presenton's geometry-capacity idea) and sets MSO_AUTO_SIZE.TEXT_TO_FIT_SHAPE only as a safety net.

Each chart element has a native value (chosen in step 4 of the flow) and a shaped BindingResult. The renderer converts rows into one of python-pptx's three chart-data classes: CategoryChartData(number_format=excel_fmt): categories from the shaped x column, one add_series(name, values, number_format) per value column. Dates become datetime, which gives the chart a date axis. XyChartData: add_series(name) then add_data_point(x, y) per row (scatter, step). BubbleChartData: add_series(name) then add_data_point(x, y, size) (bubble). python-pptx writes the embedded workbook with XlsxWriter when the chart is created (ChartPart.new calls chart_workbook.update_from_xlsx_blob(chart_data.xlsx_blob)), so PowerPoint's Edit Data opens the real rows. databound_docs/render/pptx/charts.py (sketch) The alt text reads, for example, "Revenue by month and product line, Superset chart 102, data as of 2 Nov 2026 09:14 UTC, filters: region IN EMEA". Screen readers get a real description, and the provenance survives copy and paste into other decks. Gotcha: temporal values arrive as epoch milliseconds Chart-data JSON serializes temporal columns as epoch ms (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:579-583). The Binding Resolver converts them to timezone-aware datetime during shaping. A renderer that receives raw integers produces a category axis of thirteen-digit numbers instead of a date axis. Gotcha: pie charts have no category axis chart.category_axis raises ValueError on pie charts, and chart.value_axis does too. Guard every axis access by native.

The python-pptx 1.0.2 source answers half of gate G4. Its chart XML writers skip None values when they write cached points (python-pptx 1.0.2: pptx/chart/xmlwriter.py:150-152 for category series, :1605-1606 for XY series), so a null leaves a missing c:pt rather than a zero. The chart templates write c:dispBlanksAs val="gap" for most chart types, but the area-chart template writes val="zero" (pptx/chart/xmlwriter.py:345), so a null in an area chart drops to the axis. What remains unverified, and is what G4 now tests, is that PowerPoint, Keynote and LibreOffice draw those missing points as gaps. The renderer forces gap on every chart (area included) with the post-processing step below, which is also safe to run when the template already wrote gap. databound_docs/render/pptx/nulls.py (fallback if gate G4 fails)

Tables use shapes.add_table(rows, cols, x, y, cx, cy), named dbd:table:<element_id>:<binding_id>. Header labels come from verbose names, cells hold formatted strings (tables are for reading, the workbook is for editing), and numeric columns are right-aligned. databound_docs/render/pptx/tables.py (sketch) pivot shapes (from pivot_table_v2 with result_type=post_processed) get merged header cells with _Cell.merge. heat_column applies a sequential fill from the chart's linear_color_scheme (a native "heat table" for heatmap_v2). Tables do not paginate. overflow: "continue" adds continuation slides; "truncate" adds a "+N more rows" footer; "appendix" moves the full table to an appendix section.

A KPI is a group shape named dbd:kpi:<element_id> holding three text boxes (value, label, delta) and an optional sparkline. The delta color follows the comparison fact's sign, using the theme's positive and negative colors. The sparkline is a native LINE chart with axes, gridlines and legend hidden, so it also has an embedded workbook. databound_docs/render/pptx/kpi.py (sketch) GroupShapes.add_chart is available because group shapes expose the same shape-tree API as the slide.

Text and narrative elements contain tokens ({{f:f_rev}}, {{f:f_top.label}}, {{p:region}}, {{m:b_x.as_of}}). The renderer writes each token as its own run, and records the run's location so refresh can find it later. databound_docs/render/pptx/tokens.py (sketch) Shape names: text elements are dbd:text:<element_id>; the manifest record is {slide_id, shape_name, paragraph_index, run_index, token, rendered_text}. Slide ids come from slide.slide_id, which is stable across saves, unlike slide indexes.

The renderer adds /customXml/dbd-manifest.json (content type application/json) and relates it from the presentation part with relationship type urn:databound-docs:manifest, using python-pptx's OPC Part class. It contains the document id, version and Superset base URL, every binding id with its query_hash, and the token-run map. It holds no rows and no credentials. databound_docs/render/pptx/manifest.py (sketch) Gotcha: PowerPoint may drop unknown parts on save (gate G3) Whether PowerPoint preserves an unknown custom part after a user opens, edits and saves the deck is unverified. Refresh therefore never depends on it alone: shape names (dbd:chart:<element_id>:<binding_id>), the docProps/custom.xml property DbdDocumentId, and a JSON copy in the notes of a hidden last slide are written too. Refresh tries them in that order.

refresh_document(mode="in_place") opens the last artifact (or a copy the user edited and uploaded through POST /documents/<id>/refresh-upload), re-resolves the bindings as the run identity, and rewrites only data: databound_docs/render/pptx/refresh.py (sketch) The rules that make this safe: Chart.replace_data swaps the cached series and category values and replaces the embedded workbook, leaving formatting alone. Colors are re-applied by label, because the series set can change (a new product line appears). Table rows grow up to max_rows by copying the last row's formatting; extra rows are dropped with a footer. A token run is rewritten only if its current text equals the recorded rendered_text. Otherwise a human edited it in PowerPoint, and refresh reports token_edited_skipped. A bound shape that was deleted or renamed is reported as binding.orphaned, and the slide is left unchanged. The narrative policy (keep, retoken, regenerate_on_drift, regenerate) decides whether whole narratives are rewritten first; see Scheduling and live refresh. write_manifest on refresh must replace the existing part rather than add a second relationship; the sketch elides that lookup.

docs.t: Step 9: Combo and emulated charts (DrawingML Chart Writer)
docs.x: python-pptx's ChartXmlWriter covers 29 chart types (area, bar and column, bubble, doughnut, line, pie, radar, XY) and its user guide states that it does not create multi-plot charts. Superset's mixed_timeseries (bar plus line on a secondary axis) therefore needs the DrawingML Chart Writer, databound_docs.render.drawingml.combo, which writes the c:chartSpace XML itself: a c:barChart on the primary axes and a c:lineChart on a secondary c:valAx (c:crosses val="max"), sharing one c:catAx; cached c:cat and c:val values whose c:f references match the workbook layout of python-pptx's CategoryWorkbookWriter (categories in column A, one column per series, names in row 1). databound_docs/render/drawingml/combo.py (install step, sketch, uses python-pptx internals) This is the same sequence ChartPart.new (pptx/parts/chart.py:29-43), SlidePart.add_chart_part (pptx/parts/slide.py:171-177) and _BaseGroupShapes.add_chart (pptx/shapes/shapetree.py:236-258) run inside python-pptx 1.0.2, with a different XML body. It touches private APIs, so the writer is pinned to python-pptx 1.0.2 and covered by golden tests. Until gate G1 passes (the file opens without repair in PowerPoint, Keynote and LibreOffice, and Edit Data works), mixed_timeseries renders as two stacked native charts. Refresh of a combo chart re-emits the part and copies the old part's formatting elements, because replace_data on multi-plot charts is unverified (gate G2). Emulated charts are built from stacked bars on ordinary python-pptx charts, plus small lxml edits: viz_type Emulation waterfall COLUMN_STACKED with a transparent base series and separate increase and decrease series funnel BAR_STACKED with a transparent offset series that centers each bar bullet BAR_CLUSTERED with the target as an overlapping series butterfly [M] BAR_CLUSTERED with one side negated, overlap = 100, format #,##0;#,##0 to hide the minus sign gantt_chart BAR_STACKED with a transparent start offset (dates as serials) databound_docs/render/pptx/emulate.py (waterfall, sketch) The _base series stays in the workbook, so a user editing data sees all three columns. The workbook header row explains it.

python-docx has no chart API. The DOCX Renderer writes headings, narratives and KPIs as paragraphs and runs with template styles (Heading 1, DBD KPI), and tables with document.add_table plus the template table style, merges for pivots and a repeated header row. Charts have three paths: Option A, shared DrawingML chart part (gate G5). The same chart builder that serves PPTX produces the c:chartSpace bytes (chart_data.xml_bytes(chart_type)) and the workbook blob (chart_data.xlsx_blob). They become /word/charts/chartN.xml and /word/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_SheetN.xlsx, related from the document part, and an inline w:drawing with a:graphicData uri="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/drawingml/2006/chart" goes into a run. Option B, designer template data swap. A branded DOCX master holds a designer chart inside a content control tagged slot:chart:<name>; its data is swapped with python-pptx's SeriesXmlRewriterFactory on the chart part's XML (the same machinery replace_data uses). Fallback until G5 passes, and for tier 2 and 3 types: a vector SVG computed from the rows (Step 11.2) inserted as a picture with a PNG fallback rasterized from that SVG. That is data-derived vector output, not a screenshot. databound_docs/render/docx/chart_part.py (option A, sketch behind gate G5) Gotcha: python-docx and python-pptx Part constructors differ python-pptx 1.0.2 takes (partname, content_type, package, blob=None) (pptx/opc/package.py:289-291) and python-docx 1.2.0 takes (partname, content_type, blob=None, package=None) (docx/opc/part.py:28-34). The sketches pass keywords to both, so a positional mix-up cannot write the workbook bytes into the package slot. wp:docPr ids must also be unique across the whole document; the renderer allocates them from one counter. Refresh anchors in DOCX. Bound content sits in content controls (w:sdt whose w:sdtPr/w:tag is dbd:binding:<id> or dbd:fact:<id>). Whether content controls round-trip around drawings after a Word save is unverified (gate G6); the fallback anchor is bookmarks. The same /customXml/dbd-manifest.json part is written.

GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/pages/ returns an HTML shell that loads dbd-page..js, a standalone, non-federated bundle with its own React and Apache ECharts (Apache-2.0). A Module Federation remote cannot run outside the Superset SPA without the host's share scope, so the page bundle is a second webpack entry served from the authenticated extension file endpoint /api/v1/extensions/databound/docgen/ (on 6.1 that endpoint serves flat files only, so the bundle sits at the top of frontend/dist). On open, the page calls GET /documents//render-model?live=1¶meters=.... The server re-resolves every live binding as the viewer, under the viewer's own session, so the viewer's RLS applies, and returns sections with shaped rows, facts and provenance. A viewer without access to a binding sees a placeholder. extension/frontend/src/page/renderChart.ts (sketch) Tokens render as $4.21M, re-resolved for the viewer. Parameters (period, region) render as controls; changing them re-requests the render model without the LLM. Narratives follow the RLS viewer rule in Security, RLS, auth.

docs.t: 11.2 Static HTML and vector SVG from rows
docs.x: A self-contained static HTML file serves export, email and the PDF Printer. Data is embedded as JSON (a snapshot), and each chart is a pre-rendered SVG computed from rows in Python, without a browser: a Vega-Lite spec built from the shaped rows and converted with vl-convert-python (BSD-3, a Rust wheel with no Node). Master's MCP service already builds Vega-Lite specs from chart data for previews (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/chart/preview_utils.py:207-212), and the vega_lite preview format also exists in 6.1.0. databound_docs/render/svg_vegalite.py (sketch) Optional hydration with ECharts from the embedded JSON gives interactive static pages. Vega-Lite does not reproduce the ECharts look users know; a v2 Node sidecar dbd-echarts-ssr would call ECharts renderToSVGString() (available since ECharts 5.3; Superset 6.1 uses ^5.6.0 and master ^6.1.0, apache/superset: superset-frontend/package.json:167) and, after a spike, Superset's own transformProps. Running transformProps in Node without DOM shims is unverified.

A page document can be published as a Superset dashboard: chart-source bindings reuse the existing charts; dataset-source bindings become new charts created through the same commands as the MCP generate_chart and generate_dashboard tools, after explicit confirmation and as the user; narratives become MARKDOWN components with resolved values and an "as of" stamp, because Markdown components cannot hold live tokens.

The PDF Printer prints the HTML Renderer's own static HTML, never a Superset page. Decks get one 16:9 page per section (@page { size: 13.333in 7.5in; margin: 0 }); documents get A4 or Letter with running headers. databound_docs/render/pdf.py (playwright engine, sketch) Engine (PDF_ENGINE) How Notes playwright Chromium page.pdf() on a local file, network disabled, JavaScript off (SVG is already rendered) text stays text, SVG stays vector paths; on master Playwright with Chromium is the only report and thumbnail backend (installed through the playwright extra, apache/superset: pyproject.toml:268), on 6.1 (Selenium with Firefox by default) the operator installs it printer_sidecar the same in a separate container keeps Chromium out of the worker image weasyprint browser-free (BSD) SVG fidelity unverified (gate G7) LibreOffice (optional) headless conversion of the PPTX or DOCX for "PDF identical to the PPTX"; MPL-2.0 (ASF Category B), never bundled Gotcha: a browser is not the problem, a captured UI is Chromium printing DBD's own local HTML file is not a screenshot: no Superset page, no auth cookies, no readiness wait, and the output keeps selectable text and vector paths. The import-linter rule in Step 16 still forbids superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots and superset.utils.pdf, so nobody can "simplify" this path into build_pdf_from_screenshots.

docs.t: Step 13: Text, Markdown, email and Slack
docs.x: Markdown: headings per section, narratives with tokens resolved, GitHub tables (top N rows), KPI lines such as **Revenue:** $2.91M (+8.4% vs prior year). Each chart becomes a deterministic sentence from facts plus a link to the live page, for example "Bar chart: monthly revenue by product line, Jul to Sep 2026, peak Sep 2026". Charts are never images in Markdown. Plain text: the same without markup, for MCP results and chat replies. Email: HTML from the static renderer with each inline SVG converted to PNG derived from that SVG (many clients block SVG), KPI cards, the verified narrative, a provenance footer and optional PPTX or PDF attachments. It is sent through send_email_smtp(to, subject, html_content, config, ..., images=...) (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:939, internal; the adapter passes keywords because the signature has changed between versions) with Superset's SMTP settings. Slack: mrkdwn blocks with KPI lines and narrative, tables as preformatted text of at most 10 rows, optional file upload with a bot token from DATABOUND_DOCS. Alert brief (kind: text, template alert_brief): "What fired" (alert name, threshold from validator_config_json, last value from the report execution log read in-process as the run-as user), "What changed" (facts from the alert's chart binding), "Where to look" (links). databound_docs/render/text.py (Markdown, sketch)

Tier 1 ships in the MVP. Tier 2 ships in v1 as native emulations or vector SVG. Tier 3 is an honest fallback, never a picture of the chart. Viz keys come from superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/chart/types/VizType.ts; 6.1.0 has the same enum minus butterfly and point_cluster_map. viz_type Shape PPTX DOCX HTML live Fallback Tier big_number_total, pop_kpi scalar KPI group KPI paragraph KPI card none needed 1 big_number scalar plus series KPI plus LINE sparkline KPI plus chart part KPI plus sparkline KPI only 1 echarts_timeseries_line, echarts_timeseries, echarts_timeseries_smooth, compare, time_pivot series (temporal) LINE or LINE_MARKERS, smooth for smooth chart part ECharts line table 1 echarts_timeseries_bar series COLUMN or BAR, clustered, stacked or stacked_100 chart part bar table 1 echarts_area series AREA, AREA_STACKED, AREA_STACKED_100 chart part area table 1 echarts_timeseries_step series XY_SCATTER_LINES_NO_MARKERS with duplicated points chart part step line LINE 1 echarts_timeseries_scatter xy XY_SCATTER (date serial x) chart part scatter table 1 pie series (one) PIE or DOUGHNUT, per-point colors, percentage labels chart part pie table with share 1 bubble_v2 xyz BUBBLE chart part scatter with symbol size table 1 radar series RADAR, RADAR_MARKERS, RADAR_FILLED chart part radar table 1 histogram_v2 series (bins from server histogram post-processing) COLUMN_CLUSTERED, gap_width = 0 chart part bar bin table 1 table, ag-grid-table table native table Word table sortable HTML table truncated table 1 pivot_table_v2 pivot (result_type=post_processed) table with merged headers table with merges table with spans flattened table 1 mixed_timeseries two queries DrawingML combo (gate G1) combo chart part multi-axis two native charts 2 funnel series BAR_STACKED with a transparent offset series chart part funnel ordered table 2 waterfall series COLUMN_STACKED with a transparent base series chart part stacked bar running-total table 2 gauge_chart, bullet scalar KPI with min, max and target; bullet as a BAR_CLUSTERED overlay paragraph or chart part gauge, bullet KPI text 2 heatmap_v2 pivot heat table (cell fills) shaded table heatmap plain table 2 box_plot table (quartiles from server boxplot post-processing) quartile table table boxplot quartile table 2 butterfly [M], gantt_chart series mirrored or offset stacked bars chart part bar table 2 treemap_v2,

Superset source Target Rule Dashboard json_metadata.label_colors per-series and per-point colors highest precedence Dashboard json_metadata.map_label_colors, shared_label_colors same next, so "Classic Cars" keeps its dashboard color Chart form_data.color_scheme, dashboard color_scheme palette by scheme name hex lists copied from Superset's built-in categorical and sequential schemes at wheel build time; EXTRA_CATEGORICAL_COLOR_SCHEMES and EXTRA_SEQUENTIAL_COLOR_SCHEMES merged at runtime (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1228, 1385); no REST API returns palettes Dashboard theme.json_data, else THEME_DEFAULT (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1264-1313): colorPrimary, colorSuccess, colorError, fontFamily, brandLogoUrl PPTX and DOCX accent1 to accent6 (palette first six), positive and negative colors, latin font if available, logo slot; HTML CSS variables only when the template's theme.lock is false Chart linear_color_scheme heat tables sequential scale databound_docs/render/colors.py (sketch) Colors are assigned by label, not by position, so a refresh that adds a series keeps every existing color, and the same label has the same color in the dashboard, the deck, the document and the live page.

The requirement is turned into checks that fail CI: superset-databound-docs/pyproject.toml (import-linter contract) tests/render/test_no_raster.py The same test runs on DOCX for every dbd:binding content control. The only images that may exist are template assets (image elements, never captures) and PNG conversions of DBD's own SVG for email clients.

Renderer output is XML in a zip, so it can be compared exactly once the volatile parts are normalized. Golden files are checked in per renderer version; a change to them is a reviewed change. tests/render/golden.py The renderer test layer, in full: Test What it proves Golden PPTX and DOCX canonicalized XML (sorted attributes, ids and timestamps stripped) equals the checked-in package, chart XML included Workbook read-back every embedded workbook, opened with openpyxl, holds exactly the shaped rows with raw numbers (not formatted strings) replace_data round trip refresh with new fixture rows changes only chart caches, workbooks, table cells and token runs (XML diff), and re-applied colors match labels Guarded token rewrite a run edited after rendering is reported as token_edited_skipped and left unchanged No raster no dbd:* shape or dbd:binding control targets an image part, except row-derived SVG Office compatibility LibreOffice headless conversion in CI checks page counts and text extraction (no pixel diffs); PowerPoint 365, Keynote and LibreOffice open the files with working Edit Data before each release (gates G1 to G6) PDF text is selectable and charts are vector (pdffonts output and path counts), with no image XObjects for chart areas Format mapping table-driven tests for d3_to_excel and the vendored format_number_with_config against values produced by the frontend formatter

Reads: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py, superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py, superset/tasks/decorators.py, superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py, superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/views/index.ts · Builds on: Target architecture · Time: ~45 min This chapter builds the DBD Extension (databound.docgen), the thin Superset wiring of Superset Data-Bound Documents, from an empty folder to a deployable .supx bundle. You will scaffold it with the real superset-extensions CLI, write the extension.json, the backend entrypoint, the @api REST class, the @task Global Task Framework (GTF) tasks and the @tool MCP tools, then the frontend contributions (SQL Lab panel, commands, menus, the master-only chat slot and the standalone Studio page). The chapter ends with the local development loop, bundling, deployment and testing. Every API that exists only on Superset master is flagged with the fallback that keeps the extension working on 6.1.0. The generation runtime itself (the databound_docs library that the extension calls) is the subject of the next chapter, Building the generation service. Here we only build what must live inside a .supx. Interpretation this chapter implements Data-Bound Documents is one common, output-agnostic generation framework. It turns a prompt, a chosen template and a Superset data context (a dashboard with its live filter state, saved charts, datasets with their saved metrics, or a SQL Lab query) into (a) PowerPoint decks, (b) documents (DOCX, PDF, Markdown), (c) text (narratives, summaries, emails, alert briefs) and (d) web pages (interactive HTML reports, and in v2 generated Superset dashboards). It runs on demand (button, chat, REST, MCP) or on events (cron schedules, alerts, data freshness, definition changes, webhooks). Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query executed with the requesting user's permissions and RLS, is rendered natively (editable PPTX charts with an embedded workbook, real tables, real text), is never a screenshot, and can be re-run to refresh with new data. The extension built here is the part of that framework that plugs into Superset's processes and UI. See Vision and requirements for the full requirement list.

The chapter targets two Superset lines at once, exactly as the blueprint does: Tag Meaning [6.1] Present in the 6.1.0 tag (May 2026, latest stable) and on master [M] Present only on master (apache/superset at cabd8d4, 2026-11-02). Expected in 7.0, but that mapping is not verified [M*] Present in 6.1.0 but changed on master Published tooling used in this chapter (registry metadata, all released 2026-05-11): Package Version Role apache-superset-extensions-cli (PyPI) 0.1.0 superset-extensions init / validate / build / bundle / dev apache-superset-core (PyPI) 0.1.0 superset_core backend stubs that the host replaces at startup @apache-superset/core (npm) 0.1.0 frontend type stubs and runtime namespaces Master's superset-core still declares 0.1.0 but already carries APIs that UPDATING.md describes as "available from 0.2.0" (apache/superset: UPDATING.md:331-333). Treat anything you do not find in the 0.1.0 packages as master only.

docs.t: Step 1: Decide what goes into the .supx
docs.x: A .supx is a zip with manifest.json, frontend/dist/<files> and backend/src/<files>. Any other entry is rejected with "Unexpected file in bundle" (apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:43-48, regexes FRONTEND_REGEX and BACKEND_REGEX; the check is in get_loaded_extension, apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:189-239). Every backend/src entry is handed to the in-memory importer as Python source for a module whose name is the path with the file extension stripped (InMemoryFinder._get_module_name, apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:122-131). The CLI copies only files matched by [tool.apache_superset_extensions.build] include and installs nothing (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:225-275). So the split is fixed by the platform, and the blueprint's principle "thin .supx, fat wheel" follows from it: Lives in the .supx (databound/docgen/...) Lives in the wheel superset-databound-docs (databound_docs) entrypoint.py, api.py, tasks.py, tools.py, triggers.py Document Spec models, Planner, Binding Registry, Binding Resolver core, Fact Engine superset_adapter.py (the Superset Adapter, the only module that imports Superset internals) Narrative Writer and Verifier, Renderers, DrawingML Chart Writer Frontend: SQL Lab panel, chat panel, Studio page bundle, live page bundle Template Registry and importers, LLM providers, storage backends, Alembic env celery_routing.py, the superset dbd CLI The wheel is preinstalled with python-pptx==1.0.2, python-docx==1.2.0, httpx, vl-convert-python, jsonschema and optionally playwright in every Superset image that loads the extension: web, Celery worker and MCP. Gotcha: the bundle cannot carry dependencies or binary assets [project] dependencies in the backend pyproject.toml and a requirements.txt next to it are never installed by anything. A .supx also cannot usefully carry a .pptx master in backend/src: the bundle regex accepts any file there, but the importer treats it as the source of a module named after the path, and there is no resource reader to get the bytes back. Built-in template masters therefore ship inside the wheel as package data, and admin-uploaded masters go to object storage through the Template Registry.

Install the CLI in a separate virtual environment (it does not need Superset) and scaffold non-interactively. The option names are the ones defined on init (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:792-823): Scaffold the DBD Extension init creates docgen/ with extension.json, .gitignore, frontend/{package.json, webpack.config.js, tsconfig.json, src/index.tsx} and backend/{pyproject.toml, src/databound/docgen/entrypoint.py}. Renaming the folder to extension/ matches the repository layout of the blueprint; the CLI only cares about the current working directory when you run build, bundle or dev. It also sets the npm package name to @databound/docgen and the backend project name to databound-docgen (generate_extension_names, apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/utils.py:334-390). Gotcha: the published 0.1.0 CLI and master's CLI scaffold different webpack configs Line references in this chapter are to the CLI source on master. The init options, the bundle -o option and the default bundle name are the same in the 6.1.0 tag, but the frontend template is not: the 6.1.0 template maps @apache-superset/core to window.superset with externalsType: "window" and shares only react, react-dom and antd, while master's template shares @apache-superset/core as a singleton instead. pip install apache-superset-extensions-cli==0.1.0 was released with 6.1, so expect the 6.1 form; Step 10.2 replaces the generated file with one that builds both. The names the CLI derives from publisher and name: Identifier Value How it is derived Extension id databound.docgen f"{publisher}.{name}" (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/types.py:38-84) Backend entrypoint databound.docgen.entrypoint f"{publisher_snake}.{name_snake}.entrypoint" (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:149-184) Module Federation name databound_docgen f"{camel(publisher)}_{camel(name)}" (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/utils.py:318-331) REST base /extensions/databound/docgen/v1 /extensions/{publisher}/{name} plus /{resource_name} (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:189-207) GTF task types extensions.databound.docgen.<task> prefix added in extension context (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:147-160) MCP tool names

extension/extension.json Validation rules come from BaseExtension: publisher and name match ^[a-z]([a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*)?$, displayName matches ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\s\-_\.]*$ (so the hyphen in "Data-Bound" is fine), and version matches ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$. superset-extensions validate checks these, the npm version (at least 10.8.2), the presence of an include list in backend/pyproject.toml, and the conventional entry files backend/src/databound/docgen/entrypoint.py and frontend/src/index.tsx (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:314-441). Master's CLI additionally fails when the version or license in frontend/package.json or backend/pyproject.toml differs from extension.json; the 6.1.0 CLI does not compare them. Keep all three at 1.0.0 and Apache-2.0 so both pass. Gotcha: permissions, dependencies and description do nothing at runtime No host code enforces permissions or dependencies on master (dependencies is only echoed by GET /api/v1/extensions/). Authorization comes from FAB permissions on the API class and on the MCP tools (Step 6 and Step 8). build_manifest also does not copy description or license into dist/manifest.json, so GET /api/v1/extensions/ reports an empty description for this extension. Keep "permissions": [] so nobody mistakes it for an enforcement point.

docs.t: Step 4: Lay out the project tree
docs.x: After the scaffold and the files written in this chapter, extension/ looks like this: extension/ (DBD Extension project) extension/backend/pyproject.toml copy_backend_files keeps the matched path relative to backend/, so backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py lands at dist/backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py, which is exactly what BACKEND_REGEX (^backend/src/(?!.*\.\.)(.+)$) accepts. Master's CLI rejects absolute patterns, .. components and symlinks that resolve outside backend/ (these guards were not checked in the 0.1.0 release). Exclude patterns are tested with PurePath.match, which does not treat ** as recursive, so the exclude line is only a safety net: tests live in backend/tests/, outside include.

The host imports the entrypoint once per process, inside extension_context(manifest) (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:683-686), after it has replaced every superset_core stub with the host implementation (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:318-333). Registration happens as an import side effect: there is no activate() hook. extension/backend/src/databound/docgen/entrypoint.py The same entrypoint runs in three kinds of process, because Celery workers and the MCP server also build the app with create_app() (apache/superset: superset/tasks/celery_app.py:29-33, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/flask_singleton.py:75-90): Gotcha: never import superset_core decorators from superset_config.py Injection works by assigning module attributes. A library that does from superset_core.rest_api.decorators import api before the host has run init_core_dependencies() binds the stub, which raises NotImplementedError. This is why databound_docs (the wheel) must not import Superset or superset_core decorators at module top level, and why superset_config.py imports only databound_docs.celery_routing, which imports nothing from Superset. Gotcha: one failing import disables the whole extension in that process The host logs and counts a failed entrypoint import and keeps starting (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:657-701). Registration is an import side effect, so whatever was registered before the exception stays registered and everything after it is silently missing: a typo in tasks.py leaves the REST API up but registers no GTF task and no MCP tool, so POST /documents schedules work that no worker can run. The try around tools is mandatory, and superset dbd doctor (Step 13) checks the URL map, the TaskRegistry entries and, where fastmcp is installed, the MCP tool list, so a half-loaded extension is visible.

superset_core.rest_api.decorators.api(id, name, description=None, resource_name=None) registers the class at once with appbuilder.add_api(api_class) and appbuilder._add_permission(view, True) (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:179-227). With resource_name="v1" the base path becomes /extensions/databound/docgen/v1 and the API id becomes extensions.databound.docgen.dbd_api. extension/backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py (class header) FAB turns class_permission_name plus each method permission into can_<method> on DataBoundDocs, which yields exactly the canonical set: can_read, can_generate, can_write, can_refresh, can_schedule, can_manage_templates, plus can_share_snapshot and can_admin, which the handlers check explicitly with security_manager.can_access("can_share_snapshot", "DataBoundDocs") (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:2530) because no route maps to them one to one. FAB creates permission rows only for the method permissions of exposed routes, so those two do not exist until something creates them: superset dbd db-upgrade calls security_manager.add_permission_view_menu("can_share_snapshot", "DataBoundDocs") and the same for can_admin (FAB's method, not verified against the FAB version Superset pins). Role Suggested grants on DataBoundDocs Gamma can_read, can_generate, can_write, can_refresh Alpha Gamma plus can_schedule Admin all eight Gotcha: extension APIs are CSRF exempt by inheritance RestApi subclasses FAB's BaseApi directly, not Superset's BaseSupersetApiMixin, which is where csrf_exempt = False is set (apache/superset: superset/views/base_api.py:341). FAB's BaseApi declares csrf_exempt = True. Master's UPDATING.md documents the same inheritance problem for the extension storage routes (apache/superset: UPDATING.md:109-123). Set csrf_exempt = False on the class, and send X-CSRFToken from the frontend (Step 11). The same UPDATING.md entry spells out the cost for non-browser clients: a script that authenticates with a JWT or an API key must first call GET /api/v1/security/csrf_token/, then send the token in X-CSRFToken together with the session cookie from that call, plus a same-origin Referer over HTTPS. Document this for REST callers of POST /documents, or offer them the MCP tools instead.

All routes from the canonical list are methods of this one class. The request and response bodies are specified in Building the generation service; here is the shape of the handlers, which stay thin and delegate to databound_docs. extension/backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py (selected endpoints) The task_key stored on the job is sha256(user_id, template_id@version, canonical(context), prompt, parameters). GTF deduplicates by it: .schedule() returns the already active task instead of enqueuing a second one. Because create_pending has already written a new document and job row by then, the handler checks whether that task UUID belongs to an earlier job and, if so, discards its own rows and returns the earlier ids, so a double click lands on one job. Gotcha: schedule outside any open transaction (master) On master, SubmitTaskCommand raises RuntimeError when it runs while g.in_transaction is set, because it must commit before releasing its dedup lock (apache/superset: superset/commands/tasks/submit.py:93-113). Never wrap a DBD handler in Superset's @transaction decorator, and let create_pending commit its own rows before generate_document.schedule(...). Whether 6.1.0 has the same guard was not checked. Gotcha: a Response from an HTML route still needs @protect() /studio and /pages/<document_id> return HTML, but they must stay behind @protect() with allow_browser_login = True (inherited from RestApi) so the session cookie authenticates them. Only /hooks/<token> skips @protect(). Skipping @protect() does not skip CSRF: with csrf_exempt = False the whole blueprint is checked by Flask-WTF's CSRFProtect, so a webhook POST from Alerts and Reports, which carries no token, is rejected. Add the view to WTF_CSRF_EXEMPT_LIST (apache/superset: superset/config.py:390), which Superset passes to csrf.exempt(...) at startup (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:1793-1797). Entries follow the built-in form superset.charts.data.api.data, that is <view module>.<function name>, so the DBD entry is "databound.docgen.api.hook". Confirm it on a running instance (prototype gate G10).

(enqueue). docs.t: 7.3 Route DBD tasks to their own queue, and add the beat tick
docs.x: GTF enqueues every task through one Celery task, tasks.execute, with execute_task.delay(task_uuid=..., task_type=..., args=..., kwargs=...) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:580-584). A Celery router function can therefore route on the task_type keyword without changing Superset. The router lives in the wheel (it must import nothing from Superset) and is referenced from CELERY_CONFIG.task_routes; its full source is in Building the generation service. Prototype gate G8 confirms the behavior on 6.1. GTF has no cron (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:143-150), so the extension also defines one plain Celery task that the admin adds to beat_schedule: extension/backend/src/databound/docgen/tasks.py (beat tick) superset.extensions.celery_app is an internal import, which is acceptable in the extension package (not in the wheel). The task_key makes a doubled tick harmless. Gotcha: the beat task must be importable in the beat process Celery beat only needs the task name, but the worker that consumes databound_docs.trigger_tick must have imported tasks.py. That happens only when ENABLE_EXTENSIONS is on in the worker's config. A worker without the flag drops the message as an unregistered task.

The Superset Adapter is the only module that imports non-public Superset code. It sniffs capabilities at import time and gives databound_docs a stable interface. Its full contract (resolution, filters, provenance) is built in Building the generation service; here is the part that matters for wiring. extension/backend/src/databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (wiring excerpt) Gotcha: the cancel command is internal The REST route POST /api/v1/task/<uuid>/cancel [6.1] is public, but the command behind it, CancelTaskCommand(task_uuid: UUID, force=False, tab_id=None) (class at apache/superset: superset/commands/tasks/cancel.py:51, __init__ at line 69), is internal and was read on master only; its 6.1.0 signature is not verified here. The adapter wraps it in one function, and the contract tests (Step 14) fail loudly if the import or signature moves. The import-linter contract in the wheel forbids superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots, superset.utils.screenshot_utils and superset.utils.pdf. docs.t: 10.4 The standalone Studio and live page bundles
docs.x: The Studio page (GET /studio, the 6.1 entry point for dashboards) and live pages (GET /pages/<document_id>) run outside the Superset single-page app, where no share scope and no host React exist. A federated remote cannot run there. They are built as separate, non-federated bundles that include their own React (and ECharts for pages), and are served from the same authenticated extension file endpoint. extension/frontend/webpack.page.config.js Gotcha: the page bundles cannot import @apache-superset/core The npm package is mostly export declare type stubs; at runtime the host supplies the real namespaces through window.superset (6.1) or the share scope (master), and neither exists on GET /studio or GET /pages/<id>. Shared code such as studio/api.ts imports authentication from it, so the page config aliases the package to src/studio-page/core-shim.ts, which exports an authentication.getCSRFToken() that reads a <meta name="csrf-token"> tag. The HTML shells (databound_docs.web.shells) write that tag with Flask-WTF's generate_csrf(). Code that needs sqlLab, chat or navigation must stay out of the page bundles. Gotcha: extension assets are cached for a year The file endpoint sets max_age = 31536000, public and immutable on every response, because chunk names are expected to carry a hash (apache/superset: superset/extensions/api.py:222-226). A fixed name like studio.js would never update in browsers after an upgrade. The plugin above therefore writes the hashed names into _bundles.py, and the HTML shell references them. The CLI's build runs the frontend build before copying backend files (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:554-584), so the generated module is included. Gotcha: 6.1 serves only flat files 6.1.0 accepted only ^frontend/dist/([^/]+)$; master allows nested paths (FRONTEND_REGEX, apache/superset: superset/extensions/utils.py:43). Keep both page bundles at the top of frontend/dist, disable splitChunks for them, and do not emit source maps into subfolders. Prototype gate G11 confirms that the Studio bundle loads from this endpoint on 6.1; until it passes, the SQL Lab panel is the only guaranteed 6.1 entry.

Reads: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py, superset/tasks/manager.py, superset/charts/schemas.py, servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py (Presenton), servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py (Presenton), servers/fastapi/models/sse_response.py (Presenton) · Builds on: Building the Superset extension · Time: ~50 min This chapter builds the generation runtime of Superset Data-Bound Documents: the databound_docs Python package, shipped as the superset-databound-docs wheel, that the DBD Extension's routes, GTF tasks and MCP tools call. You will lay out its modules, create its tables and object storage, implement the job model and every REST endpoint with its request and response JSON, then build the Template Registry, the LLM provider abstraction, the Binding Registry and Binding Resolver, the renderer interface, event streaming, configuration and caching. The last step maps Presenton's codebase onto this package: which directories to port, which to extend, and which to leave behind. Interpretation this chapter implements Data-Bound Documents is one common, output-agnostic generation framework that turns a prompt, a chosen template and a Superset data context (dashboard and live filters, charts, datasets, semantic views [M], SQL) into (a) PowerPoint decks, (b) documents (DOCX, PDF, Markdown), (c) text (narratives, summaries, emails, alert briefs) and (d) web pages (interactive HTML reports, and in v2 Superset dashboards), on demand or on events (schedules, alerts, data changes, webhooks). Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query run with the requesting user's permissions and RLS, is rendered natively (editable PPTX charts with embedded data, real tables, real text), is never a screenshot, and is re-runnable to refresh with new data. The runtime in this chapter is where that rule is enforced: the LLM never produces a number, and every value enters an artifact only through the Binding Resolver and the Fact Engine. Availability tags are the same as in the previous chapter: [6.1] in the 6.1.0 tag and master, [M] master only, [M*] changed on master.

docs.t: Step 1: Decide where the runtime lives
docs.x: The blueprint's decision is explicit: there is no separate generation service. "Runtime" means the databound_docs library executing inside Superset's own processes. The reasons come straight from Superset's data plane: Concern In-process library (chosen) Presenton-style sidecar (rejected) Acting as the user override_user plus ChartDataCommand in a GTF task; works with every auth type, including OAuth and SSO needs a credential path: DB/LDAP JWT login, master-only API keys, cookie forwarding, or a custom broker Numbers identical to the dashboard same ChartDataCommand, same cache key (which includes RLS, apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313) chart-data over HTTP; on 6.1 with GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES the POST returns 202 and then 401 without the async cookie Operations one wheel plus one .supx; no new web service or database server Postgres, Redis, object storage, Node and Chromium beside Superset Long jobs GTF tasks on a dedicated Celery queue a polling proxy task holding a Celery slot The only optional out-of-process component is the PDF Printer: Chromium inside the worker image (master removed Selenium and requires Playwright with Chromium for report and thumbnail screenshots, apache/superset: UPDATING.md:1621-1645), or a printer_sidecar container that prints DBD's own static HTML.

docs.t: Step 2: Lay out the databound_docs package
docs.x: core/src/databound_docs/ (wheel superset-databound-docs) Three rules keep the package portable and testable: No Superset import at module top level. Superset objects arrive through the adapter argument (the extension's superset_adapter module) or through function-local imports in db/ (which uses Flask-SQLAlchemy's session). A unit test asserts that import databound_docs leaves superset out of sys.modules. No screenshot path. An import-linter contract forbids superset.utils.webdriver, superset.utils.screenshots, superset.utils.screenshot_utils and superset.utils.pdf. Synchronous code. docs.t: Step 4: Model jobs and their states
docs.x: A job is one unit of generation work (generate, continue, regenerate, refresh, render, trigger run). It always has a dbd_job row and one GTF task. The GTF row is authoritative for execution status; dbd_job adds what GTF does not have. dbd_job.status GTF TaskStatus Terminal Notes queued PENDING no row created by POST /documents digest ... rendering (in stage) IN_PROGRESS no stage names mirror STAGES in tasks.py needs_input SUCCESS with payload {"status": "needs_input"} no for DBD, yes for GTF the task ends; continue_generation resumes from agent_state_key succeeded SUCCESS yes partially_succeeded SUCCESS yes at least one format failed to render failed FAILURE or TIMED_OUT yes error holds {message, error_type, retryable, stage} cancelled ABORTED yes via POST /jobs/<id>/cancel A failed binding never fails a job by itself: its element shows "data unavailable" and the job completes with warnings. A job fails only when no binding resolves. databound_docs/db/repo.py (job and event helpers, excerpt) Gotcha: long polls hold a web worker wait_since sleeps inside a gunicorn worker for up to 25 seconds. With sync workers, ten open Studio panels can pin ten workers. Size the web tier for it, keep wait at or below 25 (the handler clamps it), and prefer SSE only when GET /capabilities reports sse: true (gevent or eventlet workers). The expire_all() call matters: without it, the SQLAlchemy identity map returns the same stale rows for the whole request. Gotcha: 6.1 replaces the GTF payload, master merges it Coarse progress is mirrored into GTF with update_task(progress=(i, n), payload={...}) so the built-in Task List and GET /api/v1/task/<uuid>/status [6.1] show it. On 6.1 each call replaces the payload; on master it merges. The runtime always sends the complete payload (stage, document_id, job_id), so both behave the same.

The layout-fit step (deterministic bipartite matching) must discard such layouts before the schema is built, and fall back to generic_chart or generic_text.

For slide prose that is tolerable. For Data-Bound Documents it is not: an invalid outline could reference a binding id outside the enum. call_structured raises instead, and the caller degrades (fallback layout, or deterministic sentences from the Narrative Verifier). Gotcha: Presenton's helpers are async; DBD runs in sync workers Presenton's LLM utilities are async and use the llmai client library (presenton: servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py:13-21). Running an event loop inside a Celery task or a gunicorn sync worker is possible but fragile (nested loops, thread-local Flask state).
