docs.t: 10.1 What stays an extension and what could become core
docs.x: The guiding rule: Superset core gets generic, LLM-free hooks that are useful on their own; Data-Bound Documents stays an extension in its own Apache-2.0 repository. Presenton-derived code never enters apache/superset; importing a substantial body of third-party code would be a code donation needing a Software Grant and IP clearance under ASF practice (policy reasoning, UNVERIFIED for this case), which is avoidable entirely. Capability Where it belongs Reason Public chart-data API (run_chart_query, build_query_context) core (superset_core) every native export, not only DBD, needs it; replaces the riskiest internal imports Context-aware dashboard and Explore slots core (frontend) the 6.1 entry-point gap affects every extension Extension migrations core any extension with tables needs it GTF queue routing core (TaskOptions.queue) TaskOptions already lists queue routing as future work Request-time extension context core a framework bug-class, not a feature "Generator" report recipient type core ReportRecipientType is a closed enum Signed, enriched report webhooks core security improvement for every webhook consumer Palette registry endpoint core any server-side renderer needs palettes Document Spec, Planner, Binding Registry, Fact Engine, Narrative Writer and Verifier, Renderers, templates, triggers, Studio extension product logic, LLM-dependent, faster release cycle Number formatting port (format_number_with_config) already core on master [M] vendored by DBD for 6.1

docs.t: 10.2 The SIP, in Superset's own template
docs.x: Superset's SIP issue template (apache/superset: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/sip.md:1-36) asks for a title of the form "[SIP] Your Title Here", refers to the SIP-0 process (https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/5602), and has the sections Motivation, Proposed Change, New or Changed Public Interfaces, New dependencies, Migration Plan and Compatibility, and Rejected Alternatives. The draft below follows it. [SIP] Data-bound document generation hooks for extensions Motivation. Alerts and Reports deliver dashboards as PNG or raster PDF because chart rendering lives in the browser; build_pdf_from_screenshots stacks PNGs (apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41), and the notification content carrier has no field for native office files (apache/superset: superset/reports/notifications/base.py:26-42). Native, editable, refreshable outputs need stable server-side access to chart data with dashboard context, and UI entry points on dashboards and charts. Today an extension can get neither without importing internal modules or shipping a custom frontend build. Proposed Change. Eight independent, additive items: a. Public chart-data API. A superset_core.charts module that wraps ChartDataCommand, the dashboard filter context and the form_data rebuild, executing as the current g.user: proposed: superset_core/charts/api.py (stub, host-injected like other superset_core APIs) b. Context-aware frontend slots. dashboard.header.actions with props {dashboardId, dataMask, permalink(): Promise<string>}, dashboard.chart.menu with {chartId, dashboardId}, explore.header.actions with {chartId, formData}, and navigation.getEntity(). The navigation namespace's own header comment already says entity-level context is deferred to later phases (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/navigation/index.ts:21-26). proposed: @apache-superset/core contribution props c. Extension migrations: a supported Alembic branch or migration directory per extension, run by superset db upgrade. d. GTF queue routing: TaskOptions.queue, or a documented task_type routing hook. The TaskOptions docstring already lists queue and "Queue routing and priority management" as later additions (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:143-150). e. Request-time extension context: wrap extension routes, MCP tools and task executors in use_context, so get_context() works

Start with the items that are smallest and least controversial (e, d, g, h), each as its own pull request with tests, referencing the SIP. Item a is the most valuable and the most API-shaping; it should land with Data-Bound Documents' Superset Adapter switched to it as a reference consumer, which also deletes most of the adapter's internal imports. Item b needs frontend design review and is easiest to argue for once a, c and e have shown the extension model working end to end. Item f depends on the webhook work and on the report schema. Gotcha: upstream the hooks, not the product A SIP that proposes "add AI document generation to Superset" invites a much larger debate (LLM dependencies, model governance, support burden) than one that proposes eight generic hooks with a working reference consumer outside the repository. Keep the SIP's non-goals explicit: no LLM in Superset core, and Data-Bound Documents remains an independent extension.
